compiler/ast.agc:
## The syntax tree of the Agentica parser: the nodes of src/ast.rkt as structs and enums.
##
## Every node has an Int id and a span. The parser numbers the nodes in post-order: a node's children have smaller ids
## than the node, siblings are numbered in source order, the first id is the one given to the parser (0 for a single
## file), there are no gaps, and the Program has the last one. To number the modules of one program without
## renumbering, parse the next file from next_free_id of the previous Program. The checker keys its types by id,
## because Agentica has no object identity.
##
## Docs (`##` comments) are a field of the declaration, field or variant they document, not a table keyed by span.

import Source from "source"
import Types from "types"

## A value that may be absent; where src/ast.rkt uses #f.
export enum Optional[T]
  Present(T)
  Absent
end

## The value of a literal or of a literal pattern. Huge keeps an integer that does not fit an Int as its digits, with a
## leading - when a pattern negates it.
export enum LitValue
  Whole(Int)
  Huge(String)
  Real(Float)
  Text(String)
  Flag(Bool)
  Nothing
end

## A type written in the source, such as List[Int] or Mod.Type.
export struct TypeRef
  id: Int
  name: String
  args: List[TypeRef]
  span: Source.Span
end

## The root of a parsed file. It has the last id of the tree.
export struct Program
  id: Int
  declarations: List[Decl]
  module_doc: Optional[String]
  span: Source.Span
end

## A top-level declaration.
export enum Decl
  Import(ImportDecl)
  Export(ExportDecl)
  Function(FunctionDecl)
  Struct(StructDecl)
  Enum(EnumDecl)
  Constant(ConstDecl)
end

## An import: import Alias from "path" (alias is Present, names is empty), or import {A, B as C} from "path" (alias is
## Absent, names has at least one entry).
export struct ImportDecl
  id: Int
  path: String
  alias: Optional[String]
  names: List[ImportName]
  span: Source.Span
end

## One entry of an import list: the exported name, the name this file binds (the same without `as`), and the span of
## each (equal without `as`). It has no id: it is part of its ImportDecl.
export struct ImportName
  name: String
  local: String
  span: Source.Span
  local_span: Source.Span
end

## export before a def, struct or enum; its doc is the doc of the declaration.
export struct ExportDecl
  id: Int
  declaration: Decl
  doc: Optional[String]
  span: Source.Span
end

## A module constant: [export] NAME[: Type] = value (docs/future/44-module-constants.md). Unlike the other declarations
## it is not wrapped by an ExportDecl: exported says whether `export` was written, and the span starts at it. The
## linker clears exported.
export struct ConstDecl
  id: Int
  name: String
  type: Optional[TypeRef]
  value: Expr
  exported: Bool
  doc: Optional[String]
  span: Source.Span
end

## def name(params) -> Result with its body.
export struct FunctionDecl
  id: Int
  name: String
  params: List[Param]
  result: TypeRef
  body: List[Stmt]
  doc: Optional[String]
  span: Source.Span
end

## One parameter of a function.
export struct Param
  id: Int
  name: String
  type: TypeRef
  span: Source.Span
end

## A struct and its fields.
export struct StructDecl
  id: Int
  name: String
  fields: List[FieldDecl]
  doc: Optional[String]
  span: Source.Span
end

## One field of a struct.
export struct FieldDecl
  id: Int
  name: String
  type: TypeRef
  doc: Optional[String]
  span: Source.Span
end

## An enum with its type parameters and variants.
export struct EnumDecl
  id: Int
  name: String
  type_parameters: List[String]
  variants: List[EnumVariant]
  doc: Optional[String]
  span: Source.Span
end

## One variant of an enum, with the types of its payload.
export struct EnumVariant
  id: Int
  name: String
  payload_types: List[TypeRef]
  doc: Optional[String]
  span: Source.Span
end

## A statement.
export enum Stmt
  Binding(Binding)
  Return(Return)
  Expression(ExprStmt)
  If(IfStmt)
  While(WhileStmt)
  For(ForStmt)
  Control(LoopControl)
  Case(CaseStmt)
end

## name = value, name: Type = value, or the desugared name += value.
export struct Binding
  id: Int
  name: String
  type: Optional[TypeRef]
  value: Expr
  span: Source.Span
end

## return with an optional value.
export struct Return
  id: Int
  value: Optional[Expr]
  span: Source.Span
end

## An expression used as a statement.
export struct ExprStmt
  id: Int
  value: Expr
  span: Source.Span
end

## The if or elsif part of an if statement: a condition and a body.
export struct IfBranch
  id: Int
  condition: Expr
  body: List[Stmt]
  span: Source.Span
end

## if with its elsif branches. else_body is Present when the else keyword is written, even for an empty body.
export struct IfStmt
  id: Int
  branches: List[IfBranch]
  else_body: Optional[List[Stmt]]
  span: Source.Span
end

## while condition ... end.
export struct WhileStmt
  id: Int
  condition: Expr
  body: List[Stmt]
  span: Source.Span
end

## for variable in iterable ... end.
export struct ForStmt
  id: Int
  variable: String
  iterable: Expr
  body: List[Stmt]
  span: Source.Span
end

## break or next; kind is that word.
export struct LoopControl
  id: Int
  kind: String
  span: Source.Span
end

## case value ... end with its arms.
export struct CaseStmt
  id: Int
  value: Expr
  arms: List[CaseArm]
  span: Source.Span
end

## One arm of a case: a pattern and a body.
export struct CaseArm
  id: Int
  pattern: Pattern
  body: List[Stmt]
  span: Source.Span
end

## The pattern of a case arm.
export enum Pattern
  Wildcard(WildcardPattern)
  Literal(LiteralPattern)
  Variant(VariantPattern)
end

## The pattern _.
export struct WildcardPattern
  id: Int
  span: Source.Span
end

## A literal pattern: a number (possibly negative), a string, true, false or nil.
export struct LiteralPattern
  id: Int
  value: LitValue
  span: Source.Span
end

## An enum variant pattern, or ok(...) and error(...) as Result variants. A binding is Absent for _.
export struct VariantPattern
  id: Int
  enum_name: String
  variant_name: String
  bindings: List[Optional[String]]
  span: Source.Span
end

## An expression.
export enum Expr
  Literal(Literal)
  Name(NameRef)
  Call(Call)
  EnumConstructor(EnumConstructor)
  FunctionRef(FunctionRef)
  Invoke(Invoke)
  Construct(Construct)
  Update(StructUpdate)
  ListLit(ListLit)
  MapLit(MapLit)
  FieldAccess(FieldAccess)
  MethodCall(MethodCall)
  Interpolation(Interpolation)
  BlockLit(BlockLit)
  Index(IndexAccess)
  Try(TryExpr)
  Unary(Unary)
  Binary(Binary)
  TypeName(TypeName)
  Typed(TypedTarget)
  ConstRef(ConstRef)
end

## A number, string, true, false or nil.
export struct Literal
  id: Int
  value: LitValue
  span: Source.Span
end

## A variable name.
export struct NameRef
  id: Int
  name: String
  span: Source.Span
end

## A call by name, with the piped value as first argument after |>. parenthesized records whether the source had
## parentheses; only such a call may be the target of |>.
export struct Call
  id: Int
  name: String
  args: List[Expr]
  piped: Bool
  parenthesized: Bool
  span: Source.Span
end

## Enum.Variant(args), also through a module alias. named is empty from the parser. The linker fills it, and leaves
## args empty, for a call written with names such as Enum.Variant(x: 1), which the parser reads as a Construct; the
## checker refuses it (variants take positional arguments).
export struct EnumConstructor
  id: Int
  enum_name: String
  variant_name: String
  args: List[Expr]
  named: List[NamedArg]
  span: Source.Span
end

## &name or &Alias.name.
export struct FunctionRef
  id: Int
  name: String
  span: Source.Span
end

## target.call(args): a call of a function value.
export struct Invoke
  id: Int
  target: Expr
  args: List[Expr]
  span: Source.Span
end

## name: value in a struct construction.
export struct NamedArg
  id: Int
  name: String
  value: Expr
  span: Source.Span
end

## Type(name: value, ...): a struct construction.
export struct Construct
  id: Int
  type_name: String
  args: List[NamedArg]
  span: Source.Span
end

## target.with(name: value, ...): a copy of a struct with the named fields changed. There is at least one argument.
## visible is Absent from the parser. The linker sets it to the sorted linked names of the user structs that the file
## of the update may build: its own and the exported ones of the files it imports (a builtin record is always allowed,
## so it is not listed). The checker refuses an update of any other user struct (CHECK-IMPORT-NAME). src/ keeps this as
## a predicate in the node.
export struct StructUpdate
  id: Int
  target: Expr
  args: List[NamedArg]
  visible: Optional[List[String]]
  span: Source.Span
end

## [a, b, c].
export struct ListLit
  id: Int
  elements: List[Expr]
  span: Source.Span
end

## key: value in a map literal.
export struct MapEntry
  id: Int
  key: Expr
  value: Expr
  span: Source.Span
end

## {key: value, ...}.
export struct MapLit
  id: Int
  entries: List[MapEntry]
  span: Source.Span
end

## target.name without parentheses.
export struct FieldAccess
  id: Int
  target: Expr
  name: String
  span: Source.Span
end

## target.name(args), with a trailing block as the last argument.
export struct MethodCall
  id: Int
  target: Expr
  name: String
  args: List[Expr]
  span: Source.Span
end

## One part of an interpolated string: text, or an expression.
export enum Part
  Text(String)
  Code(Expr)
end

## A string with #{...} parts; empty text parts are left out.
export struct Interpolation
  id: Int
  parts: List[Part]
  span: Source.Span
end

## do |params| body end.
export struct BlockLit
  id: Int
  params: List[BlockParam]
  body: List[Stmt]
  span: Source.Span
end

## One parameter of a block, with an optional type.
export struct BlockParam
  id: Int
  name: String
  type: Optional[TypeRef]
  span: Source.Span
end

## target[index].
export struct IndexAccess
  id: Int
  target: Expr
  index: Expr
  span: Source.Span
end

## try operand.
export struct TryExpr
  id: Int
  operand: Expr
  span: Source.Span
end

## - or not applied to an operand; op is the token kind (minus or not).
export struct Unary
  id: Int
  op: String
  op_span: Source.Span
  operand: Expr
  span: Source.Span
end

## A binary operator; op is the token kind (plus, and, equal, dot-dot, ...), and a compound assignment is desugared to
## plus, minus, multiply, divide or modulo.
export struct Binary
  id: Int
  op: String
  op_span: Source.Span
  left: Expr
  right: Expr
  span: Source.Span
end

## A type name in expression position: Foo or Mod.Foo.
export struct TypeName
  id: Int
  name: String
  span: Source.Span
end

## The read of a module constant, made by the linker from NAME (name is the linked name), and the receiver of a
## rewritten NAME.method(...) or NAME.field. A receiver made from a call has the id total + the id of the call, where
## total is the number of ids of the program, so it does not clash with a node of the parser (see Linker.Linked.ids).
export struct ConstRef
  id: Int
  name: String
  span: Source.Span
end

## The receiver of a method call that the checker has already checked, with its type, so the builtin rule of the method
## checks it as the first argument without checking it twice (src/ast.rkt: typed-target). The parser never makes it. id
## and span are those of the receiver.
export struct TypedTarget
  id: Int
  target: Expr
  type: Types.Type
  span: Source.Span
end

## The id of an expression node.
export def expr_id(expr: Expr) -> Int
  case expr
    Expr.Literal(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.Name(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.Call(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.EnumConstructor(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.FunctionRef(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.Invoke(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.Construct(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.Update(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.ListLit(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.MapLit(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.FieldAccess(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.MethodCall(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.Interpolation(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.BlockLit(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.Index(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.Try(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.Unary(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.Binary(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.TypeName(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.Typed(node) -> return node.id
    Expr.ConstRef(node) -> return node.id
  end
end

## The span of an expression node.
export def expr_span(expr: Expr) -> Source.Span
  case expr
    Expr.Literal(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.Name(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.Call(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.EnumConstructor(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.FunctionRef(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.Invoke(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.Construct(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.Update(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.ListLit(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.MapLit(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.FieldAccess(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.MethodCall(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.Interpolation(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.BlockLit(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.Index(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.Try(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.Unary(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.Binary(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.TypeName(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.Typed(node) -> return node.span
    Expr.ConstRef(node) -> return node.span
  end
end

## The span of a pattern node.
export def pattern_span(pattern: Pattern) -> Source.Span
  case pattern
    Pattern.Wildcard(node) -> return node.span
    Pattern.Literal(node) -> return node.span
    Pattern.Variant(node) -> return node.span
  end
end

## The first id the next file can use: one more than the id of the Program.
export def next_free_id(program: Program) -> Int
  return program.id + 1
end

import Driver from "bdd_driver"
import Opts from "bdd_options"
import Report from "bdd_report"

# `agentica-vm --allow-run -- bdd.agcb DRIVER_OPTIONS -- ARGUMENTS...` is `agentica test`: it runs the tests and prints
# the report. The exit code is that of the report (0, 1 or 2). bdd_options.agc says what the arguments are;
# src/main.rkt starts this program until the command line itself is ported (docs/future/35-self-hosting.md, step 8).
def main() -> Void
  case Opts.parse(System.args())
    Opts.Parsed.Broken(message) ->
      IO.warn("the BDD driver was started wrongly: #{message}")
      System.exit(2)
    Opts.Parsed.Usage(message, options) -> finish(Report.usage(message, options))
    Opts.Parsed.Ready(options) -> finish(Driver.run(options))
  end
end

def finish(ending: Report.Ending) -> Void
  print(ending.text)
  IO.flush()
  System.exit(ending.code)
end
compiler/bdd_compile.agc:
## Compiling a program for the BDD driver: the Agentica front end from a file to the bytes of its .agcb (link, check,
## lower, write), with the first problem of any stage as one Problem.

import {IO_TIMEOUT} from "bdd_files"
import Report from "bdd_report"
import Writer from "bytecode_writer"
import Problems from "check_failure"
import Checker from "checker"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Env from "link_env"
import Linker from "linker"
import Lowering from "lowering"
import SourceFile from "source_file"

## The result of compiling: the bytes of the program, or the first problem.
export enum Compiled
  Bytes(List[Int])
  Rejected(Problems.Problem)
end

## Compiles the file at `path`. A file that cannot be read is RUNTIME-BDD-INFRA with the message `unreadable`; a file
## that is not UTF-8 is LEX-INVALID-UTF8, in that file. Every problem names `path` as it was given for the root file,
## and the canonical path for the files it imports.
export def file(path: String, settings: Env.Settings, unreadable: String) -> Compiled
  case SourceFile.read(path, IO_TIMEOUT)
    SourceFile.Read.Unreadable(_) -> return Compiled.Rejected(Report.located(path, "RUNTIME-BDD-INFRA", unreadable))
    SourceFile.Read.Invalid(at) -> return Compiled.Rejected(stage_problem(path, SourceFile.invalid_utf8(at)))
    SourceFile.Read.Text(_) -> return link(path, settings)
  end
end

## The problem of a stage that has no file of its own (the lexer and the parser), put in `file`.
export def stage_problem(file: String, problem: Diag.Diagnostic) -> Problems.Problem
  return Problems.problem(file, "", problem.code, problem.message, problem.span, problem.help)
end

def link(path: String, settings: Env.Settings) -> Compiled
  case Linker.link_file(path, settings)
    Linker.Linking.Failed(failure) -> return Compiled.Rejected(stage_problem(failure.file, failure.diagnostic))
    Linker.Linking.Done(linked) -> return check(linked, settings)
  end
end

def check(linked: Linker.Linked, settings: Env.Settings) -> Compiled
  case Checker.check(linked, settings.catalog)
    Checker.Checking.Failed(problem) -> return Compiled.Rejected(problem)
    Checker.Checking.Done(checked) -> return lower(linked, Lowering.lower(linked, checked, settings.catalog))
  end
end

def lower(linked: Linker.Linked, lowered: Lowering.Lowered) -> Compiled
  case lowered
    Lowering.Lowered.Failed(problem) -> return Compiled.Rejected(problem)
    Lowering.Lowered.Done(program) -> return write(Writer.write(linked.root_dir, program))
  end
end

def write(written: Writer.Written) -> Compiled
  case written
    Writer.Written.Failed(problem) -> return Compiled.Rejected(problem)
    Writer.Written.Done(bytes) -> return Compiled.Bytes(bytes)
  end
end
compiler/bdd_discover.agc:
## Finding the test files of a BDD run: the files named on the command line, and the `.feature` and `_test.agc` files
## under the folders named there. Problems come back as entries too, so the report
## shows them next to the files that run.

import {IO_TIMEOUT} from "bdd_files"

## One feature file or test file, or one problem of the search, as the runner reads it (stdlib/test/runner.agc,
## `Entry`): `problem` is "" for a file to run; `kind` is "tests", "feature" or "" (neither); `bytecode`, `source_root`
## and `front_end` are filled in by the driver for a test file.
export struct Entry
  path: String
  problem: String
  kind: String
  bytecode: String
  source_root: String
  front_end: String
end

# What the walk has found so far: the problems in the order they were met, and the files to run.
struct Found
  problems: List[Entry]
  files: List[String]
end

## The kind of a path by its name: "tests" for `_test.agc`, "feature" for `.feature`, else "".
export def kind_of(path: String) -> String
  if path.ends_with?("_test.agc")
    return "tests"
  elsif path.ends_with?(".feature")
    return "feature"
  end
  return ""
end

## The entries for the given paths: first the problems in the order they were met, then the files sorted by path, each
## once. A path is made absolute without following links. A folder is searched for the files whose names fit, in every
## folder below it; a link to a folder is skipped. A path to a file is taken whatever its name is.
export def discover(given: List[String]) -> List[Entry]
  found = Found(problems: [], files: [])
  for text in given
    path = Path.resolve(text).unwrap_or(text)
    info = File.stat(path, IO_TIMEOUT)
    if info.ok? and info.unwrap!.kind == "directory"
      found = walk(path, found)
    elsif info.ok?
      found = Found(problems: found.problems, files: found.files.push(path))
    else
      found = problem(found, path, "test path does not exist")
    end
  end
  entries = found.problems
  previous = ""
  for path in found.files.sort
    if path != previous
      entries = entries.push(entry(path, ""))
    end
    previous = path
  end
  return entries
end

def entry(path: String, problem: String) -> Entry
  return Entry(path: path, problem: problem, kind: kind_of(path), bytecode: "", source_root: "", front_end: "")
end

def problem(found: Found, path: String, message: String) -> Found
  return Found(problems: found.problems.push(entry(path, message)), files: found.files)
end

def walk(directory: String, found: Found) -> Found
  names = Dir.list(directory, IO_TIMEOUT)
  if !names.ok?
    return problem(found, directory, "cannot list the directory: #{names.message}")
  end
  after = found
  for name in names.unwrap!
    after = visit(Path.join([directory, name]).unwrap_or("#{directory}/#{name}"), name, after)
  end
  return after
end

# Dir.list decodes a name with a byte that is not UTF-8 as U+FFFD, and no path can be made from that name, so such a
# name is taken for "not UTF-8" even when the file really has a U+FFFD in its name (the only wrong report). Its kind is
# unknown, so it is a problem only when its name fits (a file) and a folder with such a name is skipped.
def visit(path: String, name: String, found: Found) -> Found
  bad_name = name.contains?(String.from_code(65533))
  info = File.lstat(path, IO_TIMEOUT)
  if !info.ok? and bad_name
    if kind_of(name) != ""
      return problem(found, path, "the file name is not valid UTF-8")
    end
    return found
  elsif !info.ok?
    return problem(found, path, "cannot read the file information: #{info.message}")
  end
  kind = info.unwrap!.kind
  if bad_name and (kind == "directory" or kind_of(name) != "")
    return problem(found, path, "the file name is not valid UTF-8")
  elsif kind == "directory"
    return walk(path, found)
  elsif kind_of(name) == ""
    return found
  elsif kind == "link"
    return follow(path, found)
  end
  return Found(problems: found.problems, files: found.files.push(path))
end

# A link takes part when it names a file that exists and is not a folder.
def follow(path: String, found: Found) -> Found
  target = File.stat(path, IO_TIMEOUT)
  if target.ok? and target.unwrap!.kind != "directory"
    return Found(problems: found.problems, files: found.files.push(path))
  end
  return problem(found, path, "the symbolic link does not name a file")
end
compiler/bdd_driver.agc:
## The BDD driver: what `agentica test` does before and after the runner. It finds the test files,
## compiles the runner, the step program and each test file into a private run directory, writes the configuration,
## starts the runner on the VM and prints its report. The runner (stdlib/test/runner.agc) runs the scenarios and the
## tests.
##
## Every failure of the driver's own work is an infrastructure error (RUNTIME-BDD-INFRA, exit code 2) in the format the
## user asked for. A failure to compile a test file or the step program is not: it goes to the runner, which reports it
## as the error of that file.

import Compile from "bdd_compile"
import Discover from "bdd_discover"
import {IO_TIMEOUT, write_bytes, write_text} from "bdd_files"
import Opts from "bdd_options"
import Report from "bdd_report"
import RunDir from "bdd_rundir"
import Runner from "bdd_runner"
import SourceRoot from "bdd_source_root"
import DiagnosticJson from "diagnostic_json"
import Paths from "import_path"
import Env from "link_env"

# The runner is a program of two lines, and the step program a program of one call when no --steps is given.
RUNNER_ROOT = "import Runner from \"std/test/runner\"\n\ndef main() -> Void\n  Runner.main()\nend\n"
DEFAULT_STEPS = "import BDD from \"std/bdd\"\n\ndef main() -> Void\n  BDD.run([])\nend\n"

# Where the tests are when no path is given.
DEFAULT_PATHS = ["specs/", "test/"]

# The std/ sources on stdin: where each goes in the stdlib/ folder, and what it holds.
struct StdSource
  path: String
  text: String
end

struct StdSources
  files: List[StdSource]
end

# The step program, compiled: where its bytecode is (nothing is written when it did not compile), the source the
# runner names in reports, the folder for the VM's --source-root, and the diagnostic that the runner reports in place
# of the steps ("" when it compiled).
struct Steps
  bytecode: String
  source: String
  root: String
  failure: String
  given: Bool
end

## Runs `agentica test` for the options and says how it ended.
export def run(options: Opts.Options) -> Report.Ending
  if options.steps.size > 1
    return Report.usage("one --steps program; import the other files from it", options)
  end
  found = File.stat(options.vm, IO_TIMEOUT)
  if !found.ok? or found.unwrap!.kind != "file"
    message = "cannot find the VM at #{options.vm}; run make vm or set AGENTICA_VM"
    return Report.infrastructure(message, options.vm, options)
  end
  temporary = RunDir.temporary_directory()
  if !temporary.ok?
    return Report.infrastructure(temporary.message, RunDir.temporary_candidates()[0], options)
  end
  claimed = RunDir.claim(temporary.unwrap!)
  if !claimed.ok?
    return Report.infrastructure(claimed.message, temporary.unwrap!, options)
  end
  run_directory = claimed.unwrap!
  RunDir.sweep(temporary.unwrap!, run_directory)
  ending = inside(run_directory.path, options, temporary.unwrap!)
  RunDir.release(run_directory)
  return ending
end

# The run in its directory. The std/ sources are written first, and the runner compiled before anything else: its
# failure is a bug of the installation.
def inside(directory: String, options: Opts.Options, temporary: String) -> Report.Ending
  installed = install_std_sources(directory)
  if !installed.ok?
    return Report.infrastructure(installed.message, temporary, options)
  end
  settings = Env.settings("#{directory}/std", Env.process_env())
  case compile_runner(directory, settings)
    Compile.Compiled.Rejected(problem) ->
      message = "the BDD runner does not compile: #{problem.message}"
      return Report.infrastructure(message, options.vm, options)
    Compile.Compiled.Bytes(bytes) ->
      ran = prepare_and_run(directory, options, settings, bytes)
      if !ran.ok?
        return Report.infrastructure(ran.message, temporary, options)
      end
      return ran.unwrap!
  end
end

# The std/ sources, which `agentica` has embedded and sends on stdin as {"files": [{"path": ..., "text": ...}]}, go to
# the `std` folder of the run directory, which is the stdlib/ folder of the linker. They live and die with the run.
def install_std_sources(directory: String) -> Result[Void]
  sources = try JSON.decode(IO.read(), StdSources)
  for source in sources.files
    path = "#{directory}/std/#{source.path}"
    try Dir.mkdir(Paths.directory_of(path), IO_TIMEOUT)
    try write_text(path, source.text)
  end
  return ok()
end

def compile_runner(directory: String, settings: Env.Settings) -> Compile.Compiled
  source = "#{directory}/runner.agc"
  written = write_text(source, RUNNER_ROOT)
  if !written.ok?
    return Compile.Compiled.Rejected(Report.located(source, "RUNTIME-BDD-INFRA", written.message))
  end
  return Compile.file(source, settings, "cannot read the runner")
end

# Compiles the step program and the tests, writes the files the runner reads, runs it and reads its report. An error
# is a failure of the driver itself, and a failure of the runner is part of the ending.
def prepare_and_run(
  directory: String, options: Opts.Options, settings: Env.Settings, runner: List[Int]
) -> Result[Report.Ending]
  try write_bytes("#{directory}/runner.agcb", runner)
  steps = try compile_steps(directory, options, settings)
  given = options.paths
  if given.size == 0
    given = DEFAULT_PATHS.filter do |path: String|
      found = File.stat(path, IO_TIMEOUT)
      found.ok? and found.unwrap!.kind == "directory"
    end
  end
  entries = try compile_tests(Discover.discover(given), directory, settings)
  config = Runner.Config(
    vm: options.vm,
    steps_bytecode: steps.bytecode,
    steps_source: steps.source,
    steps_root: steps.root,
    steps_error: steps.failure,
    steps_given: steps.given,
    agentica: options.agentica,
    count: entries.size,
    empty_path: empty_path(given),
    empty_message: empty_message(given),
    style: options.style,
    allow_run: options.allow_run,
    seeded: options.seeded,
    seed: options.seed,
    only: options.only,
    test_timeout_ms: options.test_timeout_ms,
    report_path: "#{directory}/report.txt",
  )
  try write_text("#{directory}/config.jsonl", Runner.config_text(config, entries))
  ran = Runner.run(options, "#{directory}/runner.agcb", "#{directory}/config.jsonl", config.report_path)
  case ran
    Runner.Ran.Reported(code, text) -> return ok(Report.Ending(code: code, text: "#{text}\n"))
    Runner.Ran.Failed(message) -> return ok(Report.infrastructure(message, options.vm, options))
  end
end

# The paths of the empty-run report: the first path given, or the first default folder.
def empty_path(given: List[String]) -> String
  first = DEFAULT_PATHS[0]
  if given.size > 0
    first = given[0]
  end
  return Path.resolve(first).unwrap_or(first)
end

def empty_message(given: List[String]) -> String
  if given.size == 0
    return "no .feature or *_test.agc files found: neither specs/ nor test/ exists"
  end
  return "no .feature or *_test.agc files found"
end

# The step program: the file of --steps, or the default one written in the run directory.
def compile_steps(directory: String, options: Opts.Options, settings: Env.Settings) -> Result[Steps]
  source = "#{directory}/steps.agc"
  root = ""
  compiled = Compile.Compiled.Bytes([])
  if options.steps.size == 0
    try write_text(source, DEFAULT_STEPS)
    compiled = Compile.file(source, settings, "cannot read the step program #{source}")
  else
    source = Path.resolve(options.steps[0]).unwrap_or(options.steps[0])
    root = SourceRoot.option(options.steps[0])
    compiled = Compile.file(source, settings, "cannot read the step program #{options.steps[0]}")
  end
  bytecode = "#{directory}/steps.agcb"
  given = options.steps.size > 0
  case compiled
    Compile.Compiled.Rejected(problem) ->
      error_text = JSON.encode(DiagnosticJson.json(problem))
      return ok(Steps(bytecode: bytecode, source: source, root: root, failure: error_text, given: given))
    Compile.Compiled.Bytes(bytes) ->
      try write_bytes(bytecode, bytes)
      return ok(Steps(bytecode: bytecode, source: source, root: root, failure: "", given: given))
  end
end

# Compiles each test file (`_test.agc`) into the run directory. A file that does not compile keeps its diagnostic in
# `front_end` for the runner to report, and writes nothing. The other entries (feature files and problems) are not
# compiled.
def compile_tests(
  entries: List[Discover.Entry], directory: String, settings: Env.Settings
) -> Result[List[Discover.Entry]]
  out: List[Discover.Entry] = []
  index = 0
  for entry in entries
    if entry.kind == "tests" and entry.problem == ""
      out = out.push(try compile_test(entry, "#{directory}/test-#{index}.agcb", settings))
    else
      out = out.push(entry)
    end
    index += 1
  end
  return ok(out)
end

def compile_test(entry: Discover.Entry, output: String, settings: Env.Settings) -> Result[Discover.Entry]
  front_end = ""
  case Compile.file(entry.path, settings, "cannot read the test file #{entry.path}")
    Compile.Compiled.Rejected(problem) -> front_end = JSON.encode(DiagnosticJson.json(problem))
    Compile.Compiled.Bytes(bytes) -> try write_bytes(output, bytes)
  end
  return ok(entry.with(bytecode: output, source_root: SourceRoot.option(entry.path), front_end: front_end))
end
compiler/bdd_files.agc:
## The files of a BDD run: new files that only the owner can read, written in pieces because one write takes at
## most 1 MiB.

## The deadline, in milliseconds, of each file system call of the driver.
export IO_TIMEOUT = 10000

# At most 1 MiB goes in one call. A character takes up to 4 bytes, so a piece of 250,000 characters always fits.
PIECE_BYTES = 1048576
PIECE_CHARACTERS = 250000

## Writes bytes to a new file with mode 0600. It fails when the path exists (a link in the way included).
export def write_bytes(path: String, bytes: List[Int]) -> Result[Void]
  out = try File.open(path, "create_private", IO_TIMEOUT)
  rest = bytes
  while rest.size > 0
    written = File.write_bytes(out, rest.take(PIECE_BYTES), IO_TIMEOUT)
    if !written.ok?
      File.close(out, IO_TIMEOUT)
      return written
    end
    rest = rest.drop(PIECE_BYTES)
  end
  return File.close(out, IO_TIMEOUT)
end

## Writes text to a new file with mode 0600, as write_bytes does.
export def write_text(path: String, text: String) -> Result[Void]
  out = try File.open(path, "create_private", IO_TIMEOUT)
  at = 0
  while at < text.length
    size = PIECE_CHARACTERS
    if at + size > text.length
      size = text.length - at
    end
    written = File.write(out, text.slice(at, size), IO_TIMEOUT)
    if !written.ok?
      File.close(out, IO_TIMEOUT)
      return written
    end
    at += size
  end
  return File.close(out, IO_TIMEOUT)
end
compiler/bdd_options.agc:
## The arguments of the BDD driver.
##
## `agentica test` (src/main.rkt, src/bdd-driver.rkt) starts the driver as `DRIVER_OPTIONS -- ARGUMENTS`. The driver
## options say what only the front end knows: `--vm PATH` (the VM that runs the runner and the tests), `--agentica
## WORD` (once for each word of the command that runs `agentica`), `--style plain|ai|json`, `--allow-run`, `--seed N`
## and `--test-timeout-ms N`. ARGUMENTS are the words the user wrote after `test`: paths, `--steps FILE`, `--only
## TEXT`, `--json`, `--ai` and `--allow-run`. The `std/` sources come on stdin (bdd_driver.agc).

## Everything a run needs.
export struct Options
  vm: String
  agentica: List[String]
  style: String
  allow_run: Bool
  seeded: Bool
  seed: Int
  test_timeout_ms: Int
  only: String
  steps: List[String]
  paths: List[String]
end

## What the arguments are: options to run with; a usage error of the user (RUNTIME-BDD-USAGE, with the options read so
## far, which say how to report it); or a mistake in the driver options, which is a bug of the caller.
export enum Parsed
  Ready(Options)
  Usage(String, Options)
  Broken(String)
end

## Reads the arguments.
export def parse(arguments: List[String]) -> Parsed
  options = Options(
    vm: "",
    agentica: [],
    style: "plain",
    allow_run: false,
    seeded: false,
    seed: 0,
    test_timeout_ms: 30000,
    only: "",
    steps: [],
    paths: [],
  )
  at = 0
  while at < arguments.size and arguments[at] != "--"
    word = arguments[at]
    if word == "--allow-run"
      options = options.with(allow_run: true)
      at += 1
    elsif at + 1 >= arguments.size
      return Parsed.Broken("#{word} needs a value")
    else
      options = option(options, word, arguments[at + 1])
      at += 2
    end
  end
  if at >= arguments.size
    return Parsed.Broken("the driver options end with --")
  end
  if options.vm == "" or options.agentica.size == 0
    return Parsed.Broken("--vm and --agentica are required")
  end
  return user_arguments(options, arguments.drop(at + 1))
end

# One driver option with its value. An unknown name or a bad number leaves the options as they are, and the checks of
# parse find what is missing.
def option(options: Options, name: String, value: String) -> Options
  if name == "--vm"
    return options.with(vm: value)
  elsif name == "--agentica"
    return options.with(agentica: options.agentica.push(value))
  elsif name == "--style"
    return options.with(style: value)
  elsif name == "--seed"
    return options.with(seeded: true, seed: value.to_int.unwrap_or(0))
  elsif name == "--test-timeout-ms"
    return options.with(test_timeout_ms: value.to_int.unwrap_or(options.test_timeout_ms))
  end
  return options
end

# The words of the user. The last --json or --ai decides the style of every report, usage errors included, so they are
# looked for first, in all the words (a value such as `--only --json` counts too, as it always did).
def user_arguments(options: Options, words: List[String]) -> Parsed
  shown = options
  for word in words
    if word == "--json"
      shown = shown.with(style: "json")
    elsif word == "--ai"
      shown = shown.with(style: "ai")
    end
  end
  at = 0
  while at < words.size
    word = words[at]
    if word == "--steps" or word == "--only"
      if at + 1 >= words.size
        return Parsed.Usage("option needs a value", shown)
      end
      value = words[at + 1]
      if word == "--steps"
        shown = shown.with(steps: shown.steps.push(value))
      elsif shown.only != ""
        return Parsed.Usage("one --only TEXT", shown)
      elsif value == ""
        return Parsed.Usage("--only needs a non-empty TEXT", shown)
      else
        shown = shown.with(only: value)
      end
      at += 2
    elsif word == "--json" or word == "--ai"
      at += 1
    elsif word == "--allow-run"
      shown = shown.with(allow_run: true)
      at += 1
    elsif word.starts_with?("--")
      return Parsed.Usage("unknown option #{word}", shown)
    else
      shown = shown.with(paths: shown.paths.push(word))
      at += 1
    end
  end
  return Parsed.Ready(shown)
end
compiler/bdd_report.agc:
## The reports that the driver writes itself, as one file error: a usage error and an infrastructure error. The
## reports of the tests come from the runner (stdlib/test/runner.agc).

import Opts from "bdd_options"
import Problems from "check_failure"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import DiagnosticJson from "diagnostic_json"
import Source from "source"

## How a run ends: the exit code and the text to print.
export struct Ending
  code: Int
  text: String
end

## The report of a usage error. It is located at `<arguments>`.
export def usage(message: String, options: Opts.Options) -> Ending
  return one_error("<arguments>", "RUNTIME-BDD-USAGE", message, options)
end

## The report of an infrastructure error, located at the start of `file`.
export def infrastructure(message: String, file: String, options: Opts.Options) -> Ending
  return one_error(file, "RUNTIME-BDD-INFRA", message, options)
end

## A problem with no place of its own: the start of the file, and RUNTIME-BDD-INFRA when no code is needed.
export def located(file: String, code: String, message: String) -> Problems.Problem
  start = Source.Position(offset: 0, line: 1, column: 1)
  return Problems.problem(file, "", code, message, Source.Span(start: start, stop: start), Diag.Help.NoHelp)
end

# The report of a run that ends with this one file error: exit code 2, no scenario. The text report has no seed; the
# JSON report has the seed given with --seed, else null.
def one_error(file: String, code: String, message: String, options: Opts.Options) -> Ending
  if options.style == "json"
    seed = JSON.null()
    if options.seeded
      seed = JSON.from(options.seed)
    end
    entry = {
      "path": JSON.from(file),
      "feature": JSON.from(""),
      "kind": JSON.from(""),
      "status": JSON.from("failed"),
      "scenarios": JSON.array([]),
      "error": DiagnosticJson.json(located(file, code, message)),
    }
    report = {
      "ok": JSON.from(false),
      "passed": JSON.from(0),
      "failed": JSON.from(0),
      "not_executed": JSON.from(0),
      "file_errors": JSON.from(1),
      "exit_code": JSON.from(2),
      "seed": seed,
      "files": JSON.array([JSON.object(entry)]),
    }
    return Ending(code: 2, text: "#{JSON.encode(JSON.object(report))}\n")
  end
  separator = "\n"
  if options.style == "ai"
    separator = " | "
  end
  line = "FAIL #{file}#{separator}#{file}:1:1 [#{code}] #{message}\n"
  return Ending(code: 2, text: "#{line}0 passed, 0 failed, 0 not executed, 1 file errors\n")
end
compiler/bdd_rundir.agc:
## The directory of a BDD run: a private folder in the temporary directory that holds the compiled
## runner, the test programs, the configuration and the report, and a locked file that says the run is alive.
##
## A run takes its folder in this order, so no other run can ever find it half made:
##
## 1. `Dir.mkdir_private` makes `agentica-bdd-new-HEX` (mode 0700; it fails when the name exists, so the run never
##    ends up in a folder it did not make).
## 2. A file `lock` is created in it and locked (`File.try_lock`). The lock belongs to the open file, so it ends with
##    the run, also when the run is killed.
## 3. `Path.rename` gives it its final name `agentica-bdd-HEX`, and never replaces a name that is taken.
##
## The sweep looks at final names, so it never meets a folder without a lock. A final name whose lock can be taken
## belongs to a run that has ended, and the sweep removes it. A run killed between steps 1 and 3 leaves an
## `agentica-bdd-new-HEX`; the sweep removes it too, on the same checks, but only when it has not changed for an hour,
## because a run that is alive is in step 1 or 2 for a moment and has no lock held yet.

import {IO_TIMEOUT} from "bdd_files"

# How many names a run tries before it gives up: a name can be taken, and a hostile user could take names on purpose.
ATTEMPTS = 16
STALE_NEW_SECONDS = 3600
DIGITS = "0123456789abcdef"

## A claimed run directory: its final path, and the open lock file. The lock is released when the handle is closed.
export struct Run
  path: String
  lock: FileHandle
end

## The places that can hold the temporary directory, best first: TMPDIR when it is set, then /var/tmp, /usr/tmp and
## /tmp (the choice of Racket's `find-system-path 'temp-dir`, which the Racket driver used).
export def temporary_candidates() -> List[String]
  candidates: List[String] = []
  from_environment = System.env("TMPDIR")
  if from_environment.ok?
    candidates = candidates.push(from_environment.unwrap!)
  end
  return candidates.concat(["/var/tmp", "/usr/tmp", "/tmp"])
end

## The temporary directory: the first of `temporary_candidates()` that is a directory.
export def temporary_directory() -> Result[String]
  candidates = temporary_candidates()
  for path in candidates
    info = File.stat(path, IO_TIMEOUT)
    if info.ok? and info.unwrap!.kind == "directory"
      return ok(path)
    end
  end
  return error("no temporary directory: none of #{candidates.join(", ")} is a directory")
end

## Makes the run directory in `temporary`, locked and under its final name. Nothing is left behind on a failure.
export def claim(temporary: String) -> Result[Run]
  current = try make_private(temporary)
  claimed = lock_and_name(temporary, current)
  if !claimed.ok?
    Path.remove(current, IO_TIMEOUT)
  end
  return claimed
end

## Removes the run directory and releases its lock. The removal is best effort: what stays is swept by a later run.
export def release(run: Run) -> Void
  Path.remove(run.path, IO_TIMEOUT)
  File.close(run.lock, IO_TIMEOUT)
end

## Removes the run directories of runs that have ended: the folders named `agentica-bdd-HEX` in `temporary`, and the
## old ones named `agentica-bdd-new-HEX`, made by the user of `own` (a folder of another user is never touched), that
## have a `lock` file nobody holds. `own` is not removed. A folder that cannot be inspected or removed stays.
export def sweep(temporary: String, own: Run) -> Void
  owner = File.lstat(own.path, IO_TIMEOUT)
  names = Dir.list(temporary, IO_TIMEOUT)
  if !owner.ok? or !names.ok?
    return
  end
  for name in names.unwrap!
    joined = Path.join([temporary, name])
    if !joined.ok?
      next
    end
    path = joined.unwrap!
    # The minimum age in seconds of the folder to remove, or -1 for a name that is not a run directory.
    age = -1
    if hex_name?(name, "agentica-bdd-") and path != own.path
      age = 0
    elsif hex_name?(name, "agentica-bdd-new-")
      age = STALE_NEW_SECONDS
    end
    if age >= 0
      held = abandoned(path, owner.unwrap!.user_id, age)
      if held.ok?
        Path.remove(path, IO_TIMEOUT)
        File.close(held.unwrap!, IO_TIMEOUT)
      end
    end
  end
end

# A random name: 16 bytes of /dev/urandom as hex, so it cannot be guessed (Random.int has a 31-bit seed).
def random_hex() -> Result[String]
  source = try File.open("/dev/urandom", "read", IO_TIMEOUT)
  bytes: List[Int] = []
  while bytes.size < 16
    got = File.read_bytes(source, 16 - bytes.size, IO_TIMEOUT)
    if !got.ok? or got.unwrap!.size == 0
      File.close(source, IO_TIMEOUT)
      return error("cannot read /dev/urandom")
    end
    bytes = bytes.concat(got.unwrap!)
  end
  try File.close(source, IO_TIMEOUT)
  digits = bytes.map do |byte: Int|
    "#{DIGITS.slice(byte.shift_right(4), 1)}#{DIGITS.slice(byte.bit_and(15), 1)}"
  end
  return ok(digits.join(""))
end

# The first free name among ATTEMPTS random ones. A name that is taken is skipped, and any other error ends the
# attempts the same way, with the last system error.
def make_private(temporary: String) -> Result[String]
  last = "no attempt was made"
  attempt = 0
  while attempt < ATTEMPTS
    name = try random_hex()
    path = try Path.join([temporary, "agentica-bdd-new-#{name}"])
    made = Dir.mkdir_private(path, IO_TIMEOUT)
    if made.ok?
      return ok(path)
    end
    last = made.message
    attempt += 1
  end
  return error("cannot make a private directory in #{temporary}: #{last}")
end

def lock_and_name(temporary: String, current: String) -> Result[Run]
  shared = try shared_and_not_sticky?(temporary, current)
  if shared
    return error("the temporary directory #{temporary} is shared and not sticky; set TMPDIR to a private folder")
  end
  name = try random_hex()
  final = try Path.join([temporary, "agentica-bdd-#{name}"])
  lock = try take_lock(current)
  renamed = Path.rename(current, final, IO_TIMEOUT)
  if !renamed.ok?
    File.close(lock, IO_TIMEOUT)
    return error("cannot name the run directory #{final}: #{renamed.message}")
  end
  return ok(Run(path: final, lock: lock))
end

# Creates the lock file and locks it. It is a new file, so a name in the way is an error and never a link followed.
def take_lock(directory: String) -> Result[FileHandle]
  path = try Path.join([directory, "lock"])
  lock = try File.open(path, "create_private", IO_TIMEOUT)
  taken = File.try_lock(lock, IO_TIMEOUT)
  if taken.ok? and taken.unwrap!
    return ok(lock)
  end
  File.close(lock, IO_TIMEOUT)
  return error("cannot lock #{directory}")
end

# A temporary directory where other users can write and delete our entries is not safe for a run that trusts its
# files: it is the case when others can write (mode o+w) or the group can write (g+w) and the directory is not ours
# alone in user and group without the setgid bit, and the sticky bit (which stops others from deleting our entries) is
# not set. `own` is a folder we just made, so it tells our user and group.
def shared_and_not_sticky?(temporary: String, own: String) -> Result[Bool]
  folder = try File.stat(temporary, IO_TIMEOUT)
  mine = try File.lstat(own, IO_TIMEOUT)
  mode = folder.mode
  if mode.bit_and(512) != 0
    return ok(false)
  end
  others_write = mode.bit_and(2) != 0
  group_write = mode.bit_and(16) != 0
  setgid = mode.bit_and(1024) != 0
  ours_alone = folder.user_id == mine.user_id and folder.group_id == mine.group_id and !setgid
  return ok(others_write or (group_write and !ours_alone))
end

# The prefix and then hexadecimal digits only. `agentica-bdd-` is the final name of a run, `agentica-bdd-new-` a run
# being made (the "n" of "new" is not a digit, so the first never matches the second).
def hex_name?(name: String, prefix: String) -> Bool
  if !name.starts_with?(prefix) or name.length == prefix.length
    return false
  end
  for digit in name.slice(prefix.length, name.length - prefix.length).split("")
    if !DIGITS.contains?(digit)
      return false
    end
  end
  return true
end

# The lock of a folder that may belong to a run that ended: ok(handle) when the folder is a real folder (not a link) of
# `owner` with a real `lock` file whose lock this call took, and not changed in the last `age` seconds. The handle
# keeps the folder from being claimed by another sweep until it is closed. A lock held by a live run is an error.
def abandoned(path: String, owner: Int, age: Int) -> Result[FileHandle]
  folder = try File.lstat(path, IO_TIMEOUT)
  lock_path = try Path.join([path, "lock"])
  lock_info = try File.lstat(lock_path, IO_TIMEOUT)
  if folder.kind != "directory" or folder.user_id != owner or lock_info.kind != "file"
    return error("not a run directory")
  end
  if age > 0 and Time.now_ms() / 1000 - folder.modified_seconds < age
    return error("too new to be abandoned")
  end
  lock = try File.open(lock_path, "read", IO_TIMEOUT)
  taken = File.try_lock(lock, IO_TIMEOUT)
  if taken.ok? and taken.unwrap!
    return ok(lock)
  end
  File.close(lock, IO_TIMEOUT)
  return error("the run is alive")
end
compiler/bdd_runner.agc:
## Starting the BDD runner and reading what it reports.
##
## The runner (stdlib/test/runner.agc) is a program of its own, run by the same VM as a captured child. It reads the
## configuration file, runs the tests and writes its report to a file of the run directory. It does not print the
## report: a captured child keeps 1 MiB of each stream and drops the rest, and a report of a big run is larger.

import Discover from "bdd_discover"
import {IO_TIMEOUT} from "bdd_files"
import Opts from "bdd_options"
import SourceFile from "source_file"

# The runner is an ordinary program with a 30 second start, and no limit on its run (each scenario has its own).
START_TIMEOUT = 30000
WAIT_SLICE = 3600000
MAXIMUM_EXIT_CODE = 2

## The first line of the configuration file, as the runner decodes it (`Config` in stdlib/test/runner.agc).
export struct Config
  vm: String
  steps_bytecode: String
  steps_source: String
  steps_root: String
  steps_error: String
  steps_given: Bool
  agentica: List[String]
  count: Int
  empty_path: String
  empty_message: String
  style: String
  allow_run: Bool
  seeded: Bool
  seed: Int
  only: String
  test_timeout_ms: Int
  report_path: String
end

## How a runner ended: with the exit code and the report it wrote, or with a message that says why it has no report.
export enum Ran
  Reported(Int, String)
  Failed(String)
end

## The text of the configuration file: the settings, then one line for each entry.
export def config_text(config: Config, entries: List[Discover.Entry]) -> String
  lines = [JSON.encode(config)].concat(entries.map do |entry: Discover.Entry| JSON.encode(entry) end)
  return "#{lines.join("\n")}\n"
end

## Runs the runner program `runner` on `config_file` with the VM of the options, waits for it, and reads the report at
## `report_file`. The child gets this program's process id with --driver-pid, so it ends if this program does.
export def run(options: Opts.Options, runner: String, config_file: String, report_file: String) -> Ran
  words = ["--allow-run"]
  if options.seeded
    words = words.concat(["--seed", options.seed.to_s])
  end
  words = words.concat(["--driver-pid", System.pid().to_s, "--", runner, config_file])
  spawned = Process.spawn_captured(options.vm, words, ".", START_TIMEOUT)
  if !spawned.ok?
    return Ran.Failed("cannot start the BDD runner: #{spawned.message}")
  end
  child = spawned.unwrap!
  Process.close_stdin(child, IO_TIMEOUT)
  code = wait_for(child)
  output = Process.output(child, START_TIMEOUT)
  Process.close(child)
  if !code.ok?
    return Ran.Failed("the BDD runner did not end: #{code.message}")
  elsif !output.ok?
    return Ran.Failed("the BDD runner did not close its output: #{output.message}")
  end
  stderr = output.unwrap!.stderr
  if code.unwrap! < 0 or code.unwrap! > MAXIMUM_EXIT_CODE or stderr != ""
    return Ran.Failed("the BDD runner failed with exit code #{code.unwrap!}: #{message_line(stderr)}")
  end
  return read_report(code.unwrap!, report_file)
end

# Waits as long as the run takes: a wait that times out is repeated.
def wait_for(child: Process) -> Result[Int]
  waited = Process.wait(child, WAIT_SLICE)
  while !waited.ok? and waited.message == "network: operation timed out"
    waited = Process.wait(child, WAIT_SLICE)
  end
  return waited
end

def read_report(code: Int, report_file: String) -> Ran
  case SourceFile.read(report_file, IO_TIMEOUT)
    SourceFile.Read.Text(text) -> return Ran.Reported(code, text)
    SourceFile.Read.Invalid(_) -> return Ran.Failed("the BDD runner wrote a report that is not UTF-8")
    SourceFile.Read.Unreadable(message) -> return Ran.Failed("the BDD runner wrote no report: #{message}")
  end
end

# What the runner said on stderr, in a line: the last diagnostic (the line that names its code and the one after it),
# not the stack frame that comes last. An earlier diagnostic, such as the crash of a task, is not the reason the
# runner ended.
def message_line(text: String) -> String
  lines = text.split("\n").filter do |line: String| line != "" end
  if lines.size == 0
    return "no diagnostic"
  end
  first = 0
  index = 0
  for line in lines
    if diagnostic_header?(line)
      first = index
    end
    index += 1
  end
  return lines.drop(first).take(2).join(" ")
end

# `PLACE:LINE:COLUMN error[CODE]` and nothing after it.
def diagnostic_header?(line: String) -> Bool
  marker = line.index_of(" error[")
  if !marker.ok? or !line.ends_with?("]")
    return false
  end
  place = line.slice(0, marker.unwrap!).split(":")
  code = line.slice(marker.unwrap! + 7, line.length - marker.unwrap! - 8)
  if place.size < 3 or code == "" or place.take(place.size - 2).join(":") == ""
    return false
  end
  return number?(place[place.size - 1]) and number?(place[place.size - 2]) and code_text?(code)
end

def number?(text: String) -> Bool
  return text.length > 0 and text.to_int.ok? and !text.starts_with?("-") and !text.starts_with?("+")
end

def code_text?(text: String) -> Bool
  for character in text.split("")
    point = String.code(character)
    if !((point >= 65 and point <= 90) or (point >= 48 and point <= 57) or point == 45)
      return false
    end
  end
  return true
end
compiler/bdd_source_root.agc:
## The `--source-root` option of the VM for a program (source-root-option in src/source.rkt): the folder of the program
## as the user should type it, which the VM puts before the stored names it prints, so a runtime trace names a file the
## way a compile-time diagnostic does.

import Paths from "import_path"

## The folder of the file `entry`: relative to the working directory (built from the canonical folder, so the ".."
## names of an imported file stay right through links), or absolute when the entry was typed as an absolute path. It is
## "" when the file is in the working directory, and also when a path cannot be resolved.
export def option(entry: String) -> String
  real = Path.real(entry)
  if !real.ok?
    return ""
  end
  folder = Paths.directory_of(real.unwrap!)
  if entry.starts_with?("/")
    return folder
  end
  here = Path.cwd()
  if !here.ok?
    return ""
  end
  canonical = Path.real(here.unwrap!)
  if !canonical.ok?
    return ""
  end
  return relative(parts(canonical.unwrap!), parts(folder))
end

# The path of `to` from `from`: one ".." for each part of `from` that `to` does not share, then the rest of `to`.
def relative(from: List[String], to: List[String]) -> String
  shared = 0
  while shared < from.size and shared < to.size and from[shared] == to[shared]
    shared += 1
  end
  names: List[String] = []
  for index in shared...from.size
    names = names.push("..")
  end
  for index in shared...to.size
    names = names.push(to[index])
  end
  return names.join("/")
end

def parts(path: String) -> List[String]
  return path.split("/").filter do |part: String| part != "" end
end

import Types from "types"

## The special checking rule of a builtin, the `rule` field of a src/builtins.rkt row. Plain is no rule (#f): the

  Error
  Identity
  JsonDecode
  JsonEncode
  JsonFrom
  JsonSchema
  ListAll
  ListAny
  ListAppend

  ListCount
  ListEach
  ListFilter

  SetQuery
  SetSubset
  SetToA
  Show

  TaskAwaitTimeout
  TaskSpawn
  TaskSpawnOwning
  TestEq
  TestResult
end

## A name with a type: a parameter of a builtin, or a field of a struct.
export struct Named
  name: String
  type: Types.Type
end

## One builtin. A name may have alternatives: other forms with a different number of parameters (ok(), Task.await with
## a timeout, Map.get with a default). implementation is the name of the VM builtin; effects are the capabilities it
## needs (stdout, network, ...).
export struct Builtin
  name: String
  parameters: List[Named]
  result: Types.Type
  rule: Rule
  implementation: String
  effects: List[String]
  description: String
  alternatives: List[Builtin]
end

## A builtin record type, such as HttpRequest, with its fields in declaration order.
export struct Record
  name: String
  fields: List[Named]
end

## One variant of an enum and the types of its payload.
export struct Variant
  name: String
  payload: List[Types.Type]
end

## An enum with its type parameters and variants in declaration order. The builtin enums (Await, LogLevel) and, in the
## checker, the enums of the program have this shape.
export struct EnumDef
  name: String
  parameters: List[String]
  variants: List[Variant]
end
compiler/builtins.agc:
## The builtin catalog (src/builtins.rkt, src/builtin-types.rkt): every builtin function with its signature, the
## builtin records and enums, and the lookups the linker and the checker make. One Catalog is built per run from the
## generated rows of builtins_data.agc; every lookup is a Map or Set access.

import Model from "builtin_model"
import Data from "builtins_data"
import Types from "types"

## A module only std/ may call: the std module that wraps it and the alias its help shows.
export struct StdOnly
  std_path: String
  alias: String
end

## The lookup tables of the catalog. entries holds the first form of each builtin (its alternatives are inside it).
## public_names are the names a program may call, sorted: all but those of the std-only modules. bare_names are the
## builtins written as a plain name (puts, ok). reserved is the set of type names no declaration may take.
export struct Catalog
  entries: Map[String, Model.Builtin]
  public_names: List[String]
  bare_names: Set[String]
  records: Map[String, List[Model.Named]]
  enums: Map[String, Model.EnumDef]
  opaque: Set[String]
  handles: Set[String]
  reserved: Set[String]
  std_only: Map[String, StdOnly]
end

## The catalog of this run.
export def catalog() -> Catalog
  entries = entry_table()
  std_only = std_only_table()
  names = entries.keys
  return Catalog(
    entries: entries,
    public_names: public_names(names, std_only),
    bare_names: bare_names(names),
    records: record_table(),
    enums: enum_table(),
    opaque: Set.new(Data.opaque_types()),
    handles: Set.new(Data.handle_types()),
    reserved: Set.new(Data.reserved_type_names()),
    std_only: std_only
  )
end

## The builtin of that name, or an error when there is none (builtin-ref without an arity).
export def lookup(catalog: Catalog, name: String) -> Result[Model.Builtin]
  return catalog.entries.get(name)
end

## The form of a builtin that takes that many arguments, or an error when none does.
export def form_for(entry: Model.Builtin, arity: Int) -> Result[Model.Builtin]
  if entry.parameters.size == arity
    return ok(entry)
  end
  for alternative in entry.alternatives
    if alternative.parameters.size == arity
      return ok(alternative)
    end
  end
  return error("no form with that arity")
end

## The form of the builtin name that takes that many arguments (builtin-ref with an arity).
export def ref(catalog: Catalog, name: String, arity: Int) -> Result[Model.Builtin]
  entry = try lookup(catalog, name)
  return form_for(entry, arity)
end

## True for a name inside a std-only module, such as HttpWire.client.
export def std_only_name?(catalog: Catalog, name: String) -> Bool
  return catalog.std_only.has_key?(module_of(name))
end

## The signature of every form of a builtin, one per line: name(param: Type, ...) -> Result.
export def signature(entry: Model.Builtin) -> String
  forms = [entry].concat(entry.alternatives)
  return forms.map do |form: Model.Builtin| form_signature(form) end.join("\n")
end

## The signature of one form.
export def form_signature(form: Model.Builtin) -> String
  parameters = form.parameters.map do |parameter: Model.Named|
    "#{parameter.name}: #{Types.to_text(parameter.type)}"
  end
  return "#{form.name}(#{parameters.join(", ")}) -> #{Types.to_text(form.result)}"
end

# The part of a builtin name before its first dot: the module.
def module_of(name: String) -> String
  dot = name.index_of(".")
  if dot.ok?
    return name.slice(0, dot.unwrap!)
  end
  return ""
end

def entry_table() -> Map[String, Model.Builtin]
  found: Map[String, Model.Builtin] = {}
  for row in Data.builtin_rows()
    found = found.put(row.name, row)
  end
  return found
end

def record_table() -> Map[String, List[Model.Named]]
  found: Map[String, List[Model.Named]] = {}
  for record in Data.records()
    found = found.put(record.name, record.fields)
  end
  return found
end

def enum_table() -> Map[String, Model.EnumDef]
  found: Map[String, Model.EnumDef] = {}
  for definition in Data.enums()
    found = found.put(definition.name, definition)
  end
  return found
end

def std_only_table() -> Map[String, StdOnly]
  found: Map[String, StdOnly] = {}
  imports = Data.std_only_imports()
  for name in imports.keys
    found = found.put(name, StdOnly(std_path: imports[name][0], alias: imports[name][1]))
  end
  return found
end

# Map.keys is in insertion order and the rows are sorted by name, so the lists stay sorted.
def public_names(names: List[String], std_only: Map[String, StdOnly]) -> List[String]
  return names.filter do |name: String| !std_only.has_key?(module_of(name)) end
end

def bare_names(names: List[String]) -> Set[String]
  return Set.new(names.filter do |name: String| !name.contains?(".") end)
end
