compiler/bytecode.agc:
import Writer from "bytecode_writer"
import CheckText from "check_text"
import Checker from "checker"
import Env from "link_env"
import LinkText from "link_text"
import Linker from "linker"
import Lowering from "lowering"
import LowerText from "lower_text"

# `agentica compiler/bytecode.agc [flags] ROOT -o OUT ...` links, checks, lowers and writes each ROOT file to the .agcb
# file OUT, and prints `== ROOT`, then `wrote N bytes` or the ERROR line of the first failure (those of lower.agc, and
# BYTECODE- ones). No file is written for a failure. The flags are those of link.agc and apply to the roots after them:
# `--stdlib=DIR` (the default is stdlib), `--agentica-path=V`, `--xdg-data-home=V` and `--home=V`.
def main() -> Void
  stdlib = "stdlib"
  env = Env.process_env()
  root = ""
  output_next = false
  for argument in System.args()
    if output_next
      output_next = false
      puts("== #{root}")
      puts(compile(root, argument, Env.settings(stdlib, env)))
    elsif argument == "-o"
      output_next = true
    elsif argument.starts_with?("--stdlib=")
      stdlib = argument.slice(9, argument.length - 9)
    elsif argument.starts_with?("--agentica-path=")
      env = env.with(agentica_path: argument.slice(16, argument.length - 16))
    elsif argument.starts_with?("--xdg-data-home=")
      env = env.with(xdg_data_home: argument.slice(16, argument.length - 16))
    elsif argument.starts_with?("--home=")
      env = env.with(home: argument.slice(7, argument.length - 7))
    else
      root = argument
    end
  end
end

# Compiles the file at path into the file at output, and says what happened in one line.
def compile(path: String, output: String, settings: Env.Settings) -> String
  case Linker.link_file(path, settings)
    Linker.Linking.Failed(failure) -> return LinkText.failure_text(LinkText.root_dir_of(path), failure)
    Linker.Linking.Done(linked) -> return check(linked, output, settings)
  end
end

def check(linked: Linker.Linked, output: String, settings: Env.Settings) -> String
  case Checker.check(linked, settings.catalog)
    Checker.Checking.Failed(problem) -> return CheckText.problem_text(linked.root_dir, problem)
    Checker.Checking.Done(checked) -> return lower(linked, Lowering.lower(linked, checked, settings.catalog), output)
  end
end

def lower(linked: Linker.Linked, lowered: Lowering.Lowered, output: String) -> String
  case lowered
    Lowering.Lowered.Failed(problem) -> return LowerText.problem_text(linked.root_dir, problem)
    Lowering.Lowered.Done(program) -> return write(linked.root_dir, Writer.write(linked.root_dir, program), output)
  end
end

def write(root_dir: String, written: Writer.Written, output: String) -> String
  case written
    Writer.Written.Failed(problem) -> return LowerText.problem_text(root_dir, problem)
    Writer.Written.Done(bytes) ->
      saved = save(output, bytes)
      if saved.ok?
        return "wrote #{bytes.size} bytes"
      end
      return "cannot write #{output}: #{saved.message}"
  end
end

# Saves the bytes in pieces of 1 MiB, the most File.write_bytes takes.
def save(path: String, bytes: List[Int]) -> Result[Void]
  out = try File.open(path, "write", 60000)
  rest = bytes
  while rest.size > 0
    try File.write_bytes(out, rest.take(1048576), 60000)
    rest = rest.drop(1048576)
  end
  try File.close(out, 60000)
  return ok()
end
compiler/bytecode_bytes.agc:
## The byte encoding of the bytecode writer: little-endian integers, UTF-8 text, and the chunk lists the file is
## built from. The output is a list of chunks that Binary.concat joins once; a chunk grows only by appending a small
## piece, which costs O(piece) (docs/grammar/06b-builtins.md, List.concat), so nothing copies the output twice.

import Binary from "std/binary"

# A piece of this many bytes or fewer joins the last chunk; a longer one is a chunk of its own.
SMALL_PIECE = 32

## The 2 bytes of a number in 0 .. 65535, low byte first.
export def u16(number: Int) -> List[Int]
  return [number % 256, number / 256]
end

## The 4 bytes of a number in 0 .. 4294967295, low byte first.
export def u32(number: Int) -> List[Int]
  if number < 65536
    return [number % 256, number / 256, 0, 0]
  end
  return [number % 256, (number / 256) % 256, (number / 65536) % 256, number / 16777216]
end

## The 8 bytes of a signed number, low byte first (a two's complement integer).
export def i64(number: Int) -> List[Int]
  return Binary.write_i64_le(number)
end

## The 8 bytes of the IEEE 754 binary64 of a number, low byte first.
export def f64(number: Float) -> List[Int]
  return Binary.write_f64_le(number)
end

## The UTF-8 bytes of a text. A text of ASCII characters only is its own character codes.
export def utf8(text: String) -> List[Int]
  codes = text.split("").map do |character: String| String.code(character) end
  if codes.all? do |code: Int| code < 128 end
    return codes
  end
  out: List[Int] = []
  for code in codes
    out = out.concat(encoded(code))
  end
  return out
end

## A text as the file stores it: the number of its UTF-8 bytes as a u32, then the bytes.
export def string(text: String) -> List[Int]
  data = utf8(text)
  return u32(data.size).concat(data)
end

## An empty list of chunks. It always holds a last chunk, which add appends to.
export def start() -> List[List[Int]]
  return [[]]
end

## The chunks with the piece added at the end: a small piece joins the last chunk, a long one becomes a chunk.
export def add(chunks: List[List[Int]], piece: List[Int]) -> List[List[Int]]
  if piece.size > SMALL_PIECE
    return chunks.push(piece)
  end
  last = chunks.size - 1
  return chunks.set(last, chunks[last].concat(piece))
end

## The chunks with the chunks of another list added at the end.
export def add_all(chunks: List[List[Int]], more: List[List[Int]]) -> List[List[Int]]
  out = chunks
  for chunk in more
    out = add(out, chunk)
  end
  return out
end

## All the chunks as one list of bytes.
export def join(chunks: List[List[Int]]) -> List[Int]
  return Binary.concat(chunks)
end

# The UTF-8 bytes of one code point (1 to 4 bytes; Racket strings hold no surrogates).
def encoded(code: Int) -> List[Int]
  if code < 128
    return [code]
  elsif code < 2048
    return [192 + code / 64, 128 + code % 64]
  elsif code < 65536
    return [224 + code / 4096, 128 + (code / 64) % 64, 128 + code % 64]
  end
  return [240 + code / 262144, 128 + (code / 4096) % 64, 128 + (code / 64) % 64, 128 + code % 64]
end
compiler/bytecode_failure.agc:
## The BYTECODE- problems of the writer. A failing step returns `error(...)` of a packed problem (check_failure.agc
## pack), as the lowering does, and `try` carries it to the writer, which unpacks it.

import Failure from "check_failure"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Ir from "ir"
import Source from "source"

## BYTECODE-LIMIT: the program has too many of something for the format. file is the index of the source that the span
## is in.
export def limit(program: Ir.Program, file: Int, what: String, span: Source.Span) -> String
  message = "the program has too many #{what} for the VM"
  found = Failure.problem(program.sources[file].file, "", "BYTECODE-LIMIT", message, span, Diag.Help.NoHelp)
  return Failure.pack(found)
end

## BYTECODE-INTERNAL: the IR holds something the writer cannot write. Lowering never gives such an IR; this is what
## src/bytecode.rkt reports for the Racket exception it would raise: at the span of the program, with a message of the
## writer's own.
export def internal(program: Ir.Program, message: String) -> String
  found = Failure.problem(program.sources[0].file, "", "BYTECODE-INTERNAL", message, program.span, Diag.Help.NoHelp)
  return Failure.pack(found)
end
compiler/bytecode_function.agc:
## Encodes one function of the program (src/bytecode.rkt, `encode-function`): the instructions as four u16 words, a
## label as the number of the instruction after it, runs of `step` merged, and the constants, struct updates, builtins
## and spans the instructions name interned in the tables.
##
## A function body is flat, so this is a loop over the instructions and uses no recursion.

import Wire from "bytecode_bytes"
import Failure from "bytecode_failure"
import Pool from "bytecode_pool"
import Spans from "bytecode_spans"
import {MAX_U16, NEEDS, OPCODES, PAIR_OPS, SINGLE_OPS, WIDE_OPS} from "bytecode_tables"
import Ir from "ir"

## What the writer has interned so far: the entries of the constant, struct update, builtin and span sections.
export struct Tables
  constants: Pool.Pool
  updates: Pool.Pool
  builtins: Pool.Pool
  spans: Pool.Pool
end

## The bytes of a function in the file (its header, its code and the span of each instruction, as three chunks) and
## the tables after it.
export struct Encoded
  tables: Tables
  parts: List[List[Int]]
end

# The operands an instruction is written with, and the tables after naming what it needs. The instruction is written
# as the opcode and three u16 operands, or, when generic, as the operands it has.
struct Operands
  tables: Tables
  a: Int
  b: Int
  c: Int
  generic: Bool
end

## Encodes a function. It fails with BYTECODE-LIMIT when the function has more than 65,535 registers or the program
## more than 65,535 distinct struct updates.
export def encode(program: Ir.Program, tables: Tables, function: Ir.Function) -> Result[Encoded]
  if function.slots > MAX_U16
    return error(Failure.limit(program, function.file, "registers in one function", function.span))
  end
  body = function.body
  labels = label_pcs(body)
  # The constant, update and builtin pools travel in state. The span pool is a local of its own: operands never read
  # state.spans, so it is stored back once, after the loop.
  state = tables
  span_pool = tables.spans
  code: List[Int] = []
  refs: List[Int] = []
  count = 0
  at = 0
  while at < body.size
    instr = body[at]
    op = instr.op
    if op == "label"
      at += 1
      next
    end
    run = 1
    if op == "step"
      run = step_run_end(body, at) - at
    end
    found = try operands(program, function, labels, state, instr, run)
    state = found.tables
    words = try instr_words(program, instr, found)
    code = code.concat(words)
    interned = Spans.intern_run(span_pool, body, at, run)
    span_pool = interned.pool
    refs = refs.concat(Wire.u32(interned.id))
    count += 1
    at += run
  end
  # The span of the function comes after those of its instructions.
  own = Spans.intern_one(span_pool, function.file, function.span)
  head = Wire.string(function.name).concat(Wire.u32(function.params)).concat(Wire.u32(function.captures))
  head = head.concat(Wire.u32(function.slots)).concat(Wire.u32(own.id)).concat(Wire.u32(count))
  return ok(Encoded(tables: state.with(spans: own.pool), parts: [head, code, refs]))
end

# The operands of one instruction, which is a written run of `run` instructions when it is a `step`. The tables gain
# the entry the instruction names, if it has one. The first case that matches wins, so const and the jumps come
# before WIDE_OPS, as in the chain this replaced.
def operands(
  program: Ir.Program, function: Ir.Function, labels: Map[Int, Int], tables: Tables, instr: Ir.Instr, run: Int
) -> Result[Operands]
  op = instr.op
  args = instr.args
  if !OPCODES.has_key?(op)
    return error(Failure.internal(program, "unknown opcode #{op}"))
  end
  if NEEDS.has_key?(op) and args.size < NEEDS[op]
    return error(Failure.internal(program, "#{op} needs at least #{NEEDS[op]} operands and has #{args.size}"))
  end
  if op == "const"
    return const_operands(program, tables, instr)
  elsif op == "struct-with"
    return update_operands(program, tables, args)
  elsif op == "call-builtin"
    return builtin_operands(program, tables, instr)
  elsif op == "jump" or op == "jump-if-false" or op == "jump-if-true"
    return jump_operands(program, function, labels, tables, instr)
  elsif WIDE_OPS.include?(op)
    return wide_operands(program, tables, op, args[0], args[1])
  elsif op == "step"
    return ok(plain(tables, run, 0, 0))
  elsif PAIR_OPS.include?(op)
    return ok(plain(tables, args[0], args[1], 0))
  elsif SINGLE_OPS.include?(op)
    return ok(plain(tables, args[0], 0, 0))
  elsif args.size == 3
    return ok(plain(tables, args[0], args[1], args[2]))
  end
  # Any other number of operands is written as given, as src/bytecode.rkt does; the loader rejects it.
  return ok(Operands(tables: tables, a: 0, b: 0, c: 0, generic: true))
end

def plain(tables: Tables, a: Int, b: Int, c: Int) -> Operands
  return Operands(tables: tables, a: a, b: b, c: c, generic: false)
end

# A wide operand is a 32-bit index that the VM reads from the last two, low half first.
def wide_operands(program: Ir.Program, tables: Tables, op: String, a: Int, index: Int) -> Result[Operands]
  if index < 0
    return error(Failure.internal(program, "a negative index in #{op}"))
  end
  return ok(plain(tables, a, index % 65536, index / 65536))
end

# const: the register, and the index of its constant, which is added to the table when it is new.
def const_operands(program: Ir.Program, tables: Tables, instr: Ir.Instr) -> Result[Operands]
  key = constant_key(instr.imm)
  found = Pool.find(tables.constants, key)
  if found.ok?
    return wide_operands(program, tables, instr.op, instr.args[0], found.unwrap!)
  end
  added = Pool.add(tables.constants, key, constant_bytes(instr.imm), 1)
  return wide_operands(program, tables.with(constants: added), instr.op, instr.args[0], tables.constants.count)
end

# struct-with: the two registers, and the number of its update (the struct and the positions it sets), which is added
# to the table when it is new. The VM reads that number as a u16, so the table holds at most 65,535 updates.
def update_operands(program: Ir.Program, tables: Tables, args: List[Int]) -> Result[Operands]
  positions = args.drop(3)
  fields = positions.map do |position: Int| position.to_s end.join(",")
  key = "#{args[2]}:#{fields}"
  found = Pool.find(tables.updates, key)
  if found.ok?
    return ok(plain(tables, args[0], args[1], found.unwrap!))
  end
  updates = tables.updates
  if updates.count >= MAX_U16
    return error(Failure.limit(program, 0, "struct updates", program.span))
  end
  entry = Wire.u32(args[2]).concat(Wire.u32(positions.size))
  for position in positions
    entry = entry.concat(Wire.u32(position))
  end
  return ok(plain(tables.with(updates: Pool.add(updates, key, entry, 1)), args[0], args[1], updates.count))
end

# call-builtin: the register, and the index of its builtin (the name and the argument count), which is added to the
# table when it is new.
def builtin_operands(program: Ir.Program, tables: Tables, instr: Ir.Instr) -> Result[Operands]
  args = instr.args
  key = "#{args[1]}:#{instr.name}"
  found = Pool.find(tables.builtins, key)
  if found.ok?
    return wide_operands(program, tables, instr.op, args[0], found.unwrap!)
  end
  bytes = Wire.string(instr.name).concat(Wire.u32(args[1]))
  added = Pool.add(tables.builtins, key, bytes, 1)
  return wide_operands(program, tables.with(builtins: added), instr.op, args[0], tables.builtins.count)
end

# jump, jump-if-false and jump-if-true: the register of the test, if there is one, and the number of the instruction
# the label stands before.
def jump_operands(
  program: Ir.Program, function: Ir.Function, labels: Map[Int, Int], tables: Tables, instr: Ir.Instr
) -> Result[Operands]
  args = instr.args
  register = 0
  label = args[0]
  if instr.op != "jump"
    register = args[0]
    label = args[1]
  end
  if !labels.has_key?(label)
    return error(Failure.internal(program, "the function #{function.name} jumps to a missing label"))
  end
  return wide_operands(program, tables, instr.op, register, labels[label])
end

# The instruction as bytes: the opcode, a zero, and the operands as u16.
def instr_words(program: Ir.Program, instr: Ir.Instr, found: Operands) -> Result[List[Int]]
  op = instr.op
  if found.generic
    # The operands as given, without padding.
    words = [OPCODES[op], 0]
    for arg in instr.args
      if arg < 0 or arg > MAX_U16
        return error(Failure.internal(program, "an operand of #{op} does not fit in 16 bits"))
      end
      words = words.concat(Wire.u16(arg))
    end
    return ok(words)
  end
  a = found.a
  b = found.b
  c = found.c
  if a < 0 or a > MAX_U16 or b < 0 or b > MAX_U16 or c < 0 or c > MAX_U16
    return error(Failure.internal(program, "an operand of #{op} does not fit in 16 bits"))
  end
  return ok([OPCODES[op], 0, a % 256, a / 256, b % 256, b / 256, c % 256, c / 256])
end

# The place after the run of `step` instructions that starts at `at`. A run is cut at 65,535, the most one instruction
# counts.
def step_run_end(body: List[Ir.Instr], at: Int) -> Int
  stop = at
  while stop < body.size and stop - at < MAX_U16 and body[stop].op == "step"
    stop += 1
  end
  return stop
end

# The number of the instruction each label stands before, counting a run of steps as one instruction.
def label_pcs(body: List[Ir.Instr]) -> Map[Int, Int]
  labels: Map[Int, Int] = {}
  pc = 0
  at = 0
  while at < body.size
    op = body[at].op
    if op == "label"
      labels = labels.put(body[at].args[0], pc)
      at += 1
    else
      pc += 1
      if op == "step"
        at = step_run_end(body, at)
      else
        at += 1
      end
    end
  end
  return labels
end

# The text that stands for a constant in the table: two constants are one entry when this is the same. The tag keeps
# an Int, a Float (by its bits, so 0.0 and -0.0 differ), a Bool and a String apart.
def constant_key(imm: Ir.Imm) -> String
  case imm
    Ir.Imm.Void -> return "v"
    Ir.Imm.Nil -> return "n"
    Ir.Imm.Bool(flag) -> return "b#{flag}"
    Ir.Imm.Int(number) -> return "i#{number}"
    Ir.Imm.Float(number) -> return "f#{Float.to_bits(number)}"
    Ir.Imm.Text(text) -> return "s#{text}"
  end
end

# A constant in the file: a tag (0 void, 1 nil, 2 false, 3 true, 4 Int, 5 Float, 6 String) and its value.
def constant_bytes(imm: Ir.Imm) -> List[Int]
  case imm
    Ir.Imm.Void -> return [0]
    Ir.Imm.Nil -> return [1]
    Ir.Imm.Bool(flag) -> return flag_bytes(flag)
    Ir.Imm.Int(number) -> return [4].concat(Wire.i64(number))
    Ir.Imm.Float(number) -> return [5].concat(Wire.f64(number))
    Ir.Imm.Text(text) -> return [6].concat(Wire.string(text))
  end
end

def flag_bytes(flag: Bool) -> List[Int]
  if flag
    return [3]
  end
  return [2]
end
compiler/bytecode_pool.agc:
## A table of entries the writer interns while it walks the program: the constants, the struct updates, the builtins
## and the spans. An entry is found by a text key, and the table keeps the bytes of its entries in the order they were
## added, which is the order of the section in the file.

import Wire from "bytecode_bytes"

## The entries added so far. index maps a key to the number of its first item. count is the number of items: an entry
## is one item, except a run of spans, which is one item for each span.
export struct Pool
  index: Map[String, Int]
  chunks: List[List[Int]]
  count: Int
end

## A pool and the number of an item of it.
export struct Interned
  pool: Pool
  id: Int
end

## A pool with no entry.
export def empty() -> Pool
  return Pool(index: {}, chunks: Wire.start(), count: 0)
end

## The pool with a new entry for the key: its bytes, and how many items it adds. The first item of the entry is
## numbered pool.count of the pool before.
export def add(pool: Pool, key: String, bytes: List[Int], items: Int) -> Pool
  return Pool(index: pool.index.put(key, pool.count), chunks: Wire.add(pool.chunks, bytes), count: pool.count + items)
end

## The number of the first item of the entry for the key, or an error when the pool has no such entry. Callers build
## the bytes of an entry only after this fails, so a key that is already there costs no bytes.
export def find(pool: Pool, key: String) -> Result[Int]
  return pool.index.get(key)
end

## The item of an entry with one item, added when the key is new: its number, and the pool that holds it.
export def intern(pool: Pool, key: String, bytes: List[Int]) -> Interned
  found = find(pool, key)
  if found.ok?
    return Interned(pool: pool, id: found.unwrap!)
  end
  return Interned(pool: add(pool, key, bytes, 1), id: pool.count)
end
compiler/bytecode_spans.agc:
## The span table of the .agcb: runs of spans, one run for the spans of each instruction and each function. Two runs
## with the same spans are one entry, so an instruction names its run by the number of the first span, and a run may be
## empty. A span is written as the index of its source and the line and column of its start and end.

import Pool from "bytecode_pool"
import Ir from "ir"
import Source from "source"

## The run of the spans of the written instruction that starts at body[at] and stands for `count` instructions (more
## than one for a run of `step`): the pool with it added when it is new, and its number. Nearly every instruction has
## one span, which skips the lists the general case builds.
export def intern_run(pool: Pool.Pool, body: List[Ir.Instr], at: Int, count: Int) -> Pool.Interned
  first = body[at]
  if count == 1 and first.spans.size == 1
    return intern_one(pool, first.file, first.spans[0])
  end
  keys: List[String] = []
  for offset in 0...count
    instr = body[at + offset]
    for span in instr.spans
      keys = keys.push(span_key(instr.file, span))
    end
  end
  key = keys.join(";")
  found = Pool.find(pool, key)
  if found.ok?
    return Pool.Interned(pool: pool, id: found.unwrap!)
  end
  return Pool.Interned(pool: Pool.add(pool, key, run_bytes(body, at, count), keys.size), id: pool.count)
end

## The run of one span in the source at index file.
export def intern_one(pool: Pool.Pool, file: Int, span: Source.Span) -> Pool.Interned
  key = span_key(file, span)
  found = Pool.find(pool, key)
  if found.ok?
    return Pool.Interned(pool: pool, id: found.unwrap!)
  end
  return Pool.Interned(pool: Pool.add(pool, key, span_bytes(file, span), 1), id: pool.count)
end

# The key of a run is the keys of its spans joined with ";", so a run of one span has this key.
def span_key(file: Int, span: Source.Span) -> String
  start = span.start
  stop = span.stop
  return "#{file},#{start.line},#{start.column},#{stop.line},#{stop.column}"
end

# The bytes of a run. Joining u32 lists is cheaper here than pushing each byte, which was measured slower.
def run_bytes(body: List[Ir.Instr], at: Int, count: Int) -> List[Int]
  entry: List[Int] = []
  for offset in 0...count
    instr = body[at + offset]
    for span in instr.spans
      entry = entry.concat(span_bytes(instr.file, span))
    end
  end
  return entry
end

# The five numbers of a span as u32, written out in one list: that costs about half of five calls of Wire.u32. Nearly
# every number is below 65536 and has two zero high bytes, which the first list leaves out of the arithmetic.
def span_bytes(file: Int, span: Source.Span) -> List[Int]
  start = span.start
  stop = span.stop
  first = start.line
  second = start.column
  third = stop.line
  fourth = stop.column
  if file < 65536 and first < 65536 and second < 65536 and third < 65536 and fourth < 65536
    return [
      file % 256, file / 256, 0, 0, first % 256, first / 256, 0, 0, second % 256, second / 256, 0, 0,
      third % 256, third / 256, 0, 0, fourth % 256, fourth / 256, 0, 0,
    ]
  end
  return [
    file % 256, (file / 256) % 256, (file / 65536) % 256, file / 16777216,
    first % 256, (first / 256) % 256, (first / 65536) % 256, first / 16777216,
    second % 256, (second / 256) % 256, (second / 65536) % 256, second / 16777216,
    third % 256, (third / 256) % 256, (third / 65536) % 256, third / 16777216,
    fourth % 256, (fourth / 256) % 256, (fourth / 65536) % 256, fourth / 16777216,
  ]
end
compiler/bytecode_tables.agc:
## The constants of src/bytecode.rkt: the format version, the limits of the format, the Agentica version the header
## names, and the opcode numbers with the groups of opcodes that share an operand layout. A test compares OPCODES with
## `opcodes` of src/bytecode.rkt and VERSION with src/version.rkt.

## The largest value of a u16 operand, and of every count the VM reads as a u16.
export MAX_U16 = 65535

## The format version of the .agcb header (docs/vm/03-ir-and-bytecode.md 4.6).
export FORMAT_VERSION = 5

## The deepest nesting of List and Map in a JSON field type the loader accepts.
export MAX_TYPE_DEPTH = 1024

## The Agentica version the header names (src/version.rkt); the VM accepts only its own.
export VERSION = "0.3.0"

## The number of each opcode, in the order of `opcodes` in src/bytecode.rkt and `agc_opcode` in vm/value.h.
export OPCODES = {
  "move": 0, "const": 1, "step": 2, "add-i": 3, "sub-i": 4, "mul-i": 5, "div-i": 6, "mod-i": 7, "neg-i": 8, "not": 9,
  "lt-i": 10, "le-i": 11, "eq": 12, "ne": 13, "jump": 14, "jump-if-false": 15, "jump-if-true": 16, "call": 17,
  "call-builtin": 18, "return": 19, "add-f": 20, "sub-f": 21, "mul-f": 22, "div-f": 23, "neg-f": 24, "lt-f": 25,
  "le-f": 26, "concat": 27, "to-text": 28, "inspect": 29, "list": 30, "list-len": 31, "list-get": 32, "struct": 33,
  "field": 34, "enum": 35, "is-variant": 36, "payload": 37, "same": 38, "tail-call": 39, "try": 40, "is-ok": 41,
  "result-value": 42, "map": 43, "map-get": 44, "call-value": 45, "closure": 46, "range": 47, "range-bounds": 48,
  "struct-with": 49, "global": 50, "global-set": 51,
}

## The opcodes written as their first two operands and a zero.
export PAIR_OPS = Set.new([
  "move", "neg-i", "neg-f", "not", "to-text", "inspect", "list-len", "try", "is-ok", "result-value", "range-bounds",
  "call-value",
])

## The opcodes written as their first operand and two zeros.
export SINGLE_OPS = Set.new(["return"])

## The opcodes written as their first operand and a 32-bit index split into two u16 (low half first).
export WIDE_OPS = Set.new(["call", "tail-call", "closure", "global", "global-set"])

## The fewest operands an instruction of these opcodes must have for the writer to read them; the other opcodes are
## written with the operands they have.
export NEEDS = {
  "const": 1, "jump": 1, "return": 1, "jump-if-false": 2, "jump-if-true": 2, "call-builtin": 2, "struct-with": 3,
  "move": 2, "neg-i": 2, "neg-f": 2, "not": 2, "to-text": 2, "inspect": 2, "list-len": 2, "try": 2, "is-ok": 2,
  "result-value": 2, "range-bounds": 2, "call-value": 2, "call": 2, "tail-call": 2, "closure": 2, "global": 2,
  "global-set": 2,
}
compiler/bytecode_types.agc:
## The Types and Decodable sections of the .agcb (docs/vm/03-ir-and-bytecode.md 4.6): the field types of the structs
## that JSON.decode may build, as a table of types in which a List, a Map from String and a struct name the entry of
## their item, and for each such struct the entries of its fields. src/bytecode.rkt, `type!` and `decodable`.
##
## Recursion: type_id takes 1 VM frame for each level of List and Map in a field type. The parser stops a written type
## at 1,000 levels, and the writer stops at 1,024 (BYTECODE-LIMIT), so the writer stays under 1,100 frames here.

import Wire from "bytecode_bytes"
import Failure from "bytecode_failure"
import Pool from "bytecode_pool"
import {MAX_TYPE_DEPTH, MAX_U16} from "bytecode_tables"
import Ir from "ir"
import Types from "types"

## The two sections: the type table (entries in the order they were first needed) and the bytes of the Decodable
## section after its count, with the count.
export struct Section
  types: Pool.Pool
  decodable: List[List[Int]]
  decodable_count: Int
end

## Builds the sections for the structs of the program. struct_index maps a struct name to its place in the table.
export def build(program: Ir.Program, struct_index: Map[String, Int]) -> Result[Section]
  pool = Pool.empty()
  chunks = Wire.start()
  count = 0
  index = 0
  for entry in program.structs
    if entry.decodable
      chunks = Wire.add(chunks, Wire.u32(index))
      chunks = Wire.add(chunks, Wire.string(entry.name))
      for type in entry.types
        found = try type_id(program, struct_index, pool, type)
        pool = found.pool
        chunks = Wire.add(chunks, Wire.u32(found.id))
      end
      count += 1
    end
    index += 1
  end
  if pool.count > MAX_U16
    return error(Failure.limit(program, 0, "JSON field types", program.span))
  end
  for entry in program.structs
    if entry.decodable
      for type in entry.types
        if nesting(type) > MAX_TYPE_DEPTH
          what = "nested List and Map levels in a JSON field type"
          return error(Failure.limit(program, 0, what, program.span))
        end
      end
    end
  end
  return ok(Section(types: pool, decodable: chunks, decodable_count: count))
end

# The entry of a type, added after the entries of the types it is made of. An entry is its tag (0 Int, 1 Float, 2 Bool,
# 3 String, 4 List, 5 Map from String, 6 struct) and, for the last three, the number of the item type or the struct.
def type_id(
  program: Ir.Program, struct_index: Map[String, Int], pool: Pool.Pool, type: Types.Type
) -> Result[Pool.Interned]
  case type
    Types.Type.Int -> return ok(Pool.intern(pool, "0", [0]))
    Types.Type.Float -> return ok(Pool.intern(pool, "1", [1]))
    Types.Type.Bool -> return ok(Pool.intern(pool, "2", [2]))
    Types.Type.String -> return ok(Pool.intern(pool, "3", [3]))
    Types.Type.List(item) ->
      inner = try type_id(program, struct_index, pool, item)
      return ok(entry_of(inner.pool, 4, inner.id))
    Types.Type.Map(key, value) ->
      if !Types.is(key, "String")
        return error(unsupported(program, "a Map with a key that is not a String in a JSON field type"))
      end
      inner = try type_id(program, struct_index, pool, value)
      return ok(entry_of(inner.pool, 5, inner.id))
    Types.Type.Struct(name) ->
      if !struct_index.has_key?(name)
        return error(unsupported(program, "the struct #{name} in a JSON field type is not in the table"))
      end
      return ok(entry_of(pool, 6, struct_index[name]))
    _ -> return error(unsupported(program, "a JSON field type of #{Types.tag(type)}"))
  end
end

def entry_of(pool: Pool.Pool, tag: Int, number: Int) -> Pool.Interned
  return Pool.intern(pool, "#{tag}:#{number}", [tag].concat(Wire.u32(number)))
end

def unsupported(program: Ir.Program, message: String) -> String
  return Failure.internal(program, message)
end

# The levels of List and Map around a type.
def nesting(type: Types.Type) -> Int
  case type
    Types.Type.List(item) -> return 1 + nesting(item)
    Types.Type.Map(key, item) -> return 1 + nesting(item)
    _ -> return 0
  end
end
compiler/bytecode_writer.agc:
## The bytecode writer (src/bytecode.rkt, `ir->bytecode` and `write-bytecode`): the .agcb bytes of a lowered program.
## The file is, in this order, the header, the sources, the spans, the constants, the structs, the JSON field types,
## the Decodable structs, the enums, the struct updates, the Globals count, the builtins, the functions and the entry
## (docs/vm/03-ir-and-bytecode.md 4.6). The bytes are the same as the Racket writer's, which a test compares.
##
## The functions are walked first, because they decide the entries of the constant, update, builtin and span tables,
## which come before them in the file. The output is a list of chunks that is joined once at the end.
##
## Recursion: only the JSON field types recurse (bytecode_types.agc, 1 VM frame for each level, at most 1,024 levels).

import Wire from "bytecode_bytes"
import Failure from "bytecode_failure"
import Function from "bytecode_function"
import Pool from "bytecode_pool"
import Spans from "bytecode_spans"
import {FORMAT_VERSION, MAX_U16, VERSION} from "bytecode_tables"
import JsonTypes from "bytecode_types"
import Problems from "check_failure"
import Paths from "import_path"
import Ir from "ir"
import Types from "types"

## The result of writing: the bytes of the file, or the first problem (BYTECODE-LIMIT or BYTECODE-INTERNAL).
export enum Written
  Done(List[Int])
  Failed(Problems.Problem)
end

## Writes the program. root_dir is the folder of the root file, which the stored names of the sources are relative to.
export def write(root_dir: String, program: Ir.Program) -> Written
  result = build(root_dir, program)
  if result.ok?
    return Written.Done(result.unwrap!)
  end
  return Written.Failed(Problems.unpack(result.message))
end

def build(root_dir: String, program: Ir.Program) -> Result[List[Int]]
  try check_limits(program)
  struct_index: Map[String, Int] = {}
  at = 0
  for entry in program.structs
    struct_index = struct_index.put(entry.name, at)
    at += 1
  end
  json = try JsonTypes.build(program, struct_index)
  # The span of the program is the first run of the span table.
  spans = Spans.intern_one(Pool.empty(), 0, program.span).pool
  tables = Function.Tables(constants: Pool.empty(), updates: Pool.empty(), builtins: Pool.empty(), spans: spans)
  functions = Wire.start()
  for function in program.functions
    encoded = try Function.encode(program, tables, function)
    tables = encoded.tables
    functions = Wire.add_all(functions, encoded.parts)
  end
  out = header()
  out = sources(out, root_dir, program)
  out = pool_section(out, tables.spans)
  out = pool_section(out, tables.constants)
  out = structs(out, program)
  out = pool_section(out, json.types)
  out = Wire.add(out, Wire.u32(json.decodable_count))
  out = Wire.add_all(out, json.decodable)
  out = enums(out, program)
  out = pool_section(out, tables.updates)
  out = Wire.add(out, Wire.u32(program.globals))
  out = pool_section(out, tables.builtins)
  out = Wire.add(out, Wire.u32(program.functions.size))
  out = Wire.add_all(out, functions)
  out = Wire.add(out, Wire.u32(program.entry))
  return ok(Wire.join(out))
end

# The first limits of src/bytecode.rkt, in its order. The limits of the types, the registers and the updates are met
# while those are written.
def check_limits(program: Ir.Program) -> Result[Void]
  span = program.span
  if program.structs.size > MAX_U16
    return error(Failure.limit(program, 0, "structs", span))
  end
  variants = 0
  for entry in program.enums
    variants += entry.variants.size
  end
  if variants > MAX_U16
    return error(Failure.limit(program, 0, "enum variants", span))
  end
  for entry in program.structs
    if entry.fields.size > MAX_U16
      return error(Failure.limit(program, 0, "fields in one struct", span))
    end
  end
  for entry in program.enums
    for variant in entry.variants
      if variant.size > MAX_U16
        return error(Failure.limit(program, 0, "payload items in one variant", span))
      end
    end
  end
  if program.globals > MAX_U16
    return error(Failure.limit(program, 0, "module constants", span))
  end
  return ok()
end

# The magic, the format version and the Agentica version.
def header() -> List[List[Int]]
  out = Wire.add(Wire.start(), [65, 71, 67, 66])
  out = Wire.add(out, Wire.u32(FORMAT_VERSION))
  return Wire.add(out, Wire.string(VERSION))
end

# The count of a table of entries, then its entries.
def pool_section(out: List[List[Int]], pool: Pool.Pool) -> List[List[Int]]
  return Wire.add_all(Wire.add(out, Wire.u32(pool.count)), pool.chunks)
end

# The sources: the stored name of each file and its text.
def sources(out: List[List[Int]], root_dir: String, program: Ir.Program) -> List[List[Int]]
  chunks = Wire.add(out, Wire.u32(program.sources.size))
  for source in program.sources
    chunks = Wire.add(chunks, Wire.string(Paths.stored_file(root_dir, source.file)))
    chunks = Wire.add(chunks, Wire.string(source.text))
  end
  return chunks
end

# The structs: the name as the user wrote it, and the fields.
def structs(out: List[List[Int]], program: Ir.Program) -> List[List[Int]]
  chunks = Wire.add(out, Wire.u32(program.structs.size))
  for entry in program.structs
    chunks = Wire.add(chunks, Wire.string(Types.display_name(entry.name)))
    chunks = Wire.add(chunks, Wire.u32(entry.fields.size))
    for field in entry.fields
      chunks = Wire.add(chunks, Wire.string(field))
    end
  end
  return chunks
end

# The enums: the name as the user wrote it, and the variants with their payload sizes.
def enums(out: List[List[Int]], program: Ir.Program) -> List[List[Int]]
  chunks = Wire.add(out, Wire.u32(program.enums.size))
  for entry in program.enums
    chunks = Wire.add(chunks, Wire.string(Types.display_name(entry.name)))
    chunks = Wire.add(chunks, Wire.u32(entry.variants.size))
    for variant in entry.variants
      chunks = Wire.add(chunks, Wire.string(variant.name))
      chunks = Wire.add(chunks, Wire.u32(variant.size))
    end
  end
  return chunks
end
