compiler/catalog_text.agc:
## The text form of the builtin catalog, for tests. See catalog_text. tests/frontend-catalog-common.rkt prints the same
## text from src/builtins.rkt.

import Ast from "ast"
import Model from "builtin_model"
import Builtins from "builtins"
import Suggest from "suggest"
import Text from "text"
import Types from "types"

## The whole catalog, one line per fact, then the answer to each probe. A probe is `near:WORD` (the did-you-mean help
## among the public builtin names), `ref:NAME/ARITY` (the form of NAME with that many arguments), `std:NAME` (is NAME
## inside a std-only module) `type:WORD` (the help for an unknown type: the record and enum names, and the primitive
## and handle type names), `sig:NAME` (the signature of every form of NAME) or `disp:NAME` (display_name of a linked
## name).
export def catalog_text(probes: List[String]) -> String
  catalog = Builtins.catalog()
  lines: List[String] = []
  for name in catalog.entries.keys
    lines = lines.concat(builtin_lines(catalog.entries[name]))
  end
  lines = lines.concat(record_lines(catalog)).concat(enum_lines(catalog)).concat(name_lines(catalog))
  for probe in probes
    lines = lines.push(probe_line(catalog, probe))
  end
  return lines.join("\n")
end

def builtin_lines(entry: Model.Builtin) -> List[String]
  forms = [entry].concat(entry.alternatives)
  lines: List[String] = ["builtin #{entry.name} forms=#{forms.size}"]
  for form in forms
    lines = lines.push("  #{form_line(form)}")
  end
  return lines
end

def form_line(form: Model.Builtin) -> String
  return (
    "#{Builtins.form_signature(form)} shape=#{shape_text(form)} rule=#{rule_name(form.rule)} " +
    "impl=#{Text.quote(form.implementation)} effects=#{quoted_list(form.effects)} " +
    "desc=#{Text.quote(form.description)}"
  )
end

# The parameter and result types with their variants written out, because to_text prints Struct("X"), Enum("X", []) and
# Var("X") alike.
def shape_text(form: Model.Builtin) -> String
  parameters = form.parameters.map do |parameter: Model.Named| Types.debug_text(parameter.type) end
  return "(#{parameters.join(", ")}) -> #{Types.debug_text(form.result)}"
end

def record_lines(catalog: Builtins.Catalog) -> List[String]
  lines: List[String] = []
  for name in catalog.records.keys.sort
    fields = catalog.records[name].map do |field: Model.Named| "#{field.name}: #{Types.debug_text(field.type)}" end
    lines = lines.push("record #{name} #{fields.join(", ")}")
  end
  return lines
end

def enum_lines(catalog: Builtins.Catalog) -> List[String]
  lines: List[String] = []
  for name in catalog.enums.keys.sort
    definition = catalog.enums[name]
    variants = definition.variants.map do |variant: Model.Variant| variant_text(variant) end
    lines = lines.push(
      "enum #{name} parameters=#{quoted_list(definition.parameters)} variants=#{variants.join(" | ")}",
    )
  end
  return lines
end

def name_lines(catalog: Builtins.Catalog) -> List[String]
  std_only: List[String] = []
  for name in catalog.std_only.keys.sort
    std_only = std_only.push("#{name}=#{catalog.std_only[name].std_path} as #{catalog.std_only[name].alias}")
  end
  return [
    "public #{quoted_list(catalog.public_names)}",
    "bare #{quoted_list(catalog.bare_names.to_a.sort)}",
    "opaque #{quoted_list(catalog.opaque.to_a.sort)}",
    "handles #{quoted_list(catalog.handles.to_a.sort)}",
    "reserved #{quoted_list(catalog.reserved.to_a.sort)}",
    "std-only #{std_only.join(", ")}",
  ]
end

def probe_line(catalog: Builtins.Catalog, probe: String) -> String
  colon = probe.index_of(":").unwrap!
  kind = probe.slice(0, colon)
  rest = probe.slice(colon + 1, probe.length - colon - 1)
  if kind == "near"
    near = Suggest.did_you_mean_among(rest, catalog.public_names, [])
    return "#{probe} -> #{help_text(near)}"
  elsif kind == "ref"
    return "#{probe} -> #{ref_text(catalog, rest)}"
  elsif kind == "type"
    return "#{probe} -> #{help_text(type_help(catalog, rest))}"
  elsif kind == "sig"
    return "#{probe} -> #{signature_text(catalog, rest)}"
  elsif kind == "disp"
    return "#{probe} -> #{Text.quote(Types.display_name(rest))}"
  end
  return "#{probe} -> #{Builtins.std_only_name?(catalog, rest)}"
end

def type_help(catalog: Builtins.Catalog, word: String) -> Ast.Optional[String]
  shared = [
    "Int",
    "Float",
    "Bool",
    "String",
    "Nil",
    "Void",
    "List",
    "Map",
    "Set",
    "Result",
    "Json",
    "Fn",
    "Task",
    "Channel",
    "Range",
  ].concat(catalog.opaque.to_a)
  return Suggest.did_you_mean_among(word, catalog.records.keys.concat(catalog.enums.keys), shared)
end

def signature_text(catalog: Builtins.Catalog, name: String) -> String
  found = Builtins.lookup(catalog, name)
  if found.ok?
    return Text.quote(Builtins.signature(found.unwrap!))
  end
  return "-"
end

def ref_text(catalog: Builtins.Catalog, spec: String) -> String
  parts = spec.split("/")
  found = Builtins.ref(catalog, parts[0], parts[1].to_i!)
  if found.ok?
    return form_line(found.unwrap!)
  end
  return "-"
end

def help_text(help: Ast.Optional[String]) -> String
  case help
    Ast.Optional.Present(text) -> return Text.quote(text)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return "-"
  end
end

def variant_text(variant: Model.Variant) -> String
  if variant.payload.size == 0
    return variant.name
  end
  payload = variant.payload.map do |type: Types.Type| Types.debug_text(type) end.join(", ")
  return "#{variant.name}(#{payload})"
end

def quoted_list(items: List[String]) -> String
  quoted = items.map do |item: String| Text.quote(item) end.join(", ")
  return "[#{quoted}]"
end

def rule_name(rule: Model.Rule) -> String
  case rule
    Model.Rule.Plain -> return "Plain"
    Model.Rule.ChannelNew -> return "ChannelNew"
    Model.Rule.ChannelRecv -> return "ChannelRecv"
    Model.Rule.ChannelSend -> return "ChannelSend"
    Model.Rule.ChannelTarget -> return "ChannelTarget"
    Model.Rule.Error -> return "Error"
    Model.Rule.Identity -> return "Identity"
    Model.Rule.JsonDecode -> return "JsonDecode"
    Model.Rule.JsonEncode -> return "JsonEncode"
    Model.Rule.JsonFrom -> return "JsonFrom"
    Model.Rule.JsonSchema -> return "JsonSchema"
    Model.Rule.ListAll -> return "ListAll"
    Model.Rule.ListAny -> return "ListAny"
    Model.Rule.ListAppend -> return "ListAppend"
    Model.Rule.ListAt -> return "ListAt"
    Model.Rule.ListConcat -> return "ListConcat"
    Model.Rule.ListCount -> return "ListCount"
    Model.Rule.ListEach -> return "ListEach"
    Model.Rule.ListFilter -> return "ListFilter"
    Model.Rule.ListMap -> return "ListMap"
    Model.Rule.ListReduce -> return "ListReduce"
    Model.Rule.ListRepeat -> return "ListRepeat"
    Model.Rule.ListReverse -> return "ListReverse"
    Model.Rule.ListSet -> return "ListSet"
    Model.Rule.ListSize -> return "ListSize"
    Model.Rule.ListSort -> return "ListSort"
    Model.Rule.ListSortBy -> return "ListSortBy"
    _ -> return later_rule_name(rule)
  end
end

def later_rule_name(rule: Model.Rule) -> String
  case rule
    Model.Rule.MapDelete -> return "MapDelete"
    Model.Rule.MapGet -> return "MapGet"
    Model.Rule.MapGetDefault -> return "MapGetDefault"
    Model.Rule.MapHas -> return "MapHas"
    Model.Rule.MapKeys -> return "MapKeys"
    Model.Rule.MapPut -> return "MapPut"
    Model.Rule.MapSize -> return "MapSize"
    Model.Rule.MapValues -> return "MapValues"
    Model.Rule.Ok -> return "Ok"
    Model.Rule.OkVoid -> return "OkVoid"
    Model.Rule.ResultDefault -> return "ResultDefault"
    Model.Rule.ResultMessage -> return "ResultMessage"
    Model.Rule.ResultOk -> return "ResultOk"
    Model.Rule.ResultUnwrap -> return "ResultUnwrap"
    Model.Rule.SetAdd -> return "SetAdd"
    Model.Rule.SetCombine -> return "SetCombine"
    Model.Rule.SetInclude -> return "SetInclude"
    Model.Rule.SetNew -> return "SetNew"
    Model.Rule.SetQuery -> return "SetQuery"
    Model.Rule.SetSubset -> return "SetSubset"
    Model.Rule.SetToA -> return "SetToA"
    Model.Rule.Show -> return "Show"
    Model.Rule.TaskAwait -> return "TaskAwait"
    Model.Rule.TaskAwaitTimeout -> return "TaskAwaitTimeout"
    Model.Rule.TaskSpawn -> return "TaskSpawn"
    Model.Rule.TaskSpawnOwning -> return "TaskSpawnOwning"
    Model.Rule.TestEq -> return "TestEq"
    Model.Rule.TestResult -> return "TestResult"
    _ -> return "?"
  end
end
compiler/check.agc:
import Env from "link_env"
import CheckText from "check_text"

# `agentica compiler/check.agc [flags] ROOT...` prints the text form of checking each root file (check_text.agc). The
# flags are those of link.agc: `--stdlib=DIR` (the default is stdlib), `--agentica-path=V`, `--xdg-data-home=V` and
# `--home=V`.
def main() -> Void
  stdlib = "stdlib"
  env = Env.process_env()
  for argument in System.args()
    if argument.starts_with?("--stdlib=")
      stdlib = argument.slice(9, argument.length - 9)
    elsif argument.starts_with?("--agentica-path=")
      env = env.with(agentica_path: argument.slice(16, argument.length - 16))
    elsif argument.starts_with?("--xdg-data-home=")
      env = env.with(xdg_data_home: argument.slice(16, argument.length - 16))
    elsif argument.starts_with?("--home=")
      env = env.with(home: argument.slice(7, argument.length - 7))
    else
      puts("== #{argument}")
      puts(CheckText.check_text(argument, Env.settings(stdlib, env)))
    end
  end
end
compiler/check_args.agc:
## The first argument of a builtin call that must be a collection, a channel or a Result (src/checker.rkt:
## map-argument, set-argument, list-argument, channel-argument, result-argument inside check-builtin-call). Each checks
## argument 0 against the context given and returns the new state with its type, or CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH naming the type
## it should have been.

import Ast from "ast"
import State from "check_state"
import T from "types"

## Argument 0 as a Map[K, V].
export def map_argument(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, context: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  return shaped(cx, st, site, context, "Map", T.Type.Map(T.Type.Var("K"), T.Type.Var("V")))
end

## Argument 0 as a Set[T].
export def set_argument(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, context: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  return shaped(cx, st, site, context, "Set", T.Type.Set(T.Type.Var("T")))
end

## Argument 0 as a List[T].
export def list_argument(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, context: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  return shaped(cx, st, site, context, "List", T.Type.List(T.Type.Var("T")))
end

## Argument 0 as a Channel[T].
export def channel_argument(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  return shaped(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown, "Channel", T.Type.Channel(T.Type.Var("T")))
end

## Argument 0 as a Result[T].
export def result_argument(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, context: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  return shaped(cx, st, site, context, "Result", T.Type.Result(T.Type.Var("T")))
end

## True for a list literal with no elements.
export def empty_list?(node: Ast.Expr) -> Bool
  case node
    Ast.Expr.ListLit(list) -> return list.elements.size == 0
    _ -> return false
  end
end

## True for a map literal with no entries.
export def empty_map?(node: Ast.Expr) -> Bool
  case node
    Ast.Expr.MapLit(map) -> return map.entries.size == 0
    _ -> return false
  end
end

# Argument 0, which must have the variant named by word; shape is the type the message says it should have.
def shaped(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  site: State.Site,
  context: T.Type,
  word: String,
  shape: T.Type,
) -> Result[State.Out]
  out = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[0], context)
  if !T.is(out.type, word)
    return error(State.mismatch(cx, out.st, shape, out.type, Ast.expr_span(site.args[0])))
  end
  return ok(out)
end
compiler/check_call.agc:
## Calls and constructions (src/checker.rkt: check-call, check-plain-call, check-pipe-method!, check-enum-constructor,
## check-construct, check-struct-construct, check-named-fields!, check-struct-update): a call of a builtin or of a
## function of the program, an enum variant, a struct construction and a struct update.

import Ast from "ast"
import Model from "builtin_model"
import Builtins from "builtins"
import Help from "check_help"
import Names from "check_names"
import Rules from "check_rules"
import State from "check_state"
import Types from "check_types"
import Source from "source"
import T from "types"

# What checking the arguments of a variant learned: the state and the type arguments found.
struct Inferred
  st: State.St
  substitutions: Map[String, T.Type]
end

# The names given in a construction or an update, and the state after checking their values.
struct Fields
  st: State.St
  seen: Set[String]
end

## Checks a call written by name: a builtin (and, for a piped call, that its method form is not the better one) or a
## function of the program.
export def check_call(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Call, expected: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  entry = cx.catalog.entries.get(node.name)
  if !entry.ok?
    return check_plain_call(cx, st, node)
  end
  out = try Rules.check_builtin_call(cx, st, node, expected, entry.unwrap!)
  if node.piped
    try check_pipe_method(cx, out.st, node, entry.unwrap!)
  end
  return ok(out)
end

## Checks Enum.Variant(args): the arguments against the payload types, with the enum's type arguments taken from the
## expected type or from the arguments. named is the arguments written with names, which a variant does not take.
export def check_enum_constructor(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  enum_name: String,
  variant_name: String,
  args: List[Ast.Expr],
  named: Int,
  span: Source.Span,
  expected: T.Type,
) -> Result[State.Out]
  definition = cx.enums.get(enum_name)
  if !definition.ok?
    return error(
      State.fail_maybe(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-UNKNOWN-TYPE",
        "unknown enum \"#{enum_name}\"",
        span,
        unknown_enum_help(enum_name),
      ),
    )
  end
  found = definition.unwrap!
  payload = variant_payload(found, variant_name)
  if !payload.ok?
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-UNKNOWN-VARIANT",
        "enum \"#{T.display_name(enum_name)}\" has no variant \"#{variant_name}\"",
        span,
      ),
    )
  end
  count = args.size + named
  if count != payload.unwrap!.size
    variant = "#{T.display_name(enum_name)}.#{variant_name}"
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-ARITY",
        "variant #{variant} expects #{payload.unwrap!.size} argument(s), found #{count}",
        span,
      ),
    )
  end
  if named > 0
    return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-ENUM-POSITIONAL-ARGS", "enum variants use positional arguments", span))
  end
  substitutions = expected_substitutions(found, expected)
  inferred = try infer_arguments(cx, st, payload.unwrap!, args, substitutions)
  return finish_constructor(cx, inferred.st, found, variant_name, inferred.substitutions, span, expected)
end

## Checks Type(name: value, ...): a struct, or Enum.Variant(name: value) written as a construction, which a variant
## does not take.
export def check_construct(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Construct, expected: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  parts = node.type_name.split(".")
  if parts.size == 2 and cx.enums.has_key?(parts[0])
    return check_enum_constructor(cx, st, parts[0], parts[1], [], node.args.size, node.span, expected)
  end
  return check_struct_construct(cx, st, node)
end

## Checks target.with(name: value, ...): the target is a struct, every name is one of its fields, given once, with a
## value of the field's type. A struct that its module keeps private cannot be updated from another module
## (CHECK-IMPORT-NAME).
export def check_struct_update(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.StructUpdate) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try State.expr(cx, st, node.target, T.Type.Unknown)
  if !T.is(target.type, "Struct")
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        target.st,
        "CHECK-UNKNOWN-METHOD",
        "#{T.to_text(target.type)} has no method \"with\"",
        node.span,
        "with copies a struct with some fields changed; the value before .with must be a struct",
      ),
    )
  end
  name = T.name(target.type)
  if !updatable?(cx, node.visible, name)
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        target.st,
        "CHECK-IMPORT-NAME",
        "\"#{T.display_name(name)}\" is private to its module, so a value of it cannot be updated here",
        node.span,
        "export the struct from its module, or add a function there that makes the change",
      ),
    )
  end
  fields = try check_named_fields(cx, target.st, name, cx.structs[name], node.args)
  return ok(State.Out(st: fields.st, type: target.type))
end

## The field of that name in the list, or an error.
export def find_field(fields: List[Model.Named], name: String) -> Result[Model.Named]
  for field in fields
    if field.name == name
      return ok(field)
    end
  end
  return error("no such field")
end

# The text of the source between the start of an expression, including a piped receiver, and its end.
def extent_text(cx: State.Cx, node: Ast.Expr) -> String
  text = cx.texts.get(cx.file)
  if !text.ok?
    return ""
  end
  start = extent_start(node)
  stop = Ast.expr_span(node).stop.offset
  return text.unwrap!.slice(start, stop - start)
end

# The offset where an expression starts: a piped call starts where its receiver does, and so does a try of one.
def extent_start(node: Ast.Expr) -> Int
  case node
    Ast.Expr.Call(call) -> return call_start(call)
    Ast.Expr.Try(attempt) -> return try_start(attempt)
    _ -> return Ast.expr_span(node).start.offset
  end
end

def call_start(call: Ast.Call) -> Int
  if call.piped
    return extent_start(call.args[0])
  end
  return call.span.start.offset
end

def try_start(attempt: Ast.TryExpr) -> Int
  inner = extent_start(attempt.operand)
  if inner < attempt.span.start.offset
    return inner
  end
  return attempt.span.start.offset
end

def piped?(node: Ast.Expr) -> Bool
  case node
    Ast.Expr.Call(call) -> return call.piped
    Ast.Expr.Try(attempt) -> return piped?(attempt.operand)
    _ -> return false
  end
end

# CHECK-PIPE-METHOD: a builtin that has a method form (x |> String.upcase) is written as the method, x.upcase.
def check_pipe_method(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Call, entry: Model.Builtin) -> Result[Bool]
  selected = Builtins.form_for(entry, node.args.size)
  if !selected.ok? or selected.unwrap!.parameters.size == 0
    return ok(true)
  end
  kind = Names.receiver_kind(selected.unwrap!.parameters[0].type)
  if kind == ""
    return ok(true)
  end
  method = Names.pipe_method_name(cx, kind, entry.name)
  if method == ""
    return ok(true)
  end
  return error(
    State.fail_help(
      cx,
      st,
      "CHECK-PIPE-METHOD",
      "\"#{entry.name}\" has a method form for #{kind}, so it is not piped",
      node.span,
      pipe_help(cx, node, method),
    ),
  )
end

# The method form of a piped call: receiver.method(arguments) do ... end.
def pipe_help(cx: State.Cx, node: Ast.Call, method: String) -> String
  left = node.args[0]
  receiver = "(#{extent_text(cx, left)})"
  if simple_receiver?(left) and !piped?(left)
    receiver = extent_text(cx, left)
  end
  plain: List[String] = []
  block = false
  index = 1
  while index < node.args.size
    case node.args[index]
      Ast.Expr.BlockLit(found) -> block = true
      _ -> plain = plain.push(extent_text(cx, node.args[index]))
    end
    index += 1
  end
  text = "#{receiver}.#{method}"
  if plain.size > 0
    text = "#{text}(#{plain.join(", ")})"
  end
  if block
    text = "#{text} do ... end"
  end
  return text
end

def simple_receiver?(node: Ast.Expr) -> Bool
  case node
    Ast.Expr.Name(found) -> return true
    Ast.Expr.Literal(found) -> return true
    Ast.Expr.Call(found) -> return true
    Ast.Expr.MethodCall(found) -> return true
    Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(found) -> return true
    Ast.Expr.Index(found) -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

# A function of the program: the arguments against the parameter types.
def check_plain_call(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Call) -> Result[State.Out]
  entry = cx.functions.get(node.name)
  if !entry.ok?
    return error(
      State.fail_maybe(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-UNKNOWN-NAME",
        "unknown function \"#{T.display_name(node.name)}\"",
        node.span,
        unknown_function_help(cx, node.name),
      ),
    )
  end
  signature = entry.unwrap!
  if node.args.size != signature.params.size
    return error(arity_failure(cx, st, node, signature))
  end
  current = st
  index = 0
  while index < node.args.size
    out = try State.expr(cx, current, node.args[index], signature.params[index])
    current = out.st
    index += 1
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: current, type: signature.result))
end

def arity_failure(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Call, signature: State.Signature) -> String
  name = T.display_name(node.name)
  message = "\"#{name}\" expects #{signature.params.size} argument(s), found #{node.args.size}"
  callee = "#{name}(#{T.list_text(signature.params)}) -> #{T.to_text(signature.result)}"
  return State.fail_callee(cx, st, "CHECK-ARITY", message, node.span, callee)
end

# The help of an unknown function: a name of another language, a module that needs an import, or a close name.
def unknown_function_help(cx: State.Cx, name: String) -> String
  help = Help.foreign(cx.help, name)
  if help != ""
    return help
  elsif name.starts_with?("Agent.")
    return (
      "return values from tasks and combine them with reduce, " +
      "or keep the state in one task that receives on a Channel"
    )
  elsif name.starts_with?("BDD.")
    return "import BDD from \"std/bdd\""
  elsif name.starts_with?("HTTP.")
    return "import HTTP from \"std/http\""
  end
  return Help.near(name, cx.functions.keys, cx.catalog.public_names)
end

def unknown_enum_help(name: String) -> String
  if name == "Result"
    return "Result has only Ok and Err: Result.Ok(value) or ok(value), Result.Err(\"message\") or error(\"message\")"
  end
  return ""
end

# The payload types of a variant of the enum, or an error when it has no such variant.
def variant_payload(definition: Model.EnumDef, name: String) -> Result[List[T.Type]]
  for variant in definition.variants
    if variant.name == name
      return ok(variant.payload)
    end
  end
  return error("no such variant")
end

# The type arguments the context already gives: an expected Enum of the same enum with the same number of arguments.
def expected_substitutions(definition: Model.EnumDef, expected: T.Type) -> Map[String, T.Type]
  found: Map[String, T.Type] = {}
  args = T.args(expected)
  if T.is(expected, "Enum") and T.name(expected) == definition.name and args.size == definition.parameters.size
    index = 0
    while index < args.size
      found = found.put(definition.parameters[index], args[index])
      index += 1
    end
  end
  return found
end

# Each argument against its payload type with the type variables filled in as far as they are known; an empty
# collection cannot say what a variable is.
def infer_arguments(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  payload: List[T.Type],
  args: List[Ast.Expr],
  substitutions: Map[String, T.Type],
) -> Result[Inferred]
  current = st
  found = substitutions
  index = 0
  while index < payload.size
    template = payload[index]
    context = Types.substitute(template, found)
    if Types.has_variables?(context) and empty_collection?(args[index])
      return error(
        State.fail(
          cx,
          current,
          "CHECK-ENUM-TYPE-INFERENCE",
          "cannot infer enum type arguments from an empty collection payload",
          Ast.expr_span(args[index]),
        ),
      )
    end
    wanted = context
    if Types.has_variables?(context)
      wanted = T.Type.Unknown
    end
    out = try State.expr(cx, current, args[index], wanted)
    current = out.st
    found = try Types.unify(cx, current, template, out.type, found, Ast.expr_span(args[index]))
    index += 1
  end
  return ok(Inferred(st: current, substitutions: found))
end

def empty_collection?(node: Ast.Expr) -> Bool
  case node
    Ast.Expr.ListLit(list) -> return list.elements.size == 0
    Ast.Expr.MapLit(map) -> return map.entries.size == 0
    _ -> return false
  end
end

# The enum type with its arguments, once every type parameter has been found.
def finish_constructor(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  definition: Model.EnumDef,
  variant_name: String,
  substitutions: Map[String, T.Type],
  span: Source.Span,
  expected: T.Type,
) -> Result[State.Out]
  unresolved = definition.parameters.filter do |parameter: String| !substitutions.has_key?(parameter) end
  if unresolved.size > 0
    variant = "#{T.display_name(definition.name)}.#{variant_name}"
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-ENUM-TYPE-INFERENCE",
        "cannot infer enum type parameter(s) #{unresolved.join(", ")} for #{variant}",
        span,
      ),
    )
  end
  args = definition.parameters.map do |parameter: String| substitutions[parameter] end
  type = try State.ensure(cx, st, T.Type.Enum(definition.name, args), expected, span)
  return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: type))
end

def check_struct_construct(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Construct) -> Result[State.Out]
  name = node.type_name
  fields = cx.structs.get(name)
  if !fields.ok?
    return error(
      State.fail_maybe(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-UNKNOWN-TYPE",
        "\"#{T.display_name(name)}\" is not a declared struct",
        node.span,
        Help.near(name, cx.structs.keys, []),
      ),
    )
  end
  checked = try check_named_fields(cx, st, name, fields.unwrap!, node.args)
  for field in fields.unwrap!
    if !checked.seen.include?(field.name)
      return error(
        State.fail_help(
          cx,
          checked.st,
          "CHECK-MISSING-FIELD",
          "constructor \"#{T.display_name(name)}\" is missing field \"#{field.name}\"",
          node.span,
          "add \"#{field.name}: ...\" with a value of type #{T.to_text(field.type)}",
        ),
      )
    end
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: checked.st, type: T.Type.Struct(name)))
end

# The `name: value` pairs of a construction or an update: each name is a field of the struct, given once, with a value
# of the field's type. The values are checked in source order, which is also the order they run in.
def check_named_fields(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  name: String,
  fields: List[Model.Named],
  args: List[Ast.NamedArg],
) -> Result[Fields]
  current = st
  seen: Set[String] = Set.new([])
  for arg in args
    field = find_field(fields, arg.name)
    if !field.ok?
      return error(
        State.fail_help(
          cx,
          current,
          "CHECK-UNKNOWN-FIELD",
          "\"#{T.display_name(name)}\" has no field \"#{arg.name}\"",
          arg.span,
          Help.field_help(arg.name, fields),
        ),
      )
    end
    if seen.include?(arg.name)
      return error(
        State.fail(cx, current, "CHECK-DUPLICATE-FIELD", "field \"#{arg.name}\" is given twice", arg.span),
      )
    end
    seen = seen.add(arg.name)
    out = try State.expr(cx, current, arg.value, field.unwrap!.type)
    current = out.st
  end
  return ok(Fields(st: current, seen: seen))
end

# A builtin record can always be updated; a struct of the program only when the file may build it. Absent: the program
# is not linked, every struct is visible.
def updatable?(cx: State.Cx, visible: Ast.Optional[List[String]], name: String) -> Bool
  case visible
    Ast.Optional.Present(names) ->
      return cx.catalog.records.has_key?(name) or names.any? do |item: String| item == name end
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return true
  end
end
compiler/check_collections.agc:
## The checking rules of the Map, Set, Task and Channel builtins (src/checker.rkt, check-builtin-call: task-spawn ...
## set-subset). A rule takes the call (State.Site) and returns the new state with the type of the call.

import Ast from "ast"
import Model from "builtin_model"
import Args from "check_args"
import State from "check_state"
import CheckTypes from "check_types"
import T from "types"

## Checks a call of a Task, Channel, Map or Set builtin by its rule. Any other rule is the caller's.
export def check_collection_rule(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, rule: Model.Rule) -> Result[State.Out]
  case rule
    Model.Rule.TaskSpawn -> return check_spawn(cx, st, site, false)
    Model.Rule.TaskSpawnOwning -> return check_spawn(cx, st, site, true)
    Model.Rule.TaskAwait -> return check_await(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.TaskAwaitTimeout -> return check_await_timeout(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.ChannelNew -> return check_channel_new(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.ChannelSend -> return check_channel_send(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.ChannelRecv -> return check_channel_recv(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.ChannelTarget -> return check_channel_target(cx, st, site)
    _ -> return check_map_rule(cx, st, site, rule)
  end
end

# Task.spawn and Task.spawn_owning: a function of one parameter and the argument it gets. The owning form also hands
# over a handle or channel.
def check_spawn(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, owning: Bool) -> Result[State.Out]
  callback = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[0], T.Type.Unknown)
  if !T.is(callback.type, "Fn") or T.params(callback.type).size != 1
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        callback.st,
        "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH",
        "#{site.selected.name} requires a function with one parameter",
        Ast.expr_span(site.args[0]),
      ),
    )
  end
  handed = try State.expr(cx, callback.st, site.args[1], T.params(callback.type)[0])
  if owning and !handle?(cx, handed.type) and !T.is(handed.type, "Channel")
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        handed.st,
        "CHECK-NOT-A-HANDLE",
        "Task.spawn_owning gives a handle to the new task, but the argument is #{T.to_text(handed.type)}",
        Ast.expr_span(site.args[1]),
        "pass a FileHandle, Socket, Listener, Process, HttpServer or Channel; Task.spawn passes any other value",
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: handed.st, type: T.Type.Task(T.result(callback.type))))
end

def handle?(cx: State.Cx, type: T.Type) -> Bool
  return T.is(type, "Opaque") and cx.catalog.handles.include?(T.name(type))
end

def check_await(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[0], T.task_of(site.expected))
  if !T.is(target.type, "Task")
    return error(
      State.fail(cx, target.st, "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH", "Task.await requires a task", Ast.expr_span(site.args[0])),
    )
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: target.st, type: T.item(target.type)))
end

# Task.await with a timeout gives Await[R]: Await.Done(value) or Await.TimedOut.
def check_await_timeout(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  context = T.Type.Unknown
  if T.is(site.expected, "Enum") and T.name(site.expected) == "Await"
    context = T.Type.Task(T.args(site.expected)[0])
  end
  target = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[0], context)
  if !T.is(target.type, "Task")
    return error(
      State.fail(cx, target.st, "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH", "Task.await requires a task", Ast.expr_span(site.args[0])),
    )
  end
  timeout = try State.expr(cx, target.st, site.args[1], T.Type.Int)
  return ok(State.Out(st: timeout.st, type: T.Type.Enum("Await", [T.item(target.type)])))
end

# Channel.new needs the channel type from its context.
def check_channel_new(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  capacity = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[0], T.Type.Int)
  span = site.node.span
  if T.unknown?(site.expected)
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        capacity.st,
        "CHECK-EXPECTED-TYPE",
        "a channel needs an expected type",
        span,
        "annotate the variable, for example ch: Channel[Int] = Channel.new(8)",
      ),
    )
  end
  if !T.is(site.expected, "Channel")
    return error(State.mismatch(cx, capacity.st, site.expected, T.Type.Channel(T.Type.Var("T")), span))
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: capacity.st, type: site.expected))
end

def check_channel_send(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try Args.channel_argument(cx, st, site)
  value = try State.expr(cx, target.st, site.args[1], T.item(target.type))
  timeout = try State.expr(cx, value.st, site.args[2], T.Type.Int)
  return ok(State.Out(st: timeout.st, type: T.Type.Result(T.Type.Void)))
end

def check_channel_recv(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try Args.channel_argument(cx, st, site)
  timeout = try State.expr(cx, target.st, site.args[1], T.Type.Int)
  return ok(State.Out(st: timeout.st, type: T.Type.Result(T.item(target.type))))
end

def check_channel_target(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try Args.channel_argument(cx, st, site)
  return ok(State.Out(st: target.st, type: site.selected.result))
end

def check_map_rule(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, rule: Model.Rule) -> Result[State.Out]
  case rule
    Model.Rule.MapHas -> return check_map_has(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.MapKeys ->
      target = try Args.map_argument(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown)
      return ok(State.Out(st: target.st, type: T.Type.List(T.key(target.type))))
    Model.Rule.MapValues ->
      target = try Args.map_argument(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown)
      return ok(State.Out(st: target.st, type: T.Type.List(T.value(target.type))))
    Model.Rule.MapGet -> return check_map_get(cx, st, site, false)
    Model.Rule.MapGetDefault -> return check_map_get(cx, st, site, true)
    Model.Rule.MapDelete -> return check_map_delete(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.MapSize ->
      target = try Args.map_argument(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown)
      return ok(State.Out(st: target.st, type: T.Type.Int))
    Model.Rule.MapPut -> return check_map_put(cx, st, site)
    _ -> return check_set_rule(cx, st, site, rule)
  end
end

def check_map_has(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try Args.map_argument(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown)
  key = try State.expr(cx, target.st, site.args[1], T.key(target.type))
  return ok(State.Out(st: key.st, type: T.Type.Bool))
end

# Map.get gives a Result; with a default it gives the value. The value type of the map may come from the expected type,
# or from the default when the map is the literal {}.
def check_map_get(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, with_default: Bool) -> Result[State.Out]
  value_context = T.only_result_item(site.expected)
  if with_default
    value_context = site.expected
  end
  current = st
  if T.unknown?(value_context) and with_default and Args.empty_map?(site.args[0])
    default = try State.expr(cx, current, site.args[2], T.Type.Unknown)
    current = default.st
    value_context = default.type
  end
  context = T.Type.Unknown
  if !T.unknown?(value_context)
    key = try State.expr(cx, current, site.args[1], T.Type.Unknown)
    current = key.st
    context = T.Type.Map(key.type, value_context)
  end
  target = try Args.map_argument(cx, current, site, context)
  key = try State.expr(cx, target.st, site.args[1], T.key(target.type))
  current = key.st
  if with_default
    default = try State.expr(cx, current, site.args[2], T.value(target.type))
    return ok(State.Out(st: default.st, type: T.value(target.type)))
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: current, type: T.Type.Result(T.value(target.type))))
end

def check_map_delete(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try Args.map_argument(cx, st, site, T.only_map(site.expected))
  key = try State.expr(cx, target.st, site.args[1], T.key(target.type))
  return ok(State.Out(st: key.st, type: target.type))
end

def check_map_put(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try Args.map_argument(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown)
  key = try State.expr(cx, target.st, site.args[1], T.key(target.type))
  value = try State.expr(cx, key.st, site.args[2], T.value(target.type))
  return ok(State.Out(st: value.st, type: target.type))
end

def check_set_rule(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, rule: Model.Rule) -> Result[State.Out]
  case rule
    Model.Rule.SetNew -> return check_set_new(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.SetAdd -> return check_set_add(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.SetInclude ->
      target = try Args.set_argument(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown)
      element = try State.expr(cx, target.st, site.args[1], T.item(target.type))
      return ok(State.Out(st: element.st, type: T.Type.Bool))
    Model.Rule.SetQuery ->
      target = try Args.set_argument(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown)
      return ok(State.Out(st: target.st, type: site.selected.result))
    Model.Rule.SetToA ->
      target = try Args.set_argument(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown)
      return ok(State.Out(st: target.st, type: T.Type.List(T.item(target.type))))
    Model.Rule.SetCombine -> return check_set_combine(cx, st, site, false)
    Model.Rule.SetSubset -> return check_set_combine(cx, st, site, true)
    _ -> return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-INTERNAL", "unsupported builtin rule", site.node.span))
  end
end

# Set.new: a list of Int or String; an empty list needs the set type from its context.
def check_set_new(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  items = site.args[0]
  context = T.Type.Unknown
  if T.is(site.expected, "Set")
    context = T.Type.List(T.item(site.expected))
  end
  span = site.node.span
  if Args.empty_list?(items) and T.unknown?(context)
    if !T.unknown?(site.expected)
      return error(State.mismatch(cx, st, site.expected, T.Type.Set(T.Type.Var("T")), span))
    end
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-EMPTY-SET-TYPE",
        "an empty set needs an expected type, for example \"Set[Int]\"",
        span,
        (
          "annotate the variable: seen: Set[Int] = Set.new([]); " +
          "a parameter, a field or a function result also gives the type"
        ),
      ),
    )
  end
  list = try Args.list_argument(cx, st, site, context)
  element = T.item(list.type)
  if !CheckTypes.key_type?(element)
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        list.st,
        "CHECK-SET-ELEMENT-TYPE",
        "a Set element must be Int or String, found #{T.to_text(element)}",
        Ast.expr_span(items),
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: list.st, type: T.Type.Set(element)))
end

# Set.add and Set.delete: the element has the element type.
def check_set_add(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try Args.set_argument(cx, st, site, T.only_set(site.expected))
  element = try State.expr(cx, target.st, site.args[1], T.item(target.type))
  return ok(State.Out(st: element.st, type: target.type))
end

# Set.union, intersection, difference (a set) and subset? (a Bool): the second set has the type of the first.
def check_set_combine(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, subset: Bool) -> Result[State.Out]
  context = T.Type.Unknown
  if !subset
    context = T.only_set(site.expected)
  end
  target = try Args.set_argument(cx, st, site, context)
  other = try State.expr(cx, target.st, site.args[1], target.type)
  if subset
    return ok(State.Out(st: other.st, type: T.Type.Bool))
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: other.st, type: target.type))
end
compiler/check_const.agc:
## Module constants in the checker (src/checker.rkt: check-constants!, validate-constant!;
## docs/future/44-module-constants.md 44.5 to 44.7). The constants are put in initialization order, a cycle is
## CHECK-CONSTANT-CYCLE, then each initializer is checked in that order with no locals in scope and its type recorded
## for the reads, and the value rules are applied to the checked tree: no call of a function of the program, no
## function value, no while, no builtin with effects (CHECK-CONSTANT-EXPRESSION), and only data types
## (CHECK-CONSTANT-TYPE).

import Ast from "ast"
import Model from "builtin_model"
import CheckTypes from "check_types"
import ConstWalk from "const_walk"
import State from "check_state"
import Linker from "linker"
import Source from "source"
import T from "types"

## What checking the constants leaves: the context with the type of every constant, the state with the types of the
## initializers, and the linked names of the constants in initialization order.
export struct Done
  cx: State.Cx
  st: State.St
  order: List[String]
end

# A constant with the file it is declared in.
struct Entry
  decl: Ast.ConstDecl
  file: String
end

# A constant being visited by the ordering: the index of its entry, its reads, and the next read to look at.
struct Visit
  index: Int
  reads: List[Ast.ConstRef]
  next: Int
end

## Orders and checks the constants of the program (the declarations of the linked modules, in order). A program without
## constants gives its context and state back.
export def check_all(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, modules: List[Linker.LinkedModule]) -> Result[Done]
  entries = collect(modules)
  if entries.size == 0
    return ok(Done(cx: cx, st: st, order: []))
  end
  order = try order_of(cx, st, entries)
  current = Done(cx: cx, st: st, order: [])
  for index in order
    current = try check_one(current, entries[index])
  end
  return ok(current)
end

def collect(modules: List[Linker.LinkedModule]) -> List[Entry]
  found: List[Entry] = []
  for module in modules
    for decl in module.declarations
      case decl
        Ast.Decl.Constant(node) -> found = found.push(Entry(decl: node, file: module.file))
        _ -> found = found
      end
    end
  end
  return found
end

def check_one(done: Done, entry: Entry) -> Result[Done]
  here = done.cx.with(file: entry.file)
  declared = T.Type.Unknown
  case entry.decl.type
    Ast.Optional.Present(annotation) -> declared = try CheckTypes.resolve_type(here, done.st, annotation, false)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> declared = declared
  end
  out = try State.expr(here, done.st, entry.decl.value, declared)
  try validate(here, out.st, entry.decl.value)
  type = out.type
  if !T.unknown?(declared)
    type = declared
  end
  return ok(
    Done(
      cx: done.cx.with(constants: done.cx.constants.put(entry.decl.name, type)),
      st: out.st,
      order: done.order.push(entry.decl.name),
    ),
  )
end

# The entries in initialization order, as indexes. To visit a constant, first visit the constants its initializer
# reads, in the order of the reads, then emit it; the first read that reaches a constant already on the path is a
# cycle. The path is an explicit stack: a chain of constants is not bounded by the checker's nesting limit.
def order_of(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, entries: List[Entry]) -> Result[List[Int]]
  index_of: Map[String, Int] = {}
  at = 0
  while at < entries.size
    index_of = index_of.put(entries[at].decl.name, at)
    at += 1
  end
  state: Map[String, Int] = {}
  emitted: List[Int] = []
  start = 0
  while start < entries.size
    if !state.has_key?(entries[start].decl.name)
      stack: List[Visit] = [begin_visit(entries, start)]
      state = state.put(entries[start].decl.name, 1)
      while stack.size > 0
        top = stack[stack.size - 1]
        if top.next >= top.reads.size
          stack = stack.take(stack.size - 1)
          state = state.put(entries[top.index].decl.name, 2)
          emitted = emitted.push(top.index)
        else
          read = top.reads[top.next]
          stack = stack.set(stack.size - 1, top.with(next: top.next + 1))
          seen = state.get(read.name, 0)
          if seen == 1
            return error(cycle_failure(cx, st, entries, stack, read))
          elsif seen == 0
            state = state.put(read.name, 1)
            stack = stack.push(begin_visit(entries, index_of[read.name]))
          end
        end
      end
    end
    start += 1
  end
  return ok(emitted)
end

def begin_visit(entries: List[Entry], index: Int) -> Visit
  return Visit(index: index, reads: ConstWalk.references(entries[index].decl.value), next: 0)
end

# CHECK-CONSTANT-CYCLE at the read that closes the cycle, in the file of the constant that reads it. The help lists the
# constants around the cycle, from the one that is read again: A -> B -> A.
def cycle_failure(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, entries: List[Entry], stack: List[Visit], read: Ast.ConstRef) -> String
  names: List[String] = []
  for visit in stack
    names = names.push(entries[visit.index].decl.name)
  end
  first = 0
  while names[first] != read.name
    first += 1
  end
  around = names.drop(first).push(read.name).map do |name: String| T.display_name(name) end
  here = cx.with(file: entries[stack[stack.size - 1].index].file)
  return State.fail_help(
    here,
    st,
    "CHECK-CONSTANT-CYCLE",
    "constants depend on each other in a cycle",
    read.span,
    "the cycle is #{around.join(" -> ")}",
  )
end

# The value rules on a checked initializer. A node is visited after its children, in source order; a while is refused
# before its body. A block is allowed only as an argument of a builtin.
def validate(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, root: Ast.Expr) -> Result[Bool]
  return visit(cx, st, ConstWalk.Node.Expr(root), false)
end

def visit(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: ConstWalk.Node, block_allowed: Bool) -> Result[Bool]
  try refuse_early(cx, st, node, block_allowed)
  entry = builtin_of(cx, st, node)
  inside = has_entry?(entry)
  for child in ConstWalk.children(node)
    try visit(cx, st, child, inside)
  end
  try refuse_form(cx, st, node, entry)
  return check_data(cx, st, node, block_allowed)
end

def has_entry?(entry: Ast.Optional[Model.Builtin]) -> Bool
  case entry
    Ast.Optional.Present(found) -> return true
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return false
  end
end

def refuse(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, span: Source.Span, what: String, help: String) -> String
  return State.fail_help(cx, st, "CHECK-CONSTANT-EXPRESSION", what, span, help)
end

def refuse_early(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: ConstWalk.Node, block_allowed: Bool) -> Result[Bool]
  case node
    ConstWalk.Node.Stmt(stmt) ->
      case stmt
        Ast.Stmt.While(found) -> return error(
          refuse(
            cx,
            st,
            found.span,
            "a constant cannot use a while loop",
            "loop with for over a range or a collection, or use a builtin such as reduce",
          ),
        )
        _ -> return ok(true)
      end
    ConstWalk.Node.Expr(expr) ->
      case expr
        Ast.Expr.BlockLit(found) ->
          if !block_allowed
            return error(
              refuse(
                cx,
                st,
                found.span,
                "a block in a constant must be an argument of a builtin",
                "pass the block to a builtin such as map or reduce",
              ),
            )
          end
          return ok(true)
        _ -> return ok(true)
      end
  end
end

# The builtin a call, method call or field access names: not a call of a function of the program.
def builtin_of(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: ConstWalk.Node) -> Ast.Optional[Model.Builtin]
  case node
    ConstWalk.Node.Stmt(stmt) -> return Ast.Optional.Absent
    ConstWalk.Node.Expr(expr) ->
      case expr
        Ast.Expr.Call(found) ->
          if cx.functions.has_key?(found.name)
            return Ast.Optional.Absent
          end
          return entry_named(cx, found.name)
        Ast.Expr.MethodCall(found) -> return entry_resolved(cx, st, found.id)
        Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(found) -> return entry_resolved(cx, st, found.id)
        _ -> return Ast.Optional.Absent
      end
  end
end

def entry_named(cx: State.Cx, name: String) -> Ast.Optional[Model.Builtin]
  found = cx.catalog.entries.get(name)
  if found.ok?
    return Ast.Optional.Present(found.unwrap!)
  end
  return Ast.Optional.Absent
end

def entry_resolved(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, id: Int) -> Ast.Optional[Model.Builtin]
  resolved = st.resolved.get(id)
  if !resolved.ok?
    return Ast.Optional.Absent
  end
  case resolved.unwrap!
    State.Resolved.Call(name, type) -> return entry_named(cx, name)
    _ -> return Ast.Optional.Absent
  end
end

def refuse_form(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: ConstWalk.Node, entry: Ast.Optional[Model.Builtin]) -> Result[Bool]
  case node
    ConstWalk.Node.Stmt(stmt) -> return ok(true)
    ConstWalk.Node.Expr(expr) -> return refuse_expr(cx, st, expr, entry)
  end
end

def refuse_expr(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, expr: Ast.Expr, entry: Ast.Optional[Model.Builtin]) -> Result[Bool]
  span = Ast.expr_span(expr)
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.FunctionRef(found) -> return error(
      refuse(
        cx,
        st,
        span,
        "a constant cannot hold a function value",
        "a constant is built from literals, constructors and builtins",
      ),
    )
    Ast.Expr.Invoke(found) -> return error(
      refuse(
        cx,
        st,
        span,
        "a constant cannot call a function value",
        "a constant is built from literals, constructors and builtins",
      ),
    )
    Ast.Expr.Call(found) ->
      if cx.functions.has_key?(found.name)
        return error(
          refuse(
            cx,
            st,
            span,
            "a constant cannot call #{T.display_name(found.name)}, a function declared in the program",
            "build the value from literals, constructors and builtins, or compute it in a function",
          ),
        )
      end
      return refuse_effects(cx, st, span, entry)
    _ -> return refuse_effects(cx, st, span, entry)
  end
end

def refuse_effects(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, span: Source.Span, entry: Ast.Optional[Model.Builtin]) -> Result[Bool]
  case entry
    Ast.Optional.Present(found) ->
      if found.effects.size > 0
        return error(
          refuse(
            cx,
            st,
            span,
            "a constant cannot call #{T.display_name(found.name)}, which has effects (#{found.effects.join(", ")})",
            "a constant is built from literals, constructors and builtins without effects",
          ),
        )
      end
      return ok(true)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return ok(true)
  end
end

# CHECK-CONSTANT-TYPE for an expression whose type is not a data type. A block passed to a builtin is not a value of
# the constant.
def check_data(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: ConstWalk.Node, block_allowed: Bool) -> Result[Bool]
  case node
    ConstWalk.Node.Stmt(stmt) -> return ok(true)
    ConstWalk.Node.Expr(expr) ->
      type = st.types[Ast.expr_id(expr)]
      if T.unknown?(type) or (block_allowed and block?(expr)) or CheckTypes.data?(cx, type, [])
        return ok(true)
      end
      return error(
        State.fail_help(
          cx,
          st,
          "CHECK-CONSTANT-TYPE",
          "a constant expression must have a data type, found #{T.to_text(type)}",
          Ast.expr_span(expr),
          data_help(type),
        ),
      )
  end
end

def data_help(type: T.Type) -> String
  if T.is(type, "Void")
    return "a constant's value must be data: write nil, not a Void call"
  end
  return (
    "a constant holds numbers, text, collections, structs and enums of those; " +
    "functions, tasks, channels and handles are not data"
  )
end

def block?(expr: Ast.Expr) -> Bool
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.BlockLit(found) -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end
compiler/check_expr.agc:
## Expressions (src/checker.rkt: check-expression and the checks it calls). check_expression is the function that
## Cx.expression holds: every part of the checker reaches an expression through it. It counts the nesting
## (CHECK-TOO-DEEP), checks the node by its kind, records the type by node id, and refuses a Void value that is not a
## completion.

import Ast from "ast"
import Calls from "check_call"
import Failure from "check_failure"
import Help from "check_help"
import Methods from "check_method"
import Rules from "check_rules"
import State from "check_state"
import Statements from "check_stmt"
import CheckTypes from "check_types"
import T from "types"

# What the two sides of a binary operator are, checked in order. The right side of a range is checked with the methods
# and fields of its chain marked, so that the help can say a method call on a range needs parentheses.
struct Sides
  st: State.St
  left: T.Type
  right: T.Type
end

## Checks an expression against the type the context expects (Unknown when none). completion says a Void value is
## allowed here: a statement, the last expression of a block, a return.
export def check_expression(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  node: Ast.Expr,
  expected: T.Type,
  completion: Bool,
) -> Result[State.Out]
  if st.nest >= State.nesting_limit()
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-TOO-DEEP",
        "nesting is deeper than #{State.nesting_limit()} levels",
        Ast.expr_span(node),
        "split the code into smaller functions or simpler expressions",
      ),
    )
  end
  checked = try expression_inside(cx, st.with(nest: st.nest + 1), node, expected)
  span = Ast.expr_span(node)
  if T.is(checked.type, "Void") and !completion
    return error(
      State.fail(cx, checked.st, "CHECK-VOID-VALUE", "a Void call has no value; use it as a statement", span),
    )
  end
  actual = try State.ensure(cx, checked.st, checked.type, expected, span)
  recorded = State.record_type(checked.st, Ast.expr_id(node), checked.type)
  return ok(State.Out(st: recorded.with(nest: st.nest), type: actual))
end

# An Int literal past the largest Int is CHECK-INT-RANGE, except this one under a minus.
def int_min_digits() -> String
  return "9223372036854775808"
end

# The type of the node by its kind, before the Void and expected-type checks.
def expression_inside(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Expr, expected: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  case node
    Ast.Expr.Literal(found) -> return check_literal(cx, st, found)
    Ast.Expr.Name(found) -> return check_name(cx, st, found)
    Ast.Expr.Unary(found) -> return check_unary(cx, st, found)
    Ast.Expr.Binary(found) -> return check_binary(cx, st, found)
    Ast.Expr.Call(found) -> return Calls.check_call(cx, st, found, expected)
    Ast.Expr.EnumConstructor(found) -> return Calls.check_enum_constructor(
      cx,
      st,
      found.enum_name,
      found.variant_name,
      found.args,
      found.named.size,
      found.span,
      expected,
    )
    Ast.Expr.FunctionRef(found) -> return check_function_ref(cx, st, found)
    Ast.Expr.Invoke(found) -> return check_invoke(cx, st, found)
    Ast.Expr.Try(found) -> return check_try(cx, st, found, expected)
    Ast.Expr.Construct(found) -> return Calls.check_construct(cx, st, found, expected)
    Ast.Expr.Update(found) -> return Calls.check_struct_update(cx, st, found)
    Ast.Expr.ListLit(found) -> return check_list(cx, st, found, expected)
    Ast.Expr.MapLit(found) -> return check_map(cx, st, found, expected)
    Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(found) -> return Methods.check_field_access(cx, st, found, expected)
    Ast.Expr.MethodCall(found) -> return Methods.check_method(cx, st, found, expected)
    Ast.Expr.Typed(found) -> return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: found.type))
    Ast.Expr.BlockLit(found) -> return check_block_lit(cx, st, found, expected)
    Ast.Expr.Interpolation(found) -> return check_interpolation(cx, st, found)
    Ast.Expr.Index(found) -> return check_index(cx, st, found)
    Ast.Expr.TypeName(found) -> return check_type_name(cx, st, found)
    Ast.Expr.ConstRef(found) -> return check_const_ref(cx, st, found)
  end
end

def check_literal(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Literal) -> Result[State.Out]
  case node.value
    Ast.LitValue.Whole(number) -> return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Int))
    Ast.LitValue.Huge(digits) -> return error(
      State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-INT-RANGE", "Int literal is outside the signed 64-bit range", node.span),
    )
    Ast.LitValue.Real(number) -> return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Float))
    Ast.LitValue.Text(text) -> return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.String))
    Ast.LitValue.Flag(flag) -> return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Bool))
    Ast.LitValue.Nothing -> return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Nil))
  end
end

# A name in scope. A function name is not a value, and the help of an unknown name is a close name or a name of another
# language.
def check_name(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.NameRef) -> Result[State.Out]
  binding = State.lookup(st, node.name)
  if binding.ok?
    return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: binding.unwrap!.type))
  end
  if cx.functions.has_key?(node.name) or cx.catalog.entries.has_key?(node.name)
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-UNKNOWN-NAME",
        "\"#{node.name}\" is a function; functions are not values",
        node.span,
      ),
    )
  end
  help = name_help(cx, st, node.name)
  return error(State.fail_maybe(cx, st, "CHECK-UNKNOWN-NAME", "unknown name \"#{node.name}\"", node.span, help))
end

# The help of an unknown name: a close name in scope, or the name another language uses.
def name_help(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, name: String) -> String
  guess = Help.near(name, State.visible_names(cx, st), [])
  if guess != ""
    return guess
  end
  return Help.foreign(cx.help, name)
end

# A constant is read after its initializer was checked, because the constants are checked in dependency order.
def check_const_ref(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.ConstRef) -> Result[State.Out]
  type = cx.constants.get(node.name)
  if !type.ok?
    return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-INTERNAL", "constant read before it was checked", node.span))
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: type.unwrap!))
end

def check_type_name(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.TypeName) -> Result[State.Out]
  return error(
    State.fail_maybe(
      cx,
      st,
      "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH",
      "a type name is only valid as a JSON type argument",
      node.span,
      Help.foreign(cx.help, node.name),
    ),
  )
end

def check_function_ref(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.FunctionRef) -> Result[State.Out]
  signature = cx.functions.get(node.name)
  if !signature.ok?
    return error(
      State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-UNKNOWN-NAME", "a function reference requires a declared function", node.span),
    )
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Fn(signature.unwrap!.params, signature.unwrap!.result)))
end

# target.call(args): the target is a function value and the arguments match its parameters.
def check_invoke(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Invoke) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try State.expr(cx, st, node.target, T.Type.Unknown)
  if !T.is(target.type, "Fn")
    return error(State.fail(cx, target.st, "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH", ".call requires a function value", node.span))
  end
  params = T.params(target.type)
  if params.size != node.args.size
    return error(State.fail(cx, target.st, "CHECK-ARITY", "wrong number of function arguments", node.span))
  end
  current = target.st
  index = 0
  while index < params.size
    out = try State.expr(cx, current, node.args[index], params[index])
    current = out.st
    index += 1
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: current, type: T.result(target.type)))
end

# try needs a function (not an inferring block) that returns a Result, and an operand that is a Result.
def check_try(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.TryExpr, expected: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  if !result_context?(st)
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-TRY-CONTEXT",
        "try requires a function returning Result",
        node.span,
        "return Result[T] from this function, or handle the Result explicitly",
      ),
    )
  end
  wanted = T.Type.Unknown
  if !T.unknown?(expected)
    wanted = T.Type.Result(expected)
  end
  out = try State.expr(cx, st, node.operand, wanted)
  if !T.is(out.type, "Result")
    return error(State.mismatch(cx, out.st, T.Type.Result(T.Type.Var("T")), out.type, Ast.expr_span(node.operand)))
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: out.st, type: T.item(out.type)))
end

def result_context?(st: State.St) -> Bool
  case st.result
    State.Slot.Known(type) -> return T.is(type, "Result")
    State.Slot.Infer -> return false
  end
end

def check_interpolation(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Interpolation) -> Result[State.Out]
  current = st
  for part in node.parts
    case part
      Ast.Part.Code(code) ->
        out = try State.expr(cx, current, code, T.Type.Unknown)
        try Rules.ensure_printable(cx, out.st, out.type, Ast.expr_span(code))
        current = out.st
      Ast.Part.Text(text) -> current = current
    end
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: current, type: T.Type.String))
end

# A block where a function is expected, or anywhere a type is not demanded.
def check_block_lit(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.BlockLit, expected: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  if T.unknown?(expected)
    return Statements.check_block_body(cx, st, node, Ast.Optional.Absent, T.Type.Unknown, Ast.Optional.Absent)
  elsif !T.is(expected, "Fn")
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-BLOCK-TARGET",
        "a block is passed where #{T.to_text(expected)} is expected",
        node.span,
        "a block is only allowed when the last parameter is a function (Fn[...])",
      ),
    )
  end
  return Statements.check_block_body(
    cx,
    st,
    node,
    Ast.Optional.Present(T.params(expected)),
    T.result(expected),
    Ast.Optional.Absent,
  )
end

def check_list(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.ListLit, expected: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  if !T.unknown?(expected) and !T.is(expected, "List")
    return error(
      State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH", "expected #{T.to_text(expected)}, found a list", node.span),
    )
  end
  wanted = T.Type.Unknown
  if T.is(expected, "List")
    wanted = T.item(expected)
  end
  if node.elements.size == 0
    if T.unknown?(wanted)
      return error(
        State.fail_help(
          cx,
          st,
          "CHECK-EMPTY-LIST-TYPE",
          "an empty list needs an expected type, for example \"List[Int]\"",
          node.span,
          "annotate the variable: xs: List[Int] = []; a parameter, a field or a function result also gives the type",
        ),
      )
    end
    return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: expected))
  end
  first = try State.expr(cx, st, node.elements[0], wanted)
  element = wanted
  if T.unknown?(wanted)
    element = first.type
  end
  current = first.st
  index = 1
  while index < node.elements.size
    out = try State.expr(cx, current, node.elements[index], element)
    current = out.st
    index += 1
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: current, type: T.Type.List(element)))
end

def check_map(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.MapLit, expected: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  if !T.unknown?(expected) and !T.is(expected, "Map")
    return error(
      State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH", "expected #{T.to_text(expected)}, found a map", node.span),
    )
  end
  if node.entries.size == 0
    if T.unknown?(expected)
      return error(
        State.fail_help(
          cx,
          st,
          "CHECK-EMPTY-MAP-TYPE",
          "an empty map needs an expected type, for example \"Map[String, Int]\"",
          node.span,
          (
            "annotate the variable: m: Map[String, Int] = {}; " +
            "a parameter, a field or a function result also gives the type"
          ),
        ),
      )
    end
    return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: expected))
  end
  wanted_key = T.Type.Unknown
  wanted_value = T.Type.Unknown
  if T.is(expected, "Map")
    wanted_key = T.key(expected)
    wanted_value = T.value(expected)
  end
  first = node.entries[0]
  key = try State.expr(cx, st, first.key, wanted_key)
  if !CheckTypes.key_type?(key.type)
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        key.st,
        "CHECK-MAP-KEY-TYPE",
        "a Map key must be Int or String, found #{T.to_text(key.type)}",
        Ast.expr_span(first.key),
      ),
    )
  end
  value = try State.expr(cx, key.st, first.value, wanted_value)
  current = value.st
  index = 1
  while index < node.entries.size
    entry = node.entries[index]
    k = try State.expr(cx, current, entry.key, key.type)
    v = try State.expr(cx, k.st, entry.value, value.type)
    current = v.st
    index += 1
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: current, type: T.Type.Map(key.type, value.type)))
end

def check_index(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.IndexAccess) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try State.expr(cx, st, node.target, T.Type.Unknown)
  if T.is(target.type, "Map")
    index = try State.expr(cx, target.st, node.index, T.key(target.type))
    return ok(State.Out(st: index.st, type: T.value(target.type)))
  elsif T.is(target.type, "List")
    index = try State.expr(cx, target.st, node.index, T.Type.Int)
    return ok(State.Out(st: index.st, type: T.item(target.type)))
  end
  return error(
    State.fail_maybe(
      cx,
      target.st,
      "CHECK-NOT-INDEXABLE",
      "indexing needs a list or a map, found #{T.to_text(target.type)}",
      node.span,
      index_help(target.type),
    ),
  )
end

def index_help(target: T.Type) -> String
  if T.is(target, "String")
    return (
      "strings cannot be indexed: s.at(i) reads one character, s.slice(start, length) a part, " +
      "s.split(\"\") gives all characters"
    )
  elsif T.is(target, "Result")
    return "unwrap the Result first: r.unwrap!, try r inside a function that returns Result, or case r"
  elsif T.is(target, "Struct")
    return "read a field with .name"
  elsif T.is(target, "Set")
    return "sets have no positions: s.include?(x) tests membership, s.to_a gives a list in insertion order"
  end
  return ""
end

# - and not. -9223372036854775808 is the one literal that only fits under a minus.
def check_unary(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Unary) -> Result[State.Out]
  operand = try unary_operand(cx, st, node)
  if node.op == "minus"
    if !CheckTypes.numeric?(operand.type)
      return error(
        State.fail(
          cx,
          operand.st,
          "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH",
          "unary \"-\" expects a number, found #{T.to_text(operand.type)}",
          node.op_span,
        ),
      )
    end
    return ok(operand)
  end
  if !T.is(operand.type, "Bool")
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        operand.st,
        "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH",
        "\"not\" (or \"!\") expects Bool, found #{T.to_text(operand.type)}",
        node.op_span,
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: operand.st, type: T.Type.Bool))
end

def unary_operand(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Unary) -> Result[State.Out]
  if node.op == "minus" and min_literal?(node.operand)
    return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Int))
  end
  out = try State.expr_completion(cx, st, node.operand, T.Type.Unknown)
  if T.is(out.type, "Void")
    return error(
      State.fail_maybe(
        cx,
        out.st,
        "CHECK-VOID-VALUE",
        "a Void call has no value; use it as a statement",
        Ast.expr_span(node.operand),
        void_negation_help(node),
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(out)
end

def min_literal?(node: Ast.Expr) -> Bool
  case node
    Ast.Expr.Literal(found) ->
      case found.value
        Ast.LitValue.Huge(digits) -> return digits == int_min_digits()
        _ -> return false
      end
    _ -> return false
  end
end

# -5.abs is -(5.abs): the help says to write (-5).abs.
def void_negation_help(node: Ast.Unary) -> String
  if node.op != "minus"
    return ""
  end
  case node.operand
    Ast.Expr.MethodCall(call) ->
      case call.target
        Ast.Expr.Literal(literal) ->
          case literal.value
            Ast.LitValue.Whole(n) -> return "-#{n}.#{call.name} is -(#{n}.#{call.name}); write (-#{n}).#{call.name}"
            _ -> return ""
          end
        _ -> return ""
      end
    _ -> return ""
  end
end

def check_sides(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Binary) -> Result[Sides]
  left = try State.expr(cx, st, node.left, T.Type.Unknown)
  if node.op == "dot-dot" or node.op == "dot-dot-dot"
    chained = left.st.with(range_chain: chain_ids(node.right))
    right = try State.expr(cx, chained, node.right, T.Type.Unknown)
    return ok(Sides(st: right.st.with(range_chain: left.st.range_chain), left: left.type, right: right.type))
  end
  right = try State.expr(cx, left.st, node.right, T.Type.Unknown)
  return ok(Sides(st: right.st, left: left.type, right: right.type))
end

# The ids of the method calls and field accesses along the target chain of an expression.
def chain_ids(node: Ast.Expr) -> List[Int]
  ids: List[Int] = []
  current = node
  going = true
  while going
    case current
      Ast.Expr.MethodCall(call) ->
        ids = ids.push(call.id)
        current = call.target
      Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(access) ->
        ids = ids.push(access.id)
        current = access.target
      _ -> going = false
    end
  end
  return ids
end

def check_binary(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Binary) -> Result[State.Out]
  sides = try check_sides(cx, st, node)
  type = try binary_type(cx, sides, node)
  return ok(State.Out(st: sides.st, type: type))
end

# The result type of the operator, or the first rule it breaks.
def binary_type(cx: State.Cx, sides: Sides, node: Ast.Binary) -> Result[T.Type]
  left = sides.left
  right = sides.right
  case node.op
    "plus" ->
      try same_types(cx, sides, node, true)
      return plus_type(cx, sides, node)
    "minus" -> return arithmetic_type(cx, sides, node)
    "multiply" -> return arithmetic_type(cx, sides, node)
    "divide" -> return arithmetic_type(cx, sides, node)
    "modulo" -> return modulo_type(cx, sides, node)
    "less" -> return comparison_type(cx, sides, node)
    "less-equal" -> return comparison_type(cx, sides, node)
    "greater" -> return comparison_type(cx, sides, node)
    "greater-equal" -> return comparison_type(cx, sides, node)
    "dot-dot" -> return range_type(cx, sides, node)
    "dot-dot-dot" -> return range_type(cx, sides, node)
    "equal" -> return equality_type(cx, sides, node)
    "not-equal" -> return equality_type(cx, sides, node)
    "and" -> return logical_type(cx, sides, node)
    "or" -> return logical_type(cx, sides, node)
    _ -> return error(State.fail(cx, sides.st, "CHECK-INTERNAL", "unsupported operator", node.op_span))
  end
end

def type_error(cx: State.Cx, sides: Sides, node: Ast.Binary, message: String, help: String) -> String
  return State.fail_maybe(cx, sides.st, "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH", message, node.op_span, help)
end

# Both sides have one type. with_to_s adds to the String help that to_s makes a String of the number.
def same_types(cx: State.Cx, sides: Sides, node: Ast.Binary, with_to_s: Bool) -> Result[Bool]
  if T.same(sides.left, sides.right)
    return ok(true)
  end
  left = T.to_text(sides.left)
  right = T.to_text(sides.right)
  base = Failure.problem(
    cx.file,
    sides.st.signature,
    "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH",
    "operator expects two values of the same type, found #{left} and #{right}",
    node.op_span,
    State.hint_of(same_help(sides, with_to_s)),
  )
  labels = [
    Failure.Label(span: Ast.expr_span(node.left), text: "this is #{left}"),
    Failure.Label(span: Ast.expr_span(node.right), text: "this is #{right}"),
  ]
  return error(Failure.pack(base.with(expected: left, actual: right, labels: labels)))
end

def same_help(sides: Sides, with_to_s: Bool) -> String
  either_int = T.is(sides.left, "Int") or T.is(sides.right, "Int")
  either_float = T.is(sides.left, "Float") or T.is(sides.right, "Float")
  either_string = T.is(sides.left, "String") or T.is(sides.right, "String")
  if either_int and either_float
    return (
      "make both sides the same type: n.to_f (Float.from_int) turns the Int into a Float, " +
      "x.to_i! (Float.to_int!) truncates the Float"
    )
  elsif either_string and (either_int or either_float)
    if with_to_s
      return (
        "make both sides Strings with n.to_s or interpolation \"\#{n}\"; " +
        "or make both numbers with s.to_i! or s.to_f!, which halt on text that is not a number"
      )
    end
    return (
      "make both sides numbers: s.to_i! or s.to_f! turns the String into a number, " +
      "and halts on text that is not a number"
    )
  end
  return ""
end

def plus_type(cx: State.Cx, sides: Sides, node: Ast.Binary) -> Result[T.Type]
  if CheckTypes.numeric?(sides.left) and CheckTypes.numeric?(sides.right)
    return ok(sides.left)
  elsif T.is(sides.left, "String") and T.is(sides.right, "String")
    return ok(T.Type.String)
  end
  return error(
    type_error(cx, sides, node, "\"+\" expects two numbers or two strings, found #{T.to_text(sides.left)}", ""),
  )
end

def arithmetic_type(cx: State.Cx, sides: Sides, node: Ast.Binary) -> Result[T.Type]
  try same_types(cx, sides, node, false)
  if !CheckTypes.numeric?(sides.left) or !CheckTypes.numeric?(sides.right)
    return error(type_error(cx, sides, node, "arithmetic expects two numbers, found #{T.to_text(sides.left)}", ""))
  end
  return ok(sides.left)
end

def modulo_type(cx: State.Cx, sides: Sides, node: Ast.Binary) -> Result[T.Type]
  if !T.is(sides.left, "Int") or !T.is(sides.right, "Int")
    return error(
      type_error(
        cx,
        sides,
        node,
        "\"%\" expects two Ints, found #{T.to_text(sides.left)} and #{T.to_text(sides.right)}",
        "",
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(T.Type.Int)
end

def comparison_type(cx: State.Cx, sides: Sides, node: Ast.Binary) -> Result[T.Type]
  try same_types(cx, sides, node, false)
  if !CheckTypes.numeric?(sides.left) or !CheckTypes.numeric?(sides.right)
    help = ""
    if T.is(sides.left, "String")
      help = "< <= > >= only take Int or Float; compare Strings with == and !=, or order a List[String] with xs.sort"
    end
    return error(type_error(cx, sides, node, "comparison expects two numbers, found #{T.to_text(sides.left)}", help))
  end
  return ok(T.Type.Bool)
end

def range_type(cx: State.Cx, sides: Sides, node: Ast.Binary) -> Result[T.Type]
  if !T.is(sides.left, "Int") or !T.is(sides.right, "Int")
    return error(
      type_error(
        cx,
        sides,
        node,
        "a range expects two Ints, found #{T.to_text(sides.left)} and #{T.to_text(sides.right)}",
        "",
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(T.Type.Range)
end

def equality_type(cx: State.Cx, sides: Sides, node: Ast.Binary) -> Result[T.Type]
  try same_types(cx, sides, node, true)
  if !CheckTypes.primitive?(sides.left) and !T.is(sides.left, "Range")
    help = ""
    if T.is(sides.left, "Set")
      help = "two sets are equal when each is a subset of the other: a.subset?(b) and b.subset?(a)"
    end
    return error(
      type_error(
        cx,
        sides,
        node,
        "equality is only defined for primitive values and ranges, found #{T.to_text(sides.left)}",
        help,
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(T.Type.Bool)
end

def logical_type(cx: State.Cx, sides: Sides, node: Ast.Binary) -> Result[T.Type]
  if !T.is(sides.left, "Bool") or !T.is(sides.right, "Bool")
    return error(
      type_error(
        cx,
        sides,
        node,
        "logical operator expects two Bools, found #{T.to_text(sides.left)} and #{T.to_text(sides.right)}",
        "",
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(T.Type.Bool)
end
compiler/check_failure.agc:
## How the checker reports a failure: a diagnostic with the extra notes of src/diagnostic.rkt (expected, actual,
## callee, signature, labels) and the file it is in. A Result error is a String, so the failure travels packed (pack)
## and `try` stops at the first one, as in the parser; unpack reads it back.

import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Source from "source"

## A note on a second span, such as "this is Int".
export struct Label
  span: Source.Span
  text: String
end

## The first problem the checker found. The notes are "" when the diagnostic has none (src/ uses #f). signature is the
## signature of the function being checked; callee the signature of the function or builtin called.
export struct Problem
  file: String
  code: String
  message: String
  span: Source.Span
  help: Diag.Help
  expected: String
  actual: String
  callee: String
  signature: String
  labels: List[Label]
end

## A problem with no notes.
export def problem(
  file: String,
  signature: String,
  code: String,
  message: String,
  span: Source.Span,
  help: Diag.Help,
) -> Problem
  return Problem(
    file: file,
    code: code,
    message: message,
    span: span,
    help: help,
    expected: "",
    actual: "",
    callee: "",
    signature: signature,
    labels: [],
  )
end

## The problem written as one String.
export def pack(found: Problem) -> String
  fields = [
    found.file,
    found.code,
    found.message,
    span_text(found.span),
    help_flag(found.help),
    help_text(found.help),
    found.expected,
    found.actual,
    found.callee,
    found.signature,
    found.labels.size.to_s,
  ]
  for label in found.labels
    fields = fields.concat([span_text(label.span), label.text])
  end
  parts = fields.map do |field: String| "#{field.length}\n#{field}" end
  return parts.join("")
end

## Reads back the problem that pack wrote.
export def unpack(text: String) -> Problem
  fields: List[String] = []
  at = 0
  while at < text.length
    newline = at + text.slice(at, text.length - at).index_of("\n").unwrap!
    size = text.slice(at, newline - at).to_i!
    fields = fields.push(text.slice(newline + 1, size))
    at = newline + 1 + size
  end
  labels: List[Label] = []
  index = 11
  while index < fields.size
    labels = labels.push(Label(span: read_span(fields[index]), text: fields[index + 1]))
    index += 2
  end
  help = Diag.Help.NoHelp
  if fields[4] == "1"
    help = Diag.Help.Hint(fields[5])
  end
  return Problem(
    file: fields[0],
    code: fields[1],
    message: fields[2],
    span: read_span(fields[3]),
    help: help,
    expected: fields[6],
    actual: fields[7],
    callee: fields[8],
    signature: fields[9],
    labels: labels,
  )
end

def span_text(span: Source.Span) -> String
  numbers = [span.start.offset, span.start.line, span.start.column, span.stop.offset, span.stop.line, span.stop.column]
  return numbers.map do |number: Int| number.to_s end.join(",")
end

def read_span(text: String) -> Source.Span
  numbers = text.split(",").map do |part: String| part.to_i! end
  start = Source.Position(offset: numbers[0], line: numbers[1], column: numbers[2])
  stop = Source.Position(offset: numbers[3], line: numbers[4], column: numbers[5])
  return Source.Span(start: start, stop: stop)
end

def help_flag(help: Diag.Help) -> String
  case help
    Diag.Help.Hint(text) -> return "1"
    Diag.Help.NoHelp -> return "0"
  end
end

def help_text(help: Diag.Help) -> String
  case help
    Diag.Help.Hint(text) -> return text
    Diag.Help.NoHelp -> return ""
  end
end

## What the statements of a body return (src/checker.rkt: block-returns?, missing-return-help,
## captured-assignment-help): whether every path ends in a return, and the help texts that depend only on the shape of
## the code.

import Ast from "ast"
import State from "check_state"

## True when every path of the statements ends in a return.
export def block_returns?(statements: List[Ast.Stmt]) -> Bool
  return statements.any? do |statement: Ast.Stmt| returns?(statement) end
end
