## The help of CHECK-MISSING-RETURN: what is missing at the end of the body, or "".
export def missing_return_help(body: List[Ast.Stmt], type_name: String) -> String
  if !contains_return?(body)
    return "add \"return <value>\" of type #{type_name} at the end"
  elsif body.size == 0
    return ""
  end
  last = body[body.size - 1]
  case last
    Ast.Stmt.If(node) -> return if_help(node, type_name)
    Ast.Stmt.While(node) -> return loop_help(type_name)
    Ast.Stmt.For(node) -> return loop_help(type_name)
    Ast.Stmt.Case(node) -> return (
      "every arm of the last \"case\" must end with return, or return #{type_name} after it"
    )
    _ -> return ""
  end
end

## The help of CHECK-MISSING-RETURN for a loop at the end of the body.
export def loop_help(type_name: String) -> String
  return "a loop does not count as a return; add \"return <value>\" of type #{type_name} after it"
end

## The help of CHECK-CAPTURED-ASSIGNMENT: a for loop can assign.
export def captured_help(name: String, capture: State.Capture) -> String
  element = "x"
  if capture.params.size == 1
    element = capture.params[0].name
  end
  path = ""
  case capture.each_receiver
    Ast.Optional.Present(receiver) -> path = path_text(receiver)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> path = path
  end
  if path != "" and path.length <= 40
    return "blocks capture values; use a for loop, which can assign \"#{name}\": for #{element} in #{path} ... end"
  end
  return (
    "blocks capture values; use a for loop, which can assign \"#{name}\": for #{element} in xs ... end, " +
    "or build it with xs.reduce(#{name}) do |acc, #{element}| ... end"
  )
end

def returns?(statement: Ast.Stmt) -> Bool
  case statement
    Ast.Stmt.Return(node) -> return true
    Ast.Stmt.If(node) -> return if_returns?(node)
    Ast.Stmt.Case(node) -> return node.arms.all? do |arm: Ast.CaseArm| block_returns?(arm.body) end
    _ -> return false
  end
end

# An if returns on every path when it has an else and every branch returns.
def if_returns?(node: Ast.IfStmt) -> Bool
  case node.else_body
    Ast.Optional.Present(body) ->
      return block_returns?(body) and node.branches.all? do |branch: Ast.IfBranch| block_returns?(branch.body) end
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return false
  end
end

def contains_return?(statements: List[Ast.Stmt]) -> Bool
  return statements.any? do |statement: Ast.Stmt| holds_return?(statement) end
end

def holds_return?(statement: Ast.Stmt) -> Bool
  case statement
    Ast.Stmt.Return(node) -> return true
    Ast.Stmt.If(node) -> return if_holds_return?(node)
    Ast.Stmt.While(node) -> return contains_return?(node.body)
    Ast.Stmt.For(node) -> return contains_return?(node.body)
    Ast.Stmt.Case(node) -> return node.arms.any? do |arm: Ast.CaseArm| contains_return?(arm.body) end
    _ -> return false
  end
end

def if_holds_return?(node: Ast.IfStmt) -> Bool
  if node.branches.any? do |branch: Ast.IfBranch| contains_return?(branch.body) end
    return true
  end
  case node.else_body
    Ast.Optional.Present(body) -> return contains_return?(body)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return false
  end
end

def if_help(node: Ast.IfStmt, type_name: String) -> String
  case node.else_body
    Ast.Optional.Present(body) -> return (
      "every branch of the last \"if\" must end with return, or return #{type_name} after it"
    )
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return (
      "the last \"if\" has no \"else\"; add an \"else\" that returns #{type_name}, or return after it"
    )
  end
end

# A name or a chain of field accesses as text (a.b.c), or "" for any other expression.
def path_text(expr: Ast.Expr) -> String
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.Name(node) -> return node.name
    Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(node) -> return field_path(node)
    Ast.Expr.Typed(node) -> return path_text(node.target)
    _ -> return ""
  end
end

def field_path(node: Ast.FieldAccess) -> String
  target = path_text(node.target)
  if target == ""
    return ""
  end
  return "#{target}.#{node.name}"
end
compiler/check_help.agc:
## The help texts of the checker (src/checker.rkt): the tables of check_tables.agc loaded into Maps once, and the helps
## that depend only on types or names. A help is a String, and "" means there is none.

import Ast from "ast"
import Model from "builtin_model"
import Data from "check_tables"
import Suggest from "suggest"
import Types from "types"

## The tables of check_tables.agc, built once per run. A key is the receiver kind and the name, `String.size`.
export struct Tables
  modules: Map[String, String]
  aliases: Map[String, String]
  foreign_names: Map[String, String]
  foreign_methods: Map[String, List[String]]
  kind_methods: Map[String, String]
end

## The tables of this run.
export def tables() -> Tables
  return Tables(
    modules: Data.method_modules(),
    aliases: Data.method_aliases(),
    foreign_names: Data.foreign_names(),
    foreign_methods: Data.foreign_methods(),
    kind_methods: Data.foreign_kind_methods(),
  )
end

## The help of a type mismatch: how to convert the actual type into the expected one (conversion-help).
export def conversion(expected: Types.Type, actual: Types.Type) -> String
  if Types.is(actual, "Result") and Types.same(Types.item(actual), expected)
    return (
      "this is #{Types.to_text(actual)}; unwrap it with a ! form (#{unwrap_form(expected)}), " +
      "with Result.unwrap!(...), or with try inside a function that returns Result"
    )
  end
  return convert_help(expected, actual)
end

## The help for a name another language has but Agentica does not, or "".
export def foreign(tables: Tables, name: String) -> String
  found = tables.foreign_names.get(name)
  if found.ok?
    return found.unwrap!
  end
  return ""
end

## The "did you mean" help for the closest of the candidates and the shared names, or "".
export def near(name: String, candidates: List[String], shared: List[String]) -> String
  case Suggest.did_you_mean_among(name, candidates, shared)
    Ast.Optional.Present(text) -> return text
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return ""
  end
end

## The field names alone, as "fields: a, b".
export def field_list(fields: List[Model.Named]) -> String
  names = fields.map do |field: Model.Named| field.name end
  return "fields: #{names.join(", ")}"
end

## The help of a missing or unknown field: a guess if one is close, then the field names.
export def field_help(name: String, fields: List[Model.Named]) -> String
  names = fields.map do |field: Model.Named| field.name end
  all = field_list(fields)
  guess = near(name, names, [])
  if guess == ""
    return all
  end
  return "#{guess} #{all}"
end

# What a failed unwrap suggests, by the type that was expected.
def unwrap_form(expected: Types.Type) -> String
  if Types.is(expected, "Int")
    return "s.to_i!"
  elsif Types.is(expected, "Float")
    return "s.to_f!"
  elsif Types.is(expected, "String")
    return "gets!"
  end
  return "such as s.to_i!"
end

def convert_help(expected: Types.Type, actual: Types.Type) -> String
  if Types.is(expected, "String") and Types.is(actual, "Int")
    return "convert it with String.from_int(...)"
  elsif Types.is(expected, "String") and Types.is(actual, "Float")
    return "convert it with String.from_float(...)"
  elsif Types.is(expected, "Int") and Types.is(actual, "String")
    return "convert it with String.to_int!(...)"
  elsif Types.is(expected, "Float") and Types.is(actual, "String")
    return "convert it with String.to_float!(...)"
  elsif Types.is(expected, "Float") and Types.is(actual, "Int")
    return "convert it with Float.from_int(...)"
  elsif Types.is(expected, "Result") and !Types.is(actual, "Result")
    if Types.is(Types.item(expected), "Void")
      return "give a Result with ok() or error(\"message\")"
    end
    return "give a Result with ok(...) or error(\"message\")"
  elsif Types.is(expected, "Int") and Types.is(actual, "Float")
    return "convert it with Float.to_int!(...), which truncates"
  end
  return ""
end
compiler/check_list.agc:
## The checking rules of the List builtins (src/checker.rkt, check-builtin-call: list-size ... list-repeat). A rule
## takes the call (State.Site) and returns the new state with the type of the call.

import Ast from "ast"
import Model from "builtin_model"
import Args from "check_args"
import State from "check_state"
import Stmt from "check_stmt"
import CheckTypes from "check_types"
import Source from "source"
import T from "types"

## Checks a call of a List builtin by its rule. Any other rule is the caller's.
export def check_list_rule(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, rule: Model.Rule) -> Result[State.Out]
  case rule
    Model.Rule.ListSize ->
      out = try Args.list_argument(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown)
      return ok(State.Out(st: out.st, type: T.Type.Int))
    Model.Rule.ListReverse -> return Args.list_argument(cx, st, site, T.only_list(site.expected))
    Model.Rule.ListSort -> return check_sort(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.ListSortBy -> return check_sort_by(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.ListConcat -> return check_concat(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.ListCount -> return check_count(cx, st, site, false)
    Model.Rule.ListAt -> return check_count(cx, st, site, true)
    Model.Rule.ListAppend -> return check_append(cx, st, site, false)
    Model.Rule.ListSet -> return check_append(cx, st, site, true)
    Model.Rule.ListRepeat -> return check_repeat(cx, st, site)
    _ -> return check_callback_rule(cx, st, site, rule)
  end
end

# List.sort: a list of Int, Float or String.
def check_sort(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try Args.list_argument(cx, st, site, T.only_list(site.expected))
  element = T.item(target.type)
  if !T.is(element, "Int") and !T.is(element, "Float") and !T.is(element, "String")
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        target.st,
        "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH",
        "List.sort needs List[Int], List[Float] or List[String], found #{T.to_text(target.type)}",
        Ast.expr_span(site.args[0]),
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(target)
end

# List.sort_by: the key function is a block (which gives the element type of the list) or a function value.
def check_sort_by(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  callback = site.args[1]
  case callback
    Ast.Expr.BlockLit(block) -> return sort_by_block(cx, st, site, block)
    _ -> return sort_by_function(cx, st, site, callback)
  end
end

def sort_by_block(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, block: Ast.BlockLit) -> Result[State.Out]
  annotated = try annotated_parameter(cx, st, block, 0)
  target = try Args.list_argument(cx, st, site, T.list_of(annotated))
  key = try Stmt.check_block_body(
    cx,
    target.st,
    block,
    Ast.Optional.Present([T.item(target.type)]),
    T.Type.Unknown,
    Ast.Optional.Absent,
  )
  try check_sort_key(cx, key.st, key.type, block.span)
  return ok(State.Out(st: key.st, type: target.type))
end

def sort_by_function(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, callback: Ast.Expr) -> Result[State.Out]
  key = try State.expr(cx, st, callback, T.Type.Unknown)
  try check_sort_key(cx, key.st, key.type, Ast.expr_span(callback))
  return Args.list_argument(cx, key.st, site, T.Type.List(T.params(key.type)[0]))
end

# The key function takes one parameter and gives an Int, a Float or a String.
def check_sort_key(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, callback: T.Type, span: Source.Span) -> Result[Bool]
  if !T.is(callback, "Fn") or T.params(callback).size != 1
    return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH", "sort_by requires a key function with one parameter", span))
  end
  key = T.result(callback)
  if !T.is(key, "Int") and !T.is(key, "Float") and !T.is(key, "String")
    return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH", "sort_by keys must be Int, Float or String", span))
  end
  return ok(true)
end

# List.concat: both lists have one type; an empty literal takes the type of the other side.
def check_concat(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  context = T.only_list(site.expected)
  current = st
  if T.unknown?(context) and Args.empty_list?(site.args[0])
    other = try State.expr(cx, current, site.args[1], T.Type.Unknown)
    current = other.st
    context = other.type
  end
  target = try Args.list_argument(cx, current, site, context)
  second = try State.expr(cx, target.st, site.args[1], target.type)
  return ok(State.Out(st: second.st, type: target.type))
end

# List.take, List.drop and List.at: a list and an Int; at gives the element.
def check_count(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, at: Bool) -> Result[State.Out]
  context = T.only_list(site.expected)
  if at
    context = T.list_of(site.expected)
  end
  target = try Args.list_argument(cx, st, site, context)
  count = try State.expr(cx, target.st, site.args[1], T.Type.Int)
  if at
    return ok(State.Out(st: count.st, type: T.item(target.type)))
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: count.st, type: target.type))
end

# List.append and List.set: the value has the element type; an empty literal takes it from the value.
def check_append(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, set: Bool) -> Result[State.Out]
  value = site.args[site.args.size - 1]
  context = T.only_list(site.expected)
  current = st
  if T.unknown?(context) and Args.empty_list?(site.args[0])
    first = try State.expr(cx, current, value, T.Type.Unknown)
    current = first.st
    context = T.Type.List(first.type)
  end
  target = try Args.list_argument(cx, current, site, context)
  current = target.st
  if set
    index = try State.expr(cx, current, site.args[1], T.Type.Int)
    current = index.st
  end
  checked = try State.expr(cx, current, value, T.item(target.type))
  return ok(State.Out(st: checked.st, type: target.type))
end

def check_repeat(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  context = T.Type.Unknown
  if T.is(site.expected, "List")
    context = T.item(site.expected)
  end
  element = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[0], context)
  count = try State.expr(cx, element.st, site.args[1], T.Type.Int)
  return ok(State.Out(st: count.st, type: T.Type.List(element.type)))
end

# The type written on parameter number index of a block, or Unknown when it has none.
def annotated_parameter(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, block: Ast.BlockLit, index: Int) -> Result[T.Type]
  if block.params.size <= index
    return ok(T.Type.Unknown)
  end
  case block.params[index].type
    Ast.Optional.Present(annotation) -> return CheckTypes.resolve_type(cx, st, annotation, false)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return ok(T.Type.Unknown)
  end
end

# List.map, filter, reduce, each, any? and all?: the callback is a block (which gets the element type) or a function
# value.
def check_callback_rule(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, rule: Model.Rule) -> Result[State.Out]
  callback = site.args[site.args.size - 1]
  checked = State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Unknown)
  case callback
    Ast.Expr.BlockLit(block) -> checked = try block_callback(cx, st, site, rule, block)
    _ -> checked = try State.expr(cx, st, callback, T.Type.Unknown)
  end
  arity = 1
  if reduces?(rule)
    arity = 2
  end
  if !T.is(checked.type, "Fn") or T.params(checked.type).size != arity
    return error(
      State.fail(cx, checked.st, "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH", "wrong collection callback type", Ast.expr_span(callback)),
    )
  end
  return callback_result(cx, checked.st, site, rule, callback, checked.type)
end

# The callback of a block: the list gives the element type, and the rule gives the parameters and result the block must
# have.
def block_callback(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  site: State.Site,
  rule: Model.Rule,
  block: Ast.BlockLit,
) -> Result[State.Out]
  position = 0
  if reduces?(rule)
    position = 1
  end
  annotated = try annotated_parameter(cx, st, block, position)
  list = try Args.list_argument(cx, st, site, T.list_of(annotated))
  element = T.item(list.type)
  receiver: Ast.Optional[Ast.Expr] = Ast.Optional.Absent
  if each?(rule)
    receiver = Ast.Optional.Present(site.args[0])
  end
  if reduces?(rule)
    return reduce_block(cx, list.st, site, block, element)
  end
  return Stmt.check_block_body(cx, list.st, block, Ast.Optional.Present([element]), block_result(rule), receiver)
end

def reduce_block(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  site: State.Site,
  block: Ast.BlockLit,
  element: T.Type,
) -> Result[State.Out]
  start = site.expected
  if T.unknown?(start)
    start = try annotated_parameter(cx, st, block, 0)
  end
  accumulator = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[1], start)
  return Stmt.check_block_body(
    cx,
    accumulator.st,
    block,
    Ast.Optional.Present([accumulator.type, element]),
    accumulator.type,
    Ast.Optional.Absent,
  )
end

# The result a block of the rule must give: Bool for filter, any? and all?, Void for each, none known for map.
def block_result(rule: Model.Rule) -> T.Type
  case rule
    Model.Rule.ListFilter -> return T.Type.Bool
    Model.Rule.ListAny -> return T.Type.Bool
    Model.Rule.ListAll -> return T.Type.Bool
    Model.Rule.ListEach -> return T.Type.Void
    _ -> return T.Type.Unknown
  end
end

def reduces?(rule: Model.Rule) -> Bool
  case rule
    Model.Rule.ListReduce -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

def each?(rule: Model.Rule) -> Bool
  case rule
    Model.Rule.ListEach -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

# The type of the call once the callback is checked: the list is checked against the element type of a function value,
# then the result follows from the rule.
def callback_result(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  site: State.Site,
  rule: Model.Rule,
  callback: Ast.Expr,
  type: T.Type,
) -> Result[State.Out]
  span = Ast.expr_span(callback)
  params = T.params(type)
  result = T.result(type)
  element = params[0]
  if reduces?(rule)
    element = params[1]
  end
  current = st
  if !is_block?(callback)
    list = try Args.list_argument(cx, current, site, T.Type.List(element))
    current = list.st
  end
  if reduces?(rule)
    return reduce_result(cx, current, site, callback, params[0], result)
  end
  return plain_result(cx, current, rule, span, element, result)
end

def reduce_result(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  site: State.Site,
  callback: Ast.Expr,
  accumulator: T.Type,
  result: T.Type,
) -> Result[State.Out]
  span = Ast.expr_span(callback)
  if !T.same(accumulator, result)
    return error(State.mismatch(cx, st, accumulator, result, span))
  end
  current = st
  if !is_block?(callback)
    initial = try State.expr(cx, current, site.args[1], result)
    current = initial.st
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: current, type: result))
end

def plain_result(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  rule: Model.Rule,
  span: Source.Span,
  element: T.Type,
  result: T.Type,
) -> Result[State.Out]
  case rule
    Model.Rule.ListFilter ->
      try require_type(cx, st, T.Type.Bool, result, span)
      return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.List(element)))
    Model.Rule.ListAny ->
      try require_type(cx, st, T.Type.Bool, result, span)
      return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Bool))
    Model.Rule.ListAll ->
      try require_type(cx, st, T.Type.Bool, result, span)
      return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Bool))
    Model.Rule.ListEach ->
      try require_type(cx, st, T.Type.Void, result, span)
      return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Void))
    _ -> return map_result(cx, st, span, result)
  end
end

def map_result(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, span: Source.Span, result: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  if T.is(result, "Void")
    return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-VOID-VALUE", "map callbacks must return data", span))
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.List(result)))
end

def require_type(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, expected: T.Type, actual: T.Type, span: Source.Span) -> Result[Bool]
  if !T.same(expected, actual)
    return error(State.mismatch(cx, st, expected, actual, span))
  end
  return ok(true)
end

def is_block?(node: Ast.Expr) -> Bool
  case node
    Ast.Expr.BlockLit(block) -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end
compiler/check_method.agc:
## Methods and fields (src/checker.rkt: check-method, check-field-access, check-struct-field). A method call or a field
## access that is not a struct field names a builtin of the receiver's kind; it is checked as the call of that builtin
## with the receiver as first argument, and the resolution is recorded by node id for lowering.

import Ast from "ast"
import Calls from "check_call"
import Help from "check_help"
import Names from "check_names"
import State from "check_state"
import CheckTypes from "check_types"
import Source from "source"
import T from "types"

## Checks target.name(args).
export def check_method(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.MethodCall, expected: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try State.expr(cx, st, node.target, T.Type.Unknown)
  return method_on(cx, target, node.id, node.target, node.name, node.args, node.span, expected)
end

## Checks target.name: a struct field, or a method without arguments (to_s, size, ...).
export def check_field_access(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.FieldAccess, expected: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  target = try State.expr(cx, st, node.target, T.Type.Unknown)
  if field_target?(cx, target.type, node.name)
    return check_struct_field(cx, target.st, node, target.type)
  end
  return method_on(cx, target, node.id, node.target, node.name, [], node.span, expected)
end

# A struct is read by field unless the name is to_s or inspect and the struct has no such field.
def field_target?(cx: State.Cx, target: T.Type, name: String) -> Bool
  if !T.is(target, "Struct")
    return false
  end
  if name == "to_s" or name == "inspect"
    return Calls.find_field(cx.structs[T.name(target)], name).ok?
  end
  return true
end

# The type of the field, CHECK-UNKNOWN-FIELD when the struct has none of that name.
def check_struct_field(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.FieldAccess, target: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  fields = cx.structs[T.name(target)]
  field = Calls.find_field(fields, node.name)
  if !field.ok?
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-UNKNOWN-FIELD",
        "\"#{T.display_name(T.name(target))}\" has no field \"#{node.name}\"",
        node.span,
        Help.field_help(node.name, fields),
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: field.unwrap!.type))
end

# What the method is: "self", "text" (to_s) or "inspect" for a data value, the full name of a builtin, or "" when there
# is none.
def method_kind(cx: State.Cx, target: T.Type, kind: String, name: String) -> String
  if kind != ""
    found = Names.resolve_method(cx, kind, name)
    if found != ""
      return found
    end
  end
  if name == "to_s" and CheckTypes.data?(cx, target, [])
    return "text"
  elsif name == "inspect" and CheckTypes.data?(cx, target, [])
    return "inspect"
  end
  return ""
end

# The method on a receiver that is already checked. The resolution is recorded by the id of the node.
def method_on(
  cx: State.Cx,
  target: State.Out,
  id: Int,
  target_node: Ast.Expr,
  name: String,
  args: List[Ast.Expr],
  span: Source.Span,
  expected: T.Type,
) -> Result[State.Out]
  type = target.type
  kind = Names.receiver_kind(type)
  resolved = method_kind(cx, type, kind, name)
  if resolved == ""
    return error(
      State.fail_maybe(
        cx,
        target.st,
        "CHECK-UNKNOWN-METHOD",
        "#{T.to_text(type)} has no method \"#{name}\"",
        span,
        unknown_method_help(cx, target.st, id, type, kind, name),
      ),
    )
  end
  if resolved == "self" or resolved == "text" or resolved == "inspect"
    return check_own_method(cx, target.st, id, resolved, type, name, args, span, expected)
  end
  typed = Ast.Expr.Typed(
    Ast.TypedTarget(id: Ast.expr_id(target_node), target: target_node, type: type, span: Ast.expr_span(target_node)),
  )
  call = Ast.Call(id: id, name: resolved, args: [typed].concat(args), piped: false, parenthesized: true, span: span)
  st = State.record_resolved(target.st, id, State.Resolved.Call(resolved, type))
  return Calls.check_call(cx, st, call, expected)
end

# to_s and inspect, and a to_s that is the receiver itself: they take no arguments and give a String (or the receiver).
def check_own_method(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  id: Int,
  resolved: String,
  type: T.Type,
  name: String,
  args: List[Ast.Expr],
  span: Source.Span,
  expected: T.Type,
) -> Result[State.Out]
  if args.size > 0
    return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-ARITY", "\"#{name}\" takes no arguments", span))
  end
  result = T.Type.String
  how = State.Resolved.Text(type)
  if resolved == "self"
    result = type
    how = State.Resolved.Self(type)
  elsif resolved == "inspect"
    how = State.Resolved.Inspect(type)
  end
  checked = try State.ensure(cx, st, result, expected, span)
  return ok(State.Out(st: State.record_resolved(st, id, how), type: checked))
end

# The help of CHECK-UNKNOWN-METHOD: a range that needs parentheses, then what is special about the receiver.
def unknown_method_help(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, id: Int, target: T.Type, kind: String, name: String) -> String
  if st.range_chain.any? do |link: Int| link == id end and Names.resolve_method(cx, "Range", name) != ""
    return "a method call on a range needs parentheses: (a..b).#{name}"
  elsif name == "to_s" or name == "inspect"
    return (
      "only data values have to_s and inspect: numbers, Bool, String, nil, Json, ranges, and lists, maps, sets, " +
      "Results, structs and enums of those"
    )
  elsif T.is(target, "Struct")
    return struct_help(cx, target, name)
  elsif name == "with"
    return "with copies a struct with some fields changed; the value before .with must be a struct"
  elsif kind != ""
    return kind_help(cx, target, kind, name)
  elsif CheckTypes.data?(cx, target, [])
    return Help.near(name, ["to_s", "inspect"], [])
  end
  return ""
end

# A struct has no methods: the help says what the name could be instead.
def struct_help(cx: State.Cx, target: T.Type, name: String) -> String
  fields = cx.structs[T.name(target)]
  field = Calls.find_field(fields, name)
  if cx.functions.has_key?(name)
    return "structs have no methods; call #{name}(...) with the struct as an argument"
  elsif field.ok? and T.is(field.unwrap!.type, "Fn")
    return "#{name} is a function field; call it with .#{name}.call(...)"
  elsif name == "with"
    # No did-you-mean here: a field close to "with" is not a typo of it.
    return "with needs the fields to change, as in .with(field: value); #{Help.field_list(fields)}"
  end
  return "structs have no methods; #{Help.field_help(name, fields)}"
end

# The help for a method another language has, a close name, or the methods the kind has.
def kind_help(cx: State.Cx, target: T.Type, kind: String, name: String) -> String
  foreign = Names.foreign_method_help(cx, kind, name)
  if foreign != ""
    return foreign
  end
  names = method_names(cx, target, kind)
  guess = Help.near(name, names, [])
  if guess != ""
    return guess
  end
  return "#{T.to_text(target)} methods: #{names.sort.join(", ")}"
end

# The methods of the kind, with to_s and inspect for a data value.
def method_names(cx: State.Cx, target: T.Type, kind: String) -> List[String]
  names = Names.method_names(cx, kind)
  if CheckTypes.data?(cx, target, [])
    names = names.concat(
      ["to_s", "inspect"].filter do |own: String| !names.any? do |known: String| known == own end end,
    )
  end
  return names
end
compiler/check_names.agc:
## Which builtin a method name stands for (src/checker.rkt: receiver-kind, resolve-method, catalog-method,
## method-names, pipe-method-name, foreign-method-help). A receiver kind is the word of its type ("String", "List",
## ...); "" is no kind. A method is resolved to the full name of a builtin, such as String.length, or to "self" when it
## returns the receiver (to_s on a String).

import State from "check_state"
import T from "types"

## The kind of a receiver, or "" when its type has no methods in the catalog.
export def receiver_kind(type: T.Type) -> String
  word = T.tag(type)
  if (
    word == "String" or
    word == "List" or
    word == "Map" or
    word == "Set" or
    word == "Float" or
    word == "Result" or
    word == "Json" or
    word == "Int" or
    word == "Range" or
    word == "Channel"
  )
    return word
  end
  return ""
end

## The builtin that method name of that kind stands for, "self", or "" when there is none: an alias first (size, to_i,
## push), then the builtin of the kind's module whose first parameter has that kind.
export def resolve_method(cx: State.Cx, kind: String, name: String) -> String
  alias = cx.help.aliases.get("#{kind}.#{name}")
  if alias.ok?
    return alias.unwrap!
  end
  return catalog_method(cx, kind, name)
end

## The methods a receiver kind has: its aliases and the builtins of its module, without duplicates.
export def method_names(cx: State.Cx, kind: String) -> List[String]
  names: List[String] = []
  seen: Set[String] = Set.new([])
  prefix = "#{kind}."
  for key in cx.help.aliases.keys
    if key.starts_with?(prefix)
      names = names.push(key.slice(prefix.length, key.length - prefix.length))
    end
  end
  module = cx.help.modules.get(kind)
  if module.ok?
    names = names.concat(module_methods(cx, kind, "#{module.unwrap!}."))
  end
  unique: List[String] = []
  for name in names
    if !seen.include?(name)
      seen = seen.add(name)
      unique = unique.push(name)
    end
  end
  return unique
end

## The method name a builtin is written as in method form, for the help of CHECK-PIPE-METHOD: String.upcase is upcase,
## String.to_int is the alias to_i. "" when there is none.
export def pipe_method_name(cx: State.Cx, kind: String, name: String) -> String
  dot = name.index_of(".")
  if dot.ok?
    suffix = name.slice(dot.unwrap! + 1, name.length - dot.unwrap! - 1)
    if resolve_method(cx, kind, suffix) == name
      return suffix
    end
  end
  prefix = "#{kind}."
  for key in cx.help.aliases.keys.sort
    if key.starts_with?(prefix) and cx.help.aliases[key] == name
      return key.slice(prefix.length, key.length - prefix.length)
    end
  end
  return ""
end

## The help for a method name another language has, or "".
export def foreign_method_help(cx: State.Cx, kind: String, name: String) -> String
  direct = cx.help.kind_methods.get("#{kind}.#{name}")
  if direct.ok?
    return direct.unwrap!
  end
  if kind == "Result" and string_method?(cx, name)
    return result_help(cx, name)
  elsif name == "nil?"
    return "values are never nil unless their type is Nil; compare with nil: x == nil"
  elsif name == "lazy" and (kind == "List" or kind == "Range")
    return "lists are eager; read a source that is too big for a list in a while loop"
  end
  return renamed_help(cx, kind, name)
end

# The builtin of the kind's module with that name whose first parameter has the kind, or "".
def catalog_method(cx: State.Cx, kind: String, name: String) -> String
  module = cx.help.modules.get(kind)
  if !module.ok?
    return ""
  end
  entry = cx.catalog.entries.get("#{module.unwrap!}.#{name}")
  if entry.ok? and entry.unwrap!.parameters.size > 0 and T.tag(entry.unwrap!.parameters[0].type) == kind
    return entry.unwrap!.name
  end
  return ""
end

# The names of the module's builtins that are methods of the kind.
def module_methods(cx: State.Cx, kind: String, prefix: String) -> List[String]
  names: List[String] = []
  for key in cx.catalog.entries.keys
    if key.starts_with?(prefix)
      name = key.slice(prefix.length, key.length - prefix.length)
      if catalog_method(cx, kind, name) != ""
        names = names.push(name)
      end
    end
  end
  return names
end

# True when a String has the method, or a foreign String method has help.
def string_method?(cx: State.Cx, name: String) -> Bool
  return resolve_method(cx, "String", name) != "" or cx.help.kind_methods.has_key?("String.#{name}")
end

# A method of a String that a Result does not have: unwrap the Result first.
def result_help(cx: State.Cx, name: String) -> String
  string_help = foreign_method_help(cx, "String", name)
  text = "this is a Result; unwrap it first with r.unwrap! (use gets! to read a line without a Result)"
  if string_help != ""
    return "#{text}, then: #{string_help}"
  end
  return text
end

# A method another language names differently: the Agentica method of that kind, if there is one.
def renamed_help(cx: State.Cx, kind: String, name: String) -> String
  candidates = cx.help.foreign_methods.get(name)
  if !candidates.ok?
    return ""
  end
  for candidate in candidates.unwrap!
    if resolve_method(cx, kind, candidate) != ""
      return "use .#{candidate}"
    end
  end
  return ""
end
compiler/check_register.agc:
## Registration: the first four passes of `check` in src/checker.rkt, which read every declaration of the program in
## order and fill the tables of Cx before any function body is checked: the names of the enums, the structs and their
## fields, the variants of the enums, and the signatures of the functions. Then check_main. A problem is
## CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME, CHECK-VOID-TYPE or another type problem, or CHECK-MAIN.

import Ast from "ast"
import Model from "builtin_model"
import State from "check_state"
import Types from "check_types"
import Linker from "linker"
import Source from "source"
import T from "types"

## The context with the enums, structs and functions of the program added to the builtin ones.
export def register(cx: State.Cx, modules: List[Linker.LinkedModule]) -> Result[State.Cx]
  found = try register_enum_names(cx, modules)
  found = try register_structs(found, modules)
  found = try register_enum_variants(found, modules)
  found = try register_functions(found, modules)
  return ok(found)
end

## CHECK-MAIN unless the program declares main() -> Void; the first main is the one that counts. root is the span of
## the program.
export def check_main(cx: State.Cx, modules: List[Linker.LinkedModule], root: Source.Span) -> Result[Bool]
  st = State.fresh()
  for module in modules
    for decl in module.declarations
      case decl
        Ast.Decl.Function(node) ->
          if node.name == "main"
            return main_signature(cx.with(file: module.file), st, node)
          end
        _ -> st = st
      end
    end
  end
  return error(
    State.fail(
      cx.with(file: modules[0].file),
      st,
      "CHECK-MAIN",
      "a program must declare exactly one main() -> Void",
      root,
    ),
  )
end

def main_signature(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.FunctionDecl) -> Result[Bool]
  result = try Types.resolve_type(cx, st, node.result, true)
  if node.params.size != 0 or !T.is(result, "Void")
    return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-MAIN", "main must take no parameters and return Void", node.span))
  end
  return ok(true)
end

# The enum names, with their type parameters and no variants yet.
def register_enum_names(cx: State.Cx, modules: List[Linker.LinkedModule]) -> Result[State.Cx]
  st = State.fresh()
  found = cx
  for module in modules
    for decl in module.declarations
      case decl
        Ast.Decl.Enum(node) -> found = try register_enum_name(found.with(file: module.file), st, node)
        _ -> st = st
      end
    end
  end
  return ok(found)
end

def register_enum_name(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.EnumDecl) -> Result[State.Cx]
  try check_new_name(cx, st, node.name, node.span)
  seen: Set[String] = Set.new([])
  for parameter in node.type_parameters
    if seen.include?(parameter)
      return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME", "duplicate enum type parameter", node.span))
    end
    seen = seen.add(parameter)
  end
  for parameter in node.type_parameters
    if cx.catalog.reserved.include?(parameter)
      return error(
        State.fail(
          cx,
          st,
          "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME",
          "\"#{parameter}\" cannot be used as an enum type parameter",
          node.span,
        ),
      )
    end
  end
  return ok(
    cx.with(
      enums: cx.enums.put(node.name, Model.EnumDef(name: node.name, parameters: node.type_parameters, variants: [])),
    ),
  )
end

# CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME when a struct or enum name is reserved or already taken.
def check_new_name(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, name: String, span: Source.Span) -> Result[Bool]
  if (
    cx.catalog.reserved.include?(name) or
    cx.structs.has_key?(name) or
    cx.enums.has_key?(name) or
    cx.functions.has_key?(name)
  )
    return error(
      State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME", "\"#{T.display_name(name)}\" is already defined", span),
    )
  end
  return ok(true)
end

# The struct names first, with no fields, so a field may name a struct declared later; then the fields.
def register_structs(cx: State.Cx, modules: List[Linker.LinkedModule]) -> Result[State.Cx]
  st = State.fresh()
  found = cx
  for module in modules
    for decl in module.declarations
      case decl
        Ast.Decl.Struct(node) ->
          here = found.with(file: module.file)
          try check_new_name(here, st, node.name, node.span)
          found = here.with(structs: found.structs.put(node.name, []))
        _ -> st = st
      end
    end
  end
  for module in modules
    for decl in module.declarations
      case decl
        Ast.Decl.Struct(node) -> found = try register_fields(found.with(file: module.file), st, node)
        _ -> st = st
      end
    end
  end
  return ok(found)
end

def register_fields(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.StructDecl) -> Result[State.Cx]
  seen: Set[String] = Set.new([])
  fields: List[Model.Named] = []
  for field in node.fields
    try State.reserve_constructor(cx, st, field.name, field.span)
    if seen.include?(field.name)
      return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME", "duplicate field \"#{field.name}\"", field.span))
    end
    seen = seen.add(field.name)
    type = try Types.resolve_type(cx, st, field.type, false)
    # value.with(...) is always the struct update, so a function field named with could never be called without .call.
    if field.name == "with" and T.is(type, "Fn")
      return error(
        State.fail_help(
          cx,
          st,
          "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME",
          "a field named \"with\" cannot hold a function",
          field.span,
          "value.with(...) is the struct update; rename the field",
        ),
      )
    end
    fields = fields.push(Model.Named(name: field.name, type: type))
  end
  return ok(cx.with(structs: cx.structs.put(node.name, fields)))
end

def register_enum_variants(cx: State.Cx, modules: List[Linker.LinkedModule]) -> Result[State.Cx]
  st = State.fresh()
  found = cx
  for module in modules
    for decl in module.declarations
      case decl
        Ast.Decl.Enum(node) -> found = try register_variants(found.with(file: module.file), st, node)
        _ -> st = st
      end
    end
  end
  return ok(found)
end

# The variants of one enum, resolved with the enum's type parameters in scope.
def register_variants(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.EnumDecl) -> Result[State.Cx]
  here = cx.with(type_params: node.type_parameters)
  seen: Set[String] = Set.new([])
  variants: List[Model.Variant] = []
  for variant in node.variants
    if seen.include?(variant.name)
      return error(
        State.fail(
          here,
          st,
          "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME",
          "duplicate variant \"#{variant.name}\" in enum \"#{T.display_name(node.name)}\"",
          variant.span,
        ),
      )
    end
    seen = seen.add(variant.name)
    payload = try Types.resolve_all(here, st, variant.payload_types)
    variants = variants.push(Model.Variant(name: variant.name, payload: payload))
  end
  definition = Model.EnumDef(name: node.name, parameters: node.type_parameters, variants: variants)
  return ok(cx.with(enums: cx.enums.put(node.name, definition)))
end

def register_functions(cx: State.Cx, modules: List[Linker.LinkedModule]) -> Result[State.Cx]
  st = State.fresh()
  found = cx
  for module in modules
    for decl in module.declarations
      case decl
        Ast.Decl.Function(node) -> found = try register_function(found.with(file: module.file), st, node)
        _ -> st = st
      end
    end
  end
  return ok(found)
end

def register_function(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.FunctionDecl) -> Result[State.Cx]
  taken = (
    cx.catalog.entries.has_key?(node.name) or
    cx.functions.has_key?(node.name) or
    cx.structs.has_key?(node.name) or
    cx.enums.has_key?(node.name)
  )
  if taken
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME",
        "\"#{T.display_name(node.name)}\" is already defined",
        node.span,
      ),
    )
  end
  seen: Set[String] = Set.new([])
  params: List[T.Type] = []
  for param in node.params
    if seen.include?(param.name)
      return error(
        State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME", "duplicate parameter \"#{param.name}\"", param.span),
      )
    end
    seen = seen.add(param.name)
    params = params.push(try Types.resolve_type(cx, st, param.type, false))
  end
  result = try Types.resolve_type(cx, st, node.result, true)
  return ok(cx.with(functions: cx.functions.put(node.name, State.Signature(params: params, result: result))))
end
compiler/check_rules.agc:
## A call of a builtin (src/checker.rkt, check-builtin-call): the form that takes this many arguments, a block only
## where the last parameter is a function, then the rule of the builtin. The List, Map, Set, Task and Channel rules are
## in check_list.agc and check_collections.agc; the rest are here.

import Ast from "ast"
import Model from "builtin_model"
import Builtins from "builtins"
import Args from "check_args"
import Collections from "check_collections"
import Failure from "check_failure"
import Lists from "check_list"
import State from "check_state"
import CheckTypes from "check_types"
import Source from "source"
import T from "types"

## Checks a call of the builtin entry (the first form of the name). expected is the type the context wants, Unknown
## when none.
export def check_builtin_call(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  node: Ast.Call,
  expected: T.Type,
  entry: Model.Builtin,
) -> Result[State.Out]
  selected = Builtins.form_for(entry, node.args.size)
  if !selected.ok?
    return error(arity_failure(cx, st, node, entry))
  end
  form = selected.unwrap!
  try check_block_target(cx, st, node, form)
  site = State.Site(node: node, args: node.args, selected: form, expected: expected)
  return check_rule(cx, st, site, form.rule)
end

## CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH unless the type can be printed or interpolated (it has to_s).
export def ensure_printable(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, type: T.Type, span: Source.Span) -> Result[Bool]
  if !CheckTypes.data?(cx, type, [])
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH",
        "#{T.to_text(type)} has no to_s, so it cannot be printed or interpolated",
        span,
        (
          "only data values have to_s: numbers, Bool, String, nil, Json, ranges, and lists, maps, sets, Results, " +
          "structs and enums of those"
        ),
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(true)
end

# CHECK-ARITY: no form of the builtin takes this many arguments. The note is the signature of every form.
def arity_failure(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Call, entry: Model.Builtin) -> String
  counts = [entry].concat(entry.alternatives).map do |form: Model.Builtin| form.parameters.size.to_s end
  expected = counts.join(" or ")
  message = "\"#{entry.name}\" expects #{expected} argument(s), found #{node.args.size}"
  base = Failure.problem(cx.file, st.signature, "CHECK-ARITY", message, node.span, State.hint_of(""))
  return Failure.pack(base.with(callee: Builtins.signature(entry)))
end

# A block as the last argument needs a function as the last parameter.
def check_block_target(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Call, form: Model.Builtin) -> Result[Bool]
  if node.args.size == 0
    return ok(true)
  end
  last = node.args[node.args.size - 1]
  case last
    Ast.Expr.BlockLit(block) ->
      if !T.is(form.parameters[form.parameters.size - 1].type, "Fn")
        return error(
          State.fail_help(
            cx,
            st,
            "CHECK-BLOCK-TARGET",
            "\"#{form.name}\" does not take a block: its last parameter is not a function",
            block.span,
            "a block is only allowed when the last parameter is a function (Fn[...])",
          ),
        )
      end
    _ -> return ok(true)
  end
  return ok(true)
end

# The rule of the builtin, which says how its arguments are checked and what type the call has.
def check_rule(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, rule: Model.Rule) -> Result[State.Out]
  case rule
    Model.Rule.Plain -> return check_plain(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.Show -> return check_show(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.Identity -> return State.expr(cx, st, site.args[0], site.expected)
    Model.Rule.Ok -> return check_ok(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.OkVoid -> return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Result(T.Type.Void)))
    Model.Rule.Error -> return check_error(cx, st, site)
    Model.Rule.JsonDecode -> return check_json_type(cx, st, site, true)
    Model.Rule.JsonSchema -> return check_json_type(cx, st, site, false)
    Model.Rule.JsonEncode -> return check_json_encode(cx, st, site, false)
    Model.Rule.JsonFrom -> return check_json_encode(cx, st, site, true)
    Model.Rule.TestEq -> return check_test_eq(cx, st, site)
    _ -> return check_result_rule(cx, st, site, rule)
  end
end

# A builtin with no rule: each argument against its parameter.
def check_plain(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  current = st
  index = 0
  while index < site.args.size and index < site.selected.parameters.size
    out = try State.expr(cx, current, site.args[index], site.selected.parameters[index].type)
    current = out.st
    index += 1
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: current, type: site.selected.result))
end

# puts and print: any value that can be printed.
def check_show(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  out = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[0], T.Type.Unknown)
  try ensure_printable(cx, out.st, out.type, Ast.expr_span(site.args[0]))
  return ok(State.Out(st: out.st, type: T.Type.Void))
end

def check_ok(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  out = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[0], T.only_result_item(site.expected))
  return ok(State.Out(st: out.st, type: T.Type.Result(out.type)))
end

# error(message) needs the Result type from its context.
def check_error(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  message = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[0], T.Type.String)
  expected = site.expected
  span = site.node.span
  if !T.unknown?(expected) and !T.is(expected, "Result")
    return error(State.mismatch(cx, message.st, expected, T.Type.Result(T.Type.Var("T")), span))
  end
  if T.unknown?(expected)
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        message.st,
        "CHECK-RESULT-TYPE",
        "an error needs an expected Result type",
        span,
        "add a Result[T] annotation, for example r: Result[Int] = error(message)",
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: message.st, type: expected))
end

# JSON.decode(text, Type) and JSON.schema(Type): the type argument is a struct name whose fields can all be decoded.
def check_json_type(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, decode: Bool) -> Result[State.Out]
  current = st
  target = site.args[0]
  if decode
    text = try State.expr(cx, current, site.args[0], T.Type.String)
    current = text.st
    target = site.args[1]
  end
  case target
    Ast.Expr.TypeName(node) -> return json_target(cx, current, node, decode)
    _ -> return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        current,
        "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH",
        "JSON type argument requires a struct name",
        Ast.expr_span(target),
      ),
    )
  end
end

def json_target(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.TypeName, decode: Bool) -> Result[State.Out]
  ref = Ast.TypeRef(id: node.id, name: node.name, args: [], span: node.span)
  type = try CheckTypes.resolve_type(cx, st, ref, false)
  if !T.is(type, "Struct") or !CheckTypes.decodable?(cx, type, [])
    return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-NOT-DECODABLE", "target contains types that cannot be decoded", node.span))
  end
  if decode
    return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Result(type)))
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Json))
end

# JSON.encode and JSON.from: any value that can be written as JSON.
def check_json_encode(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, from: Bool) -> Result[State.Out]
  out = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[0], T.Type.Unknown)
  if !CheckTypes.encodable?(cx, out.type, [])
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        out.st,
        "CHECK-NOT-ENCODABLE",
        "cannot JSON.encode #{T.to_text(out.type)} or its nested types",
        Ast.expr_span(site.args[0]),
      ),
    )
  end
  if from
    return ok(State.Out(st: out.st, type: T.Type.Json))
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: out.st, type: T.Type.String))
end

# Test.eq: two values of one type that has equality.
def check_test_eq(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site) -> Result[State.Out]
  actual = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[0], T.Type.Unknown)
  wanted = try State.expr(cx, actual.st, site.args[1], actual.type)
  if !T.same(actual.type, wanted.type)
    return error(State.mismatch(cx, wanted.st, actual.type, wanted.type, Ast.expr_span(site.args[1])))
  end
  if !CheckTypes.data?(cx, actual.type, [])
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        wanted.st,
        "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH",
        "Test.eq needs a type with equality, found #{T.to_text(actual.type)}",
        Ast.expr_span(site.args[0]),
        (
          "Test.eq compares numbers, Bool, String, nil, ranges, Json, and lists, maps, sets, Results, " +
          "structs and enums of those"
        ),
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(State.Out(st: wanted.st, type: T.Type.Result(T.Type.Void)))
end

def check_result_rule(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, rule: Model.Rule) -> Result[State.Out]
  case rule
    Model.Rule.TestResult ->
      target = try Args.result_argument(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown)
      return ok(State.Out(st: target.st, type: T.Type.Result(T.Type.Void)))
    Model.Rule.ResultOk ->
      target = try Args.result_argument(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown)
      return ok(State.Out(st: target.st, type: T.Type.Bool))
    Model.Rule.ResultMessage ->
      target = try Args.result_argument(cx, st, site, T.Type.Unknown)
      return ok(State.Out(st: target.st, type: T.Type.String))
    Model.Rule.ResultUnwrap ->
      target = try Args.result_argument(cx, st, site, T.result_of(site.expected))
      return ok(State.Out(st: target.st, type: T.item(target.type)))
    Model.Rule.ResultDefault ->
      default = try State.expr(cx, st, site.args[1], site.expected)
      target = try Args.result_argument(cx, default.st, site, T.Type.Result(default.type))
      return ok(State.Out(st: target.st, type: default.type))
    _ -> return check_other_rule(cx, st, site, rule)
  end
end

# The rules of the Task, Channel, Map and Set builtins, then of the List builtins.
def check_other_rule(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, site: State.Site, rule: Model.Rule) -> Result[State.Out]
  if is_list_rule?(rule)
    return Lists.check_list_rule(cx, st, site, rule)
  end
  return Collections.check_collection_rule(cx, st, site, rule)
end

def is_list_rule?(rule: Model.Rule) -> Bool
  case rule
    Model.Rule.ListSize -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListReverse -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListSort -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListSortBy -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListConcat -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListCount -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListAt -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListAppend -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListSet -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListRepeat -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListMap -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListFilter -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListReduce -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListEach -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListAny -> return true
    Model.Rule.ListAll -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end
compiler/check_state.agc:
## The state of the checker (src/checker.rkt has it as mutable variables inside `check`): what is fixed for the run
## (Cx), what changes while the tree is walked (St), and the small operations on them that every part of the checker
## uses. A check function takes Cx and St and returns the new St with its result (Out for an expression), or fails with
## a packed Problem (check_failure.agc), so `try` stops at the first diagnostic.

import Ast from "ast"
import Model from "builtin_model"
import Builtins from "builtins"
import Help from "check_help"
import Failure from "check_failure"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Source from "source"
import Types from "types"

## A name in scope: its type, whether it cannot be assigned (a for variable), and how many scopes were open when it was
## introduced (a block cannot assign a name from outside it, so the level tells which side a name is on).
export struct Binding
  type: Types.Type
  immutable: Bool
  level: Int
end

## The result type of the function or block being checked. Infer is a block whose result is not known yet: the first
## return or the last expression gives it.
export enum Slot
  Infer
  Known(Types.Type)
end

## The block being checked and the scope depth at its start, for CHECK-CAPTURED-ASSIGNMENT. each_receiver is the list
## of a List.each call, which the help text names.
export struct Capture
  boundary: Int
  params: List[Ast.BlockParam]
  each_receiver: Ast.Optional[Ast.Expr]
end

## What a method call, or a field access that names a method, resolved to: the receiver stays as it is (Self, for to_s
## on a String), it is printed (Text, to_s) or inspected (Inspect), or it is the first argument of the builtin Call.
## Each holds the type of the receiver. src/ keeps this as the `resolved` field of the node.
export enum Resolved
  Self(Types.Type)
  Text(Types.Type)
  Inspect(Types.Type)
  Call(String, Types.Type)
end

## The parameter types and the result type of a function.
export struct Signature
  params: List[Types.Type]
  result: Types.Type
end

## What is fixed while the declarations are checked. structs and enums hold the builtin ones and the program's;
## functions the program's; constants the type of each module constant by linked name, which grows as the initializers
## are checked in order. type_params are the type parameters in scope (only while the variants of a generic enum are
## registered). file is the file of the declaration being checked, texts the source of every file by name. expression
## checks an expression: the cycle between expressions and statements goes through this field (check_expr.agc puts its
## own function here), because a module cannot import one that imports it.
export struct Cx
  catalog: Builtins.Catalog
  help: Help.Tables
  structs: Map[String, List[Model.Named]]
  enums: Map[String, Model.EnumDef]
  functions: Map[String, Signature]
  constants: Map[String, Types.Type]
  type_params: List[String]
  file: String
  texts: Map[String, String]
  expression: Fn[Cx, St, Ast.Expr, Types.Type, Bool, Result[Out]]
end

## What changes while a function is checked: the type of each node in a list indexed by id (set once the run starts,
## with one slot per node id of the program) and the resolution of the nodes that have one in a Map, the names in
## scope, how many scopes are open, the result type, the loop depth, the block being checked, the nodes of the range
## chain being checked, the signature of the function (for the diagnostics) and the nesting depth (CHECK-TOO-DEEP). The
## names in scope are one persistent Map: a scope is a snapshot of it, so closing a scope puts the snapshot back and
## nothing is ever deleted.
export struct St
  types: List[Types.Type]
  resolved: Map[Int, Resolved]
  vars: Map[String, Binding]
  depth: Int
  result: Slot
  loops: Int
  capture: Ast.Optional[Capture]
  range_chain: List[Int]
  signature: String
  nest: Int
end

## A call of a builtin that has its own rule: the call, its arguments, the form of the builtin that takes that many
## arguments, and the type the context expects (Unknown when none).
export struct Site
  node: Ast.Call
  args: List[Ast.Expr]
  selected: Model.Builtin
  expected: Types.Type
end

## The result of checking an expression: the new state and the type.
export struct Out
  st: St
  type: Types.Type
end

## The deepest nesting of expressions and statements the checker accepts (CHECK-TOO-DEEP beyond it). src/checker.rkt
## has the same limit and counts the same way.
export def nesting_limit() -> Int
  return 1000
end

## The state at the start of a function: no names, no types.
export def fresh() -> St
  return St(
    types: [],
    resolved: {},
    vars: {},
    depth: 0,
    result: Slot.Known(Types.Type.Void),
    loops: 0,
    capture: Ast.Optional.Absent,
    range_chain: [],
    signature: "",
    nest: 0,
  )
end

## The failure of a diagnostic with a help text.
export def fail_help(cx: Cx, st: St, code: String, message: String, span: Source.Span, help: String) -> String
  return Failure.pack(Failure.problem(cx.file, st.signature, code, message, span, Diag.Help.Hint(help)))
end

## The failure of a diagnostic with no help.
export def fail(cx: Cx, st: St, code: String, message: String, span: Source.Span) -> String
  return Failure.pack(Failure.problem(cx.file, st.signature, code, message, span, Diag.Help.NoHelp))
end

## The failure of a diagnostic whose help may be absent ("" is no help).
export def fail_maybe(cx: Cx, st: St, code: String, message: String, span: Source.Span, help: String) -> String
  if help == ""
    return fail(cx, st, code, message, span)
  end
  return fail_help(cx, st, code, message, span, help)
end

## The failure of a diagnostic with the signature of the callee as a note.
export def fail_callee(cx: Cx, st: St, code: String, message: String, span: Source.Span, callee: String) -> String
  base = Failure.problem(cx.file, st.signature, code, message, span, Diag.Help.NoHelp)
  return Failure.pack(base.with(callee: callee))
end

## The failure of a type mismatch: "expected T, found U" with the types as notes and the conversion help.
export def mismatch(cx: Cx, st: St, expected: Types.Type, actual: Types.Type, span: Source.Span) -> String
  base = Failure.problem(
    cx.file,
    st.signature,
    "CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH",
    "expected #{Types.to_text(expected)}, found #{Types.to_text(actual)}",
    span,
    hint_of(Help.conversion(expected, actual)),
  )
  return Failure.pack(base.with(expected: Types.to_text(expected), actual: Types.to_text(actual)))
end

## actual, or the failure of a mismatch when there is an expected type and it differs.
export def ensure(cx: Cx, st: St, actual: Types.Type, expected: Types.Type, span: Source.Span) -> Result[Types.Type]
  if !Types.unknown?(expected) and !Types.same(actual, expected)
    return error(mismatch(cx, st, expected, actual, span))
  end
  return ok(actual)
end

## Checks an expression through the hook, where a Void value is an error.
export def expr(cx: Cx, st: St, node: Ast.Expr, expected: Types.Type) -> Result[Out]
  return cx.expression.call(cx, st, node, expected, false)
end

## Checks an expression where a Void value is allowed (a statement, a completion).
export def expr_completion(cx: Cx, st: St, node: Ast.Expr, expected: Types.Type) -> Result[Out]
  return cx.expression.call(cx, st, node, expected, true)
end

## Checks an expression where a Void value is allowed only when completion is true.
export def expr_completion_if(cx: Cx, st: St, node: Ast.Expr, expected: Types.Type, completion: Bool) -> Result[Out]
  return cx.expression.call(cx, st, node, expected, completion)
end

## The state with the type of a node recorded.
export def record_type(st: St, id: Int, type: Types.Type) -> St
  return st.with(types: st.types.set(id, type))
end

## The state with the resolution of a node recorded.
export def record_resolved(st: St, id: Int, resolved: Resolved) -> St
  return st.with(resolved: st.resolved.put(id, resolved))
end

## The binding of a name, or an error when the name is not in scope.
export def lookup(st: St, name: String) -> Result[Binding]
  return st.vars.get(name)
end

## Opens a scope: the state to give back to leave when it is closed.
export def enter(st: St) -> St
  return st.with(depth: st.depth + 1)
end

## Closes the scope opened from before: the names, the depth and nothing else go back; types and resolutions stay.
export def leave(st: St, before: St) -> St
  return st.with(vars: before.vars, depth: before.depth)
end

## Introduces a name (a parameter, a binding, a pattern variable, a for variable) in the scope: no builtin constructor
## or function name, and no shadowing.
export def introduce(cx: Cx, st: St, name: String, type: Types.Type, span: Source.Span, immutable: Bool) -> Result[St]
  try reserve_local(cx, st, name, span)
  existing = st.vars.get(name)
  if existing.ok?
    if existing.unwrap!.immutable
      return error(
        fail_help(
          cx,
          st,
          "CHECK-SHADOWED-NAME",
          "\"#{name}\" is already visible; Agentica does not allow shadowing",
          span,
          "choose another name",
        ),
      )
    end
    return error(
      fail_help(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-SHADOWED-NAME",
        "\"#{name}\" is already visible; Agentica does not allow shadowing",
        span,
        "assign to it with \"#{name} = value\" instead of introducing it again, or choose another name",
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(st.with(vars: st.vars.put(name, Binding(type: type, immutable: immutable, level: st.depth))))
end

## CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME for ok and error, which are builtin constructors.
export def reserve_constructor(cx: Cx, st: St, name: String, span: Source.Span) -> Result[Bool]
  if name == "ok" or name == "error"
    return error(fail(cx, st, "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME", "\"#{name}\" is a builtin constructor", span))
  end
  return ok(true)
end

## CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME for the names a local may not take: ok, error, puts, print, gets and gets!.
export def reserve_local(cx: Cx, st: St, name: String, span: Source.Span) -> Result[Bool]
  try reserve_constructor(cx, st, name, span)
  if name == "puts" or name == "print" or name == "gets" or name == "gets!"
    return error(
      fail_help(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME",
        "\"#{name}\" is a builtin function",
        span,
        "choose another name, such as line or text",
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(true)
end

## The names a program may use as a value or a call, for the did-you-mean help: names in scope, functions, public
## builtins.
export def visible_names(cx: Cx, st: St) -> List[String]
  return st.vars.keys.concat(cx.functions.keys).concat(cx.catalog.public_names)
end

## A Diag.Help for a help text that may be absent ("" is absent).
export def hint_of(text: String) -> Diag.Help
  if text == ""
    return Diag.Help.NoHelp
  end
  return Diag.Help.Hint(text)
end
compiler/check_stmt.agc:
## Statements, blocks, case and functions (src/checker.rkt: check-statement, check-block-body, check-case,
## check-function). Expressions are checked through State.expr, because they are in a module that imports this one.

import Ast from "ast"
import Model from "builtin_model"
import Flow from "check_flow"
import State from "check_state"
import Types from "check_types"
import Unused from "check_unused"
import Source from "source"
import T from "types"

## What the arms of a case have covered so far: the variants named, the literals seen, and whether a wildcard arm came.
struct Arms
  covered: List[String]
  literals: List[Ast.LitValue]
  wildcard: Bool
end

# The arm after checking: the state and what the arms cover now.
struct ArmDone
  st: State.St
  arms: Arms
end

## Checks a function: its body with the parameters in scope, then that every path returns a value when the result is
## not Void.
export def check_function(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.FunctionDecl) -> Result[State.St]
  signature = cx.functions[node.name]
  here = st.with(loops: 0, result: State.Slot.Known(signature.result), signature: signature_text(node, signature))
  inner = State.enter(here)
  index = 0
  while index < node.params.size
    param = node.params[index]
    inner = try State.introduce(cx, inner, param.name, signature.params[index], param.span, false)
    index += 1
  end
  inner = try check_block(cx, inner, node.body)
  if !T.is(signature.result, "Void") and !Flow.block_returns?(node.body)
    return error(
      State.fail_maybe(
        cx,
        inner,
        "CHECK-MISSING-RETURN",
        "function \"#{T.display_name(node.name)}\" must return #{T.to_text(signature.result)} on every path",
        node.span,
        Flow.missing_return_help(node.body, T.to_text(signature.result)),
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(State.leave(inner, here))
end

## Checks the statements in order.
export def check_block(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, statements: List[Ast.Stmt]) -> Result[State.St]
  current = st
  for statement in statements
    current = try check_statement(cx, current, statement)
  end
  return ok(current)
end

## Checks the body of a block literal (do |x| ... end) against the parameter types and result type its context knows
## (Absent and Unknown when it knows none). The block's type is Fn(parameters, result), and it is recorded for the
## block's id. each_receiver is the list of a List.each call, for the help of CHECK-CAPTURED-ASSIGNMENT.
export def check_block_body(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  block: Ast.BlockLit,
  known_params: Ast.Optional[List[T.Type]],
  known_result: T.Type,
  each_receiver: Ast.Optional[Ast.Expr],
) -> Result[State.Out]
  types = try block_parameter_types(cx, st, block, known_params)
  slot = State.Slot.Infer
  if !T.unknown?(known_result)
    slot = State.Slot.Known(known_result)
  end
  inside = st.with(
    loops: 0,
    result: slot,
    capture: Ast.Optional.Present(
      State.Capture(boundary: st.depth, params: block.params, each_receiver: each_receiver),
    ),
  )
  inside = State.enter(inside)
  index = 0
  while index < types.size
    param = block.params[index]
    inside = try State.introduce(cx, inside, param.name, types[index], param.span, false)
    index += 1
  end
  done = try block_statements(cx, inside, block.body)
  result = block_result(done.st.result, done.type)
  if !T.is(result, "Void") and T.unknown?(done.type) and !Flow.block_returns?(block.body)
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        done.st,
        "CHECK-MISSING-RETURN",
        "this block must give #{T.to_text(result)} on every path",
        block.span,
        "end the block with an expression, or return a value on every path",
      ),
    )
  end
  block_type = T.Type.Fn(types, result)
  after = State.leave(done.st, st).with(result: st.result, capture: st.capture, loops: st.loops)
  return ok(State.Out(st: State.record_type(after, block.id, block_type), type: block_type))
end

# The statement checked; a nesting past the limit is CHECK-TOO-DEEP.
def check_statement(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, statement: Ast.Stmt) -> Result[State.St]
  if st.nest >= State.nesting_limit()
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-TOO-DEEP",
        "nesting is deeper than #{State.nesting_limit()} levels",
        statement_span(statement),
        "split the code into smaller functions or simpler expressions",
      ),
    )
  end
  done = try statement_inside(cx, st.with(nest: st.nest + 1), statement)
  return ok(done.with(nest: st.nest))
end

def statement_inside(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, statement: Ast.Stmt) -> Result[State.St]
  case statement
    Ast.Stmt.Binding(node) -> return check_binding(cx, st, node)
    Ast.Stmt.Return(node) -> return check_return(cx, st, node)
    Ast.Stmt.Expression(node) -> return check_expression_statement(cx, st, node)
    Ast.Stmt.If(node) -> return check_if(cx, st, node)
    Ast.Stmt.Case(node) -> return check_case(cx, st, node)
    Ast.Stmt.While(node) -> return check_while(cx, st, node)
    Ast.Stmt.For(node) -> return check_for(cx, st, node)
    Ast.Stmt.Control(node) -> return check_loop_control(cx, st, node)
  end
end

def check_expression_statement(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.ExprStmt) -> Result[State.St]
  out = try State.expr_completion(cx, st, node.value, T.Type.Unknown)
  try Unused.check_unused_value(cx, out.st, node.value, out.type)
  return ok(out.st)
end

def check_loop_control(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.LoopControl) -> Result[State.St]
  if st.loops > 0
    return ok(st)
  end
  help = "use it inside while or for; a function cannot break its caller's loop, so return a value and test it there"
  case st.capture
    Ast.Optional.Present(capture) ->
      help = "inside a block, return leaves the block (Ruby's next); a block cannot break its caller's loop"
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> help = help
  end
  return error(
    State.fail_help(cx, st, "CHECK-LOOP-CONTROL", "#{node.kind} is only valid inside while or for", node.span, help),
  )
end

def check_binding(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Binding) -> Result[State.St]
  try State.reserve_local(cx, st, node.name, node.span)
  declared = T.Type.Unknown
  case node.type
    Ast.Optional.Present(annotation) -> declared = try Types.resolve_type(cx, st, annotation, false)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> declared = declared
  end
  existing = State.lookup(st, node.name)
  if existing.ok?
    return check_assignment(cx, st, node, existing.unwrap!)
  end
  out = try State.expr(cx, st, node.value, declared)
  type = declared
  if T.unknown?(declared)
    type = out.type
  end
  return State.introduce(cx, out.st, node.name, type, node.span, false)
end

# A binding of a name that is already in scope is an assignment: not from inside a block, not with an annotation, not
# to a for variable.
def check_assignment(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Binding, existing: State.Binding) -> Result[State.St]
  case st.capture
    Ast.Optional.Present(capture) ->
      if existing.level <= capture.boundary
        return error(
          State.fail_help(
            cx,
            st,
            "CHECK-CAPTURED-ASSIGNMENT",
            "a block cannot assign to \"#{node.name}\", which belongs to the enclosing code",
            node.span,
            Flow.captured_help(node.name, capture),
          ),
        )
      end
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> existing = existing
  end
  case node.type
    Ast.Optional.Present(annotation) -> return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-ANNOTATION-ON-EXISTING",
        "an annotation is only allowed when \"#{node.name}\" is introduced",
        node.span,
      ),
    )
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> existing = existing
  end
  if existing.immutable
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-IMMUTABLE-ASSIGNMENT",
        "\"#{node.name}\" cannot be assigned",
        node.span,
        "\"for\" variables cannot be assigned; copy the value to a new name",
      ),
    )
  end
  out = try State.expr(cx, st, node.value, existing.type)
  return ok(out.st)
end

def check_return(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Return) -> Result[State.St]
  case st.result
    State.Slot.Infer -> return return_inferred(cx, st, node)
    State.Slot.Known(expected) -> return return_known(cx, st, node, expected)
  end
end

# A return in a block whose result is not known yet gives it.
def return_inferred(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Return) -> Result[State.St]
  case node.value
    Ast.Optional.Present(value) ->
      out = try State.expr_completion(cx, st, value, T.Type.Unknown)
      return ok(out.st.with(result: State.Slot.Known(out.type)))
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return ok(st.with(result: State.Slot.Known(T.Type.Void)))
  end
end

def return_known(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.Return, expected: T.Type) -> Result[State.St]
  case node.value
    Ast.Optional.Present(value) ->
      out = try State.expr_completion_if(cx, st, value, expected, T.is(expected, "Void"))
      return ok(out.st)
    Ast.Optional.Absent ->
      try State.ensure(cx, st, T.Type.Void, expected, node.span)
      return ok(st)
  end
end

def check_if(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.IfStmt) -> Result[State.St]
  current = st
  for branch in node.branches
    condition = try State.expr(cx, current, branch.condition, T.Type.Bool)
    inner = try check_block(cx, State.enter(condition.st), branch.body)
    current = State.leave(inner, condition.st)
  end
  case node.else_body
    Ast.Optional.Present(body) ->
      inner = try check_block(cx, State.enter(current), body)
      current = State.leave(inner, current)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> current = current
  end
  return ok(current)
end

def check_while(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.WhileStmt) -> Result[State.St]
  condition = try State.expr(cx, st, node.condition, T.Type.Bool)
  inner = try in_loop(cx, State.enter(condition.st), node.body)
  return ok(State.leave(inner, condition.st))
end

def check_for(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.ForStmt) -> Result[State.St]
  iterable = try State.expr(cx, st, node.iterable, T.Type.Unknown)
  type = iterable.type
  if !T.is(type, "List") and !T.is(type, "Set") and !T.is(type, "Range")
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        iterable.st,
        "CHECK-NOT-A-LIST",
        "\"for\" iterates over a list, a set or a range, found #{T.to_text(type)}",
        node.span,
      ),
    )
  end
  element = T.Type.Int
  if !T.is(type, "Range")
    element = T.item(type)
  end
  inner = try State.introduce(cx, State.enter(iterable.st), node.variable, element, node.span, true)
  inner = try in_loop(cx, inner, node.body)
  return ok(State.leave(inner, iterable.st))
end

def in_loop(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, body: List[Ast.Stmt]) -> Result[State.St]
  done = try check_block(cx, st.with(loops: st.loops + 1), body)
  return ok(done.with(loops: st.loops))
end

def check_case(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, node: Ast.CaseStmt) -> Result[State.St]
  value = try State.expr(cx, st, node.value, T.Type.Unknown)
  value_type = value.type
  names = variant_names(cx, value_type)
  current = value.st
  arms = Arms(covered: [], literals: [], wildcard: false)
  for arm in node.arms
    if arms.wildcard or (names.ok? and all_covered?(names.unwrap!, arms.covered))
      return error(State.fail(cx, current, "CHECK-UNREACHABLE-CASE-ARM", "case arm is unreachable", arm.span))
    end
    checked = try check_arm(cx, current, arm, value_type, arms)
    current = checked.st
    arms = checked.arms
  end
  if !arms.wildcard
    try check_exhaustive(cx, current, node, value_type, names, arms)
  end
  return ok(current)
end

def check_arm(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, arm: Ast.CaseArm, value_type: T.Type, arms: Arms) -> Result[ArmDone]
  case arm.pattern
    Ast.Pattern.Wildcard(pattern) ->
      body = try arm_body(cx, st, arm.body)
      return ok(ArmDone(st: body, arms: arms.with(wildcard: true)))
    Ast.Pattern.Literal(pattern) -> return check_literal_arm(cx, st, arm, pattern, value_type, arms)
    Ast.Pattern.Variant(pattern) -> return check_variant_arm(cx, st, arm, pattern, value_type, arms)
  end
end

def check_literal_arm(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  arm: Ast.CaseArm,
  pattern: Ast.LiteralPattern,
  value_type: T.Type,
  arms: Arms,
) -> Result[ArmDone]
  pattern_type = literal_type(pattern.value)
  if !Types.primitive?(value_type) or !T.same(value_type, pattern_type)
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-PATTERN-TYPE",
        "literal pattern has type #{T.to_text(pattern_type)}, but case value has type #{T.to_text(value_type)}",
        pattern.span,
      ),
    )
  end
  if arms.literals.any? do |seen: Ast.LitValue| same_literal(seen, pattern.value) end
    return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-UNREACHABLE-CASE-ARM", "duplicate literal case arm", arm.span))
  end
  body = try arm_body(cx, st, arm.body)
  return ok(ArmDone(st: body, arms: arms.with(literals: arms.literals.push(pattern.value))))
end

def check_variant_arm(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  arm: Ast.CaseArm,
  pattern: Ast.VariantPattern,
  value_type: T.Type,
  arms: Arms,
) -> Result[ArmDone]
  payload = payload_types(cx, pattern, value_type)
  if !payload.ok?
    return error(variant_mismatch(cx, st, pattern, value_type))
  end
  if arms.covered.any? do |name: String| name == pattern.variant_name end
    return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-UNREACHABLE-CASE-ARM", "duplicate enum variant arm", arm.span))
  end
  types = payload.unwrap!
  if pattern.bindings.size != types.size
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-ARITY",
        "variant pattern expects #{types.size} binding(s), found #{pattern.bindings.size}",
        pattern.span,
      ),
    )
  end
  bound = try bind_pattern(cx, State.enter(st), pattern, types)
  body = try check_block(cx, bound, arm.body)
  return ok(ArmDone(st: State.leave(body, st), arms: arms.with(covered: arms.covered.push(pattern.variant_name))))
end

# Introduces the names of a pattern; a Void payload must be discarded with _.
def bind_pattern(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, pattern: Ast.VariantPattern, types: List[T.Type]) -> Result[State.St]
  current = st
  index = 0
  while index < types.size
    case pattern.bindings[index]
      Ast.Optional.Present(name) ->
        if T.is(types[index], "Void")
          return error(
            State.fail(cx, current, "CHECK-VOID-TYPE", "a Void payload must be discarded with _", pattern.span),
          )
        end
        current = try State.introduce(cx, current, name, types[index], pattern.span, false)
      Ast.Optional.Absent -> current = current
    end
    index += 1
  end
  return ok(current)
end

def arm_body(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, body: List[Ast.Stmt]) -> Result[State.St]
  inner = try check_block(cx, State.enter(st), body)
  return ok(State.leave(inner, st))
end

# The payload types of a variant pattern: Ok and Err of a Result, or the variant of the enum the value has, with its
# type arguments filled in. An error when the pattern names another enum or no such variant.
def payload_types(cx: State.Cx, pattern: Ast.VariantPattern, value_type: T.Type) -> Result[List[T.Type]]
  if T.is(value_type, "Result") and pattern.enum_name == "Result" and pattern.variant_name == "Ok"
    return ok([T.item(value_type)])
  elsif T.is(value_type, "Result") and pattern.enum_name == "Result" and pattern.variant_name == "Err"
    return ok([T.Type.String])
  elsif T.is(value_type, "Enum") and pattern.enum_name == T.name(value_type)
    definition = cx.enums.get(pattern.enum_name)
    if definition.ok?
      return variant_payload(definition.unwrap!, pattern.variant_name, T.args(value_type))
    end
  end
  return error("no such variant")
end

def variant_payload(definition: Model.EnumDef, variant_name: String, args: List[T.Type]) -> Result[List[T.Type]]
  substitutions: Map[String, T.Type] = {}
  index = 0
  while index < definition.parameters.size and index < args.size
    substitutions = substitutions.put(definition.parameters[index], args[index])
    index += 1
  end
  for variant in definition.variants
    if variant.name == variant_name
      return ok(Types.substitute_all(variant.payload, substitutions))
    end
  end
  return error("no such variant")
end
