def variant_mismatch(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, pattern: Ast.VariantPattern, value_type: T.Type) -> String
  if T.is(value_type, "Enum") and pattern.enum_name == T.name(value_type)
    return State.fail(
      cx,
      st,
      "CHECK-UNKNOWN-VARIANT",
      "enum \"#{T.display_name(pattern.enum_name)}\" has no variant \"#{pattern.variant_name}\"",
      pattern.span,
    )
  end
  variant = "#{T.display_name(pattern.enum_name)}.#{pattern.variant_name}"
  return State.fail(
    cx,
    st,
    "CHECK-PATTERN-TYPE",
    "variant pattern \"#{variant}\" does not match #{T.to_text(value_type)}",
    pattern.span,
  )
end

# The variant names a case on this type must cover: Ok and Err for a Result, the variants of an enum; an error for any
# other type.
def variant_names(cx: State.Cx, value_type: T.Type) -> Result[List[String]]
  if T.is(value_type, "Result")
    return ok(["Ok", "Err"])
  elsif T.is(value_type, "Enum")
    definition = cx.enums.get(T.name(value_type))
    if definition.ok?
      return ok(definition.unwrap!.variants.map do |variant: Model.Variant| variant.name end)
    end
  end
  return error("not an enum")
end

def all_covered?(names: List[String], covered: List[String]) -> Bool
  return names.all? do |name: String| covered.any? do |seen: String| seen == name end end
end

def check_exhaustive(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  node: Ast.CaseStmt,
  value_type: T.Type,
  names: Result[List[String]],
  arms: Arms,
) -> Result[Bool]
  if !names.ok?
    return error(
      State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-NON-EXHAUSTIVE-CASE", "case on a non-enum value requires a final _ arm", node.span),
    )
  end
  if !all_covered?(names.unwrap!, arms.covered)
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-NON-EXHAUSTIVE-CASE",
        "case must cover every variant of #{T.to_text(value_type)} or include _",
        node.span,
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(true)
end

# The type of a literal.
def literal_type(value: Ast.LitValue) -> T.Type
  case value
    Ast.LitValue.Whole(number) -> return T.Type.Int
    Ast.LitValue.Huge(digits) -> return T.Type.Int
    Ast.LitValue.Real(number) -> return T.Type.Float
    Ast.LitValue.Text(text) -> return T.Type.String
    Ast.LitValue.Flag(flag) -> return T.Type.Bool
    Ast.LitValue.Nothing -> return T.Type.Nil
  end
end

# equal? on literals: a float matches on its bits, so 0.0 and -0.0 differ.
def same_literal(a: Ast.LitValue, b: Ast.LitValue) -> Bool
  case a
    Ast.LitValue.Whole(x) -> return whole_is?(b, x)
    Ast.LitValue.Huge(x) -> return huge_is?(b, x)
    Ast.LitValue.Real(x) -> return real_is?(b, x)
    Ast.LitValue.Text(x) -> return text_is?(b, x)
    Ast.LitValue.Flag(x) -> return flag_is?(b, x)
    Ast.LitValue.Nothing -> return nothing?(b)
  end
end

def whole_is?(b: Ast.LitValue, x: Int) -> Bool
  case b
    Ast.LitValue.Whole(y) -> return x == y
    _ -> return false
  end
end

def huge_is?(b: Ast.LitValue, x: String) -> Bool
  case b
    Ast.LitValue.Huge(y) -> return x == y
    _ -> return false
  end
end

def real_is?(b: Ast.LitValue, x: Float) -> Bool
  case b
    Ast.LitValue.Real(y) -> return Float.to_bits(x) == Float.to_bits(y)
    _ -> return false
  end
end

def text_is?(b: Ast.LitValue, x: String) -> Bool
  case b
    Ast.LitValue.Text(y) -> return x == y
    _ -> return false
  end
end

def flag_is?(b: Ast.LitValue, x: Bool) -> Bool
  case b
    Ast.LitValue.Flag(y) -> return x == y
    _ -> return false
  end
end

def nothing?(b: Ast.LitValue) -> Bool
  case b
    Ast.LitValue.Nothing -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

def block_parameter_types(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  block: Ast.BlockLit,
  known: Ast.Optional[List[T.Type]],
) -> Result[List[T.Type]]
  case known
    Ast.Optional.Present(types) ->
      if types.size != block.params.size
        return error(
          State.fail(
            cx,
            st,
            "CHECK-ARITY",
            "this block takes #{types.size} parameter(s), found #{block.params.size}",
            block.span,
          ),
        )
      end
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> known = known
  end
  out: List[T.Type] = []
  index = 0
  while index < block.params.size
    out = out.push(try block_parameter_type(cx, st, block.params[index], known, index))
    index += 1
  end
  return ok(out)
end

# The type of one block parameter: the annotation and the context agree, or one of them gives it.
def block_parameter_type(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  param: Ast.BlockParam,
  known: Ast.Optional[List[T.Type]],
  index: Int,
) -> Result[T.Type]
  annotated = T.Type.Unknown
  case param.type
    Ast.Optional.Present(annotation) -> annotated = try Types.resolve_type(cx, st, annotation, false)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> annotated = annotated
  end
  context = T.Type.Unknown
  case known
    Ast.Optional.Present(types) -> context = types[index]
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> context = context
  end
  if !T.unknown?(annotated) and !T.unknown?(context)
    if !T.same(annotated, context)
      return error(State.mismatch(cx, st, context, annotated, param.span))
    end
    return ok(context)
  elsif !T.unknown?(annotated)
    return ok(annotated)
  elsif !T.unknown?(context)
    return ok(context)
  end
  return error(
    State.fail_help(
      cx,
      st,
      "CHECK-BLOCK-TYPE",
      "the type of block parameter \"#{param.name}\" is not known here",
      param.span,
      "annotate it, as in do |#{param.name}: Int| ... end",
    ),
  )
end

# The statements of a block: all but the last are statements; the last one, an expression, is the value of the block.
# The type in the result is Unknown when the last statement gives no value.
def block_statements(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, statements: List[Ast.Stmt]) -> Result[State.Out]
  if statements.size == 0
    return ok(State.Out(st: st, type: T.Type.Unknown))
  end
  current = st
  index = 0
  while index < statements.size - 1
    current = try check_statement(cx, current, statements[index])
    index += 1
  end
  final = statements[statements.size - 1]
  case final
    Ast.Stmt.Expression(node) -> return final_expression(cx, current, node.value)
    _ ->
      done = try check_statement(cx, current, final)
      return ok(State.Out(st: done, type: T.Type.Unknown))
  end
end

def final_expression(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, value: Ast.Expr) -> Result[State.Out]
  case st.result
    State.Slot.Infer -> return State.expr_completion(cx, st, value, T.Type.Unknown)
    State.Slot.Known(expected) -> return final_known(cx, st, value, expected)
  end
end

def final_known(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, value: Ast.Expr, expected: T.Type) -> Result[State.Out]
  if T.is(expected, "Void")
    out = try State.expr_completion(cx, st, value, T.Type.Unknown)
    try Unused.check_unused_value(cx, out.st, value, out.type)
    return ok(State.Out(st: out.st, type: T.Type.Unknown))
  end
  return State.expr_completion_if(cx, st, value, expected, T.is(expected, "Result"))
end

# The result type of a block: the one it was given or a return gave, else the type of its last expression, else Void.
def block_result(slot: State.Slot, last: T.Type) -> T.Type
  case slot
    State.Slot.Known(type) -> return type
    State.Slot.Infer -> return infer_result(last)
  end
end

def infer_result(last: T.Type) -> T.Type
  if T.unknown?(last)
    return T.Type.Void
  end
  return last
end

# The text of a function's signature in the diagnostics: name(param: Type, ...) -> Result.
def signature_text(node: Ast.FunctionDecl, signature: State.Signature) -> String
  parts: List[String] = []
  index = 0
  while index < node.params.size
    parts = parts.push("#{node.params[index].name}: #{T.to_text(signature.params[index])}")
    index += 1
  end
  return "#{T.display_name(node.name)}(#{parts.join(", ")}) -> #{T.to_text(signature.result)}"
end

def statement_span(statement: Ast.Stmt) -> Source.Span
  case statement
    Ast.Stmt.Binding(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.Return(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.Expression(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.If(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.While(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.For(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.Control(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.Case(node) -> return node.span
  end
end

## The method tables and help texts of src/checker.rkt as data. Generated by tools/gen-check-tables.rkt from the
## definitions in src/checker.rkt: change them there and run the tool, never edit this file by hand (a test checks it).
## A key `Kind.name` pairs the kind of the receiver (String, List, ...) with a method name.

## The builtin module that holds the methods of each receiver kind.
export def method_modules() -> Map[String, String]
  return {
    "Channel": "Channel",
    "Float": "Float",
    "Int": "Int",
    "Json": "JSON",
    "List": "List",
    "Map": "Map",
    "Range": "Range",
    "Result": "Result",
    "Set": "Set",
    "String": "String",
  }
end

## The method names that are another builtin; `self` means the method returns the receiver.
export def method_aliases() -> Map[String, String]
  return {
    "Float.to_i": "Float.to_int",
    "Float.to_i!": "Float.to_int!",
    "Float.to_s": "String.from_float",
    "Int.to_f": "Float.from_int",
    "Int.to_s": "String.from_int",
    "List.join": "String.join",
    "List.length": "List.size",
    "List.push": "List.append",
    "String.end_with?": "String.ends_with?",
    "String.include?": "String.contains?",
    "String.size": "String.length",
    "String.start_with?": "String.starts_with?",
    "String.strip": "String.trim",

compiler/check_text.agc:
## The text form of a check, for tests. See check.agc.

import Failure from "check_failure"
import State from "check_state"
import Checker from "checker"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Paths from "import_path"
import Env from "link_env"
import LinkText from "link_text"
import Linker from "linker"
import Text from "text"
import T from "types"

## The text form of checking the file at path: the linked program of link_text with the type of each checked expression
## added at the end of its line (and, when the program has constants, a last line `constant-order ["A","B"]` with the
## linked names in initialization order) (` type=Int`, the types written by Types.debug_text) and, for a method call or
## a field access that names a builtin, ` resolved=` and what it became; or the ERROR line of the first failure. A
## failure of the checker has the notes of the diagnostic that are present,
## ` expected="..." actual="..." callee="..." signature="..." labels=[SPAN "text", ...]`, then ` file="path"`.
## tests/frontend-check-common.rkt prints the same text from the Racket checker.
export def check_text(path: String, settings: Env.Settings) -> String
  case Linker.link_file(path, settings)
    Linker.Linking.Failed(failure) -> return LinkText.failure_text(LinkText.root_dir_of(path), failure)
    Linker.Linking.Done(linked) -> return checked_text(linked, settings)
  end
end

## The ERROR line of a failure of the checker, with its notes and the file (relative to the folder of the root).
export def problem_text(root_dir: String, problem: Failure.Problem) -> String
  line = Text.diagnostic_line(
    Diag.Diagnostic(code: problem.code, message: problem.message, span: problem.span, help: problem.help),
  )
  line = (
    line +
    note(" expected=", problem.expected) +
    note(" actual=", problem.actual) +
    note(" callee=", problem.callee) +
    note(" signature=", problem.signature)
  )
  if problem.labels.size > 0
    labels = problem.labels.map do |label: Failure.Label| "#{Text.span_text(label.span)} #{Text.quote(label.text)}" end
    line = "#{line} labels=[#{labels.join(", ")}]"
  end
  return "#{line} file=#{Text.quote(Paths.stored_file(root_dir, problem.file))}"
end

def checked_text(linked: Linker.Linked, settings: Env.Settings) -> String
  case Checker.check(linked, settings.catalog)
    Checker.Checking.Done(checked) ->
      lines = LinkText.program_lines(linked, notes_of(checked)).concat(order_lines(checked))
      return lines.join("\n")
    Checker.Checking.Failed(problem) -> return problem_text(linked.root_dir, problem)
  end
end

# The order the constants are initialized in, after the program, when there are constants.
def order_lines(checked: Checker.Checked) -> List[String]
  if checked.constants.size == 0
    return []
  end
  names = checked.constants.map do |name: String| Text.quote(name) end
  return ["constant-order [#{names.join(",")}]"]
end

# The text added to the lines, by node id: the type, then the resolution.
def notes_of(checked: Checker.Checked) -> Map[Int, String]
  notes: Map[Int, String] = {}
  index = 0
  while index < checked.types.size
    if !T.unknown?(checked.types[index])
      notes = notes.put(index, " type=#{T.debug_text(checked.types[index])}")
    end
    index += 1
  end
  for id in checked.resolved.keys
    before = notes.get(id)
    text = ""
    if before.ok?
      text = before.unwrap!
    end
    notes = notes.put(id, "#{text} resolved=#{resolved_text(checked.resolved[id])}")
  end
  return notes
end

def resolved_text(resolved: State.Resolved) -> String
  case resolved
    State.Resolved.Self(type) -> return "self(#{T.debug_text(type)})"
    State.Resolved.Text(type) -> return "text(#{T.debug_text(type)})"
    State.Resolved.Inspect(type) -> return "inspect(#{T.debug_text(type)})"
    State.Resolved.Call(name, type) -> return "call(#{Text.quote(name)}, #{T.debug_text(type)})"
  end
end

def note(label: String, text: String) -> String
  if text == ""
    return ""
  end
  return label + Text.quote(text)
end
compiler/check_types.agc:
## Types in the checker: reading a type written in the source (resolve_type), the questions the rules ask of a type
## (can it be printed, encoded to JSON, decoded from JSON), and the type variables of generic enums (substitute,
## unify). These are the helpers of src/checker.rkt that do not depend on the walk of the tree.

import Ast from "ast"
import Help from "check_help"
import State from "check_state"
import Source from "source"
import Types from "types"

## The type a type written in the source stands for. completion says Void is allowed here (a result type, or the item
## of a Result or Task). The first problem is CHECK-VOID-TYPE, CHECK-MAP-KEY-TYPE, CHECK-SET-ELEMENT-TYPE or
## CHECK-UNKNOWN-TYPE.
export def resolve_type(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, ref: Ast.TypeRef, completion: Bool) -> Result[Types.Type]
  name = ref.name
  args = ref.args
  if args.size == 0
    return resolve_plain(cx, st, ref, completion)
  end
  if name == "Result" and args.size == 1
    return ok(Types.Type.Result(try resolve_type(cx, st, args[0], true)))
  elsif name == "Task" and args.size == 1
    return ok(Types.Type.Task(try resolve_type(cx, st, args[0], true)))
  elsif name == "Channel" and args.size == 1
    return ok(Types.Type.Channel(try resolve_type(cx, st, args[0], false)))
  elsif name == "Fn"
    return resolve_function(cx, st, args)
  elsif name == "List" and args.size == 1
    return ok(Types.Type.List(try resolve_type(cx, st, args[0], false)))
  elsif name == "Map" and args.size == 2
    return resolve_map(cx, st, args)
  elsif name == "Set" and args.size == 1
    return resolve_set(cx, st, args[0])
  end
  return resolve_generic(cx, st, ref)
end

## The types of several type references, in order.
export def resolve_all(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, refs: List[Ast.TypeRef]) -> Result[List[Types.Type]]
  out: List[Types.Type] = []
  for ref in refs
    out = out.push(try resolve_type(cx, st, ref, false))
  end
  return ok(out)
end

## True for Int and String, the types of a Map key or a Set element.
export def key_type?(type: Types.Type) -> Bool
  return Types.is(type, "Int") or Types.is(type, "String")
end

## True for Int and Float.
export def numeric?(type: Types.Type) -> Bool
  return Types.is(type, "Int") or Types.is(type, "Float")
end

## True for Int, Float, Bool, String and Nil, the types that == compares.
export def primitive?(type: Types.Type) -> Bool
  return numeric?(type) or Types.is(type, "Bool") or Types.is(type, "String") or Types.is(type, "Nil")
end

## True when JSON.encode can write a value of the type: primitives, Json, lists, maps with String keys, and structs of
## those.
export def encodable?(cx: State.Cx, type: Types.Type, seen: List[String]) -> Bool
  if primitive?(type) or Types.is(type, "Json")
    return true
  elsif Types.is(type, "List")
    return encodable?(cx, Types.item(type), seen)
  elsif Types.is(type, "Map")
    return Types.is(Types.key(type), "String") and encodable?(cx, Types.value(type), seen)
  elsif Types.is(type, "Struct")
    return struct_all?(cx, Types.name(type), seen, 0)
  end
  return false
end

## True when JSON.decode can read a value of the type: Int, Float, Bool, String, lists, maps with String keys, and
## structs of those.
export def decodable?(cx: State.Cx, type: Types.Type, seen: List[String]) -> Bool
  if Types.is(type, "Int") or Types.is(type, "Float") or Types.is(type, "Bool") or Types.is(type, "String")
    return true
  elsif Types.is(type, "List")
    return decodable?(cx, Types.item(type), seen)
  elsif Types.is(type, "Map")
    return Types.is(Types.key(type), "String") and decodable?(cx, Types.value(type), seen)
  elsif Types.is(type, "Struct")
    return struct_all?(cx, Types.name(type), seen, 1)
  end
  return false
end

## True for a type that has to_s: the data types. Numbers, Bool, String, nil, Json, ranges, type variables, and lists,
## maps, sets, Results, structs and enums of those. seen holds the structs and enums already being looked at
## ("Struct:name"), so a recursive type ends.
export def data?(cx: State.Cx, type: Types.Type, seen: List[String]) -> Bool
  if primitive?(type) or Types.is(type, "Json") or Types.is(type, "Range") or Types.is(type, "Var")
    return true
  elsif Types.is(type, "List")
    return data?(cx, Types.item(type), seen)
  elsif Types.is(type, "Map")
    return data?(cx, Types.key(type), seen) and data?(cx, Types.value(type), seen)
  elsif Types.is(type, "Set")
    return true
  elsif Types.is(type, "Result")
    return Types.is(Types.item(type), "Void") or data?(cx, Types.item(type), seen)
  elsif Types.is(type, "Struct") or Types.is(type, "Enum")
    return nominal_data?(cx, type, seen)
  end
  return false
end

## True when the type has a type variable inside.
export def has_variables?(type: Types.Type) -> Bool
  case type
    Types.Type.Var(name) -> return true
    Types.Type.Result(item) -> return has_variables?(item)
    Types.Type.Task(item) -> return has_variables?(item)
    Types.Type.Channel(item) -> return has_variables?(item)
    Types.Type.List(item) -> return has_variables?(item)
    Types.Type.Set(item) -> return has_variables?(item)
    Types.Type.Map(key, value) -> return has_variables?(key) or has_variables?(value)
    Types.Type.Fn(params, result) ->
      return params.any? do |param: Types.Type| has_variables?(param) end or has_variables?(result)
    Types.Type.Enum(name, args) -> return args.any? do |arg: Types.Type| has_variables?(arg) end
    _ -> return false
  end
end

## The type with each type variable that has a substitution replaced.
export def substitute(type: Types.Type, substitutions: Map[String, Types.Type]) -> Types.Type
  case type
    Types.Type.Var(name) -> return substitution(type, name, substitutions)
    Types.Type.Result(item) -> return Types.Type.Result(substitute(item, substitutions))
    Types.Type.Task(item) -> return Types.Type.Task(substitute(item, substitutions))
    Types.Type.Channel(item) -> return Types.Type.Channel(substitute(item, substitutions))
    Types.Type.List(item) -> return Types.Type.List(substitute(item, substitutions))
    Types.Type.Set(item) -> return Types.Type.Set(substitute(item, substitutions))
    Types.Type.Map(key, value) -> return Types.Type.Map(
      substitute(key, substitutions),
      substitute(value, substitutions),
    )
    Types.Type.Fn(params, result) -> return Types.Type.Fn(
      substitute_all(params, substitutions),
      substitute(result, substitutions),
    )
    Types.Type.Enum(name, args) -> return Types.Type.Enum(name, substitute_all(args, substitutions))
    _ -> return type
  end
end

## substitute for each type of a list.
export def substitute_all(types: List[Types.Type], substitutions: Map[String, Types.Type]) -> List[Types.Type]
  return types.map do |type: Types.Type| substitute(type, substitutions) end
end

## Matches the actual type against a template that may have type variables, and returns the substitutions with what the
## match learned. A variable already set must match again; a template with no variable must equal the actual type, else
## CHECK-TYPE-MISMATCH.
export def unify(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  template: Types.Type,
  actual: Types.Type,
  substitutions: Map[String, Types.Type],
  span: Source.Span,
) -> Result[Map[String, Types.Type]]
  if Types.is(template, "Var")
    previous = substitutions.get(Types.name(template))
    if previous.ok?
      try State.ensure(cx, st, actual, previous.unwrap!, span)
      return ok(substitutions)
    end
    return ok(substitutions.put(Types.name(template), actual))
  end
  if composite?(template) and Types.tag(template) == Types.tag(actual)
    return unify_inside(cx, st, template, actual, substitutions, span)
  end
  try State.ensure(cx, st, actual, template, span)
  return ok(substitutions)
end

# The type resolved when it has no arguments: a type parameter, Void, a primitive, a handle, an enum or a struct.
def resolve_plain(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, ref: Ast.TypeRef, completion: Bool) -> Result[Types.Type]
  name = ref.name
  if cx.type_params.any? do |parameter: String| parameter == name end
    return ok(Types.Type.Var(name))
  elsif name == "Void"
    if !completion
      return error(State.fail(cx, st, "CHECK-VOID-TYPE", "Void is only valid in a completion type position", ref.span))
    end
    return ok(Types.Type.Void)
  elsif name == "Int"
    return ok(Types.Type.Int)
  elsif name == "Float"
    return ok(Types.Type.Float)
  elsif name == "Bool"
    return ok(Types.Type.Bool)
  elsif name == "String"
    return ok(Types.Type.String)
  elsif name == "Nil"
    return ok(Types.Type.Nil)
  elsif name == "Json"
    return ok(Types.Type.Json)
  elsif name == "Range"
    return ok(Types.Type.Range)
  elsif cx.catalog.opaque.include?(name)
    return ok(Types.Type.Opaque(name))
  end
  return resolve_generic(cx, st, ref)
end

def resolve_function(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, args: List[Ast.TypeRef]) -> Result[Types.Type]
  params: List[Types.Type] = []
  index = 0
  while index < args.size - 1
    params = params.push(try resolve_type(cx, st, args[index], false))
    index += 1
  end
  result = try resolve_type(cx, st, args[args.size - 1], true)
  return ok(Types.Type.Fn(params, result))
end

def resolve_map(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, args: List[Ast.TypeRef]) -> Result[Types.Type]
  key = try resolve_type(cx, st, args[0], false)
  if !key_type?(key)
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-MAP-KEY-TYPE",
        "a Map key must be Int or String, found #{Types.to_text(key)}",
        args[0].span,
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(Types.Type.Map(key, try resolve_type(cx, st, args[1], false)))
end

def resolve_set(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, arg: Ast.TypeRef) -> Result[Types.Type]
  element = try resolve_type(cx, st, arg, false)
  if !key_type?(element)
    return error(
      State.fail(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-SET-ELEMENT-TYPE",
        "a Set element must be Int or String, found #{Types.to_text(element)}",
        arg.span,
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(Types.Type.Set(element))
end

# An enum (with its type arguments), a struct, or the unknown type.
def resolve_generic(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, ref: Ast.TypeRef) -> Result[Types.Type]
  name = ref.name
  definition = cx.enums.get(name)
  if definition.ok?
    parameters = definition.unwrap!.parameters
    if parameters.size != ref.args.size
      return error(
        State.fail(
          cx,
          st,
          "CHECK-UNKNOWN-TYPE",
          "enum #{Types.display_name(name)} expects #{parameters.size} type argument(s), found #{ref.args.size}",
          ref.span,
        ),
      )
    end
    return ok(Types.Type.Enum(name, try resolve_all(cx, st, ref.args)))
  elsif cx.structs.has_key?(name) and ref.args.size == 0
    return ok(Types.Type.Struct(name))
  end
  candidates = cx.structs.keys.concat(cx.enums.keys)
  help = Help.foreign(cx.help, name)
  if help == ""
    help = Help.near(name, candidates, shared_type_names(cx))
  end
  return error(
    State.fail_maybe(
      cx,
      st,
      "CHECK-UNKNOWN-TYPE",
      "unknown type \"#{Types.display_name(name)}\"",
      ref.span,
      help,
    ),
  )
end

# The type names offered as a guess for an unknown type besides the structs and enums.
def shared_type_names(cx: State.Cx) -> List[String]
  return [
    "Int",
    "Float",
    "Bool",
    "String",
    "Nil",
    "Void",
    "List",
    "Map",
    "Set",
    "Result",
    "Json",
    "Fn",
    "Task",
    "Channel",
    "Range",
  ].concat(cx.catalog.opaque.to_a)
end

# True when every field of the struct passes the test: 0 for encodable, 1 for decodable. A struct already in seen is
# true (the type is recursive).
def struct_all?(cx: State.Cx, name: String, seen: List[String], test: Int) -> Bool
  if seen.any? do |item: String| item == name end
    return true
  end
  inner = seen.push(name)
  for field in cx.structs[name]
    if test == 0 and !encodable?(cx, field.type, inner)
      return false
    elsif test == 1 and !decodable?(cx, field.type, inner)
      return false
    end
  end
  return true
end

def nominal_data?(cx: State.Cx, type: Types.Type, seen: List[String]) -> Bool
  name = Types.name(type)
  key = "#{Types.tag(type)}:#{name}"
  for argument in Types.args(type)
    builtin_void = Types.is(argument, "Void") and cx.catalog.enums.has_key?(name)
    if !builtin_void and !data?(cx, argument, seen)
      return false
    end
  end
  if seen.any? do |item: String| item == key end
    return true
  end
  inner = seen.push(key)
  if Types.is(type, "Struct")
    for field in cx.structs[name]
      if !data?(cx, field.type, inner)
        return false
      end
    end
    return true
  end
  for variant in cx.enums[name].variants
    for payload in variant.payload
      if !data?(cx, payload, inner)
        return false
      end
    end
  end
  return true
end

def substitution(type: Types.Type, name: String, substitutions: Map[String, Types.Type]) -> Types.Type
  found = substitutions.get(name)
  if found.ok?
    return found.unwrap!
  end
  return type
end

# True for a type with other types inside: the ones unify matches part by part.
def composite?(type: Types.Type) -> Bool
  return parts(type).size > 0
end

# unify for two types with the same head: the arguments pair by pair. An enum must have the same name.
def unify_inside(
  cx: State.Cx,
  st: State.St,
  template: Types.Type,
  actual: Types.Type,
  substitutions: Map[String, Types.Type],
  span: Source.Span,
) -> Result[Map[String, Types.Type]]
  pairs = parts(template)
  others = parts(actual)
  if Types.is(template, "Enum") and Types.name(template) != Types.name(actual)
    try State.ensure(cx, st, actual, template, span)
  end
  if pairs.size != others.size
    try State.ensure(cx, st, actual, template, span)
  end
  found = substitutions
  index = 0
  while index < pairs.size
    found = try unify(cx, st, pairs[index], others[index], found, span)
    index += 1
  end
  return ok(found)
end

# The types inside a type, in order: the item, the key and value, the parameters then the result, the type arguments.
def parts(type: Types.Type) -> List[Types.Type]
  case type
    Types.Type.Result(item) -> return [item]
    Types.Type.Task(item) -> return [item]
    Types.Type.Channel(item) -> return [item]
    Types.Type.List(item) -> return [item]
    Types.Type.Set(item) -> return [item]
    Types.Type.Map(key, value) -> return [key, value]
    Types.Type.Fn(params, result) -> return params.concat([result])
    Types.Type.Enum(name, args) -> return args
    _ -> return []
  end
end
compiler/check_unused.agc:
## CHECK-UNUSED-VALUE (src/checker.rkt: check-unused-value!): a value that is dropped, and could only have been used
## for itself, is an error.

import Ast from "ast"
import Model from "builtin_model"
import State from "check_state"
import T from "types"

## CHECK-UNUSED-VALUE when a value that is dropped could only have been used for itself: a pure builtin, a to_s on a
## data value, a .with. Anything else, and any Void value, is fine.
export def check_unused_value(cx: State.Cx, st: State.St, value: Ast.Expr, type: T.Type) -> Result[Bool]
  if T.is(type, "Void")
    return ok(true)
  end
  resolved = resolution(st, value)
  name = call_name(value, resolved)
  entry = cx.catalog.entries.get(name)
  if unused_result?(value, resolved, entry)
    return error(
      State.fail_help(
        cx,
        st,
        "CHECK-UNUSED-VALUE",
        "the result of #{unused_subject(name)} is not used",
        Ast.expr_span(value),
        unused_help(value, resolved, entry),
      ),
    )
  end
  return ok(true)
end

# What a method call or field access resolved to; Absent for any other expression.
def resolution(st: State.St, value: Ast.Expr) -> Ast.Optional[State.Resolved]
  case value
    Ast.Expr.MethodCall(node) -> return found_resolution(st, node.id)
    Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(node) -> return found_resolution(st, node.id)
    _ -> return Ast.Optional.Absent
  end
end

def found_resolution(st: State.St, id: Int) -> Ast.Optional[State.Resolved]
  found = st.resolved.get(id)
  if found.ok?
    return Ast.Optional.Present(found.unwrap!)
  end
  return Ast.Optional.Absent
end

# The builtin a dropped value calls: the one a method resolved to, or a call written by name. "" for anything else.
def call_name(value: Ast.Expr, resolved: Ast.Optional[State.Resolved]) -> String
  case resolved
    Ast.Optional.Present(found) -> return resolved_call_name(found)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return plain_call_name(value)
  end
end

def resolved_call_name(found: State.Resolved) -> String
  case found
    State.Resolved.Call(name, receiver) -> return name
    _ -> return ""
  end
end

def plain_call_name(value: Ast.Expr) -> String
  case value
    Ast.Expr.Call(node) -> return node.name
    _ -> return ""
  end
end

# True when dropping the value loses something: a method that resolved to the receiver, to_s or inspect, a struct
# update, or a call of a pure builtin.
def unused_result?(value: Ast.Expr, resolved: Ast.Optional[State.Resolved], entry: Result[Model.Builtin]) -> Bool
  if struct_update?(value) or yields_value?(resolved)
    return true
  end
  if !entry.ok?
    return false
  end
  found = entry.unwrap!
  return found.effects.size == 0 and !takes_function?(found) and !found.name.ends_with?("!")
end

def struct_update?(value: Ast.Expr) -> Bool
  case value
    Ast.Expr.Update(node) -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

def yields_value?(resolved: Ast.Optional[State.Resolved]) -> Bool
  case resolved
    Ast.Optional.Present(found) -> return !resolved_is_call?(found)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return false
  end
end

def resolved_is_call?(found: State.Resolved) -> Bool
  case found
    State.Resolved.Call(name, receiver) -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

def takes_function?(entry: Model.Builtin) -> Bool
  return entry.parameters.any? do |parameter: Model.Named| T.is(parameter.type, "Fn") end
end

def unused_subject(name: String) -> String
  if name == ""
    return "this expression"
  end
  return name
end

# The help of CHECK-UNUSED-VALUE: assign the result to the name the call was made on, when there is one.
def unused_help(value: Ast.Expr, resolved: Ast.Optional[State.Resolved], entry: Result[Model.Builtin]) -> String
  target = receiver_name(value)
  keeps = struct_update?(value) or resolved_self?(resolved) or (entry.ok? and keeps_first_type?(entry.unwrap!))
  if target != "" and keeps
    return "values are immutable, so this call changes nothing; assign the result, for example #{target} = ..."
  end
  return "values are immutable, so this call changes nothing; assign or use the result"
end

# The name a value is a call on, when the receiver is a plain name: xs in xs.push(1), xs.with(...) or List.append(xs,
# 1).
def receiver_name(value: Ast.Expr) -> String
  case value
    Ast.Expr.MethodCall(node) -> return name_of(node.target)
    Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(node) -> return name_of(node.target)
    Ast.Expr.Update(node) -> return name_of(node.target)
    Ast.Expr.Call(node) -> return first_argument_name(node.args)
    _ -> return ""
  end
end

def first_argument_name(args: List[Ast.Expr]) -> String
  if args.size == 0
    return ""
  end
  return name_of(args[0])
end

def name_of(expr: Ast.Expr) -> String
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.Name(node) -> return node.name
    _ -> return ""
  end
end

def resolved_self?(resolved: Ast.Optional[State.Resolved]) -> Bool
  case resolved
    Ast.Optional.Present(found) -> return self_resolution?(found)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return false
  end
end

def self_resolution?(found: State.Resolved) -> Bool
  case found
    State.Resolved.Self(receiver) -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

# True when the builtin returns the type of its first argument, so the call is a change of that value.
def keeps_first_type?(entry: Model.Builtin) -> Bool
  return entry.parameters.size > 0 and T.same(entry.parameters[0].type, entry.result)
end
compiler/checker.agc:
## The type checker (src/checker.rkt, `check`): takes a linked program and gives the type of every expression and the
## resolution of every method call, or the first problem. The declarations are registered first (enums, structs,
## variants, functions, main), then the module constants are ordered and checked, then each function is checked in
## program order, file by file.

import Ast from "ast"
import Builtins from "builtins"
import Constants from "check_const"
import Expr from "check_expr"
import Failure from "check_failure"
import Help from "check_help"
import Register from "check_register"
import State from "check_state"
import Statements from "check_stmt"
import Linker from "linker"
import T from "types"

## What checking learned: the type of each expression and block, in a list indexed by node id (Unknown for a node that
## has none: node ids are dense, so a list is faster than a Map to write and read), what each method call or field
## access resolved to, by node id (lower.rkt reads them), and the linked names of the module constants in
## initialization order (the lowering reads that too, and does not order them again).
export struct Checked
  types: List[T.Type]
  resolved: Map[Int, State.Resolved]
  constants: List[String]
end

## The result of checking: the types, or the first problem.
export enum Checking
  Done(Checked)
  Failed(Failure.Problem)
end

## Checks a linked program. The catalog is the one the linker used.
export def check(linked: Linker.Linked, catalog: Builtins.Catalog) -> Checking
  result = run(linked, catalog)
  if result.ok?
    return Checking.Done(result.unwrap!)
  end
  return Checking.Failed(Failure.unpack(result.message))
end

## A list of count slots with no type, built from repeats of at most chunk, so no runtime error escapes for a huge
## program.
export def no_types(count: Int, chunk: Int) -> List[T.Type]
  types: List[T.Type] = []
  left = count
  while left > 0
    size = chunk
    if left < chunk
      size = left
    end
    types = types.concat(List.repeat(T.Type.Unknown, size))
    left -= size
  end
  return types
end

# The context of the run: the builtin records and enums, the tables built once, and the text of each file.
def start(linked: Linker.Linked, catalog: Builtins.Catalog) -> State.Cx
  texts: Map[String, String] = {}
  for module in linked.modules
    texts = texts.put(module.file, module.text)
  end
  return State.Cx(
    catalog: catalog,
    help: Help.tables(),
    structs: catalog.records,
    enums: catalog.enums,
    functions: {},
    constants: {},
    type_params: [],
    file: linked.modules[0].file,
    texts: texts,
    expression: &Expr.check_expression,
  )
end

def run(linked: Linker.Linked, catalog: Builtins.Catalog) -> Result[Checked]
  cx = try Register.register(start(linked, catalog), linked.modules)
  try Register.check_main(cx, linked.modules, linked.root.span)
  st = State.fresh().with(types: no_types(ids_of(linked), max_repeat()))
  done = try Constants.check_all(cx, st, linked.modules)
  cx = done.cx
  st = done.st
  for module in linked.modules
    here = cx.with(file: module.file)
    for decl in module.declarations
      case decl
        Ast.Decl.Function(node) -> st = try Statements.check_function(here, st, node)
        _ -> st = st
      end
    end
  end
  return ok(Checked(types: st.types, resolved: st.resolved, constants: done.order))
end

# The number of node ids of the program, with the room the linker took for the receivers of constants (Linked.ids).
def ids_of(linked: Linker.Linked) -> Int
  return linked.ids
end

# List.repeat halts above this count (RUNTIME-INVALID-COUNT), and a program of about 5.7 MB of source has more node
# ids.
def max_repeat() -> Int
  return 1048576
end
compiler/const_walk.agc:
## How the checker reads the tree of a constant's initializer (docs/future/44-module-constants.md): the children of a
## node in source order, and the reads of other constants below it. src/constants.rkt has the same two functions on the
## Racket tree.

import Ast from "ast"

## An expression or a statement, the two kinds of node a block body mixes.
export enum Node
  Expr(Ast.Expr)
  Stmt(Ast.Stmt)
end

## The expressions and statements directly below a node, in source order. Named arguments, map entries, if branches and
## case arms are not nodes of their own here: their parts come in the place of the wrapper, which is what
## src/constants.rkt reaches by going through them.
export def children(node: Node) -> List[Node]
  case node
    Node.Expr(expr) -> return expr_children(expr)
    Node.Stmt(stmt) -> return stmt_children(stmt)
  end
end

## The start offset of a read, the key the reads are ordered by.
export def read_offset(read: Ast.ConstRef) -> Int
  return read.span.start.offset
end

## The reads of constants below an initializer, ordered by the start offsets of the reads in the source text, so the
## order does not depend on how a tree stores its parts (a map entry gives its key before its value). It walks with a
## worklist and no recursion: it runs before the checker has bounded the depth of the tree.
export def references(root: Ast.Expr) -> List[Ast.ConstRef]
  found: List[Ast.ConstRef] = []
  work: List[Node] = [Node.Expr(root)]
  at = 0
  while at < work.size
    node = work[at]
    at += 1
    case node
      Node.Expr(expr) -> found = push_read(found, expr)
      Node.Stmt(stmt) -> found = found
    end
    for child in children(node)
      work = work.push(child)
    end
  end
  return found.sort_by do |read: Ast.ConstRef| read_offset(read) end
end

def push_read(found: List[Ast.ConstRef], expr: Ast.Expr) -> List[Ast.ConstRef]
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.ConstRef(read) -> return found.push(read)
    _ -> return found
  end
end

def exprs(items: List[Ast.Expr]) -> List[Node]
  return items.map do |item: Ast.Expr| Node.Expr(item) end
end

def stmts(items: List[Ast.Stmt]) -> List[Node]
  return items.map do |item: Ast.Stmt| Node.Stmt(item) end
end

def named_values(args: List[Ast.NamedArg]) -> List[Node]
  return args.map do |arg: Ast.NamedArg| Node.Expr(arg.value) end
end

def expr_children(expr: Ast.Expr) -> List[Node]
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.Call(node) -> return exprs(node.args)
    Ast.Expr.EnumConstructor(node) -> return exprs(node.args).concat(named_values(node.named))
    Ast.Expr.Invoke(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.target)].concat(exprs(node.args))
    Ast.Expr.Construct(node) -> return named_values(node.args)
    Ast.Expr.Update(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.target)].concat(named_values(node.args))
    Ast.Expr.ListLit(node) -> return exprs(node.elements)
    Ast.Expr.MapLit(node) -> return entries(node.entries)
    Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.target)]
    Ast.Expr.MethodCall(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.target)].concat(exprs(node.args))
    Ast.Expr.Interpolation(node) -> return interpolated(node.parts)
    Ast.Expr.BlockLit(node) -> return stmts(node.body)
    Ast.Expr.Index(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.target), Node.Expr(node.index)]
    Ast.Expr.Try(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.operand)]
    Ast.Expr.Unary(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.operand)]
    Ast.Expr.Binary(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.left), Node.Expr(node.right)]
    Ast.Expr.Typed(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.target)]
    _ -> return []
  end
end

def entries(items: List[Ast.MapEntry]) -> List[Node]
  out: List[Node] = []
  for entry in items
    out = out.push(Node.Expr(entry.key)).push(Node.Expr(entry.value))
  end
  return out
end

def interpolated(parts: List[Ast.Part]) -> List[Node]
  out: List[Node] = []
  for part in parts
    case part
      Ast.Part.Code(code) -> out = out.push(Node.Expr(code))
      Ast.Part.Text(text) -> out = out
    end
  end
  return out
end

def stmt_children(stmt: Ast.Stmt) -> List[Node]
  case stmt
    Ast.Stmt.Binding(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.value)]
    Ast.Stmt.Return(node) -> return optional_value(node.value)
    Ast.Stmt.Expression(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.value)]
    Ast.Stmt.If(node) -> return if_children(node)
    Ast.Stmt.While(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.condition)].concat(stmts(node.body))
    Ast.Stmt.For(node) -> return [Node.Expr(node.iterable)].concat(stmts(node.body))
    Ast.Stmt.Case(node) -> return case_children(node)
    Ast.Stmt.Control(node) -> return []
  end
end

def optional_value(value: Ast.Optional[Ast.Expr]) -> List[Node]
  case value
    Ast.Optional.Present(found) -> return [Node.Expr(found)]
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return []
  end
end

def if_children(node: Ast.IfStmt) -> List[Node]
  out: List[Node] = []
  for branch in node.branches
    out = out.push(Node.Expr(branch.condition)).concat(stmts(branch.body))
  end
  case node.else_body
    Ast.Optional.Present(body) -> return out.concat(stmts(body))
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return out
  end
end

def case_children(node: Ast.CaseStmt) -> List[Node]
  out: List[Node] = [Node.Expr(node.value)]
  for arm in node.arms
    out = out.concat(stmts(arm.body))
  end
  return out
end
compiler/declarations.agc:
## Helpers for the top-level declarations of a parsed file, and the declaration order rule (CHECK-DECL-ORDER).

import Ast from "ast"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Failure from "link_failure"
import Source from "source"
import Base from "parse_base"

## What a top-level declaration is.
export enum Kind
  Struct
  Enum
  Function
  Constant
  Import
end

## The declaration inside an export, or the declaration itself.
export def unwrap(decl: Ast.Decl) -> Ast.Decl
  case decl
    Ast.Decl.Export(node) -> return node.declaration
    _ -> return decl
  end
end

## The span of a declaration (of the whole export, for an exported one).
export def span_of(decl: Ast.Decl) -> Source.Span
  case decl
    Ast.Decl.Import(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Decl.Export(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Decl.Function(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Decl.Struct(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Decl.Enum(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Decl.Constant(node) -> return node.span
  end
end

## The name a struct, enum, function or constant declares; "" for an import.
export def name_of(decl: Ast.Decl) -> String
  case unwrap(decl)
    Ast.Decl.Function(node) -> return node.name
    Ast.Decl.Struct(node) -> return node.name
    Ast.Decl.Enum(node) -> return node.name
    Ast.Decl.Constant(node) -> return node.name
    _ -> return ""
  end
end

## The kind of the declaration inside an export, or of the declaration itself.
export def kind_of(decl: Ast.Decl) -> Kind
  case unwrap(decl)
    Ast.Decl.Function(node) -> return Kind.Function
    Ast.Decl.Struct(node) -> return Kind.Struct
    Ast.Decl.Enum(node) -> return Kind.Enum
    Ast.Decl.Constant(node) -> return Kind.Constant
    _ -> return Kind.Import
  end
end

## True for a struct.
export def struct?(kind: Kind) -> Bool
  case kind
    Kind.Struct -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

## True for a function.
export def function?(kind: Kind) -> Bool
  case kind
    Kind.Function -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

## True for an enum.
export def enum?(kind: Kind) -> Bool
  case kind
    Kind.Enum -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

## True for a constant.
export def constant?(kind: Kind) -> Bool
  case kind
    Kind.Constant -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

## True for an import.
export def import?(kind: Kind) -> Bool
  case kind
    Kind.Import -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

## True for an export, or a constant written with export.
export def exported?(decl: Ast.Decl) -> Bool
  case decl
    Ast.Decl.Export(node) -> return true
    Ast.Decl.Constant(node) -> return node.exported
    _ -> return false
  end
end

## The text of the import line a help shows, for the path as written (quoted): the alias form, or the name list.
export def import_line(written: String, decl: Ast.ImportDecl) -> String
  case decl.alias
    Ast.Optional.Present(alias) -> return "import #{alias} from #{written}"
    Ast.Optional.Absent ->
      pieces = decl.names.map do |entry| entry_text(entry) end
      return "import {#{pieces.join(", ")}} from #{written}"
  end
end

## The alias of an import, or "" for an import list (an alias is never empty).
export def alias_of(decl: Ast.ImportDecl) -> String
  case decl.alias
    Ast.Optional.Present(alias) -> return alias
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return ""
  end
end

## True when the name starts with a capital letter, as a TYPE_NAME token does: the case rule that tells a type from a
## function.
export def type_name?(name: String) -> Bool
  return "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ".contains?(name.slice(0, 1))
end

## True for the name of a constant: capitals, digits and `_`, starting with a capital, at least two characters.
export def constant_name?(name: String) -> Bool
  return Base.constant_name?(name)
end

## The imports of a file, in order.
export def imports_of(declarations: List[Ast.Decl]) -> List[Ast.ImportDecl]
  found: List[Ast.ImportDecl] = []
  for decl in declarations
    case decl
      Ast.Decl.Import(node) -> found = found.push(node)
      _ -> next
    end
  end
  return found
end

## CHECK-DECL-ORDER, in file, for the first declaration that comes after a later group. The groups are: imports, then
## constants, then struct and enum (exported or not), then export def, then def. The span is that of the declaration
## out of place; the help names the group it belongs to. This is a style rule with no meaning for evaluation
## (src/modules.rkt, declaration-order-error).
export def check_order(file: String, declarations: List[Ast.Decl]) -> Result[Void]
  highest = 0
  for decl in declarations
    group = rank(decl)
    if group < highest
      problem = Diag.fail(
        "CHECK-DECL-ORDER",
        "declaration is out of order",
        span_of(decl),
        Diag.Help.Hint(order_help(group)),
      )
      return error(Failure.from_stage(file, problem))
    end
    if group > highest
      highest = group
    end
  end
  return ok()
end

def rank(decl: Ast.Decl) -> Int
  case decl
    Ast.Decl.Import(node) -> return 0
    Ast.Decl.Constant(node) -> return 1
    Ast.Decl.Struct(node) -> return 2
    Ast.Decl.Enum(node) -> return 2
    Ast.Decl.Export(node) ->
      case node.declaration
        Ast.Decl.Struct(inner) -> return 2
        Ast.Decl.Enum(inner) -> return 2
        _ -> return 3
      end
    Ast.Decl.Function(node) -> return 4
  end
end

def order_help(group: Int) -> String
  case group
    0 -> return "imports come first, before any constant, struct, enum or function"
    1 -> return "constants come right after the imports"
    2 -> return "structs and enums come before functions"
    _ -> return "exported functions come before private functions"
  end
end

def entry_text(entry: Ast.ImportName) -> String
  if entry.name == entry.local
    return entry.name
  end
  return "#{entry.name} as #{entry.local}"
end
compiler/diagnostic.agc:
import Source from "source"

export struct Diagnostic
  code: String
  message: String
  span: Source.Span
  help: Help
end

export enum Help
  NoHelp
  Hint(String)
end

export enum Outcome[T]
  Done(T)
  Failed(Diagnostic)
end

export def fail(code: String, message: String, span: Source.Span, help: Help) -> Diagnostic
  return Diagnostic(code: code, message: message, span: span, help: help)
end
compiler/diagnostic_json.agc:
## A diagnostic as the JSON object `--json` writes (diagnostic->jsexpr in src/diagnostic.rkt).
##
## The keys are `code`, `message`, `file` and `range` (`start` and `end`, each with a `line` and a `column`), then,
## only when the diagnostic has them, `expected`, `actual`, `callee`, `function` (the signature of the function being
## checked), `help` and `labels` (a `range` and a `text` each). The BDD driver sends it to the runner as the text of a
## file that did not compile.

import Problems from "check_failure"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Source from "source"

## The JSON object of the problem.
export def json(problem: Problems.Problem) -> Json
  fields: Map[String, Json] = {
    "code": JSON.from(problem.code),
    "message": JSON.from(problem.message),
    "file": JSON.from(problem.file),
    "range": range(problem.span),
  }
  fields = note(fields, "expected", problem.expected)
  fields = note(fields, "actual", problem.actual)
  fields = note(fields, "callee", problem.callee)
  fields = note(fields, "function", problem.signature)
  fields = note(fields, "help", help_text(problem.help))
  if problem.labels.size > 0
    labels = problem.labels.map do |label: Problems.Label|
      JSON.object({"range": range(label.span), "text": JSON.from(label.text)})
    end
    fields = fields.put("labels", JSON.array(labels))
  end
  return JSON.object(fields)
end

def help_text(help: Diag.Help) -> String
  case help
    Diag.Help.Hint(text) -> return text
    Diag.Help.NoHelp -> return ""
  end
end

# A note that the diagnostic does not have is the empty text.
def note(fields: Map[String, Json], key: String, text: String) -> Map[String, Json]
  if text == ""
    return fields
  end
  return fields.put(key, JSON.from(text))
end

def range(span: Source.Span) -> Json
  return JSON.object({"start": position(span.start), "end": position(span.stop)})
end

def position(at: Source.Position) -> Json
  return JSON.object({"line": JSON.from(at.line), "column": JSON.from(at.column)})
end
compiler/import_path.agc:
## The import path rules of src/modules.rkt that need no file system: the module file name, the std/ and pkg/ path
## check, and the path helpers.

import Ast from "ast"
import Declarations from "declarations"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Failure from "link_failure"
import Unicode from "unicode"

## The text after the last "/" of a path.
export def last_part(text: String) -> String
  parts = text.split("/")
  return parts[parts.size - 1]
end

## The folder of a file path: everything before the last "/" (empty for a name alone, "/" for a file in the root
## folder).
export def directory_of(path: String) -> String
  tail = last_part(path).length
  if tail == path.length
    return ""
  end
  if tail + 1 == path.length
    return "/"
  end
  return path.slice(0, path.length - tail - 1)
end

## Two path parts joined by one "/".
export def join(base: String, rest: String) -> String
  if base.ends_with?("/")
    return base + rest
  end
  return "#{base}/#{rest}"
end

## The path a file is stored under in the program and in the .agcb, and printed by the text forms: src/source.rkt,
## stored-source-names. root_dir is the folder of the root file. A file inside it is its path from there, with no "./";
## a file above it keeps the ".." parts ("../shared/x.agc"); a std/NAME.agc key is unchanged, and a user file under a
## std/ folder is "./std/NAME.agc". The bytes of an .agcb then do not depend on where the project lives.
export def stored_name(root_dir: String, file: String) -> String
  if root_dir == "" or !file.starts_with?("/")
    return file
  end
  from = path_parts(root_dir)
  to = path_parts(file)
  shared = 0
  while shared < from.size and shared < to.size and from[shared] == to[shared]
    shared = shared + 1
  end
  out: List[String] = []
  for index in shared...from.size
    out = out.push("..")
  end
  for index in shared...to.size
    out = out.push(to[index])
  end
  stored = out.join("/")
  # A user file under a std/ folder must not look like a standard module (the VM puts --source-root before every name
  # but those).
  if stored.starts_with?("std/")
    return "./#{stored}"
  end
  return stored
end

## The stored name of the file of a failure. The root file of a failure is the path as given (Path.resolve keeps
## links), so it is made canonical first, as the key of a loaded file is.
export def stored_file(root_dir: String, file: String) -> String
  if file.starts_with?("std/")
    return file
  end
  real = Path.real(file)
  if real.ok?
    return stored_name(root_dir, real.unwrap!)
  end
  return stored_name(root_dir, file)
end

## The file an import names: "util" is "util.agc". A path that names a file with an extension, or no module at all, is
## CHECK-IMPORT-PATH with a help that shows the fix, written as the import line of decl (the alias form or the name
## list).
export def module_file(decl: Ast.ImportDecl, site: Failure.Site) -> Result[String]
  path = decl.path
  stem = ""
  has_stem = path.ends_with?(".agc")
  if has_stem
    stem = path.slice(0, path.length - 4)
  end
  guess = without_extension(path)
  if module_name?(path)
    return ok("#{path}.agc")
  elsif has_stem and module_name?(stem)
    return error(
      refuse(
        site,
        "import paths name a module without the .agc extension",
        "write #{Declarations.import_line(Unicode.written_text(stem), decl)}",
      ),
    )
  elsif last_part(path) == "" or last_part(path) == "." or last_part(path) == ".."
    return error(
      refuse(
        site,
        "import paths name a module file",
        "write #{Declarations.import_line("\"models\"", decl)} to load models.agc",
      ),
    )
  elsif module_name?(guess)
    return error(
      refuse(
        site,
        "import paths name a module without an extension",
        "write #{Declarations.import_line(Unicode.written_text(guess), decl)} to load #{guess}.agc",
      ),
    )
  end
  return error(
    refuse(
      site,
      "a module file name has no dot apart from .agc",
      "rename the file so its name has no dot apart from .agc",
    ),
  )
end

## CHECK-IMPORT-PATH unless a std/ or pkg/ path is made of plain parts: no backslash, no empty, "." or ".." part, and
## no ":" in a part.
export def validate_library_path(path: String, site: Failure.Site) -> Result[Void]
  if path.contains?("\\")
    return error(invalid_library_path(site))
  end
  for part in path.split("/")
    if part == "" or part == "." or part == ".." or part.contains?(":")
      return error(invalid_library_path(site))
    end
  end
  return ok()
end

def invalid_library_path(site: Failure.Site) -> String
  return Failure.fail_at(site, "CHECK-IMPORT-PATH", "invalid library path", Diag.Help.NoHelp)
end

def refuse(site: Failure.Site, message: String, help: String) -> String
  return Failure.fail_at(site, "CHECK-IMPORT-PATH", message, Failure.hint(help))
end

# A name has text and no dot: "models" is a module name, "models.rb" is not.
def module_name?(text: String) -> Bool
  name = last_part(text)
  return name != "" and !name.contains?(".")
end

# The path without a final ".ext" (the regexp [.][^./]*$ of src/modules.rkt).
def without_extension(path: String) -> String
  pieces = last_part(path).split(".")
  if pieces.size == 1
    return path
  end
  return path.slice(0, path.length - pieces[pieces.size - 1].length - 1)
end

# The parts of an absolute path, with no empty part.
def path_parts(path: String) -> List[String]
  return path.split("/").filter do |part| part != "" end
end
compiler/ir.agc:
## The VM IR that lowering gives (the ir-program, ir-function and ir-instr structs of src/lower.rkt) as data. The
## bytecode writer of step 6 reads it.
##
## A function body is a flat list of instructions. A label is an Instr with the op "label" and one argument (the label
## id). The ops are the names of src/bytecode.rkt (`add-i`, `jump-if-false`, ...). Arguments are registers, label ids,
## function, struct, variant and global indexes, counts and builtin arities, in the order src/lower.rkt gives them;
## `const` takes its value in imm and `call-builtin` its name in name. `struct-with` takes dst, window and struct, then
## the positions of the changed fields (src/ keeps the positions as one list argument).

import Source from "source"
import Types from "types"

## The value of a `const` instruction. Void and Nil are the values of those types.
export enum Imm
  Void
  Nil
  Bool(Bool)
  Int(Int)
  Float(Float)
  Text(String)
end

## One instruction, or a label. file is the index in Program.sources of the file the spans are in: a Span has no file
## in compiler/, and the spans of one instruction are always in one file.
export struct Instr
  op: String
  args: List[Int]
  imm: Imm
  name: String
  file: Int
  spans: List[Source.Span]
end

## One function of the table: a declared function, a kept constant, `<start>` or a block. The span is the one of the
## declaration (the program's for `<start>`), in the file at index file.
export struct Function
  name: String
  params: Int
  captures: Int
  slots: Int
  body: List[Instr]
  file: Int
  span: Source.Span
end

## A struct of the table. decodable says that JSON.decode may build it, and types then lists its field types in field
## order.
export struct StructDef
  name: String
  fields: List[String]
  decodable: Bool
  types: List[Types.Type]
end

## One variant of an enum, with the number of its payload items.
export struct VariantDef
  name: String
  size: Int
end

## An enum of the table. The variants of all enums are numbered one after the other in table order.
export struct EnumDef
  name: String
  variants: List[VariantDef]
end

## A source file of the program, in the order the spans refer to it: the canonical path (std/NAME.agc for a standard
## module) and the text.
export struct SourceFile
  file: String
  text: String
end

## The lowered program. globals is the number of slots of the module constants. entry is the index in functions of the
## function the VM starts: `main`, or `<start>` when globals is above zero. The span is the root file's.
export struct Program
  sources: List[SourceFile]
  structs: List[StructDef]
  enums: List[EnumDef]
  functions: List[Function]
  entry: Int
  globals: Int
  span: Source.Span
end

## The instruction with no immediate and no builtin name.
export def instr(op: String, args: List[Int], file: Int, spans: List[Source.Span]) -> Instr
  return Instr(op: op, args: args, imm: Imm.Void, name: "", file: file, spans: spans)
end

## The label with that id.
export def label(id: Int, file: Int) -> Instr
  return Instr(op: "label", args: [id], imm: Imm.Void, name: "", file: file, spans: [])
end
