import Env from "link_env"
import LowerText from "lower_text"

# `agentica compiler/lower.agc [flags] ROOT...` prints the text form of lowering each root file (lower_text.agc). The
# flags are those of link.agc: `--stdlib=DIR` (the default is stdlib), `--agentica-path=V`, `--xdg-data-home=V` and
# `--home=V`, and `--burn=N`, which starts the lowering N VM calls deeper (lower_text_after).
def main() -> Void
  stdlib = "stdlib"
  burn = 0
  env = Env.process_env()
  for argument in System.args()
    if argument.starts_with?("--stdlib=")
      stdlib = argument.slice(9, argument.length - 9)
    elsif argument.starts_with?("--agentica-path=")
      env = env.with(agentica_path: argument.slice(16, argument.length - 16))
    elsif argument.starts_with?("--xdg-data-home=")
      env = env.with(xdg_data_home: argument.slice(16, argument.length - 16))
    elsif argument.starts_with?("--burn=")
      burn = argument.slice(7, argument.length - 7).to_i!
    elsif argument.starts_with?("--home=")
      env = env.with(home: argument.slice(7, argument.length - 7))
    else
      puts("== #{argument}")
      puts(LowerText.lower_text_after(argument, Env.settings(stdlib, env), burn))
    end
  end
end
compiler/lower_const.agc:
## Module constants in the lowering (src/constants.rkt: plan-constants; docs/future/44-module-constants.md 44.7). The
## functions reachable from `main` decide which constants are built, a constant read by a function that is emitted gets
## a slot, and a constant that is one scalar literal gets neither: its reads are the literal.

import Ast from "ast"
import Ir from "ir"
import Scans from "lower_scan"
import {INT_MIN, INT_MIN_DIGITS} from "lower_tables"

## What the lowering does with the constants. kept are the constants to build, in initialization order. slots maps the
## linked name of every non-literal constant that an emitted function reads to its slot of the Globals table, numbered
## in initialization order, so its size is the Globals count. literals maps the constants whose initializer is one
## scalar literal to its value.
export struct Plan
  kept: List[Ast.ConstDecl]
  slots: Map[String, Int]
  literals: Map[String, Ir.Imm]
end

## Decides which constants are built and which get a slot. The functions reachable from `main` (by calls, `&f` and the
## blocks inside, to a fixed point) decide the kept constants, then the constants those read. A slot is given to every
## non-literal constant that any emitted function reads, reachable or not, so the code of an unreachable function still
## loads. functions and constants are the declarations in program order, with the scan of each body; order is the
## initialization order of the constants (their linked names).
export def plan(
  functions: List[Ast.FunctionDecl], function_scans: List[Scans.Scan], constants: List[Ast.ConstDecl],
  constant_scans: List[Scans.Scan], order: List[String]
) -> Plan
  by_name: Map[String, Int] = {}
  literals: Map[String, Ir.Imm] = {}
  at = 0
  while at < constants.size
    by_name = by_name.put(constants[at].name, at)
    value = literal_value(constants[at].value)
    case value
      Ast.Optional.Present(imm) -> literals = literals.put(constants[at].name, imm)
      Ast.Optional.Absent -> literals = literals
    end
    at += 1
  end
  by_function: Map[String, Int] = {}
  at = 0
  while at < functions.size
    by_function = by_function.put(functions[at].name, at)
    at += 1
  end
  kept_set = kept_names(function_scans, by_function, constant_scans, by_name, literals)
  slot_set = kept_set
  for scan in function_scans
    for name in scan.consts
      if !literals.has_key?(name)
        slot_set = slot_set.add(name)
      end
    end
  end
  kept: List[Ast.ConstDecl] = []
  slots: Map[String, Int] = {}
  for name in order
    if kept_set.include?(name)
      kept = kept.push(constants[by_name[name]])
    end
    if slot_set.include?(name)
      slots = slots.put(name, slots.size)
    end
  end
  return Plan(kept: kept, slots: slots, literals: literals)
end

## The value of a scalar literal initializer: one literal, or `-` and a number literal. Absent for any other
## initializer.
export def literal_value(value: Ast.Expr) -> Ast.Optional[Ir.Imm]
  case value
    Ast.Expr.Literal(node) -> return plain(node.value)
    Ast.Expr.Unary(node) ->
      if node.op != "minus"
        return Ast.Optional.Absent
      end
      case node.operand
        Ast.Expr.Literal(inner) -> return negated(inner.value)
        _ -> return Ast.Optional.Absent
      end
    _ -> return Ast.Optional.Absent
  end
end

# The names of the constants to build: those the reachable functions read, then, to a fixed point, those they read.
def kept_names(
  function_scans: List[Scans.Scan], by_function: Map[String, Int], constant_scans: List[Scans.Scan],
  by_name: Map[String, Int], literals: Map[String, Ir.Imm]
) -> Set[String]
  reached: Set[String] = Set.new([])
  pending: List[String] = ["main"]
  wanted: List[String] = []
  at = 0
  while at < pending.size
    name = pending[at]
    at += 1
    if by_function.has_key?(name) and !reached.include?(name)
      reached = reached.add(name)
      scan = function_scans[by_function[name]]
      wanted = wanted.concat(scan.consts)
      pending = pending.concat(scan.calls)
    end
  end
  kept: Set[String] = Set.new([])
  at = 0
  while at < wanted.size
    name = wanted[at]
    at += 1
    if !literals.has_key?(name) and !kept.include?(name)
      kept = kept.add(name)
      wanted = wanted.concat(constant_scans[by_name[name]].consts)
    end
  end
  return kept
end

def plain(value: Ast.LitValue) -> Ast.Optional[Ir.Imm]
  case value
    Ast.LitValue.Whole(number) -> return Ast.Optional.Present(Ir.Imm.Int(number))
    Ast.LitValue.Real(number) -> return Ast.Optional.Present(Ir.Imm.Float(number))
    Ast.LitValue.Text(text) -> return Ast.Optional.Present(Ir.Imm.Text(text))
    Ast.LitValue.Flag(flag) -> return Ast.Optional.Present(Ir.Imm.Bool(flag))
    Ast.LitValue.Nothing -> return Ast.Optional.Present(Ir.Imm.Nil)
    Ast.LitValue.Huge(digits) -> return Ast.Optional.Absent
  end
end

def negated(value: Ast.LitValue) -> Ast.Optional[Ir.Imm]
  case value
    Ast.LitValue.Whole(number) -> return Ast.Optional.Present(Ir.Imm.Int(0 - number))
    Ast.LitValue.Real(number) -> return Ast.Optional.Present(Ir.Imm.Float(-number))
    Ast.LitValue.Huge(digits) ->
      if digits == INT_MIN_DIGITS
        return Ast.Optional.Present(Ir.Imm.Int(INT_MIN))
      end
      return Ast.Optional.Absent
    _ -> return Ast.Optional.Absent
  end
end
compiler/lower_data.agc:
## Lists, maps, enum values, structs and struct updates (src/lower.rkt: lower-list, lower-map, lower-enum,
## lower-struct, lower-update). Each is a `step`, the items computed into consecutive registers, and one instruction
## that gathers them.

import Ast from "ast"
import Ir from "ir"
import State from "lower_state"
import {MAX_CHUNK} from "lower_tables"
import Source from "source"
import Types from "types"

## A list literal. One `list` instruction gathers at most MAX_CHUNK items; a longer literal is built in chunks joined
## with List.concat.
export def lower_list(cx: State.Cx, fx: State.Fx, node: Ast.ListLit, want: Int) -> Result[State.Out]
  span = node.span
  fx = State.step(fx, span)
  saved = fx.next
  count = node.elements.size
  dst = want
  if count <= MAX_CHUNK
    made = State.target(fx, want)
    fx = made.fx
    dst = made.slot
    start = fx.next
    fx = try items(cx, fx, node.elements, 0, count)
    first = start
    if count == 0
      first = dst
    end
    fx = State.emit_at(fx, "list", [dst, first, count], span)
  else
    fx = State.alloc(fx)
    base = fx.next - 1
    at = 0
    while at < count
      size = count - at
      if size > MAX_CHUNK
        size = MAX_CHUNK
      end
      fx = fx.with(next: base + 1)
      start = fx.next
      fx = try items(cx, fx, node.elements, at, at + size)
      if at == 0
        fx = State.emit_at(fx, "list", [base, start, size], span)
      else
        fx = State.emit_at(fx, "list", [start, start, size], span)
        fx = State.emit_builtin(fx, base, "List.concat", 2, [span, span, span])
      end
      at += size
    end
    dst = base
    if want >= 0
      fx = State.emit_at(fx, "move", [want, base], span)
      dst = want
    end
  end
  return ok(State.Out(fx: State.release(fx, saved, want, dst), slot: dst))
end

## A map literal: key and value registers one after the other. One `map` instruction gathers at most MAX_CHUNK entries;
## the rest are added with Map.put.
export def lower_map(cx: State.Cx, fx: State.Fx, node: Ast.MapLit, want: Int) -> Result[State.Out]
  span = node.span
  fx = State.step(fx, span)
  saved = fx.next
  count = node.entries.size
  dst = want
  if count <= MAX_CHUNK
    made = State.target(fx, want)
    fx = made.fx
    dst = made.slot
    start = fx.next
    fx = try entries(cx, fx, node.entries, 0, count)
    first = start
    if count == 0
      first = dst
    end
    fx = State.emit_at(fx, "map", [dst, first, count], span)
  else
    fx = State.alloc(fx)
    base = fx.next - 1
    start = fx.next
    fx = try entries(cx, fx, node.entries, 0, MAX_CHUNK)
    fx = State.emit_at(fx, "map", [base, start, MAX_CHUNK], span)
    at = MAX_CHUNK
    while at < count
      fx = fx.with(next: base + 1)
      fx = try entries(cx, fx, node.entries, at, at + 1)
      fx = State.emit_builtin(fx, base, "Map.put", 3, [span, span, span, span])
      at += 1
    end
    dst = base
    if want >= 0
      fx = State.emit_at(fx, "move", [want, base], span)
      dst = want
    end
  end
  return ok(State.Out(fx: State.release(fx, saved, want, dst), slot: dst))
end

## An enum value: the payload items in consecutive registers and an `enum` instruction with the id of the variant.
export def lower_enum(
  cx: State.Cx, fx: State.Fx, enum_name: String, variant_name: String, args: List[Ast.Expr], span: Source.Span,
  want: Int
) -> Result[State.Out]
  fx = State.step(fx, span)
  saved = fx.next
  made = State.target(fx, want)
  fx = made.fx
  dst = made.slot
  id = cx.variants["#{enum_name}.#{variant_name}"]
  start = fx.next
  for arg in args
    fx = State.alloc(fx)
    out = try cx.expression.call(cx, fx, arg, fx.next - 1, false, false)
    fx = out.fx
  end
  first = start
  if args.size == 0
    first = dst
  end
  fx = State.emit_at(fx, "enum", [dst, first, id], span)
  return ok(State.Out(fx: State.release(fx, saved, want, dst), slot: dst))
end

## A struct construction: a register for each field, each value computed into the register of its field, in source
## order, and a `struct` instruction.
export def lower_struct(cx: State.Cx, fx: State.Fx, node: Ast.Construct, want: Int) -> Result[State.Out]
  span = node.span
  info = cx.structs[node.type_name]
  fx = State.step(fx, span)
  saved = fx.next
  made = State.target(fx, want)
  fx = made.fx
  dst = made.slot
  start = fx.next
  for field in info.fields
    fx = State.alloc(fx)
  end
  after = fx.next
  for arg in node.args
    out = try cx.expression.call(cx, fx, arg.value, start + info.positions[arg.name], false, false)
    fx = out.fx.with(next: after)
  end
  first = start
  if info.fields.size == 0
    first = dst
  end
  fx = State.emit_at(fx, "struct", [dst, first, info.index], span)
  return ok(State.Out(fx: State.release(fx, saved, want, dst), slot: dst))
end

## A struct update, `target.with(f: v)`: the receiver goes to the first register of a window and the new values after
## it, in the order of the struct's fields (the order of the update table of the bytecode), so one `struct-with` copies
## the receiver and overwrites those fields. The receiver runs first, then the values in source order; the register a
## value lands in does not depend on where it is written.
export def lower_update(cx: State.Cx, fx: State.Fx, node: Ast.StructUpdate, want: Int) -> Result[State.Out]
  span = node.span
  info = cx.structs[Types.name(State.type_of(cx, Ast.Expr.Update(node)))]
  fx = State.step(fx, span)
  saved = fx.next
  made = State.target(fx, want)
  fx = made.fx
  dst = made.slot
  fx = State.alloc(fx)
  window = fx.next - 1
  out = try cx.expression.call(cx, fx, node.target, window, false, false)
  fx = out.fx
  positions = node.args.map do |arg: Ast.NamedArg| info.positions[arg.name] end.sort
  for position in positions
    fx = State.alloc(fx)
  end
  after = fx.next
  for arg in node.args
    rank = rank_of(positions, info.positions[arg.name])
    done = try cx.expression.call(cx, fx, arg.value, window + 1 + rank, false, false)
    fx = done.fx.with(next: after)
  end
  fx = State.emit_at(fx, "struct-with", [dst, window, info.index].concat(positions), span)
  return ok(State.Out(fx: State.release(fx, saved, want, dst), slot: dst))
end

# Lowers items[from] up to items[stop] into consecutive new registers. A literal item needs no type check of its own:
# the list's type was checked.
def items(cx: State.Cx, fx: State.Fx, elements: List[Ast.Expr], from: Int, stop: Int) -> Result[State.Fx]
  at = from
  while at < stop
    fx = State.alloc(fx)
    out = try cx.expression.call(cx, fx, elements[at], fx.next - 1, false, true)
    fx = out.fx
    at += 1
  end
  return ok(fx)
end

# The same for map entries: the key, then the value.
def entries(cx: State.Cx, fx: State.Fx, pairs: List[Ast.MapEntry], from: Int, stop: Int) -> Result[State.Fx]
  at = from
  while at < stop
    fx = State.alloc(fx)
    key = try cx.expression.call(cx, fx, pairs[at].key, fx.next - 1, false, true)
    fx = State.alloc(key.fx)
    value = try cx.expression.call(cx, fx, pairs[at].value, fx.next - 1, false, true)
    fx = value.fx
    at += 1
  end
  return ok(fx)
end

# The index of a value in the sorted positions.
def rank_of(positions: List[Int], position: Int) -> Int
  at = 0
  while positions[at] != position
    at += 1
  end
  return at
end
compiler/lower_expr.agc:
## Expressions and calls (src/lower.rkt: lower-expression, lower-value, lower-call, lower-binary and the forms below
## them). Every function takes the register to compute into (want, or -1 for a new one) and returns the register that
## holds the value. The registers above it are free again, except the one returned when none was asked for.
##
## A method call or a field access that names a builtin is not rewritten in compiler/: the lowering reads its Resolved
## and does what src/lower.rkt does with the synthetic node in the `resolved` field of the node.

import Ast from "ast"
import Builtins from "builtins"
import State from "check_state"
import ConstWalk from "const_walk"
import Ir from "ir"
import Data from "lower_data"
import Lowering from "lower_state"
import {FLOAT_OPS, INT_MIN, INT_MIN_DIGITS, INT_OPS, STRING_OPS, VM_BUILTINS} from "lower_tables"
import Source from "source"
import Types from "types"

## Lowers an expression into the register want (-1: any). void allows a Void value (a statement, a completion); known
## skips the type check of an item whose list or map was checked as a whole.
export def lower_expression(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, expr: Ast.Expr, want: Int, void: Bool, known: Bool
) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.Call(node) -> return lower_call(cx, fx, node, want, void, false, false)
    Ast.Expr.Binary(node) ->
      try typed(cx, expr, known)
      return lower_binary(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.Name(node) ->
      try typed(cx, expr, known)
      return lower_name(fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.Literal(node) ->
      try typed(cx, expr, known)
      return lower_literal(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.ConstRef(node) ->
      try typed(cx, expr, known)
      return lower_const_read(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.Unary(node) -> return lower_unary_checked(cx, fx, expr, node, want, known)
    Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(node) -> return lower_field_checked(cx, fx, expr, node, want, void, known)
    Ast.Expr.MethodCall(node) -> return lower_method_checked(cx, fx, expr, node, want, void, known)
    Ast.Expr.Typed(node) ->
      try Lowering.require_type(cx, node.target, false, node.type)
      return lower_expression(cx, fx, node.target, want, false, false)
    Ast.Expr.TypeName(node) -> return lower_type_name(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.Interpolation(node) -> return lower_interpolation(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.Try(node) ->
      try Lowering.require_type(cx, expr, void, Lowering.type_of(cx, expr))
      return lower_try(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.Invoke(node) ->
      try Lowering.require_type(cx, expr, void, Lowering.type_of(cx, expr))
      return lower_invoke(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.ListLit(node) ->
      try typed(cx, expr, known)
      return Data.lower_list(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.MapLit(node) ->
      try typed(cx, expr, known)
      return Data.lower_map(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.EnumConstructor(node) ->
      try typed(cx, expr, known)
      return Data.lower_enum(cx, fx, node.enum_name, node.variant_name, node.args, node.span, want)
    Ast.Expr.Construct(node) ->
      try typed(cx, expr, known)
      return Data.lower_struct(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.Update(node) ->
      try typed(cx, expr, known)
      return Data.lower_update(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.Index(node) ->
      try typed(cx, expr, known)
      return lower_index(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.FunctionRef(node) ->
      try typed(cx, expr, known)
      return lower_function_ref(cx, fx, node, want)
    Ast.Expr.BlockLit(node) ->
      try typed(cx, expr, known)
      return lower_block_lit(cx, fx, node, want)
  end
end

## Lowers a call of a function or builtin by name. checked is set for the call made from a resolved method call, whose
## type check was the method call's own; tail makes it a `tail-call` (a return of a call of a function of the program).
export def lower_call(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.Call, want: Int, void: Bool, checked: Bool, tail: Bool
) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  span = node.span
  count = node.args.size
  form = Builtins.ref(cx.catalog, node.name, count)
  key = ""
  if form.ok?
    key = form.unwrap!.implementation
  end
  if key == "Task.await"
    key = try await_key(cx, node, checked, count)
  end
  builtin = key != "" and VM_BUILTINS.include?(key)
  if form.ok? and !builtin
    return error(Lowering.unsupported(cx, "the builtin #{node.name}", span))
  end
  if !builtin and !cx.functions.has_key?(node.name)
    return error(Lowering.unsupported(cx, "the call to #{node.name}", span))
  end
  if !checked
    expr = Ast.Expr.Call(node)
    try Lowering.require_type(cx, expr, void, Lowering.type_of(cx, expr))
  end
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, span)
  saved = fx.next
  fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
  base = fx.next - 1
  index = 0
  while index < count
    fx = Lowering.alloc(fx.with(next: base + index))
    out = try lower_expression(cx, fx, node.args[index], fx.next - 1, false, false)
    fx = out.fx
    index += 1
  end
  if builtin
    spans = [span].concat(node.args.map do |arg: Ast.Expr| Ast.expr_span(arg) end)
    fx = Lowering.emit_builtin(fx, base, key, count, spans)
    if tail
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "return", [base], span)
    end
  else
    op = "call"
    if tail
      op = "tail-call"
    end
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, op, [base, cx.functions[node.name]], span)
  end
  if want >= 0
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "move", [want, base], span)
    return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: fx.with(next: saved), slot: want))
  end
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: fx.with(next: base + 1), slot: base))
end

# The type of an expression must be one the VM holds, unless the item was checked with its list.
def typed(cx: Lowering.Cx, expr: Ast.Expr, known: Bool) -> Result[Bool]
  if known
    return ok(true)
  end
  return Lowering.require_type(cx, expr, false, Lowering.type_of(cx, expr))
end

# The key of a Task.await: Task.await_result when the task's result is a Result, because the VM turns a crash into an
# error value then. A call made from a method call has no type of its own.
def await_key(cx: Lowering.Cx, node: Ast.Call, checked: Bool, count: Int) -> Result[String]
  type = Lowering.type_of(cx, Ast.Expr.Call(node))
  if checked or Types.unknown?(type)
    return error(Lowering.internal(cx, "lower: Task.await has no checked type", node.span))
  end
  if count == 2
    type = Types.args(type)[0]
  end
  if Types.is(type, "Result")
    return ok("Task.await_result")
  end
  return ok("Task.await")
end

def lower_name(fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.NameRef, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, node.span)
  slot = Lowering.lookup(fx, node.name)
  if want >= 0
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "move", [want, slot], node.span)
    return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: fx, slot: want))
  end
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: fx, slot: slot))
end

def lower_literal(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.Literal, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  value = Ir.Imm.Nil
  case node.value
    Ast.LitValue.Whole(number) -> value = Ir.Imm.Int(number)
    Ast.LitValue.Real(number) -> value = Ir.Imm.Float(number)
    Ast.LitValue.Text(text) -> value = Ir.Imm.Text(text)
    Ast.LitValue.Flag(flag) -> value = Ir.Imm.Bool(flag)
    Ast.LitValue.Nothing -> value = Ir.Imm.Nil
    Ast.LitValue.Huge(digits) -> return error(Lowering.internal(cx, "lower: integer literal out of range", node.span))
  end
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, node.span)
  made = Lowering.target(fx, want)
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: Lowering.emit_const(made.fx, made.slot, value, node.span), slot: made.slot))
end

# A read of a module constant: the literal itself, or the slot of the Globals table the entry filled.
def lower_const_read(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.ConstRef, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, node.span)
  made = Lowering.target(fx, want)
  read = cx.reads.get(node.name)
  if !read.ok?
    return error(Lowering.internal(cx, "lower: constant #{node.name} has no slot", node.span))
  end
  case read.unwrap!
    Lowering.Read.Literal(value) -> fx = Lowering.emit_const(made.fx, made.slot, value, node.span)
    Lowering.Read.Slot(slot) -> fx = Lowering.emit_at(made.fx, "global", [made.slot, slot], node.span)
  end
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: fx, slot: made.slot))
end

# A type name as a value (JSON.decode(Person, text)): the name as a string, for a struct the VM can decode.
def lower_type_name(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.TypeName, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  if !cx.json_structs.include?(node.name)
    return error(Lowering.unsupported(cx, "the type #{Types.display_name(node.name)}", node.span))
  end
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, node.span)
  made = Lowering.target(fx, want)
  fx = Lowering.emit_const(made.fx, made.slot, Ir.Imm.Text(node.name), node.span)
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: fx, slot: made.slot))
end

# -9223372036854775808 is the only negative literal whose positive part does not fit an Int, so it is one `const`.
def lower_unary_checked(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, expr: Ast.Expr, node: Ast.Unary, want: Int, known: Bool
) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  case node.operand
    Ast.Expr.Literal(literal) ->
      case literal.value
        Ast.LitValue.Huge(digits) ->
          if node.op == "minus" and digits == INT_MIN_DIGITS
            return lower_min_int(fx, node, literal, want)
          end
        _ -> fx = fx
      end
    _ -> fx = fx
  end
  try typed(cx, expr, known)
  return lower_unary(cx, fx, node, want)
end

def lower_min_int(fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.Unary, literal: Ast.Literal, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(Lowering.step(fx, node.span), literal.span)
  made = Lowering.target(fx, want)
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: Lowering.emit_const(made.fx, made.slot, Ir.Imm.Int(INT_MIN), node.span), slot: made.slot))
end

def lower_unary(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.Unary, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, node.span)
  saved = fx.next
  made = Lowering.target(fx, want)
  fx = made.fx
  operand = try lower_expression(cx, fx, node.operand, -1, false, false)
  op = "neg-i"
  if node.op == "not"
    op = "not"
  elsif Types.is(Lowering.type_of(cx, node.operand), "Float")
    op = "neg-f"
  end
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(operand.fx, op, [made.slot, operand.slot], node.op_span)
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: Lowering.release(fx, saved, want, made.slot), slot: made.slot))
end

def lower_binary(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.Binary, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, node.span)
  saved = fx.next
  made = Lowering.target(fx, want)
  fx = made.fx
  dst = made.slot
  op = node.op
  if op == "dot-dot" or op == "dot-dot-dot"
    fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
    window = fx.next - 1
    left = try lower_expression(cx, fx, node.left, window, false, false)
    right_at = Lowering.alloc(left.fx)
    right = try lower_expression(cx, right_at, node.right, right_at.next - 1, false, false)
    exclusive = 0
    if op == "dot-dot-dot"
      exclusive = 1
    end
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(right.fx, "range", [dst, window, exclusive], node.op_span)
  elsif op == "and" or op == "or"
    fx = Lowering.new_label(fx)
    end_label = fx.labels - 1
    left = try lower_expression(cx, fx, node.left, dst, false, false)
    jump = "jump-if-false"
    if op == "or"
      jump = "jump-if-true"
    end
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(left.fx, jump, [dst, end_label], node.op_span)
    right = try lower_expression(cx, fx, node.right, dst, false, false)
    fx = Lowering.place(right.fx, end_label)
  else
    ops = INT_OPS
    side = Lowering.type_of(cx, node.left)
    if Types.is(side, "Float")
      ops = FLOAT_OPS
    elsif Types.is(side, "String")
      ops = STRING_OPS
    end
    left = try lower_expression(cx, fx, node.left, -1, false, false)
    right = try lower_expression(cx, left.fx, node.right, -1, false, false)
    fx = right.fx
    if op == "equal"
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "eq", [dst, left.slot, right.slot], node.op_span)
    elsif op == "not-equal"
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "ne", [dst, left.slot, right.slot], node.op_span)
    elsif op == "greater" or op == "greater-equal"
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, ops[op], [dst, right.slot, left.slot], node.op_span)
    else
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, ops[op], [dst, left.slot, right.slot], node.op_span)
    end
  end
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: Lowering.release(fx, saved, want, dst), slot: dst))
end

def lower_field(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.FieldAccess, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, node.span)
  saved = fx.next
  made = Lowering.target(fx, want)
  source = try lower_expression(cx, made.fx, node.target, -1, false, false)
  info = cx.structs[Types.name(Lowering.static_type(cx, node.target))]
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(source.fx, "field", [made.slot, source.slot, info.positions[node.name]], node.span)
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: Lowering.release(fx, saved, want, made.slot), slot: made.slot))
end

def lower_index(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.IndexAccess, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, node.span)
  saved = fx.next
  made = Lowering.target(fx, want)
  items = try lower_expression(cx, made.fx, node.target, -1, false, false)
  index = try lower_expression(cx, items.fx, node.index, -1, false, false)
  op = "list-get"
  if Types.is(Lowering.static_type(cx, node.target), "Map")
    op = "map-get"
  end
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(index.fx, op, [made.slot, items.slot, index.slot], Ast.expr_span(node.index))
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: Lowering.release(fx, saved, want, made.slot), slot: made.slot))
end

def lower_try(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.TryExpr, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, node.span)
  saved = fx.next
  made = Lowering.target(fx, want)
  operand = try lower_expression(cx, made.fx, node.operand, -1, false, false)
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(operand.fx, "try", [made.slot, operand.slot], node.span)
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: Lowering.release(fx, saved, want, made.slot), slot: made.slot))
end

# A string with #{...} parts: the first part goes to the result register, each later one to a new register that is
# joined on with `concat`. A part that is not a String is converted with `to-text`.
def lower_interpolation(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.Interpolation, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  span = node.span
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, span)
  saved = fx.next
  made = Lowering.target(fx, want)
  fx = made.fx
  dst = made.slot
  if node.parts.size == 0
    fx = Lowering.emit_const(fx, dst, Ir.Imm.Text(""), span)
  else
    fx = try lower_part(cx, fx, node.parts[0], dst, span)
    index = 1
    while index < node.parts.size
      fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
      slot = fx.next - 1
      fx = try lower_part(cx, fx, node.parts[index], slot, span)
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "concat", [dst, dst, slot], span)
      fx = fx.with(next: slot)
      index += 1
    end
  end
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: Lowering.release(fx, saved, want, dst), slot: dst))
end

def lower_part(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, part: Ast.Part, slot: Int, span: Source.Span) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  case part
    Ast.Part.Text(text) -> return ok(Lowering.emit_const(fx, slot, Ir.Imm.Text(text), span))
    Ast.Part.Code(code) ->
      out = try lower_expression(cx, fx, code, slot, false, false)
      return text_of(out.fx, Lowering.static_type(cx, code), slot, span)
  end
end

# The conversion of a value in slot to its text, unless it is a String already.
def text_of(fx: Lowering.Fx, type: Types.Type, slot: Int, span: Source.Span) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  if Types.is(type, "String")
    return ok(fx)
  end
  return ok(Lowering.emit_at(fx, "to-text", [slot, slot], span))
end

def lower_function_ref(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.FunctionRef, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, node.span)
  return ok(lower_closure(fx, cx.functions[node.name], [], node.span, want))
end

# A block: the names it reads that are in scope here are copied into the registers just before a `closure` instruction,
# which makes the function value from them; the block itself becomes a function of the table (cx.block).
def lower_block_lit(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.BlockLit, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, node.span)
  captured: List[String] = []
  for name in referenced_names(node.body)
    if Lowering.lookup(fx, name) >= 0
      captured = captured.push(name)
    end
  end
  index = fx.block_count
  fx = try cx.block.call(cx, fx, node, captured)
  slots = captured.map do |name: String| Lowering.lookup(fx, name) end
  return ok(lower_closure(fx, index, slots, node.span, want))
end

def lower_invoke(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.Invoke, want: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, node.span)
  saved = fx.next
  fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
  base = fx.next - 1
  target = try lower_expression(cx, fx, node.target, base, false, false)
  fx = target.fx
  index = 1
  while index <= node.args.size
    fx = Lowering.alloc(fx.with(next: base + index))
    out = try lower_expression(cx, fx, node.args[index - 1], fx.next - 1, false, false)
    fx = out.fx
    index += 1
  end
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "call-value", [base, node.args.size], node.span)
  if want >= 0
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "move", [want, base], node.span)
    return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: fx.with(next: saved), slot: want))
  end
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: fx.with(next: base + 1), slot: base))
end

# A closure with at most one captured register is built in the result register itself; otherwise the registers are
# copied to a window first.
def lower_closure(fx: Lowering.Fx, index: Int, slots: List[Int], span: Source.Span, want: Int) -> Lowering.Out
  if want >= 0 and slots.size <= 1
    for slot in slots
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "move", [want, slot], span)
    end
    return Lowering.Out(fx: Lowering.emit_at(fx, "closure", [want, index], span), slot: want)
  end
  saved = fx.next
  fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
  base = fx.next - 1
  at = 0
  while at < slots.size
    to = base
    if at > 0
      fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
      to = fx.next - 1
    end
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "move", [to, slots[at]], span)
    at += 1
  end
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "closure", [base, index], span)
  if want >= 0
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "move", [want, base], span)
    return Lowering.Out(fx: fx.with(next: saved), slot: want)
  end
  return Lowering.Out(fx: fx.with(next: base + 1), slot: base)
end

# The resolution of a method call, or of a field access that names a builtin: it takes the type check of the call
# itself.
def lower_method_checked(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, expr: Ast.Expr, node: Ast.MethodCall, want: Int, void: Bool, known: Bool
) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  resolved = cx.resolved.get(node.id)
  if resolved.ok?
    try Lowering.require_type(cx, expr, void, Lowering.type_of(cx, expr))
    return lower_resolved(cx, fx, node.target, node.args, node.span, node.id, resolved.unwrap!, want, void)
  end
  try typed(cx, expr, known)
  return error(Lowering.unsupported(cx, "this expression", node.span))
end

def lower_field_checked(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, expr: Ast.Expr, node: Ast.FieldAccess, want: Int, void: Bool, known: Bool
) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  resolved = cx.resolved.get(node.id)
  if resolved.ok?
    try Lowering.require_type(cx, expr, void, Lowering.type_of(cx, expr))
    return lower_resolved(cx, fx, node.target, [], node.span, node.id, resolved.unwrap!, want, void)
  end
  try typed(cx, expr, known)
  return lower_field(cx, fx, node, want)
end

# What the synthetic node of src/checker.rkt becomes. The receiver is checked already, with the type the resolution
# carries.
def lower_resolved(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, receiver: Ast.Expr, args: List[Ast.Expr], span: Source.Span, id: Int,
  resolved: State.Resolved, want: Int, void: Bool
) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  case resolved
    State.Resolved.Self(type) ->
      try Lowering.require_type(cx, receiver, false, type)
      return lower_expression(cx, fx, receiver, want, false, false)
    State.Resolved.Text(type) -> return lower_text(cx, fx, receiver, type, span, want)
    State.Resolved.Inspect(type) -> return lower_inspect(cx, fx, receiver, type, span, want)
    State.Resolved.Call(name, type) ->
      target = Ast.TypedTarget(id: Ast.expr_id(receiver), target: receiver, type: type, span: Ast.expr_span(receiver))
      call = Ast.Call(
        id: id,
        name: name,
        args: [Ast.Expr.Typed(target)].concat(args),
        piped: false,
        parenthesized: false,
        span: span,
      )
      return lower_call(cx, fx, call, want, void, true, false)
  end
end

# to_s on a value: the interpolation of one part.
def lower_text(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, receiver: Ast.Expr, type: Types.Type, span: Source.Span, want: Int
) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, span)
  saved = fx.next
  made = Lowering.target(fx, want)
  try Lowering.require_type(cx, receiver, false, type)
  out = try lower_expression(cx, made.fx, receiver, made.slot, false, false)
  fx = try text_of(out.fx, type, made.slot, span)
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: Lowering.release(fx, saved, want, made.slot), slot: made.slot))
end

def lower_inspect(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, receiver: Ast.Expr, type: Types.Type, span: Source.Span, want: Int
) -> Result[Lowering.Out]
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, span)
  saved = fx.next
  made = Lowering.target(fx, want)
  try Lowering.require_type(cx, receiver, false, type)
  operand = try lower_expression(cx, made.fx, receiver, -1, false, false)
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(operand.fx, "inspect", [made.slot, operand.slot], span)
  return ok(Lowering.Out(fx: Lowering.release(fx, saved, want, made.slot), slot: made.slot))
end

# The names a block's body reads, in the order of their first read: the walk collects every name and sorts them by
# where they start in the source, which is the order src/lower.rkt finds them in.
def referenced_names(body: List[Ast.Stmt]) -> List[String]
  work: List[ConstWalk.Node] = body.map do |stmt: Ast.Stmt| ConstWalk.Node.Stmt(stmt) end
  reads: List[Ast.NameRef] = []
  at = 0
  while at < work.size
    node = work[at]
    at += 1
    case node
      ConstWalk.Node.Expr(expr) -> reads = push_name(reads, expr)
      ConstWalk.Node.Stmt(stmt) -> reads = reads
    end
    work = work.concat(ConstWalk.children(node))
  end
  ordered = reads.sort_by do |read: Ast.NameRef| read.span.start.offset end
  seen: Set[String] = Set.new([])
  names: List[String] = []
  for read in ordered
    if !seen.include?(read.name)
      seen = seen.add(read.name)
      names = names.push(read.name)
    end
  end
  return names
end

def push_name(reads: List[Ast.NameRef], expr: Ast.Expr) -> List[Ast.NameRef]
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.Name(read) -> return reads.push(read)
    _ -> return reads
  end
end
compiler/lower_program.agc:
## The struct and enum tables of the lowered program (src/lower.rkt: user-tables, used-builtin-structs,
## used-builtin-enums, decodable-structs). The program's structs come first, then the builtin records it uses, each in
## the order of the catalog; enums likewise, and their variants are numbered in table order.

import Ast from "ast"
import Builtins from "builtins"
import Model from "builtin_model"
import Ir from "ir"
import State from "lower_state"
import {BUILTIN_STRUCTS, STRUCT_NEEDS} from "lower_tables"
import Types from "types"

## The tables, and what the lowering looks up in them. user_types maps each name in the tables to "Struct" or "Enum",
## structs gives the index and the fields of a struct by name, variants the id of "Enum.Variant", and json_structs the
## structs JSON.decode may build.
export struct Tables
  structs: List[Ir.StructDef]
  enums: List[Ir.EnumDef]
  user_types: Map[String, String]
  infos: Map[String, State.StructInfo]
  variants: Map[String, Int]
  json_structs: Set[String]
end

## Builds the tables. decls are all the declarations of the program in order. used are the watched type names that the
## program writes or whose types some expression has (a builtin record or enum is in the tables only then). type_value
## says that a function uses a type name as a value, which is when the user structs that JSON can build are looked for.
export def build(catalog: Builtins.Catalog, decls: List[Ast.Decl], used: Set[String], type_value: Bool) -> Tables
  struct_decls: List[Ast.StructDecl] = []
  enum_decls: List[Ast.EnumDecl] = []
  for decl in decls
    case decl
      Ast.Decl.Struct(node) -> struct_decls = struct_decls.push(node)
      Ast.Decl.Enum(node) -> enum_decls = enum_decls.push(node)
      _ -> struct_decls = struct_decls
    end
  end
  builtin_types = builtin_decodable(catalog)
  decodable = user_decodable(struct_decls, builtin_types, type_value)
  structs: List[Ir.StructDef] = []
  for decl in struct_decls
    fields = decl.fields.map do |field: Ast.FieldDecl| field.name end
    types: List[Types.Type] = []
    if decodable.has_key?(decl.name)
      types = decodable[decl.name]
    end
    known = decodable.has_key?(decl.name)
    structs = structs.push(Ir.StructDef(name: decl.name, fields: fields, decodable: known, types: types))
  end
  structs = structs.concat(builtin_structs(catalog, used, builtin_types))
  enums: List[Ir.EnumDef] = []
  for decl in enum_decls
    variants = decl.variants.map do |variant: Ast.EnumVariant|
      Ir.VariantDef(name: variant.name, size: variant.payload_types.size)
    end
    enums = enums.push(Ir.EnumDef(name: decl.name, variants: variants))
  end
  for name in catalog.enums.keys
    if used.include?(name)
      variants = catalog.enums[name].variants.map do |variant: Model.Variant|
        Ir.VariantDef(name: variant.name, size: variant.payload.size)
      end
      enums = enums.push(Ir.EnumDef(name: name, variants: variants))
    end
  end
  return index(structs, enums)
end

# The lookups over the finished tables.
def index(structs: List[Ir.StructDef], enums: List[Ir.EnumDef]) -> Tables
  user_types: Map[String, String] = {}
  infos: Map[String, State.StructInfo] = {}
  json_structs: Set[String] = Set.new([])
  at = 0
  for entry in structs
    positions: Map[String, Int] = {}
    place = 0
    for field in entry.fields
      positions = positions.put(field, place)
      place += 1
    end
    user_types = user_types.put(entry.name, "Struct")
    infos = infos.put(entry.name, State.StructInfo(index: at, fields: entry.fields, positions: positions))
    if entry.decodable
      json_structs = json_structs.add(entry.name)
    end
    at += 1
  end
  variants: Map[String, Int] = {}
  id = 0
  for entry in enums
    user_types = user_types.put(entry.name, "Enum")
    for variant in entry.variants
      variants = variants.put("#{entry.name}.#{variant.name}", id)
      id += 1
    end
  end
  return Tables(
    structs: structs,
    enums: enums,
    user_types: user_types,
    infos: infos,
    variants: variants,
    json_structs: json_structs,
  )
end

# The field types of the builtin records JSON.decode can build: all but those with an enum field.
def builtin_decodable(catalog: Builtins.Catalog) -> Map[String, List[Types.Type]]
  found: Map[String, List[Types.Type]] = {}
  for name in BUILTIN_STRUCTS
    types = catalog.records[name].map do |field: Model.Named| field.type end
    if !types.any? do |type: Types.Type| Types.is(type, "Enum") end
      found = found.put(name, types)
    end
  end
  return found
end

# The builtin records the program uses, and the ones those have a field of, in the order of BUILTIN_STRUCTS.
def builtin_structs(
  catalog: Builtins.Catalog, used: Set[String], decodable: Map[String, List[Types.Type]]
) -> List[Ir.StructDef]
  wanted: Set[String] = Set.new([])
  for name in BUILTIN_STRUCTS
    if used.include?(name)
      wanted = wanted.add(name)
      for needed in STRUCT_NEEDS.get(name, [])
        wanted = wanted.add(needed)
      end
    end
  end
  found: List[Ir.StructDef] = []
  for name in BUILTIN_STRUCTS
    if wanted.include?(name)
      fields = catalog.records[name].map do |field: Model.Named| field.name end
      types: List[Types.Type] = []
      if decodable.has_key?(name)
        types = decodable[name]
      end
      found = found.push(Ir.StructDef(name: name, fields: fields, decodable: decodable.has_key?(name), types: types))
    end
  end
  return found
end

# The user structs JSON.decode can build, with their field types: every field is an Int, Float, Bool or String, or a
# List or a Map from String of such a type or of a struct that can be built itself. Only looked for when some function
# uses a type name as a value.
def user_decodable(
  structs: List[Ast.StructDecl], builtin: Map[String, List[Types.Type]], type_value: Bool
) -> Map[String, List[Types.Type]]
  if !type_value
    return {}
  end
  names: Set[String] = Set.new(BUILTIN_STRUCTS)
  for decl in structs
    names = names.add(decl.name)
  end
  table = builtin
  for decl in structs
    types: List[Types.Type] = []
    complete = true
    for field in decl.fields
      found = json_field_type(field.type, names)
      case found
        Ast.Optional.Present(type) -> types = types.push(type)
        Ast.Optional.Absent -> complete = false
      end
    end
    if complete
      table = table.put(decl.name, types)
    end
  end
  size = table.size + 1
  while table.size < size
    size = table.size
    kept: Map[String, List[Types.Type]] = {}
    for name in table.keys
      if references_known?(table[name], table)
        kept = kept.put(name, table[name])
      end
    end
    table = kept
  end
  return table
end

# True when every struct a list of field types names is in the table.
def references_known?(types: List[Types.Type], table: Map[String, List[Types.Type]]) -> Bool
  for type in types
    for name in struct_names_in(type)
      if !table.has_key?(name)
        return false
      end
    end
  end
  return true
end

# The struct a field type is made of, under any List or Map around it.
def struct_names_in(type: Types.Type) -> List[String]
  case type
    Types.Type.Struct(name) -> return [name]
    Types.Type.List(item) -> return struct_names_in(item)
    Types.Type.Map(key, value) -> return struct_names_in(value)
    _ -> return []
  end
end

# The type of a struct field as JSON.decode builds it, or Absent when it cannot.
def json_field_type(ref: Ast.TypeRef, names: Set[String]) -> Ast.Optional[Types.Type]
  args = ref.args
  if args.size == 0 and ref.name == "Int"
    return Ast.Optional.Present(Types.Type.Int)
  elsif args.size == 0 and ref.name == "Float"
    return Ast.Optional.Present(Types.Type.Float)
  elsif args.size == 0 and ref.name == "Bool"
    return Ast.Optional.Present(Types.Type.Bool)
  elsif args.size == 0 and ref.name == "String"
    return Ast.Optional.Present(Types.Type.String)
  elsif ref.name == "List" and args.size == 1
    item = json_field_type(args[0], names)
    case item
      Ast.Optional.Present(type) -> return Ast.Optional.Present(Types.Type.List(type))
      Ast.Optional.Absent -> return Ast.Optional.Absent
    end
  elsif ref.name == "Map" and args.size == 2 and args[0].name == "String" and args[0].args.size == 0
    value = json_field_type(args[1], names)
    case value
      Ast.Optional.Present(type) -> return Ast.Optional.Present(Types.Type.Map(Types.Type.String, type))
      Ast.Optional.Absent -> return Ast.Optional.Absent
    end
  elsif args.size == 0 and names.include?(ref.name)
    return Ast.Optional.Present(Types.Type.Struct(ref.name))
  end
  return Ast.Optional.Absent
end
compiler/lower_scan.agc:
## What lowering reads off the tree before it lowers anything (src/lower.rkt: walk-ast, names-below,
## has-type-expression?; src/constants.rkt: names-below): the module constants, the functions and the watched type
## names a body mentions. One walk per body, with a worklist, so the depth of the tree does not matter.

import Ast from "ast"
import ConstWalk from "const_walk"

## What a body mentions. consts are the linked names of the constants it reads and calls the names of the functions it
## calls or takes with `&`, in the order found. written are the watched type names it writes (a type, a type used as a
## value, an enum constructor, a pattern), and type_value says that it uses a type name as a value (JSON.decode(Person,
## ...)).
export struct Scan
  consts: List[String]
  calls: List[String]
  written: List[String]
  type_value: Bool
end

## The scan of the statements of a function body, and of the types it writes.
export def scan_body(body: List[Ast.Stmt], watched: Set[String]) -> Scan
  work: List[ConstWalk.Node] = body.map do |stmt: Ast.Stmt| ConstWalk.Node.Stmt(stmt) end
  return walk(work, watched, empty())
end

## The scan of the initializer of a constant.
export def scan_value(value: Ast.Expr, watched: Set[String]) -> Scan
  return walk([ConstWalk.Node.Expr(value)], watched, empty())
end

## The watched names a type annotation writes, nested names included.
export def written_in(ref: Ast.TypeRef, watched: Set[String]) -> List[String]
  found: List[String] = []
  if watched.include?(ref.name)
    found = [ref.name]
  end
  for arg in ref.args
    found = found.concat(written_in(arg, watched))
  end
  return found
end

## The watched names the signature of a function writes: its parameters and result.
export def written_signature(decl: Ast.FunctionDecl, watched: Set[String]) -> List[String]
  found = written_in(decl.result, watched)
  for param in decl.params
    found = found.concat(written_in(param.type, watched))
  end
  return found
end

def empty() -> Scan
  return Scan(consts: [], calls: [], written: [], type_value: false)
end

def walk(start: List[ConstWalk.Node], watched: Set[String], first: Scan) -> Scan
  work = start
  found = first
  at = 0
  while at < work.size
    node = work[at]
    at += 1
    case node
      ConstWalk.Node.Expr(expr) -> found = see_expr(found, expr, watched)
      ConstWalk.Node.Stmt(stmt) -> found = see_stmt(found, stmt, watched)
    end
    work = work.concat(ConstWalk.children(node))
  end
  return found
end

def see_expr(found: Scan, expr: Ast.Expr, watched: Set[String]) -> Scan
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.ConstRef(node) -> return found.with(consts: found.consts.push(node.name))
    Ast.Expr.Call(node) -> return found.with(calls: found.calls.push(node.name))
    Ast.Expr.FunctionRef(node) -> return found.with(calls: found.calls.push(node.name))
    Ast.Expr.TypeName(node) -> return found.with(written: named(found.written, node.name, watched), type_value: true)
    Ast.Expr.EnumConstructor(node) -> return found.with(written: named(found.written, node.enum_name, watched))
    Ast.Expr.BlockLit(node) -> return found.with(written: block_types(found.written, node, watched))
    _ -> return found
  end
end

def see_stmt(found: Scan, stmt: Ast.Stmt, watched: Set[String]) -> Scan
  case stmt
    Ast.Stmt.Binding(node) -> return found.with(written: optional_type(found.written, node.type, watched))
    Ast.Stmt.Case(node) -> return found.with(written: arm_names(found.written, node.arms, watched))
    _ -> return found
  end
end

def named(written: List[String], name: String, watched: Set[String]) -> List[String]
  if watched.include?(name)
    return written.push(name)
  end
  return written
end

def optional_type(written: List[String], type: Ast.Optional[Ast.TypeRef], watched: Set[String]) -> List[String]
  case type
    Ast.Optional.Present(ref) -> return written.concat(written_in(ref, watched))
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return written
  end
end

def block_types(written: List[String], node: Ast.BlockLit, watched: Set[String]) -> List[String]
  for param in node.params
    written = optional_type(written, param.type, watched)
  end
  return written
end

def arm_names(written: List[String], arms: List[Ast.CaseArm], watched: Set[String]) -> List[String]
  for arm in arms
    case arm.pattern
      Ast.Pattern.Variant(pattern) -> written = named(written, pattern.enum_name, watched)
      _ -> written = written
    end
  end
  return written
end
compiler/lower_state.agc:
## The state of the lowering (src/lower.rkt has it as mutable variables inside `lower` and `lower-function`): what is
## fixed for the run (Cx), what changes while one function is lowered (Fx), and the small operations on them that every
## part of the lowering uses. A lowering function takes Cx and Fx and returns the new Fx with its register (Out), or
## fails with a packed LOWER- diagnostic (check_failure.agc), so `try` stops at the first one.

import Ast from "ast"
import Builtins from "builtins"
import Failure from "check_failure"
import State from "check_state"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Ir from "ir"
import Source from "source"
import Types from "types"

## A struct of the program as the lowering reads it: its index in the struct table, its fields in order, and the
## position of each field.
export struct StructInfo
  index: Int
  fields: List[String]
  positions: Map[String, Int]
end

## What a read of a module constant becomes: the literal itself, or a read of the slot of the Globals table.
export enum Read
  Literal(Ir.Imm)
  Slot(Int)
end

## What is fixed while the program is lowered. types and resolved are those of the checker. user_types maps a struct or
## enum name (the program's and the builtin ones it uses) to "Struct" or "Enum"; structs the struct info by name;
## variants the id of "Enum.Variant"; json_structs the structs JSON.decode may build; functions the index of each
## declared function; reads what a constant read becomes. file is the file of the function being lowered and index its
## position in the sources. expression lowers an expression, and block lowers a block as a function: the cycles between
## expressions, statements and blocks go through these two fields, because a module cannot import one that imports it.
export struct Cx
  types: List[Types.Type]
  resolved: Map[Int, State.Resolved]
  catalog: Builtins.Catalog
  user_types: Map[String, String]
  structs: Map[String, StructInfo]
  variants: Map[String, Int]
  json_structs: Set[String]
  functions: Map[String, Int]
  reads: Map[String, Read]
  file: String
  index: Int
  expression: Fn[Cx, Fx, Ast.Expr, Int, Bool, Bool, Result[Out]]
  block: Fn[Cx, Fx, Ast.BlockLit, List[String], Result[Fx]]
end

## What changes while a function is lowered: the code so far (in order), the next free register and the highest one
## used, the names in scope with their registers (one persistent Map: a scope is a snapshot of it), the number of
## labels made, the labels `next` and `break` jump to (-1 outside a loop), the instructions to put after the next
## statement's `step` (the read of the element of a `for`), the file index of the instructions, and, shared with the
## blocks lowered inside it, the block functions made so far by function index and the next function index.
export struct Fx
  code: List[Ir.Instr]
  next: Int
  high: Int
  vars: Map[String, Int]
  labels: Int
  loop_next: Int
  loop_exit: Int
  pending: List[Ir.Instr]
  file: Int
  blocks: Map[Int, Ir.Function]
  block_count: Int
end

## The result of lowering an expression: the new state and the register that holds the value.
export struct Out
  fx: Fx
  slot: Int
end

## The state at the start of a function in file index: nothing emitted, no names, no registers.
export def fresh(file: Int, blocks: Map[Int, Ir.Function], block_count: Int) -> Fx
  return Fx(
    code: [], next: 0, high: 0, vars: {}, labels: 0, loop_next: -1, loop_exit: -1, pending: [], file: file,
    blocks: blocks, block_count: block_count
  )
end

## The failure of a form the VM does not support: LOWER-UNSUPPORTED "the VM does not support WHAT yet".
export def unsupported(cx: Cx, what: String, span: Source.Span) -> String
  message = "the VM does not support #{what} yet"
  return Failure.pack(Failure.problem(cx.file, "", "LOWER-UNSUPPORTED", message, span, Diag.Help.NoHelp))
end

## The failure for a program the lowering cannot make sense of (an exception in src/lower.rkt).
export def internal(cx: Cx, message: String, span: Source.Span) -> String
  return Failure.pack(Failure.problem(cx.file, "", "LOWER-INTERNAL", message, span, Diag.Help.NoHelp))
end

## The state with an instruction emitted. The spans are those the VM reports an error or a stack frame at.
export def emit(fx: Fx, op: String, args: List[Int], spans: List[Source.Span]) -> Fx
  return fx.with(code: fx.code.push(Ir.instr(op, args, fx.file, spans)))
end

## The state with an instruction that has one span.
export def emit_at(fx: Fx, op: String, args: List[Int], span: Source.Span) -> Fx
  return fx.with(code: fx.code.push(Ir.instr(op, args, fx.file, [span])))
end

## The state with a `step` for a node.
export def step(fx: Fx, span: Source.Span) -> Fx
  return fx.with(code: fx.code.push(Ir.instr("step", [], fx.file, [span])))
end

## The state with a `const` of a value.
export def emit_const(fx: Fx, dst: Int, value: Ir.Imm, span: Source.Span) -> Fx
  made = Ir.Instr(op: "const", args: [dst], imm: value, name: "", file: fx.file, spans: [span])
  return fx.with(code: fx.code.push(made))
end

## The state with a `call-builtin` of a name and the number of its arguments. spans is the call's span and then each
## argument's.
export def emit_builtin(fx: Fx, base: Int, name: String, count: Int, spans: List[Source.Span]) -> Fx
  made = Ir.Instr(op: "call-builtin", args: [base, count], imm: Ir.Imm.Void, name: name, file: fx.file, spans: spans)
  return fx.with(code: fx.code.push(made))
end

## The state with a label placed here.
export def place(fx: Fx, id: Int) -> Fx
  return fx.with(code: fx.code.push(Ir.label(id, fx.file)))
end

## The state with a new label id; the id is labels - 1 of the result.
export def new_label(fx: Fx) -> Fx
  return fx.with(labels: fx.labels + 1)
end

## The state with one more register taken; the register is next - 1 of the result.
export def alloc(fx: Fx) -> Fx
  next = fx.next + 1
  high = fx.high
  if next > high
    high = next
  end
  return fx.with(next: next, high: high)
end

## The register to compute into: want when there is one (a register of 0 or more), else a new one.
export def target(fx: Fx, want: Int) -> Out
  if want >= 0
    return Out(fx: fx, slot: want)
  end
  taken = alloc(fx)
  return Out(fx: taken, slot: taken.next - 1)
end

## The state after a value is in dst: the registers go back to saved when the caller gave a register to fill (want),
## else only dst stays taken.
export def release(fx: Fx, saved: Int, want: Int, dst: Int) -> Fx
  if want >= 0
    return fx.with(next: saved)
  end
  return fx.with(next: dst + 1)
end

## The register of a name in scope, or -1.
export def lookup(fx: Fx, name: String) -> Int
  return fx.vars.get(name, -1)
end

## The type the checker recorded for an expression (Unknown when none).
export def type_of(cx: Cx, expr: Ast.Expr) -> Types.Type
  return cx.types[Ast.expr_id(expr)]
end

## The type of an expression, or the type a TypedTarget carries.
export def static_type(cx: Cx, expr: Ast.Expr) -> Types.Type
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.Typed(node) -> return node.type
    _ -> return type_of(cx, expr)
  end
end

## True when the VM has a representation for values of the type (vm-type? of src/lower.rkt).
export def vm_type?(cx: Cx, type: Types.Type) -> Bool
  case type
    Types.Type.List(item) -> return vm_type?(cx, item)
    Types.Type.Map(key, value) -> return vm_type?(cx, value)
    Types.Type.Set(item) -> return true
    Types.Type.Result(item) -> return Types.is(item, "Void") or vm_type?(cx, item)
    Types.Type.Task(item) -> return Types.is(item, "Void") or vm_type?(cx, item)
    Types.Type.Channel(item) -> return vm_type?(cx, item)
    Types.Type.Struct(name) -> return cx.user_types.get(name, "") == "Struct"
    Types.Type.Enum(name, args) -> return cx.user_types.get(name, "") == "Enum"
    Types.Type.Fn(params, result) -> return fn_type?(cx, params, result)
    Types.Type.Opaque(name) -> return cx.catalog.opaque.include?(name)
    Types.Type.Int -> return true
    Types.Type.Float -> return true
    Types.Type.Bool -> return true
    Types.Type.Nil -> return true
    Types.Type.String -> return true
    Types.Type.Range -> return true
    Types.Type.Json -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

## Fails with LOWER-UNSUPPORTED unless the expression has a type the VM can hold. void allows Void; type is the type to
## test (the checker's, or a TypedTarget's).
export def require_type(cx: Cx, expr: Ast.Expr, void: Bool, type: Types.Type) -> Result[Bool]
  if vm_type?(cx, type) or (void and Types.is(type, "Void"))
    return ok(true)
  end
  what = "this expression"
  if !Types.unknown?(type)
    what = "values of type #{Types.to_text(type)}"
  end
  return error(unsupported(cx, what, Ast.expr_span(expr)))
end

def fn_type?(cx: Cx, params: List[Types.Type], result: Types.Type) -> Bool
  for param in params
    if !vm_type?(cx, param)
      return false
    end
  end
  return Types.is(result, "Void") or vm_type?(cx, result)
end
compiler/lower_stmt.agc:
## Statements, loops, case and functions (src/lower.rkt: lower-function, lower-block, lower-statement,
## lower-range-for). Expressions are lowered through lower_expr.agc. A block literal becomes a function through
## lower_block_function, which Cx.block points to.

import Ast from "ast"
import Builtins from "builtins"
import Paths from "import_path"
import Ir from "ir"
import Expr from "lower_expr"
import Lowering from "lower_state"
import {INT_MIN, INT_MIN_DIGITS} from "lower_tables"
import Source from "source"
import Types from "types"

## A lowered function, and the state after it: the block functions made inside it and the next function index, for the
## program to collect.
export struct Built
  function: Ir.Function
  fx: Lowering.Fx
end

## Lowers a function. fx is fresh (Lowering.fresh) for the file of the function; the parameters take the first
## registers and the captured names of a block the ones after them. A block gives its last expression statement as its
## value; any other function ends with a Void return.
export def lower_function(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, name: String, params: List[String], captures: List[String],
  statements: List[Ast.Stmt], span: Source.Span, block: Bool
) -> Result[Built]
  for param in params
    fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
    fx = fx.with(vars: fx.vars.put(param, fx.next - 1))
  end
  count = fx.next
  for capture in captures
    fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
    fx = fx.with(vars: fx.vars.put(capture, fx.next - 1))
  end
  last = statements.size - 1
  if block and last >= 0 and final_expression?(statements[last])
    fx = try lower_block(cx, fx, statements.take(last))
    final = final_value(statements[last])
    final_span = statement_span(statements[last])
    fx = Lowering.step(fx, final_span)
    out = try Expr.lower_expression(cx, fx, final, -1, true, false)
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(out.fx, "return", [out.slot], final_span)
  else
    fx = try lower_block(cx, fx, statements)
    fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
    slot = fx.next - 1
    fx = Lowering.emit_const(fx, slot, Ir.Imm.Void, span)
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "return", [slot], span)
  end
  made = Ir.Function(
    name: name,
    params: count,
    captures: captures.size,
    slots: fx.high,
    body: fx.code,
    file: fx.file,
    span: span,
  )
  return ok(Built(function: made, fx: fx))
end

## Lowers a block literal as a function of the table (Cx.block). The block takes the next function index before its
## body is lowered, so the blocks inside it come after it, as in src/lower.rkt. The state it gives back is the
## caller's, with the blocks and the index count updated.
export def lower_block_function(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.BlockLit, captured: List[String]
) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  index = fx.block_count
  name = "block@#{Paths.last_part(cx.file)}:#{node.span.start.line}:#{node.span.start.column}"
  params = node.params.map do |param: Ast.BlockParam| param.name end
  inner = Lowering.fresh(cx.index, fx.blocks, index + 1)
  built = try lower_function(cx, inner, name, params, captured, node.body, node.span, true)
  return ok(fx.with(blocks: built.fx.blocks.put(index, built.function), block_count: built.fx.block_count))
end

# The statements in order.
def lower_block(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, statements: List[Ast.Stmt]) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  for statement in statements
    fx = try lower_statement(cx, fx, statement)
  end
  return ok(fx)
end

# A statement: its `step`, the instructions the loop above it asked for after the step, then its own code.
def lower_statement(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, statement: Ast.Stmt) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  span = statement_span(statement)
  saved = fx.next
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, span)
  if fx.pending.size > 0
    for item in fx.pending
      fx = fx.with(code: fx.code.push(item))
    end
    fx = fx.with(pending: [])
  end
  case statement
    Ast.Stmt.Binding(node) -> return lower_binding(cx, fx, node, saved)
    Ast.Stmt.Return(node) -> return lower_return(cx, fx, node, saved)
    Ast.Stmt.Expression(node) ->
      out = try Expr.lower_expression(cx, fx, node.value, -1, true, false)
      return ok(out.fx.with(next: saved))
    Ast.Stmt.If(node) -> return lower_if(cx, fx, node, saved)
    Ast.Stmt.While(node) -> return lower_while(cx, fx, node, saved)
    Ast.Stmt.Control(node) -> return lower_control(cx, fx, node)
    Ast.Stmt.For(node) -> return lower_for(cx, fx, node, saved)
    Ast.Stmt.Case(node) -> return lower_case(cx, fx, node, saved)
  end
end

# A new name takes the register its value is computed in; an assignment to a name in scope computes the value anywhere
# and moves it.
def lower_binding(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.Binding, saved: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  existing = Lowering.lookup(fx, node.name)
  if existing >= 0
    out = try Expr.lower_expression(cx, fx, node.value, -1, false, false)
    fx = out.fx
    if out.slot != existing
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "move", [existing, out.slot], node.span)
    end
    return ok(fx.with(next: saved))
  end
  fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
  slot = fx.next - 1
  out = try Expr.lower_expression(cx, fx, node.value, slot, false, false)
  return ok(out.fx.with(vars: out.fx.vars.put(node.name, slot)))
end

# A return of a call of a function of the program is a tail call, which returns by itself.
def lower_return(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.Return, saved: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  case node.value
    Ast.Optional.Present(value) ->
      call = tail_call(cx, value)
      case call
        Ast.Optional.Present(found) ->
          out = try Expr.lower_call(cx, fx, found, -1, true, false, true)
          return ok(out.fx.with(next: saved))
        Ast.Optional.Absent -> fx = fx
      end
      out = try Expr.lower_expression(cx, fx, value, -1, true, false)
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(out.fx, "return", [out.slot], node.span)
    Ast.Optional.Absent ->
      fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
      slot = fx.next - 1
      fx = Lowering.emit_const(fx, slot, Ir.Imm.Void, node.span)
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "return", [slot], node.span)
  end
  return ok(fx.with(next: saved))
end

# The call when an expression is a call of a function of the program (not a builtin).
def tail_call(cx: Lowering.Cx, value: Ast.Expr) -> Ast.Optional[Ast.Call]
  case value
    Ast.Expr.Call(node) ->
      if Builtins.ref(cx.catalog, node.name, node.args.size).ok?
        return Ast.Optional.Absent
      end
      return Ast.Optional.Present(node)
    _ -> return Ast.Optional.Absent
  end
end

def lower_if(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.IfStmt, saved: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  fx = Lowering.new_label(fx)
  end_label = fx.labels - 1
  has_else = false
  case node.else_body
    Ast.Optional.Present(body) -> has_else = true
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> has_else = false
  end
  index = 1
  for branch in node.branches
    fx = Lowering.new_label(fx)
    skip = fx.labels - 1
    condition = try Expr.lower_expression(cx, fx, branch.condition, -1, false, false)
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(condition.fx, "jump-if-false", [condition.slot, skip], Ast.expr_span(branch.condition))
    fx = fx.with(next: saved)
    fx = try scoped(cx, fx, branch.body)
    if has_else or index < node.branches.size
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "jump", [end_label], node.span)
    end
    fx = Lowering.place(fx, skip)
    index += 1
  end
  case node.else_body
    Ast.Optional.Present(body) -> fx = try scoped(cx, fx, body)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> fx = fx
  end
  return ok(Lowering.place(fx, end_label))
end

def lower_while(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.WhileStmt, saved: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  fx = Lowering.new_label(Lowering.new_label(fx))
  head = fx.labels - 2
  exit = fx.labels - 1
  fx = Lowering.place(fx, head)
  condition = try Expr.lower_expression(cx, fx, node.condition, -1, false, false)
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(condition.fx, "jump-if-false", [condition.slot, exit], Ast.expr_span(node.condition))
  fx = fx.with(next: saved)
  outer_next = fx.loop_next
  outer_exit = fx.loop_exit
  fx = fx.with(loop_next: head, loop_exit: exit)
  fx = try scoped(cx, fx, node.body)
  fx = fx.with(loop_next: outer_next, loop_exit: outer_exit)
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "jump", [head], node.span)
  return ok(Lowering.place(fx, exit))
end

# break and next jump to the labels of the innermost loop.
def lower_control(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.LoopControl) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  if fx.loop_next < 0
    return error(Lowering.unsupported(cx, "this statement", node.span))
  end
  label = fx.loop_next
  if node.kind == "break"
    label = fx.loop_exit
  end
  return ok(Lowering.emit_at(fx, "jump", [label], node.span))
end

# A for over a list or a set (a set is read as a list in first-insertion order): the length is read once, an index
# counts up, and each pass starts by reading the element, in the instruction put after the body's first `step`.
def lower_for(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.ForStmt, saved: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  span = node.span
  type = Lowering.static_type(cx, node.iterable)
  if Types.is(type, "Range")
    fx = try lower_range_for(cx, fx, node, span)
    return ok(fx.with(next: saved))
  end
  fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
  items = fx.next - 1
  out = try Expr.lower_expression(cx, fx, node.iterable, items, false, false)
  fx = out.fx
  if Types.is(type, "Set")
    fx = Lowering.emit_builtin(fx, items, "Set.to_a", 1, [span, span])
  end
  if node.body.size > 0
    fx = Lowering.alloc(Lowering.alloc(Lowering.alloc(Lowering.alloc(fx))))
    index = fx.next - 4
    count = fx.next - 3
    temp = fx.next - 2
    one = fx.next - 1
    fx = Lowering.new_label(Lowering.new_label(Lowering.new_label(Lowering.new_label(fx))))
    top = fx.labels - 4
    increment = fx.labels - 3
    test = fx.labels - 2
    exit = fx.labels - 1
    fx = Lowering.emit_const(fx, index, Ir.Imm.Int(0), span)
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "list-len", [count, items], span)
    fx = Lowering.emit_const(fx, one, Ir.Imm.Int(1), span)
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "jump", [test], span)
    outer_next = fx.loop_next
    outer_exit = fx.loop_exit
    fx = fx.with(loop_next: increment, loop_exit: exit)
    before = fx
    fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
    element = fx.next - 1
    fx = fx.with(vars: fx.vars.put(node.variable, element))
    fx = Lowering.place(fx, top)
    fx = fx.with(pending: [Ir.instr("list-get", [element, items, index], fx.file, [span])])
    fx = try lower_block(cx, fx, node.body)
    fx = leave(fx, before)
    fx = fx.with(loop_next: outer_next, loop_exit: outer_exit)
    fx = Lowering.place(fx, increment)
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "add-i", [index, index, one], span)
    fx = Lowering.place(fx, test)
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "lt-i", [temp, index, count], span)
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "jump-if-true", [temp, top], span)
    fx = Lowering.place(fx, exit)
  end
  return ok(fx.with(next: saved))
end

# A for over a range counts its bounds in registers; a literal range a..b or a...b is not built, and the body runs
# while the counter has not reached the last value.
def lower_range_for(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.ForStmt, span: Source.Span) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  fx = Lowering.alloc(Lowering.alloc(Lowering.alloc(fx)))
  bounds = fx.next - 3
  last_slot = fx.next - 2
  nonempty = fx.next - 1
  literal = false
  exclusive = false
  case node.iterable
    Ast.Expr.Binary(range) ->
      if range.op == "dot-dot" or range.op == "dot-dot-dot"
        literal = true
        exclusive = range.op == "dot-dot-dot"
        fx = Lowering.step(fx, range.span)
        left = try Expr.lower_expression(cx, fx, range.left, bounds, false, false)
        right = try Expr.lower_expression(cx, left.fx, range.right, last_slot, false, false)
        compare = "le-i"
        if exclusive
          compare = "lt-i"
        end
        fx = Lowering.emit_at(right.fx, compare, [nonempty, bounds, last_slot], span)
      end
    _ -> literal = false
  end
  if !literal
    source = try Expr.lower_expression(cx, fx, node.iterable, -1, false, false)
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(source.fx, "range-bounds", [bounds, source.slot], span)
  end
  fx = Lowering.new_label(Lowering.new_label(Lowering.new_label(fx)))
  exit = fx.labels - 3
  top = fx.labels - 2
  increment = fx.labels - 1
  fx = Lowering.alloc(Lowering.alloc(fx))
  one = fx.next - 2
  temp = fx.next - 1
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "jump-if-false", [nonempty, exit], span)
  fx = Lowering.emit_const(fx, one, Ir.Imm.Int(1), span)
  if exclusive
    fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "sub-i", [last_slot, last_slot, one], span)
  end
  outer_next = fx.loop_next
  outer_exit = fx.loop_exit
  fx = fx.with(loop_next: increment, loop_exit: exit)
  before = fx
  fx = fx.with(vars: fx.vars.put(node.variable, bounds))
  fx = Lowering.place(fx, top)
  fx = Lowering.step(fx, span)
  fx = try lower_block(cx, fx, node.body)
  fx = leave(fx, before)
  fx = fx.with(loop_next: outer_next, loop_exit: outer_exit)
  fx = Lowering.place(fx, increment)
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "eq", [temp, bounds, last_slot], span)
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "jump-if-true", [temp, exit], span)
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "add-i", [bounds, bounds, one], span)
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "jump", [top], span)
  return ok(Lowering.place(fx, exit))
end

# A case: each arm tests the scrutinee, jumps to the next arm when it does not match, binds the payload names in a
# scope of its own, and jumps to the end after its body (except the last arm).
def lower_case(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.CaseStmt, saved: Int) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  type = Lowering.static_type(cx, node.value)
  scrutinee = try Expr.lower_expression(cx, fx, node.value, -1, false, false)
  fx = Lowering.new_label(scrutinee.fx)
  end_label = fx.labels - 1
  value = scrutinee.slot
  index = 1
  for arm in node.arms
    fx = Lowering.new_label(fx)
    skip = fx.labels - 1
    test_slot = fx.next
    fx = try lower_test(cx, fx, arm.pattern, type, value, skip)
    fx = fx.with(next: test_slot)
    before = fx
    fx = try bind_payload(cx, fx, arm.pattern, type, value)
    fx = try lower_block(cx, fx, arm.body)
    fx = leave(fx, before)
    if index < node.arms.size
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "jump", [end_label], node.span)
    end
    fx = Lowering.place(fx, skip)
    index += 1
  end
  return ok(Lowering.place(fx, end_label).with(next: saved))
end

# The instructions that jump to skip when the scrutinee in value does not match the pattern.
def lower_test(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, pattern: Ast.Pattern, type: Types.Type, value: Int, skip: Int
) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  span = Ast.pattern_span(pattern)
  case pattern
    Ast.Pattern.Wildcard(node) -> return ok(fx)
    Ast.Pattern.Literal(node) -> return lower_literal_test(cx, fx, node, value, skip)
    Ast.Pattern.Variant(node) ->
      fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
      slot = fx.next - 1
      if Types.is(type, "Result")
        fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "is-ok", [slot, value], span)
        jump = "jump-if-true"
        if node.variant_name == "Ok"
          jump = "jump-if-false"
        end
        return ok(Lowering.emit_at(fx, jump, [slot, skip], span))
      end
      id = cx.variants["#{node.enum_name}.#{node.variant_name}"]
      fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "is-variant", [slot, value, id], span)
      return ok(Lowering.emit_at(fx, "jump-if-false", [slot, skip], span))
  end
end

# A literal pattern compares with `same`. An integer that is not an Int never matches, so its arm is skipped at once.
def lower_literal_test(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, node: Ast.LiteralPattern, value: Int, skip: Int
) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  imm = Ir.Imm.Nil
  case node.value
    Ast.LitValue.Whole(number) -> imm = Ir.Imm.Int(number)
    Ast.LitValue.Real(number) -> imm = Ir.Imm.Float(number)
    Ast.LitValue.Text(text) -> imm = Ir.Imm.Text(text)
    Ast.LitValue.Flag(flag) -> imm = Ir.Imm.Bool(flag)
    Ast.LitValue.Nothing -> imm = Ir.Imm.Nil
    Ast.LitValue.Huge(digits) ->
      if digits != "-#{INT_MIN_DIGITS}"
        return ok(Lowering.emit_at(fx, "jump", [skip], node.span))
      end
      imm = Ir.Imm.Int(INT_MIN)
  end
  fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
  slot = fx.next - 1
  fx = Lowering.emit_const(fx, slot, imm, node.span)
  fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "same", [slot, value, slot], node.span)
  return ok(Lowering.emit_at(fx, "jump-if-false", [slot, skip], node.span))
end

# The names of a variant pattern get a register each, filled from the payload of the scrutinee (a `_` takes none).
def bind_payload(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, pattern: Ast.Pattern, type: Types.Type, value: Int
) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  case pattern
    Ast.Pattern.Variant(node) ->
      item = 0
      for binding in node.bindings
        case binding
          Ast.Optional.Present(name) ->
            fx = Lowering.alloc(fx)
            slot = fx.next - 1
            fx = fx.with(vars: fx.vars.put(name, slot))
            if Types.is(type, "Result")
              fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "result-value", [slot, value], node.span)
            else
              fx = Lowering.emit_at(fx, "payload", [slot, value, item], node.span)
            end
          Ast.Optional.Absent -> fx = fx
        end
        item += 1
      end
    _ -> fx = fx
  end
  return ok(fx)
end

# A block of statements in a scope of its own: the names it makes and the registers it takes are gone after it.
def scoped(cx: Lowering.Cx, fx: Lowering.Fx, statements: List[Ast.Stmt]) -> Result[Lowering.Fx]
  inner = try lower_block(cx, fx, statements)
  return ok(leave(inner, fx))
end

# Closes a scope: the names and the register count go back to what they were when it opened.
def leave(fx: Lowering.Fx, before: Lowering.Fx) -> Lowering.Fx
  return fx.with(vars: before.vars, next: before.next)
end

def final_expression?(statement: Ast.Stmt) -> Bool
  case statement
    Ast.Stmt.Expression(node) -> return true
    _ -> return false
  end
end

def final_value(statement: Ast.Stmt) -> Ast.Expr
  case statement
    Ast.Stmt.Expression(node) -> return node.value
    _ -> return Ast.Expr.Literal(Ast.Literal(id: 0, value: Ast.LitValue.Nothing, span: statement_span(statement)))
  end
end

# The span of a statement node.
def statement_span(statement: Ast.Stmt) -> Source.Span
  case statement
    Ast.Stmt.Binding(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.Return(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.Expression(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.If(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.While(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.For(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.Control(node) -> return node.span
    Ast.Stmt.Case(node) -> return node.span
  end
end

## The instruction of an operator on two Ints, by the token kind of the operator. `>` and `>=` use the instruction of
## `<` and `<=` with the operands swapped.
export INT_OPS: Map[String, String] = {
  "plus": "add-i", "minus": "sub-i", "multiply": "mul-i", "divide": "div-i", "modulo": "mod-i",
  "less": "lt-i", "less-equal": "le-i", "greater": "lt-i", "greater-equal": "le-i"
}

## The operators on two Strings: only `+`.
export STRING_OPS: Map[String, String] = {"plus": "concat"}

## The same for two Floats.
export FLOAT_OPS: Map[String, String] = {
  "plus": "add-f", "minus": "sub-f", "multiply": "mul-f", "divide": "div-f",
  "less": "lt-f", "less-equal": "le-f", "greater": "lt-f", "greater-equal": "le-f"
}

## The builtin records the VM can build as structs, in the order the struct table lists the ones a program uses.
export BUILTIN_STRUCTS = [
  "FileInfo", "Header", "HttpRequest", "HttpResponse", "HttpClientOptions", "HttpServerOptions", "ProcessOutput",
  "LogEvent"
]

## The builtin structs that another one has a field of: using the key also puts these in the table.
export STRUCT_NEEDS: Map[String, List[String]] = {"HttpResponse": ["Header"], "HttpRequest": ["Header"]}

## The most items one `list` instruction gathers and the most entries one `map` instruction gathers; larger literals
## are built in chunks.
export MAX_CHUNK = 255

## The smallest and largest Int, and the digits of the first (a literal `9223372036854775808` is the digits of an Int
## that does not fit).
export INT_MIN = -9223372036854775807 - 1
export INT_MAX = 9223372036854775807
export INT_MIN_DIGITS = "9223372036854775808"
