## The text form of lowering, for tests. See lower.agc.

import Builtins from "builtins"
import Failure from "check_failure"
import CheckText from "check_text"
import Checker from "checker"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Ir from "ir"
import Paths from "import_path"
import Env from "link_env"
import LinkText from "link_text"
import Linker from "linker"
import Lowering from "lowering"
import Source from "source"
import Text from "text"
import Types from "types"

## The text form of lowering the file at path: the IR as lines, or the ERROR line of the first failure of the linker,
## the checker or the lowering.
##
## `program SPAN entry=N globals=N`, then `source N "path" chars=N` for each file (the path relative to the folder of
## the root file), `struct sN "Name" ["field",...]` with ` types=[...]` when JSON can build it, `enum "Name"
## vN="Variant"/SIZE ...`, and each function as `fnN "name" params=P captures=C slots=S [entry] @ SPAN` followed by its
## instructions: a label as `  LN:` and an instruction as `    op ARGS @ SPAN ...`. A span is
## FILE:LINE:COLUMN-LINE:COLUMN, with the index of its source. A register is `rN`, a function `fnN`, a struct `sN`, a
## variant `vN`, a global `gN`, a label `LN`; a `const` shows its value as `void`, `nil`, `true`, `false`, `int:N`,
## `float:bits:N` or a quoted string. tests/frontend-lower-common.rkt prints the same text from the Racket lowering.
export def lower_text(path: String, settings: Env.Settings) -> String
  return lower_text_after(path, settings, 0)
end

## The same, with the lowering started `frames` VM calls deeper than it would be. A test uses it to show how much of
## the call depth limit the lowering of a deep tree leaves free.
export def lower_text_after(path: String, settings: Env.Settings, frames: Int) -> String
  case Linker.link_file(path, settings)
    Linker.Linking.Failed(failure) -> return LinkText.failure_text(LinkText.root_dir_of(path), failure)
    Linker.Linking.Done(linked) -> return linked_text(linked, settings, frames)
  end
end

## The ERROR line of a problem of the lowering or of the bytecode writer: the line of its diagnostic with
## ` file="path"` added.
export def problem_text(root_dir: String, problem: Failure.Problem) -> String
  shown = Diag.Diagnostic(code: problem.code, message: problem.message, span: problem.span, help: problem.help)
  return "#{Text.diagnostic_line(shown)} file=#{Text.quote(Paths.stored_file(root_dir, problem.file))}"
end

def linked_text(linked: Linker.Linked, settings: Env.Settings, frames: Int) -> String
  case Checker.check(linked, settings.catalog)
    Checker.Checking.Failed(problem) -> return CheckText.problem_text(linked.root_dir, problem)
    Checker.Checking.Done(checked) ->
      return lowered_text(linked, lower_deeper(linked, checked, settings.catalog, frames))
  end
end

# Lowers after `frames` calls that wait for it, which are not tail calls.
def lower_deeper(
  linked: Linker.Linked, checked: Checker.Checked, catalog: Builtins.Catalog, frames: Int
) -> Lowering.Lowered
  if frames == 0
    return Lowering.lower(linked, checked, catalog)
  end
  done = lower_deeper(linked, checked, catalog, frames - 1)
  return done
end

def lowered_text(linked: Linker.Linked, lowered: Lowering.Lowered) -> String
  case lowered
    Lowering.Lowered.Failed(problem) -> return problem_text(linked.root_dir, problem)
    Lowering.Lowered.Done(program) -> return program_lines(linked.root_dir, program).join("\n")
  end
end

def program_lines(root_dir: String, program: Ir.Program) -> List[String]
  head = "program #{span_text(0, program.span)} entry=#{program.entry}"
  lines: List[String] = ["#{head} globals=#{program.globals}"]
  index = 0
  for source in program.sources
    shown = Text.quote(Paths.stored_file(root_dir, source.file))
    lines = lines.push("source #{index} #{shown} chars=#{source.text.length}")
    index += 1
  end
  index = 0
  for entry in program.structs
    lines = lines.push(struct_line(index, entry))
    index += 1
  end
  id = 0
  for entry in program.enums
    names = ""
    for variant in entry.variants
      names = "#{names} v#{id}=#{Text.quote(variant.name)}/#{variant.size}"
      id += 1
    end
    lines = lines.push("enum #{Text.quote(entry.name)}#{names}")
  end
  index = 0
  for function in program.functions
    lines = function_lines(lines, index, function, index == program.entry)
    index += 1
  end
  return lines
end

def struct_line(index: Int, entry: Ir.StructDef) -> String
  fields = entry.fields.map do |field: String| Text.quote(field) end.join(",")
  line = "struct s#{index} #{Text.quote(entry.name)} [#{fields}]"
  if entry.decodable
    types = entry.types.map do |type: Types.Type| Types.debug_text(type) end.join(", ")
    line = "#{line} types=[#{types}]"
  end
  return line
end

def function_lines(out: List[String], index: Int, function: Ir.Function, entry: Bool) -> List[String]
  head = "fn#{index} #{Text.quote(function.name)} params=#{function.params}"
  head = "#{head} captures=#{function.captures} slots=#{function.slots}"
  if entry
    head = "#{head} entry"
  end
  lines = out.push("#{head} @ #{span_text(function.file, function.span)}")
  for instr in function.body
    if instr.op == "label"
      lines = lines.push("  L#{instr.args[0]}:")
    else
      lines = lines.push(instr_line(instr))
    end
  end
  return lines
end

def instr_line(instr: Ir.Instr) -> String
  text = "    #{instr.op}"
  shown = instr.args.size
  if instr.op == "struct-with"
    shown = 4
  end
  at = 0
  while at < shown
    text = "#{text} #{arg_text(instr, at)}"
    at += 1
  end
  if instr.op == "const"
    text = "#{text} #{imm_text(instr.imm)}"
  end
  spans = instr.spans.map do |span: Source.Span| span_text(instr.file, span) end
  return "#{text} @ #{spans.join(" ")}"
end

# One argument of an instruction, by the op: labels, functions, structs, variants and globals have their own prefix.
def arg_text(instr: Ir.Instr, at: Int) -> String
  op = instr.op
  value = instr.args[at]
  if instr.op == "call-builtin"
    if at == 0
      return "r#{value} #{Text.quote(instr.name)}"
    end
    return value.to_s
  end
  if (op == "jump" and at == 0) or ((op == "jump-if-false" or op == "jump-if-true") and at == 1)
    return "L#{value}"
  elsif (op == "call" or op == "tail-call" or op == "closure") and at == 1
    return "fn#{value}"
  elsif (op == "global" or op == "global-set") and at == 1
    return "g#{value}"
  elsif (op == "enum" or op == "is-variant") and at == 2
    return "v#{value}"
  elsif (op == "struct" or op == "struct-with") and at == 2
    return "s#{value}"
  elsif op == "struct-with" and at == 3
    positions = instr.args.drop(3).map do |position: Int| position.to_s end.join(" ")
    return "[#{positions}]"
  elsif (op == "field" or op == "payload" or op == "list" or op == "map") and at == 2
    return value.to_s
  elsif op == "call-value" and at == 1
    return value.to_s
  elsif op == "range" and at == 2
    if value == 1
      return "..."
    end
    return ".."
  end
  return "r#{value}"
end

def imm_text(imm: Ir.Imm) -> String
  case imm
    Ir.Imm.Void -> return "void"
    Ir.Imm.Nil -> return "nil"
    Ir.Imm.Bool(flag) -> return flag.to_s
    Ir.Imm.Int(number) -> return "int:#{number}"
    Ir.Imm.Float(number) -> return "float:bits:#{Float.to_bits(number)}"
    Ir.Imm.Text(text) -> return Text.quote(text)
  end
end

def span_text(file: Int, span: Source.Span) -> String
  return "#{file}:#{span.start.line}:#{span.start.column}-#{span.stop.line}:#{span.stop.column}"
end
compiler/lowering.agc:
## The lowering (src/lower.rkt, `lower`): takes a linked and checked program and gives the VM IR (ir.agc), or the first
## LOWER- problem. The function table is, in this order: the declared functions in program order, the kept constants in
## initialization order, `<start>` when the program has constant slots, then the blocks in the order they were found
## (docs/future/44-module-constants.md 44.7).
##
## Recursion: lowering an expression or a statement takes at most 3 VM frames for each level of the tree (most shapes
## take 1 or 2, because many calls are tail calls), and the checker allows 1,000 levels (CHECK-TOO-DEEP), so it uses
## about 3,000 of the 10,000 frames of the VM. The scans that read the whole tree use a worklist and do not recurse.

import Ast from "ast"
import Builtins from "builtins"
import Failure from "check_failure"
import Checker from "checker"
import Ir from "ir"
import Const from "lower_const"
import Expr from "lower_expr"
import Program from "lower_program"
import Scans from "lower_scan"
import Lowering from "lower_state"
import Stmt from "lower_stmt"
import {BUILTIN_STRUCTS} from "lower_tables"
import Linker from "linker"
import Source from "source"
import Types from "types"

## The result of lowering: the program, or the first problem (the file it is in comes with it).
export enum Lowered
  Done(Ir.Program)
  Failed(Failure.Problem)
end

# A function or constant of the program with the file it is declared in.
struct Located
  file: String
  function: Ast.FunctionDecl
end

struct LocatedConst
  file: String
  constant: Ast.ConstDecl
end

# The functions lowered so far, with the block functions their bodies made and the next free index of the table.
struct Table
  functions: List[Ir.Function]
  blocks: Map[Int, Ir.Function]
  block_count: Int
end

# What the scans of all the bodies give: one per function and constant, and the watched type names written anywhere,
# with whether a function uses a type name as a value.
struct Scanned
  function_scans: List[Scans.Scan]
  constant_scans: List[Scans.Scan]
  written: List[String]
  type_value: Bool
end

## Lowers a linked program that the checker accepted.
export def lower(linked: Linker.Linked, checked: Checker.Checked, catalog: Builtins.Catalog) -> Lowered
  result = run(linked, checked, catalog)
  if result.ok?
    return Lowered.Done(result.unwrap!)
  end
  return Lowered.Failed(Failure.unpack(result.message))
end

def run(linked: Linker.Linked, checked: Checker.Checked, catalog: Builtins.Catalog) -> Result[Ir.Program]
  functions: List[Located] = []
  constants: List[LocatedConst] = []
  decls: List[Ast.Decl] = []
  for module in linked.modules
    for decl in module.declarations
      decls = decls.push(decl)
      case decl
        Ast.Decl.Function(node) -> functions = functions.push(Located(file: module.file, function: node))
        Ast.Decl.Constant(node) -> constants = constants.push(LocatedConst(file: module.file, constant: node))
        _ -> functions = functions
      end
    end
  end
  function_decls = functions.map do |entry: Located| entry.function end
  constant_decls = constants.map do |entry: LocatedConst| entry.constant end
  watched = Set.new(BUILTIN_STRUCTS.concat(catalog.enums.keys))
  scanned = scan_all(decls, function_decls, constant_decls, watched)
  used = Set.new(scanned.written.concat(mentioned_in(checked.types, watched)))
  tables = Program.build(catalog, decls, used, scanned.type_value)
  plan = Const.plan(function_decls, scanned.function_scans, constant_decls, scanned.constant_scans, checked.constants)
  start = plan.slots.size > 0
  files_of = constant_files(constants)
  files = source_order(linked, functions, plan.kept, files_of)
  index_of: Map[String, Int] = {}
  for file in files
    index_of = index_of.put(file, index_of.size)
  end
  by_name: Map[String, Int] = {}
  at = 0
  for entry in functions
    by_name = by_name.put(entry.function.name, at)
    at += 1
  end
  main_index = by_name["main"]
  cx = Lowering.Cx(
    types: checked.types,
    resolved: checked.resolved,
    catalog: catalog,
    user_types: tables.user_types,
    structs: tables.infos,
    variants: tables.variants,
    json_structs: tables.json_structs,
    functions: by_name,
    reads: reads_of(plan),
    file: linked.modules[0].file,
    index: 0,
    expression: &Expr.lower_expression,
    block: &Stmt.lower_block_function
  )
  table_size = functions.size + plan.kept.size
  if start
    table_size += 1
  end
  table = Table(functions: [], blocks: {}, block_count: table_size)
  for entry in functions
    params = entry.function.params.map do |param: Ast.Param| param.name end
    function = entry.function
    table = try add_function(
      cx, table, entry.file, index_of[entry.file], function.name, params, function.body, function.span,
    )
  end
  for entry in plan.kept
    file = files_of[entry.name]
    body = [Ast.Stmt.Return(Ast.Return(id: entry.id, value: Ast.Optional.Present(entry.value), span: entry.span))]
    table = try add_function(cx, table, file, index_of[file], entry.name, [], body, entry.span)
  end
  built = table.functions
  blocks = table.blocks
  block_count = table.block_count
  if start
    built = built.push(start_function(linked.root.span, plan, files_of, index_of, functions.size, main_index))
  end
  index = table_size
  while index < block_count
    built = built.push(blocks[index])
    index += 1
  end
  entry = main_index
  if start
    entry = functions.size + plan.kept.size
  end
  sources = linked.modules.map do |module: Linker.LinkedModule| Ir.SourceFile(file: module.file, text: module.text) end
  return ok(Ir.Program(
    sources: used_sources(sources, files),
    structs: tables.structs,
    enums: tables.enums,
    functions: built,
    entry: entry,
    globals: plan.slots.size,
    span: linked.root.span
  ))
end

# Lowers one function into a new table whose index is the next to fill, and adds the blocks it made.
def add_function(
  cx: Lowering.Cx, table: Table, file: String, index: Int, name: String, params: List[String], body: List[Ast.Stmt],
  span: Source.Span
) -> Result[Table]
  here = cx.with(file: file, index: index)
  inner = Lowering.fresh(index, table.blocks, table.block_count)
  done = try Stmt.lower_function(here, inner, name, params, [], body, span, false)
  return ok(Table(
    functions: table.functions.push(done.function),
    blocks: done.fx.blocks,
    block_count: done.fx.block_count
  ))
end

def scan_all(
  decls: List[Ast.Decl], functions: List[Ast.FunctionDecl], constants: List[Ast.ConstDecl], watched: Set[String]
) -> Scanned
  function_scans: List[Scans.Scan] = []
  constant_scans: List[Scans.Scan] = []
  written: List[String] = []
  type_value = false
  for decl in functions
    scan = Scans.scan_body(decl.body, watched)
    function_scans = function_scans.push(scan)
    written = written.concat(scan.written).concat(Scans.written_signature(decl, watched))
    if scan.type_value
      type_value = true
    end
  end
  for decl in constants
    scan = Scans.scan_value(decl.value, watched)
    constant_scans = constant_scans.push(scan)
    written = written.concat(scan.written)
    case decl.type
      Ast.Optional.Present(ref) -> written = written.concat(Scans.written_in(ref, watched))
      Ast.Optional.Absent -> written = written
    end
  end
  for decl in decls
    written = written.concat(declared_names(decl, watched))
  end
  return Scanned(
    function_scans: function_scans,
    constant_scans: constant_scans,
    written: written,
    type_value: type_value,
  )
end

# The watched type names the field types of a struct and the payload types of an enum write.
def declared_names(decl: Ast.Decl, watched: Set[String]) -> List[String]
  found: List[String] = []
  case decl
    Ast.Decl.Struct(node) ->
      for field in node.fields
        found = found.concat(Scans.written_in(field.type, watched))
      end
    Ast.Decl.Enum(node) ->
      for variant in node.variants
        for ref in variant.payload_types
          found = found.concat(Scans.written_in(ref, watched))
        end
      end
    _ -> found = found
  end
  return found
end

# The watched struct and enum names that the type of some expression mentions.
def mentioned_in(types: List[Types.Type], watched: Set[String]) -> List[String]
  found: List[String] = []
  for type in types
    found = found.concat(names_in(type, watched))
  end
  return found
end

def names_in(type: Types.Type, watched: Set[String]) -> List[String]
  case type
    Types.Type.Struct(name) -> return only(name, watched)
    Types.Type.Enum(name, args) -> return only(name, watched).concat(names_in_all(args, watched))
    Types.Type.List(item) -> return names_in(item, watched)
    Types.Type.Set(item) -> return names_in(item, watched)
    Types.Type.Result(item) -> return names_in(item, watched)
    Types.Type.Task(item) -> return names_in(item, watched)
    Types.Type.Channel(item) -> return names_in(item, watched)
    Types.Type.Map(key, value) -> return names_in(key, watched).concat(names_in(value, watched))
    Types.Type.Fn(params, result) -> return names_in_all(params, watched).concat(names_in(result, watched))
    _ -> return []
  end
end

def names_in_all(types: List[Types.Type], watched: Set[String]) -> List[String]
  found: List[String] = []
  for type in types
    found = found.concat(names_in(type, watched))
  end
  return found
end

def only(name: String, watched: Set[String]) -> List[String]
  if watched.include?(name)
    return [name]
  end
  return []
end

# What a read of each constant becomes: the literal of a scalar constant, else its slot.
def reads_of(plan: Const.Plan) -> Map[String, Lowering.Read]
  reads: Map[String, Lowering.Read] = {}
  for name in plan.literals.keys
    reads = reads.put(name, Lowering.Read.Literal(plan.literals[name]))
  end
  for name in plan.slots.keys
    reads = reads.put(name, Lowering.Read.Slot(plan.slots[name]))
  end
  return reads
end

# The files in the order src/lower.rkt first emits an instruction of each: the root, then the file of each function,
# then of each kept constant.
def source_order(
  linked: Linker.Linked, functions: List[Located], kept: List[Ast.ConstDecl], files_of: Map[String, String]
) -> List[String]
  seen: Set[String] = Set.new([linked.modules[0].file])
  files: List[String] = [linked.modules[0].file]
  for entry in functions
    if !seen.include?(entry.file)
      seen = seen.add(entry.file)
      files = files.push(entry.file)
    end
  end
  for decl in kept
    file = files_of[decl.name]
    if !seen.include?(file)
      seen = seen.add(file)
      files = files.push(file)
    end
  end
  return files
end

# The file each constant is declared in, by name.
def constant_files(constants: List[LocatedConst]) -> Map[String, String]
  files: Map[String, String] = {}
  for entry in constants
    files = files.put(entry.constant.name, entry.file)
  end
  return files
end

# The source files in the order of files.
def used_sources(sources: List[Ir.SourceFile], files: List[String]) -> List[Ir.SourceFile]
  by_file: Map[String, Ir.SourceFile] = {}
  for source in sources
    by_file = by_file.put(source.file, source)
  end
  return files.map do |file: String| by_file[file] end
end

# `<start>`: a step, then for each kept constant a call of its function and a store of the result in its slot, then a
# tail call of main. The loader wants a function to start with a step and to end with a return, so a `const` and a
# `return` follow the tail call.
def start_function(
  span: Source.Span, plan: Const.Plan, files_of: Map[String, String], index_of: Map[String, Int], declared: Int,
  main_index: Int
) -> Ir.Function
  body: List[Ir.Instr] = [Ir.instr("step", [], 0, [span])]
  offset = 0
  for decl in plan.kept
    file = index_of[files_of[decl.name]]
    body = body.push(Ir.instr("call", [0, declared + offset], file, [decl.span]))
    body = body.push(Ir.instr("global-set", [0, plan.slots[decl.name]], file, [decl.span]))
    offset += 1
  end
  body = body.push(Ir.instr("tail-call", [0, main_index], 0, [span]))
  body = body.push(Ir.Instr(op: "const", args: [0], imm: Ir.Imm.Void, name: "", file: 0, spans: [span]))
  body = body.push(Ir.instr("return", [0], 0, [span]))
  return Ir.Function(name: "<start>", params: 0, captures: 0, slots: 1, body: body, file: 0, span: span)
end
compiler/modules.agc:
## The module loader: starting at the root file, reads, lexes and parses every file the imports reach, once, and checks
## each one. This is the first half of link-program in src/modules.rkt (the visit function); rewrite.agc is the second.
##
## The walk is a loop over an explicit stack of files that still have imports to read, so a long chain of imports uses
## no VM call depth. Files are met in the order Racket meets them (a file is read at its import, before the imports
## after it), so the first failure is the same, and so are the node ids: every file is parsed from the next free id of
## the file read before it (parse, Ast.next_free_id).

import Ast from "ast"
import Declarations from "declarations"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Paths from "import_path"
import Lexer from "lexer"
import Env from "link_env"
import Failure from "link_failure"
import Parser from "parser"
import Resolve from "resolve_import"
import Source from "source"
import SourceFile from "source_file"
import Suggest from "suggest"

## A name bound by import {Name} from "path" (or {Name as Local}): the key of the module that exports it and the
## exported name.
export struct Named
  target: String
  name: String
end

## A file of the program once it is loaded. named maps each local name of an import list to what it names.
export struct Module
  key: String
  file: String
  prefix: String
  first_id: Int
  text: String
  program: Ast.Program
  names: Map[String, Declarations.Kind]
  public: Map[String, Declarations.Kind]
  aliases: Map[String, String]
  paths: Map[String, String]
  named: Map[String, Named]
end

## Every module of a program. order lists the keys with the root first, each file before the files its imports read; a
## file imported twice appears once. root_dir is the folder of the root file.
export struct Loaded
  order: List[String]
  modules: Map[String, Module]
  root_dir: String
end

# A file whose imports are being read: the module so far (its aliases, the paths written for them and named imports are
# filled in as imports are read), and the index of the next import to read. pending is the key of the file that the
# import at next names while its names wait to be checked: they need the exports of that file, so they are checked once
# it is loaded, as src/modules.rkt checks them after visit. "" when no import waits.
struct Frame
  module: Module
  aliases: Map[String, String]
  paths: Map[String, String]
  named: Map[String, Named]
  imports: List[Ast.ImportDecl]
  next: Int
  pending: String
end

# seen maps a key to 1 while its file is on the stack, and to 0 once it is done.
struct Walk
  stack: List[Frame]
  seen: Map[String, Int]
  done: Map[String, Module]
  order: List[String]
  next_id: Int
  root_dir: String
end

struct Collected
  names: Map[String, Declarations.Kind]
  public: Map[String, Declarations.Kind]
end

## Loads the root file and everything it imports. A failure is a packed failure (link_failure.agc): CHECK-IMPORT-*,
## CHECK-DECL-ORDER and CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME, or the diagnostic of the lexer or the parser for a file.
export def load(root: String, settings: Env.Settings) -> Result[Loaded]
  file = Path.resolve(root).unwrap_or(root)
  text = try root_text(root, file)
  program = try parse_source(file, text, 0)
  key = Path.real(root)
  if !key.ok?
    return error(
      Failure.fail_at(Failure.Site(file: file, span: program.span), "CHECK-IMPORT-IO", key.message, Diag.Help.NoHelp),
    )
  end
  empty = Walk(stack: [], seen: {}, done: {}, order: [], next_id: 0, root_dir: Paths.directory_of(key.unwrap!))
  walk = try enter(settings, empty, key.unwrap!, file, text, program, 0)
  finished = try run(settings, walk)
  return ok(Loaded(order: finished.order, modules: finished.done, root_dir: finished.root_dir))
end

def start_span() -> Source.Span
  start = Source.Position(offset: 0, line: 1, column: 1)
  return Source.Span(start: start, stop: start)
end

def parse_source(file: String, text: String, first_id: Int) -> Result[Ast.Program]
  case Lexer.lex(text)
    Diag.Outcome.Failed(problem) -> return error(Failure.from_stage(file, problem))
    Diag.Outcome.Done(tokens) ->
      case Parser.parse(tokens, first_id)
        Diag.Outcome.Failed(problem) -> return error(Failure.from_stage(file, problem))
        Diag.Outcome.Done(program) -> return ok(program)
      end
  end
end

# Each step reads one import of the file on top of the stack, or finishes that file.
def run(settings: Env.Settings, walk: Walk) -> Result[Walk]
  if walk.stack.size == 0
    return ok(walk)
  end
  following = try step(settings, walk)
  return run(settings, following)
end

def step(settings: Env.Settings, walk: Walk) -> Result[Walk]
  frame = walk.stack[walk.stack.size - 1]
  if frame.next >= frame.imports.size
    return ok(finish(walk, frame))
  end
  if frame.pending != ""
    return bind_names(settings, walk, frame, frame.imports[frame.next])
  end
  return read_import(settings, walk, frame, frame.imports[frame.next])
end

def finish(walk: Walk, frame: Frame) -> Walk
  module = frame.module.with(aliases: frame.aliases, paths: frame.paths, named: frame.named)
  return walk.with(
    stack: walk.stack.take(walk.stack.size - 1),
    seen: walk.seen.put(module.key, 0),
    done: walk.done.put(module.key, module),
  )
end

# One import of the file on top: the alias, the path, then the file it names (read and entered unless it was seen). The
# names of an import list wait for the file to be loaded (bind_names).
def read_import(settings: Env.Settings, walk: Walk, frame: Frame, decl: Ast.ImportDecl) -> Result[Walk]
  module = frame.module
  site = Failure.Site(file: module.file, span: decl.span)
  alias = Declarations.alias_of(decl)
  aliases = frame.aliases
  paths = frame.paths
  if (
    alias != "" and
    (
      aliases.has_key?(alias) or
      module.names.has_key?(alias) or
      frame.named.has_key?(alias) or
      settings.catalog.reserved.include?(alias)
    )
  )
    return error(Failure.fail_at(site, "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME", "duplicate or reserved import alias", Diag.Help.NoHelp))
  end
  file = try Paths.module_file(decl, site)
  target = try Resolve.resolve_import(settings, walk.root_dir, module.key, file, site)
  if alias != ""
    aliases = aliases.put(alias, target)
    paths = paths.put(alias, decl.path)
  end
  with_frame = replace_top(walk, after_read(frame.with(paths: paths), aliases, target, decl))
  state = walk.seen.get(target, -1)
  if state == 1
    return error(Failure.fail_at(site, "CHECK-IMPORT-CYCLE", "import cycle", Diag.Help.NoHelp))
  elsif state == 0
    return ok(with_frame)
  end
  return load_file(settings, with_frame, target, site)
end

# An alias import is done once read; a name list waits for its file (pending).
def after_read(frame: Frame, aliases: Map[String, String], target: String, decl: Ast.ImportDecl) -> Frame
  if decl.names.size == 0
    return frame.with(aliases: aliases, next: frame.next + 1)
  end
  return frame.with(aliases: aliases, pending: target)
end

# The names of the import at next, once its file is loaded: each must be an export, keep the case rule of its kind, and
# join the names of the file like a declaration. The first problem is reported, in the order of the list.
def bind_names(settings: Env.Settings, walk: Walk, frame: Frame, decl: Ast.ImportDecl) -> Result[Walk]
  target = walk.done[frame.pending]
  named = frame.named
  for entry in decl.names
    named = try bind_name(settings, frame, target, entry, named)
  end
  return ok(replace_top(walk, frame.with(named: named, next: frame.next + 1, pending: "")))
end

def bind_name(
  settings: Env.Settings,
  frame: Frame,
  target: Module,
  entry: Ast.ImportName,
  named: Map[String, Named],
) -> Result[Map[String, Named]]
  file = frame.module.file
  if !target.public.has_key?(entry.name)
    return error(
      Failure.fail_at(
        Failure.Site(file: file, span: entry.span),
        "CHECK-IMPORT-NAME",
        "unknown or private imported name",
        Suggest.unknown_import_help(target.key, target.public, entry.name, false),
      ),
    )
  end
  kind = target.public[entry.name]
  at_local = Failure.Site(file: file, span: entry.local_span)
  if !rename_ok?(entry.local, kind)
    return error(
      Failure.fail_at(
        at_local,
        "CHECK-IMPORT-RENAME",
        "the new name does not follow the case rule of the imported name",
        Failure.hint(rename_help(kind)),
      ),
    )
  end
  taken = (
    frame.module.names.has_key?(entry.local) or
    frame.aliases.has_key?(entry.local) or
    named.has_key?(entry.local)
  )
  if taken or settings.catalog.bare_names.include?(entry.local) or settings.catalog.reserved.include?(entry.local)
    return error(
      Failure.fail_at(at_local, "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME", "duplicate or reserved imported name", Diag.Help.NoHelp),
    )
  end
  return ok(named.put(entry.local, Named(target: target.key, name: entry.name)))
end

# A struct or an enum is renamed to a type name (a capital first letter), a function to a lowercase one, a constant to
# another constant name.
def rename_ok?(local: String, kind: Declarations.Kind) -> Bool
  if Declarations.constant?(kind)
    return Declarations.constant_name?(local)
  elsif Declarations.function?(kind)
    return !Declarations.type_name?(local)
  end
  return Declarations.type_name?(local)
end

def rename_help(kind: Declarations.Kind) -> String
  case kind
    Declarations.Kind.Struct -> return "a struct is renamed to another type name, which starts with a capital letter"
    Declarations.Kind.Enum -> return "an enum is renamed to another type name, which starts with a capital letter"
    Declarations.Kind.Constant -> return "a constant is renamed to another constant name, in capitals with underscores"
    _ -> return "a function is renamed to another lowercase name"
  end
end

def replace_top(walk: Walk, frame: Frame) -> Walk
  return walk.with(stack: walk.stack.set(walk.stack.size - 1, frame))
end

def load_file(settings: Env.Settings, walk: Walk, key: String, site: Failure.Site) -> Result[Walk]
  text = try imported_text(settings, key, site)
  program = try parse_source(key, text, walk.next_id)
  return enter(settings, walk, key, key, text, program, walk.next_id)
end

# The text of the root file: CHECK-IMPORT-IO at its start with the system's message, or LEX-INVALID-UTF8.
def root_text(root: String, file: String) -> Result[String]
  case SourceFile.read(root, Env.io_timeout())
    SourceFile.Read.Text(text) -> return ok(text)
    SourceFile.Read.Invalid(at) -> return error(Failure.from_stage(file, SourceFile.invalid_utf8(at)))
    SourceFile.Read.Unreadable(message) ->
      site = Failure.Site(file: file, span: start_span())
      return error(Failure.fail_at(site, "CHECK-IMPORT-IO", message, Diag.Help.NoHelp))
  end
end

# The text of an imported file: CHECK-IMPORT-IO at the import, or LEX-INVALID-UTF8 in the imported file.
def imported_text(settings: Env.Settings, key: String, site: Failure.Site) -> Result[String]
  case SourceFile.read(Resolve.source_path(settings, key), Env.io_timeout())
    SourceFile.Read.Text(text) -> return ok(text)
    SourceFile.Read.Invalid(at) -> return error(Failure.from_stage(key, SourceFile.invalid_utf8(at)))
    SourceFile.Read.Unreadable(_) ->
      return error(Failure.fail_at(site, "CHECK-IMPORT-IO", "cannot read import", Diag.Help.NoHelp))
  end
end

# Registers a parsed file: the declaration order, then the declared names, then it goes on the stack with the imports
# to read.
def enter(
  settings: Env.Settings,
  walk: Walk,
  key: String,
  file: String,
  text: String,
  program: Ast.Program,
  first_id: Int,
) -> Result[Walk]
  try Declarations.check_order(file, program.declarations)
  collected = try collect(settings, file, program.declarations)
  count = walk.seen.size + 1
  prefix = "@#{count}::"
  if walk.order.size == 0
    prefix = ""
  end
  module = Module(
    key: key,
    file: file,
    prefix: prefix,
    first_id: first_id,
    text: text,
    program: program,
    names: collected.names,
    public: collected.public,
    aliases: {},
    paths: {},
    named: {},
  )
  frame = Frame(
    module: module,
    aliases: {},
    paths: {},
    named: {},
    imports: Declarations.imports_of(program.declarations),
    next: 0,
    pending: "",
  )
  return ok(
    walk.with(
      stack: walk.stack.push(frame),
      seen: walk.seen.put(key, 1),
      order: walk.order.push(key),
      next_id: Ast.next_free_id(program),
    ),
  )
end

# The names a file declares, and those it exports; a repeated name, a builtin name or a reserved type name is
# CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME at the declaration.
def collect(settings: Env.Settings, file: String, declarations: List[Ast.Decl]) -> Result[Collected]
  names: Map[String, Declarations.Kind] = {}
  public: Map[String, Declarations.Kind] = {}
  for wrapped in declarations
    kind = Declarations.kind_of(wrapped)
    if Declarations.import?(kind)
      next
    end
    name = Declarations.name_of(wrapped)
    if names.has_key?(name) or settings.catalog.bare_names.include?(name) or settings.catalog.reserved.include?(name)
      return error(
        Failure.fail_at(
          Failure.Site(file: file, span: Declarations.span_of(wrapped)),
          "CHECK-REDEFINED-NAME",
          "duplicate or reserved declaration",
          Diag.Help.NoHelp,
        ),
      )
    end
    names = names.put(name, kind)
    if Declarations.exported?(wrapped)
      public = public.put(name, kind)
    end
  end
  return ok(Collected(names: names, public: public))
end

import ParseText from "parse_text"
import SourceFile from "source_file"
import Text from "text"

# An argument `--first-id=N` sets the first node id of the files after it (the default is 0). The argument
# `--continue` numbers each file from the next free id of the one before it (Ast.next_free_id).
def main() -> Void
  first_id = 0
  continuing = false
  for path in System.args()
    if path.starts_with?("--first-id=")
      first_id = path.slice(11, path.length - 11).to_i!
      next
    end
    if path == "--continue"
      continuing = true
      next
    end
    puts("== #{path}")
    case SourceFile.read(path, 10000)
      SourceFile.Read.Text(text) ->
        printed = ParseText.print_from(text, first_id)
        puts(printed.text)
        if continuing
          first_id = printed.next_id
        end
      SourceFile.Read.Invalid(at) -> puts(Text.diagnostic_line(SourceFile.invalid_utf8(at)))
      SourceFile.Read.Unreadable(message) -> puts("!! #{message}")
    end
  end
end
compiler/parse_base.agc:
## The shared part of the Agentica parser: the context, the results, the failures, and the parts of the grammar that
## need no expressions (types and case patterns).
##
## src/parser.rkt keeps its state in variables that it changes (the position, the nesting, the block flags). Agentica
## has no such variables, so every parse function takes the context (Env), a position and the next free node id, and
## returns the node with the new position and id. A failure is a Result error whose String is the packed diagnostic, so
## `try` stops at the first one, as the Racket stages do.

import Ast from "ast"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Source from "source"
import Tokens from "token"
import Unicode from "unicode"

## What a parse function reads and never changes: the tokens, the context of the construct being parsed, and the
## nesting level. depth is the block depth (0 outside a do block body), allow_blocks tells whether `do` after a call
## starts a block, and brace_at and brace_form remember a `{` right after a block head, for the help of
## PARSE-UNEXPECTED-TOKEN.
export struct Env
  tokens: List[Tokens.Token]
  size: Int
  allow_blocks: Bool
  depth: Int
  brace_at: Int
  brace_form: String
  nesting: Int
end

## The result of parsing an expression: the node, the position of the next token, and the next free node id.
export struct ExprAt
  node: Ast.Expr
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

## A list of expressions with the next position and the next free node id.
export struct ExprsAt
  nodes: List[Ast.Expr]
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

## A statement with the next position and the next free node id.
export struct StmtAt
  node: Ast.Stmt
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

## A list of statements with the next position and the next free node id.
export struct StmtsAt
  nodes: List[Ast.Stmt]
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

## A type with the next position and the next free node id.
export struct TypeAt
  node: Ast.TypeRef
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

## A pattern with the next position and the next free node id.
export struct PatternAt
  node: Ast.Pattern
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

struct BindingsAt
  names: List[Ast.Optional[String]]
  pos: Int
end

## The deepest nesting the parser accepts (PARSE-TOO-DEEP beyond it). Each statement, expression, prefix operator and
## type level counts one, and so does each operator or suffix (link) of a chain such as a + b + c or a.b.c: everything
## parsed after the k-th link of a chain (its right operand, arguments, index or block) starts from the depth of the
## chain plus k. The counter bounds the calls of the parser: a level uses up to about 8 VM calls (equality and
## comparison add no level but cost frames; measured: `M.f(1 == 1 < ` nested overflows near 1,250 levels, 1.25 times
## the limit), so the limit stays below the VM limit of 10,000 (RUNTIME-STACK-OVERFLOW). It does not bound the depth of
## the tree: the right operand of the first link of a chain hangs below the whole chain, so nested chains build deeper
## trees, and a pass that recurses on the tree needs its own stack or limit. src/parser.rkt has the same limit and
## counts the same way.
export def nesting_limit() -> Int
  return 1000
end

## The context for the start of a file.
export def make_env(tokens: List[Tokens.Token]) -> Env
  return Env(tokens: tokens, size: tokens.size, allow_blocks: true, depth: 0, brace_at: -1, brace_form: "", nesting: 0)
end

## The same context, with `do` blocks allowed or not. Headers of case, while and for do not allow them.
export def with_blocks(e: Env, allow: Bool) -> Env
  return Env(
    tokens: e.tokens,
    size: e.size,
    allow_blocks: allow,
    depth: e.depth,
    brace_at: e.brace_at,
    brace_form: e.brace_form,
    nesting: e.nesting,
  )
end

## The same context for the body of a block or a case arm.
export def with_depth(e: Env, depth: Int) -> Env
  return Env(
    tokens: e.tokens,
    size: e.size,
    allow_blocks: e.allow_blocks,
    depth: depth,
    brace_at: e.brace_at,
    brace_form: e.brace_form,
    nesting: e.nesting,
  )
end

## The context for the body of a do block, remembering a `{` that follows the block head.
export def with_block_body(e: Env, brace_at: Int, brace_form: String) -> Env
  return Env(
    tokens: e.tokens,
    size: e.size,
    allow_blocks: true,
    depth: 1,
    brace_at: brace_at,
    brace_form: brace_form,
    nesting: e.nesting,
  )
end

## The kind of the token at an index. Like src/parser.rkt, an index past the end reads the last token (EOF).
export def kind_at(e: Env, index: Int) -> String
  if index < e.size
    return e.tokens[index].kind
  end
  return e.tokens[e.size - 1].kind
end

## True for the name of a module constant: capitals, digits and `_`, starting with a capital, at least two characters
## (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE). The lexer makes every such name a type-name token; this tells it from a CamelCase type.
## src/ast.rkt has the same test (constant-name?).
export def constant_name?(text: String) -> Bool
  codes = text.split("").map do |character| String.code(character) end
  if codes.size < 2 or codes[0] < 65 or codes[0] > 90
    return false
  end
  index = 1
  while index < codes.size
    code = codes[index]
    if !((code >= 65 and code <= 90) or (code >= 48 and code <= 57) or code == 95)
      return false
    end
    index += 1
  end
  return true
end

## The span from the start of the token at start to the end of the last token before pos, that is, the last consumed
## token.
export def span_from(e: Env, start: Int, pos: Int) -> Source.Span
  return Source.Span(start: e.tokens[start].span.start, stop: e.tokens[pos - 1].span.stop)
end

## How a token is named in "found ..." messages. This copies the Racket write form of the lexeme on purpose.
export def describe(token: Tokens.Token) -> String
  if token.lexeme == ""
    return token.kind
  end
  if token.kind == "NL"
    return "a newline"
  end
  if token.kind == "interp-middle" or token.kind == "interp-end"
    return "\"}\""
  end
  return Unicode.written_text(token.lexeme)
end

## Reads back the failure that pack wrote.
export def unpack(text: String) -> Diag.Diagnostic
  parts = text.split("\n")
  consumed = 0
  index = 0
  while index < 9
    consumed += parts[index].length + 1
    index += 1
  end
  body = text.slice(consumed, text.length - consumed)
  size = parts[8].to_i!
  help = Diag.Help.NoHelp
  if parts[7] == "1"
    help = Diag.Help.Hint(body.slice(size, body.length - size))
  end
  start = Source.Position(offset: parts[1].to_i!, line: parts[2].to_i!, column: parts[3].to_i!)
  stop = Source.Position(offset: parts[4].to_i!, line: parts[5].to_i!, column: parts[6].to_i!)
  return Diag.fail(parts[0], body.slice(0, size), Source.Span(start: start, stop: stop), help)
end

## A help text.
export def hint(text: String) -> Diag.Help
  return Diag.Help.Hint(text)
end

## The failure for a span that is not the span of one token.
export def bail_span(code: String, message: String, span: Source.Span, help: Diag.Help) -> String
  return pack(code, message, span, help)
end

## The failure for the token at at. A doc comment token always gives PARSE-DETACHED-DOC, except for
## PARSE-MISSING-BLANK-LINE, as in src/parser.rkt.
export def bail(e: Env, at: Int, code: String, message: String, help: Diag.Help) -> String
  token = e.tokens[at]
  if token.kind == "DOC" and code != "PARSE-MISSING-BLANK-LINE"
    return detached_doc(token)
  end
  return pack(code, message, token.span, help)
end

## The PARSE-DETACHED-DOC failure for the doc token at at.
export def bail_detached(e: Env, at: Int) -> String
  return detached_doc(e.tokens[at])
end

## A PARSE-UNEXPECTED-TOKEN failure without help.
export def unexpected(e: Env, at: Int, message: String) -> String
  return bail(e, at, "PARSE-UNEXPECTED-TOKEN", message, Diag.Help.NoHelp)
end

## A PARSE-UNEXPECTED-TOKEN failure with a help text.
export def unexpected_help(e: Env, at: Int, message: String, help: String) -> String
  return bail(e, at, "PARSE-UNEXPECTED-TOKEN", message, hint(help))
end

## "expected X, found Y" for the token at at.
export def found(e: Env, at: Int, expected: String) -> String
  return unexpected(e, at, "expected #{expected}, found #{describe(e.tokens[at])}")
end

## The context `levels` deeper than e; PARSE-TOO-DEEP when that passes nesting_limit. enter adds one level, deepen adds
## the k links of a chain so far.
export def deepen(e: Env, pos: Int, levels: Int) -> Result[Env]
  if e.nesting + levels > nesting_limit()
    return error(too_deep(e, pos))
  end
  return ok(
    Env(
      tokens: e.tokens,
      size: e.size,
      allow_blocks: e.allow_blocks,
      depth: e.depth,
      brace_at: e.brace_at,
      brace_form: e.brace_form,
      nesting: e.nesting + levels,
    ),
  )
end

## Counts one more level of nesting; PARSE-TOO-DEEP when that passes nesting_limit.
export def enter(e: Env, pos: Int) -> Result[Env]
  return deepen(e, pos, 1)
end

## A failure for a state the grammar functions cannot reach, so that no code path needs a bare string error:
## PARSE-UNEXPECTED-TOKEN at the token at pos.
export def impossible(e: Env, pos: Int) -> String
  return unexpected(e, pos, "the parser cannot continue at #{describe(e.tokens[pos])}")
end

## True for a name token without a ? or ! suffix: the names of fields, parameters and bindings.
export def plain_name?(token: Tokens.Token) -> Bool
  return token.kind == "name" and !decorated?(token.lexeme)
end

## The position after the token at pos when it has the kind. A name that ends in ? or ! is refused unless suffix is
## true, which only function and method names allow.
export def expect(e: Env, pos: Int, kind: String, description: String, suffix: Bool) -> Result[Int]
  token = e.tokens[pos]
  if token.kind == kind and !(kind == "name" and !suffix and decorated?(token.lexeme))
    return ok(pos + 1)
  end
  return error(found(e, pos, description))
end

## The position of the first token at or after pos that is not NL.
export def skip_newlines(e: Env, pos: Int) -> Int
  cursor = pos
  while e.tokens[cursor].kind == "NL"
    cursor += 1
  end
  return cursor
end

## The text of a token whose value is a string.
export def token_text(token: Tokens.Token) -> String
  case token.value
    Tokens.Value.Text(text) -> return text
    _ -> return ""
  end
end

## The literal value of an integer, float or string token.
export def literal_value(token: Tokens.Token) -> Ast.LitValue
  case token.value
    Tokens.Value.Whole(number) -> return Ast.LitValue.Whole(number)
    Tokens.Value.Huge(digits) -> return Ast.LitValue.Huge(digits)
    Tokens.Value.Real(number) -> return Ast.LitValue.Real(number)
    Tokens.Value.Text(text) -> return Ast.LitValue.Text(text)
    _ -> return Ast.LitValue.Nothing
  end
end

## Parses a type: Name, Mod.Name, or Name[Type, ...].
export def parse_type(e: Env, pos: Int, ids: Int) -> Result[TypeAt]
  inner = try enter(e, pos)
  name = e.tokens[pos].lexeme
  cursor = try expect(e, pos, "type-name", "a type name", false)
  if is_kind(e, cursor, "dot")
    stop = try expect(e, cursor + 1, "type-name", "an imported type name", false)
    name = "#{name}.#{e.tokens[cursor + 1].lexeme}"
    cursor = stop
  end
  args: List[Ast.TypeRef] = []
  next_id = ids
  if is_kind(e, cursor, "left-bracket")
    first = try parse_type(inner, cursor + 1, next_id)
    args = args.push(first.node)
    cursor = first.pos
    next_id = first.ids
    while is_kind(e, cursor, "comma")
      more = try parse_type(inner, cursor + 1, next_id)
      args = args.push(more.node)
      cursor = more.pos
      next_id = more.ids
    end
    cursor = try expect(e, cursor, "right-bracket", "\"]\"", false)
  end
  node = Ast.TypeRef(id: next_id, name: name, args: args, span: span_from(e, pos, cursor))
  return ok(TypeAt(node: node, pos: cursor, ids: next_id + 1))
end

## Parses the pattern of a case arm.
export def parse_pattern(e: Env, pos: Int, ids: Int) -> Result[PatternAt]
  token = e.tokens[pos]
  kind = token.kind
  if kind == "name"
    return parse_name_pattern(e, pos, ids)
  end
  if kind == "integer" or kind == "float" or kind == "string"
    return literal_pattern(e, ids, literal_value(token), pos, pos + 1)
  end
  if kind == "true" or kind == "false"
    return literal_pattern(e, ids, Ast.LitValue.Flag(kind == "true"), pos, pos + 1)
  end
  if kind == "nil"
    return literal_pattern(e, ids, Ast.LitValue.Nothing, pos, pos + 1)
  end
  if kind == "minus"
    number = e.tokens[pos + 1]
    if number.kind != "integer" and number.kind != "float"
      return error(unexpected(e, pos + 1, "expected a number after - in a pattern"))
    end
    return literal_pattern(e, ids, negated(literal_value(number)), pos, pos + 2)
  end
  if kind == "type-name"
    return parse_variant_pattern(e, pos, ids)
  end
  return error(unexpected(e, pos, "expected a pattern"))
end

## Whether the tokens at pos start a case arm, that is, a pattern followed by ->. A case body ends there, because arms
## have no closing token.
export def case_arm_start?(e: Env, pos: Int) -> Bool
  stop = pattern_end(e, pos)
  return stop >= 0 and kind_at(e, stop) == "arrow"
end

def is_kind(e: Env, pos: Int, kind: String) -> Bool
  return e.tokens[pos].kind == kind
end

# A Result error is a String, so the diagnostic travels packed: the code, the six numbers of the span, a help flag, the
# length of the message, then the message followed by the help.
def pack(code: String, message: String, span: Source.Span, help: Diag.Help) -> String
  numbers = [span.start.offset, span.start.line, span.start.column, span.stop.offset, span.stop.line, span.stop.column]
  fields = numbers.map do |number| number.to_s end
  rest = message
  flag = "0"
  case help
    Diag.Help.Hint(text) ->
      rest = message + text
      flag = "1"
    Diag.Help.NoHelp -> flag = "0"
  end
  return "#{code}\n#{fields.join("\n")}\n#{flag}\n#{message.length}\n#{rest}"
end

def detached_doc(token: Tokens.Token) -> String
  return pack(
    "PARSE-DETACHED-DOC",
    "a doc comment must be followed by a declaration, field or variant on the next line",
    token.span,
    hint(
      (
        "put the doc block directly above the declaration, field or variant it documents; " +
        "use # for a note that documents nothing"
      ),
    ),
  )
end

# The PARSE-TOO-DEEP failure at the token at pos.
def too_deep(e: Env, pos: Int) -> String
  return bail(
    e,
    pos,
    "PARSE-TOO-DEEP",
    "nesting is deeper than #{nesting_limit()} levels",
    hint("split the code into smaller functions or simpler expressions"),
  )
end

def decorated?(lexeme: String) -> Bool
  return lexeme.ends_with?("?") or lexeme.ends_with?("!")
end

# A binding of `_` is Absent, as the Racket parser keeps #f.
def binding_name(e: Env, pos: Int) -> Result[Ast.Optional[String]]
  advanced = try expect(e, pos, "name", "a pattern binding or _", false)
  lexeme = e.tokens[pos].lexeme
  if lexeme == "_"
    return ok(Ast.Optional.Absent)
  end
  return ok(Ast.Optional.Present(lexeme))
end

def parse_pattern_bindings(e: Env, pos: Int, empty_help: String) -> Result[BindingsAt]
  if is_kind(e, pos + 1, "right-paren")
    return error(unexpected_help(e, pos + 1, "a pattern with parentheses needs a binding or _", empty_help))
  end
  names: List[Ast.Optional[String]] = []
  cursor = pos + 1
  names = names.push(try binding_name(e, cursor))
  cursor += 1
  while is_kind(e, cursor, "comma")
    names = names.push(try binding_name(e, cursor + 1))
    cursor += 2
  end
  cursor = try expect(e, cursor, "right-paren", ")", false)
  return ok(BindingsAt(names: names, pos: cursor))
end

def pattern_node(
  e: Env,
  id: Int,
  enum_name: String,
  variant_name: String,
  bindings: List[Ast.Optional[String]],
  start: Int,
  cursor: Int,
) -> Ast.Pattern
  return Ast.Pattern.Variant(
    Ast.VariantPattern(
      id: id,
      enum_name: enum_name,
      variant_name: variant_name,
      bindings: bindings,
      span: span_from(e, start, cursor),
    ),
  )
end

# A negative literal pattern is a single literal with the negated value (an Int too big for Int keeps its digits).
def literal_pattern(e: Env, ids: Int, value: Ast.LitValue, start: Int, cursor: Int) -> Result[PatternAt]
  node = Ast.Pattern.Literal(Ast.LiteralPattern(id: ids, value: value, span: span_from(e, start, cursor)))
  return ok(PatternAt(node: node, pos: cursor, ids: ids + 1))
end

def negated(value: Ast.LitValue) -> Ast.LitValue
  case value
    Ast.LitValue.Whole(number) -> return Ast.LitValue.Whole(0 - number)
    Ast.LitValue.Huge(digits) -> return Ast.LitValue.Huge("-#{digits}")
    Ast.LitValue.Real(number) -> return Ast.LitValue.Real(-number)
    _ -> return value
  end
end

def parse_name_pattern(e: Env, pos: Int, ids: Int) -> Result[PatternAt]
  token = e.tokens[pos]
  lexeme = token.lexeme
  if lexeme == "_"
    node = Ast.Pattern.Wildcard(Ast.WildcardPattern(id: ids, span: token.span))
    return ok(PatternAt(node: node, pos: pos + 1, ids: ids + 1))
  end
  if (lexeme == "ok" or lexeme == "error") and is_kind(e, pos + 1, "left-paren")
    parsed = try parse_pattern_bindings(e, pos + 1, "write #{lexeme}(_) to match without binding the value")
    variant = "Err"
    if lexeme == "ok"
      variant = "Ok"
    end
    node = pattern_node(e, ids, "Result", variant, parsed.names, pos, parsed.pos)
    return ok(PatternAt(node: node, pos: parsed.pos, ids: ids + 1))
  end
  if lexeme == "when"
    return error(
      unexpected_help(
        e,
        pos,
        "expected a pattern, found \"when\"",
        "case arms have no when: write the pattern and ->, as in 1 -> puts(\"one\")",
      ),
    )
  end
  return error(unexpected(e, pos, "expected a pattern"))
end

def variant_help(enum_name: String, variant_name: String) -> String
  if enum_name == "Result" or (enum_name == "Await" and variant_name == "Done")
    return "write #{enum_name}.#{variant_name}(_) to match without binding the value"
  end
  return "a variant without payload has no parentheses: #{enum_name}.#{variant_name}"
end

def parse_variant_pattern(e: Env, pos: Int, ids: Int) -> Result[PatternAt]
  if !is_kind(e, pos + 1, "dot") and constant_name?(e.tokens[pos].lexeme)
    return error(
      unexpected_help(
        e,
        pos + 1,
        "expected a dot between an enum and variant, found #{describe(e.tokens[pos + 1])}",
        "a constant is not a pattern; compare with if",
      ),
    )
  end
  cursor = try expect(e, pos + 1, "dot", "a dot between an enum and variant", false)
  after = try expect(e, cursor, "type-name", "a variant name", false)
  enum_name = e.tokens[pos].lexeme
  variant_name = e.tokens[cursor].lexeme
  cursor = after
  if is_kind(e, cursor, "dot")
    last = try expect(e, cursor + 1, "type-name", "a variant name", false)
    enum_name = "#{enum_name}.#{variant_name}"
    variant_name = e.tokens[cursor + 1].lexeme
    cursor = last
  end
  bindings: List[Ast.Optional[String]] = []
  if is_kind(e, cursor, "left-paren")
    parsed = try parse_pattern_bindings(e, cursor, variant_help(enum_name, variant_name))
    bindings = parsed.names
    cursor = parsed.pos
  end
  node = pattern_node(e, ids, enum_name, variant_name, bindings, pos, cursor)
  return ok(PatternAt(node: node, pos: cursor, ids: ids + 1))
end

# The case_arm_start? helpers look ahead without consuming, like case-arm-start? of src/parser.rkt: they return the
# index after the pattern, or -1.
def binders_end(e: Env, at: Int) -> Int
  cursor = at + 1
  while kind_at(e, cursor) == "name"
    if kind_at(e, cursor + 1) == "comma"
      cursor += 2
    elsif kind_at(e, cursor + 1) == "right-paren"
      return cursor + 2
    else
      return -1
    end
  end
  return -1
end

def variant_end(e: Env, index: Int) -> Int
  at = index + 1
  segments = 1
  while kind_at(e, at) == "dot"
    if segments >= 3 or kind_at(e, at + 1) != "type-name"
      return -1
    end
    at += 2
    segments += 1
  end
  if segments < 2
    return -1
  end
  if kind_at(e, at) == "left-paren"
    return binders_end(e, at)
  end
  return at
end

def pattern_end(e: Env, start: Int) -> Int
  token = e.tokens[start]
  kind = token.kind
  if kind == "name"
    if token.lexeme == "_"
      return start + 1
    end
    if (token.lexeme == "ok" or token.lexeme == "error") and kind_at(e, start + 1) == "left-paren"
      return binders_end(e, start + 1)
    end
    return -1
  end
  if kind == "integer" or kind == "float" or kind == "string" or kind == "true" or kind == "false" or kind == "nil"
    return start + 1
  end
  if kind == "minus"
    following = kind_at(e, start + 1)
    if following == "integer" or following == "float"
      return start + 2
    end
    return -1
  end
  if kind == "type-name"
    return variant_end(e, start)
  end
  return -1
end
compiler/parse_text.agc:
## The text form of a parse, for tests. See parse_text.

import Ast from "ast"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Lexer from "lexer"
import Parser from "parser"
import Source from "source"
import Text from "text"

## The text form of a parse and the first node id the next file can use (first_id again when the parse failed).
export struct Printed
  text: String
  next_id: Int
end

## Where a line is printed: its indent, the number subtracted from every node id, and the text added at the end of the
## line of a node, by the node's id (the checker's text form adds the type of each expression this way). A file of a
## linked program prints ids that start at 0 inside the file, so the text does not depend on which files came before
## it.
export struct Margin
  indent: String
  base: Int
  notes: Map[Int, String]
end

## Lexes and parses a file and returns the text form of the tree, or the ERROR line of the first diagnostic. One node
## per line: `role: kind #id span attributes`, children indented by two spaces. tests/frontend-parser-common.rkt prints
## the same text from the Racket tree.
export def parse_text(text: String) -> String
  return parse_text_from(text, 0)
end

## Like parse_text, with the ids of the nodes starting at first_id.
export def parse_text_from(text: String, first_id: Int) -> String
  return print_from(text, first_id).text
end

## Like parse_text_from, and also gives Ast.next_free_id of the Program, so the next file can continue the numbering.
export def print_from(text: String, first_id: Int) -> Printed
  case Lexer.lex(text)
    Diag.Outcome.Failed(problem) -> return Printed(text: Text.diagnostic_line(problem), next_id: first_id)
    Diag.Outcome.Done(tokens) ->
      case Parser.parse(tokens, first_id)
        Diag.Outcome.Failed(problem) -> return Printed(text: Text.diagnostic_line(problem), next_id: first_id)
        Diag.Outcome.Done(program) -> return Printed(
          text: print_program(program).join("\n"),
          next_id: Ast.next_free_id(program),
        )
      end
  end
end

## The margin one level deeper.
export def deeper(at: Margin) -> Margin
  return at.with(indent: "#{at.indent}  ")
end

## The first line of a node: the indent, the role if there is one (the root has none), the kind, the id relative to the
## margin, the span and the attributes.
export def head(at: Margin, role: String, kind: String, id: Int, span: Source.Span, attrs: String) -> String
  label = ""
  if role != ""
    label = "#{role}: "
  end
  note = at.notes.get(id)
  extra = ""
  if note.ok?
    extra = note.unwrap!
  end
  # "##{...}" writes a literal "#" and then the node number relative to the base, such as: Foo #3 1:1-1:4
  return "#{at.indent}#{label}#{kind} ##{id - at.base} #{Text.span_text(span)}#{attrs}#{extra}"
end

## The label followed by the quoted text of an optional string, or the empty string when it is absent.
export def text_attr(label: String, doc: Ast.Optional[String]) -> String
  case doc
    Ast.Optional.Present(text) -> return label + Text.quote(text)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return ""
  end
end

## Prints a declaration and everything under it, one line per node, after the lines already in out.
export def print_decl(out: List[String], at: Margin, role: String, decl: Ast.Decl) -> List[String]
  child = deeper(at)
  case decl
    Ast.Decl.Import(node) -> return out.push(head(at, role, "import-decl", node.id, node.span, import_attrs(node)))
    Ast.Decl.Export(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "export-decl", node.id, node.span, doc_attr(node.doc)))
      return print_decl(lines, child, "declaration", node.declaration)
    Ast.Decl.Function(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "function-decl", node.id, node.span, name_attr(node.name) + doc_attr(node.doc)))
      for param in node.params
        lines = print_param(lines, child, param)
      end
      lines = print_type(lines, child, "result", node.result)
      return print_stmts(lines, child, "body", node.body)
    Ast.Decl.Struct(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "struct-decl", node.id, node.span, name_attr(node.name) + doc_attr(node.doc)))
      for field in node.fields
        lines = print_field(lines, child, field)
      end
      return lines
    Ast.Decl.Constant(node) ->
      exported = ""
      if node.exported
        exported = " exported=true"
      end
      lines = out.push(
        head(at, role, "const-decl", node.id, node.span, name_attr(node.name) + exported + doc_attr(node.doc)),
      )
      lines = print_optional_type(lines, child, "type", node.type)
      return print_expr(lines, child, "value", node.value)
    Ast.Decl.Enum(node) ->
      parameters = node.type_parameters.map do |name| Text.quote(name) end
      lines = out.push(
        head(
          at,
          role,
          "enum-decl",
          node.id,
          node.span,
          "#{name_attr(node.name)} type-parameters=#{list_text(parameters)}#{doc_attr(node.doc)}",
        ),
      )
      for variant in node.variants
        lines = print_variant(lines, child, variant)
      end
      return lines
  end
end

def doc_attr(doc: Ast.Optional[String]) -> String
  return text_attr(" doc=", doc)
end

def name_attr(name: String) -> String
  return " name=#{Text.quote(name)}"
end

def value_text(value: Ast.LitValue) -> String
  case value
    Ast.LitValue.Whole(number) -> return "int:#{number}"
    Ast.LitValue.Huge(digits) -> return "int:#{digits}"
    Ast.LitValue.Real(number) -> return "float:bits:#{Float.to_bits(number)}"
    Ast.LitValue.Text(text) -> return "string:#{Text.quote(text)}"
    Ast.LitValue.Flag(flag) -> return "bool:#{flag}"
    Ast.LitValue.Nothing -> return "nil"
  end
end

def visible_attr(visible: Ast.Optional[List[String]]) -> String
  case visible
    Ast.Optional.Present(names) ->
      quoted = names.map do |name| Text.quote(name) end
      return " visible=#{list_text(quoted)}"
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return ""
  end
end

def list_text(items: List[String]) -> String
  return "[#{items.join(",")}]"
end

def print_type(out: List[String], at: Margin, role: String, type: Ast.TypeRef) -> List[String]
  lines = out.push(head(at, role, "type-ref", type.id, type.span, name_attr(type.name)))
  return print_types(lines, deeper(at), "arg", type.args)
end

def print_types(out: List[String], at: Margin, role: String, types: List[Ast.TypeRef]) -> List[String]
  lines = out
  for type in types
    lines = print_type(lines, at, role, type)
  end
  return lines
end

def print_optional_type(out: List[String], at: Margin, role: String, type: Ast.Optional[Ast.TypeRef]) -> List[String]
  case type
    Ast.Optional.Present(found) -> return print_type(out, at, role, found)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return out
  end
end

def print_exprs(out: List[String], at: Margin, role: String, items: List[Ast.Expr]) -> List[String]
  lines = out
  for item in items
    lines = print_expr(lines, at, role, item)
  end
  return lines
end

def print_stmts(out: List[String], at: Margin, role: String, items: List[Ast.Stmt]) -> List[String]
  lines = out
  for item in items
    lines = print_stmt(lines, at, role, item)
  end
  return lines
end

def print_named_args(out: List[String], at: Margin, items: List[Ast.NamedArg]) -> List[String]
  lines = out
  for item in items
    lines = out_named(lines, at, item)
  end
  return lines
end

def out_named(out: List[String], at: Margin, item: Ast.NamedArg) -> List[String]
  lines = out.push(head(at, "arg", "named-arg", item.id, item.span, name_attr(item.name)))
  return print_expr(lines, deeper(at), "value", item.value)
end

def print_part(out: List[String], at: Margin, part: Ast.Part) -> List[String]
  case part
    Ast.Part.Text(text) -> return out.push("#{at.indent}part: text #{Text.quote(text)}")
    Ast.Part.Code(code) -> return print_expr(out, at, "part", code)
  end
end

def print_block_param(out: List[String], at: Margin, param: Ast.BlockParam) -> List[String]
  lines = out.push(head(at, "param", "block-param", param.id, param.span, name_attr(param.name)))
  return print_optional_type(lines, deeper(at), "type", param.type)
end

def print_map_entry(out: List[String], at: Margin, entry: Ast.MapEntry) -> List[String]
  lines = out.push(head(at, "entry", "map-entry", entry.id, entry.span, ""))
  lines = print_expr(lines, deeper(at), "key", entry.key)
  return print_expr(lines, deeper(at), "value", entry.value)
end

def op_attrs(op: String, op_span: Source.Span) -> String
  return " op=#{op} op-span=#{Text.span_text(op_span)}"
end

def print_call_like(
  out: List[String],
  at: Margin,
  role: String,
  kind: String,
  id: Int,
  span: Source.Span,
  attrs: String,
  args: List[Ast.Expr],
) -> List[String]
  lines = out.push(head(at, role, kind, id, span, attrs))
  return print_exprs(lines, deeper(at), "arg", args)
end

def print_expr(out: List[String], at: Margin, role: String, expr: Ast.Expr) -> List[String]
  child = deeper(at)
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.Literal(node) -> return out.push(
      head(at, role, "literal", node.id, node.span, " value=#{value_text(node.value)}"),
    )
    Ast.Expr.Name(node) -> return out.push(head(at, role, "name-ref", node.id, node.span, name_attr(node.name)))
    Ast.Expr.TypeName(node) -> return out.push(
      head(at, role, "type-expression", node.id, node.span, name_attr(node.name)),
    )
    Ast.Expr.ConstRef(node) -> return out.push(head(at, role, "const-ref", node.id, node.span, name_attr(node.name)))
    Ast.Expr.FunctionRef(node) -> return out.push(
      head(at, role, "function-ref", node.id, node.span, name_attr(node.name)),
    )
    Ast.Expr.Call(node) -> return print_call_like(
      out,
      at,
      role,
      "call",
      node.id,
      node.span,
      "#{name_attr(node.name)} piped=#{node.piped}",
      node.args,
    )
    Ast.Expr.EnumConstructor(node) ->
      lines = print_call_like(
        out,
        at,
        role,
        "enum-constructor",
        node.id,
        node.span,
        " enum=#{Text.quote(node.enum_name)} variant=#{Text.quote(node.variant_name)}",
        node.args,
      )
      return print_named_args(lines, child, node.named)
    Ast.Expr.Invoke(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "invoke", node.id, node.span, ""))
      lines = print_expr(lines, child, "target", node.target)
      return print_exprs(lines, child, "arg", node.args)
    Ast.Expr.Construct(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "construct", node.id, node.span, " type=#{Text.quote(node.type_name)}"))
      return print_named_args(lines, child, node.args)
    Ast.Expr.Update(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "struct-update", node.id, node.span, visible_attr(node.visible)))
      lines = print_expr(lines, child, "target", node.target)
      return print_named_args(lines, child, node.args)
    _ -> return print_container_expr(out, at, role, expr)
  end
end

def print_container_expr(out: List[String], at: Margin, role: String, expr: Ast.Expr) -> List[String]
  child = deeper(at)
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.ListLit(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "list-lit", node.id, node.span, ""))
      return print_exprs(lines, child, "element", node.elements)
    Ast.Expr.MapLit(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "map-lit", node.id, node.span, ""))
      for entry in node.entries
        lines = print_map_entry(lines, child, entry)
      end
      return lines
    Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "field-access", node.id, node.span, name_attr(node.name)))
      return print_expr(lines, child, "target", node.target)
    Ast.Expr.MethodCall(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "method-call", node.id, node.span, name_attr(node.name)))
      lines = print_expr(lines, child, "target", node.target)
      return print_exprs(lines, child, "arg", node.args)
    Ast.Expr.Interpolation(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "interpolation", node.id, node.span, ""))
      for part in node.parts
        lines = print_part(lines, child, part)
      end
      return lines
    Ast.Expr.BlockLit(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "block-lit", node.id, node.span, ""))
      for param in node.params
        lines = print_block_param(lines, child, param)
      end
      return print_stmts(lines, child, "body", node.body)
    Ast.Expr.Index(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "index-access", node.id, node.span, ""))
      lines = print_expr(lines, child, "target", node.target)
      return print_expr(lines, child, "index", node.index)
    Ast.Expr.Try(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "try-expr", node.id, node.span, ""))
      return print_expr(lines, child, "operand", node.operand)
    Ast.Expr.Unary(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "unary", node.id, node.span, op_attrs(node.op, node.op_span)))
      return print_expr(lines, child, "operand", node.operand)
    Ast.Expr.Binary(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "binary", node.id, node.span, op_attrs(node.op, node.op_span)))
      lines = print_expr(lines, child, "left", node.left)
      return print_expr(lines, child, "right", node.right)
    # print_expr handles every other variant before it calls this one.
    _ -> return out
  end
end

def print_pattern(out: List[String], at: Margin, role: String, pattern: Ast.Pattern) -> List[String]
  case pattern
    Ast.Pattern.Wildcard(node) -> return out.push(head(at, role, "wildcard-pattern", node.id, node.span, ""))
    Ast.Pattern.Literal(node) -> return out.push(
      head(at, role, "literal-pattern", node.id, node.span, " value=#{value_text(node.value)}"),
    )
    Ast.Pattern.Variant(node) ->
      names = node.bindings.map do |binding| binding_text(binding) end
      return out.push(
        head(
          at,
          role,
          "variant-pattern",
          node.id,
          node.span,
          " enum=#{Text.quote(node.enum_name)} variant=#{Text.quote(node.variant_name)} bindings=#{list_text(names)}",
        ),
      )
  end
end

def binding_text(binding: Ast.Optional[String]) -> String
  case binding
    Ast.Optional.Present(name) -> return Text.quote(name)
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return "-"
  end
end

def print_branch(out: List[String], at: Margin, branch: Ast.IfBranch) -> List[String]
  lines = out.push(head(at, "branch", "if-branch", branch.id, branch.span, ""))
  lines = print_expr(lines, deeper(at), "condition", branch.condition)
  return print_stmts(lines, deeper(at), "body", branch.body)
end

def print_arm(out: List[String], at: Margin, arm: Ast.CaseArm) -> List[String]
  lines = out.push(head(at, "arm", "case-arm", arm.id, arm.span, ""))
  lines = print_pattern(lines, deeper(at), "pattern", arm.pattern)
  return print_stmts(lines, deeper(at), "body", arm.body)
end

def print_stmt(out: List[String], at: Margin, role: String, stmt: Ast.Stmt) -> List[String]
  child = deeper(at)
  case stmt
    Ast.Stmt.Binding(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "binding", node.id, node.span, name_attr(node.name)))
      lines = print_optional_type(lines, child, "type", node.type)
      return print_expr(lines, child, "value", node.value)
    Ast.Stmt.Return(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "return-stmt", node.id, node.span, ""))
      case node.value
        Ast.Optional.Present(value) -> return print_expr(lines, child, "value", value)
        Ast.Optional.Absent -> return lines
      end
    Ast.Stmt.Expression(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "expr-stmt", node.id, node.span, ""))
      return print_expr(lines, child, "value", node.value)
    Ast.Stmt.If(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "if-stmt", node.id, node.span, ""))
      for branch in node.branches
        lines = print_branch(lines, child, branch)
      end
      case node.else_body
        Ast.Optional.Present(body) ->
          lines = lines.push("#{child.indent}else:")
          return print_stmts(lines, deeper(child), "body", body)
        Ast.Optional.Absent -> return lines
      end
    Ast.Stmt.While(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "while-stmt", node.id, node.span, ""))
      lines = print_expr(lines, child, "condition", node.condition)
      return print_stmts(lines, child, "body", node.body)
    Ast.Stmt.For(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "for-stmt", node.id, node.span, " variable=#{Text.quote(node.variable)}"))
      lines = print_expr(lines, child, "iterable", node.iterable)
      return print_stmts(lines, child, "body", node.body)
    Ast.Stmt.Control(node) -> return out.push(head(at, role, "loop-control", node.id, node.span, " kind=#{node.kind}"))
    Ast.Stmt.Case(node) ->
      lines = out.push(head(at, role, "case-stmt", node.id, node.span, ""))
      lines = print_expr(lines, child, "value", node.value)
      for arm in node.arms
        lines = print_arm(lines, child, arm)
      end
      return lines
  end
end

def print_param(out: List[String], at: Margin, param: Ast.Param) -> List[String]
  lines = out.push(head(at, "param", "param", param.id, param.span, name_attr(param.name)))
  return print_type(lines, deeper(at), "type", param.type)
end

def print_field(out: List[String], at: Margin, field: Ast.FieldDecl) -> List[String]
  lines = out.push(head(at, "field", "field-decl", field.id, field.span, name_attr(field.name) + doc_attr(field.doc)))
  return print_type(lines, deeper(at), "type", field.type)
end

def print_variant(out: List[String], at: Margin, variant: Ast.EnumVariant) -> List[String]
  lines = out.push(
    head(at, "variant", "enum-variant", variant.id, variant.span, name_attr(variant.name) + doc_attr(variant.doc)),
  )
  return print_types(lines, deeper(at), "payload", variant.payload_types)
end

def print_program(program: Ast.Program) -> List[String]
  lines: List[String] = [
    head(
      Margin(indent: "", base: 0, notes: {}),
      "",
      "program",
      program.id,
      program.span,
      text_attr(" module-doc=", program.module_doc),
    ),
  ]
  for decl in program.declarations
    lines = print_decl(lines, Margin(indent: "  ", base: 0, notes: {}), "declaration", decl)
  end
  return lines
end

# ` path="x" alias="Mod"`, or ` path="x" names=[...]` with each name and its span, and `as` with the local name for a
# rename.
def import_attrs(node: Ast.ImportDecl) -> String
  case node.alias
    Ast.Optional.Present(alias) -> return " path=#{Text.quote(node.path)} alias=#{Text.quote(alias)}"
    Ast.Optional.Absent ->
      texts = node.names.map do |entry| import_name_text(entry) end
      return " path=#{Text.quote(node.path)} names=[#{texts.join(",")}]"
  end
end

def import_name_text(entry: Ast.ImportName) -> String
  text = "#{Text.quote(entry.name)}@#{Text.span_text(entry.span)}"
  if entry.local != entry.name
    text += " as #{Text.quote(entry.local)}@#{Text.span_text(entry.local_span)}"
  end
  return text
end
compiler/parser.agc:
## The Agentica parser: a port of src/parser.rkt, with the same tree, the same spans and the same first diagnostic.
##
## It is a recursive descent parser. Every function takes the context (Env, parse_base.agc), a position and the next
## free node id, and returns a Result: the node, the next position and id, or the packed diagnostic. The grammar
## functions mirror the ones of the Racket parser; the differences are listed where they are made: precedence climbing
## for the binary operators, ids assigned at construction, and the nesting limit.

import Ast from "ast"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Base from "parse_base"
import Tokens from "token"

# A declaration with the next position and the next free node id.
struct DeclAt
  node: Ast.Decl
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

struct DocAt
  doc: Ast.Optional[String]
  pos: Int
end

struct ImportNameAt
  node: Ast.ImportName
  pos: Int
end

struct ImportNamesAt
  nodes: List[Ast.ImportName]
  pos: Int
end

struct BlockParamsAt
  params: List[Ast.BlockParam]
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

struct NamedArgsAt
  nodes: List[Ast.NamedArg]
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

struct MapEntryAt
  node: Ast.MapEntry
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

struct IfBranchAt
  node: Ast.IfBranch
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

struct ParamsAt
  nodes: List[Ast.Param]
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

struct FieldAt
  node: Ast.FieldDecl
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

struct VariantAt
  node: Ast.EnumVariant
  pos: Int
  ids: Int
end

struct TypeParametersAt
  names: List[String]
  pos: Int
end

## Parses the tokens of the lexer into a Program, or returns the first PARSE- diagnostic. It stops at the first error
## and never fails otherwise. The nodes are numbered in post-order from first_id (see ast.agc), so that the modules of
## one program can share one numbering: start the next file at Ast.next_free_id(program).
export def parse(tokens: List[Tokens.Token], first_id: Int) -> Diag.Outcome[Ast.Program]
  case parse_program(Base.make_env(tokens), first_id)
    ok(program) -> return Diag.Outcome.Done(program)
    error(text) -> return Diag.Outcome.Failed(Base.unpack(text))
  end
end

def brace_help(form: String) -> String
  return "blocks have no braces: write \"#{form}\" ... \"end\""
end

# The newline that ends the head of a def, if, case, while or for. A `{` here gets the help that blocks have no braces.
def expect_head_end(e: Base.Env, pos: Int, description: String, form: String) -> Result[Int]
  if e.tokens[pos].kind == "left-brace"
    return error(
      Base.unexpected_help(
        e,
        pos,
        "expected #{description}, found #{Base.describe(e.tokens[pos])}",
        brace_help(form),
      ),
    )
  end
  return Base.expect(e, pos, "NL", description, false)
end

# Inside a do block body a statement may also end at `end` on the same line; the end is not consumed
# (expect_statement_end).
def statement_end?(e: Base.Env, pos: Int) -> Bool
  kind = e.tokens[pos].kind
  return kind == "NL" or (e.depth > 0 and kind == "end")
end

def expect_statement_end(e: Base.Env, pos: Int, description: String) -> Result[Int]
  token = e.tokens[pos]
  if token.kind == "if" or token.kind == "while"
    return error(
      Base.unexpected_help(
        e,
        pos,
        "expected a newline after the statement, found #{Base.describe(token)}",
        "there are no #{token.lexeme} modifiers: put the statement inside #{token.lexeme} cond ... end",
      ),
    )
  end
  if e.depth > 0 and token.kind == "end"
    return ok(pos)
  end
  return Base.expect(e, pos, "NL", description, false)
end

def expect_end(e: Base.Env, pos: Int) -> Result[Int]
  kind = e.tokens[pos].kind
  if kind == "end"
    return ok(pos + 1)
  end
  if kind == "EOF"
    return error(Base.bail(e, pos, "PARSE-UNCLOSED-BLOCK", "unclosed block, expected \"end\"", Diag.Help.NoHelp))
  end
  return error(Base.found(e, pos, "\"end\""))
end

# The binding level of a binary operator, 0 for a token that is not one. 1 or, 2 and, 3 equality, 4 comparison, 5 |>,
# 6 + -, 7 * / %.
def level_of(kind: String) -> Int
  case kind
    "or" -> return 1
    "and" -> return 2
    "equal" -> return 3
    "not-equal" -> return 3
    "less" -> return 4
    "less-equal" -> return 4
    "greater" -> return 4
    "greater-equal" -> return 4
    "pipe-forward" -> return 5
    "plus" -> return 6
    "minus" -> return 6
    "multiply" -> return 7
    "divide" -> return 7
    "modulo" -> return 7
    _ -> return 0
  end
end

def compound_operator(kind: String) -> String
  case kind
    "plus-assign" -> return "plus"
    "minus-assign" -> return "minus"
    "multiply-assign" -> return "multiply"
    "divide-assign" -> return "divide"
    "modulo-assign" -> return "modulo"
    _ -> return ""
  end
end

def expr_at(node: Ast.Expr, pos: Int, ids: Int) -> Result[Base.ExprAt]
  return ok(Base.ExprAt(node: node, pos: pos, ids: ids + 1))
end

def call_node(
  e: Base.Env,
  start: Int,
  name: String,
  args: List[Ast.Expr],
  parenthesized: Bool,
  ids: Int,
  cursor: Int,
) -> Result[Base.ExprAt]
  node = Ast.Expr.Call(
    Ast.Call(
      id: ids,
      name: name,
      args: args,
      piped: false,
      parenthesized: parenthesized,
      span: Base.span_from(e, start, cursor),
    ),
  )
  return expr_at(node, cursor, ids)
end

# Ranges bind loosest and do not chain: a range is parsed here, over operands of level 1 and above.
# Every expression counts one level of nesting.
def parse_expression(e: Base.Env, pos: Int, ids: Int) -> Result[Base.ExprAt]
  inner = try Base.enter(e, pos)
  left = try parse_climb(inner, pos, ids, 1)
  kind = e.tokens[left.pos].kind
  if kind != "dot-dot" and kind != "dot-dot-dot"
    return ok(left)
  end
  right = try parse_climb(inner, left.pos + 1, left.ids, 1)
