# The registry of src/stdlib.rkt is the files of the stdlib/ folder (a test checks that they are the same list).
def standard(settings: Env.Settings, file: String, site: Failure.Site) -> Result[String]
  try Paths.validate_library_path(file, site)
  if !file?(source_path(settings, file))
    return error(io_failure(site, "unknown standard library module"))
  end
  return ok(file)
end

def library(settings: Env.Settings, root_dir: String, file: String, site: Failure.Site) -> Result[String]
  try Paths.validate_library_path(file, site)
  roots = try library_roots(settings, root_dir, site)
  rest = file.slice(4, file.length - 4)
  for root in roots
    candidate = Paths.join(root, rest)
    if file?(candidate)
      return contained(root, candidate, site)
    end
  end
  return error(io_failure(site, "cannot find library module"))
end

# The search roots of pkg/: agc_libs/ next to the root file, AGENTICA_PATH, the user data folder, then the system
# folders. Every AGENTICA_PATH entry must be absolute, whether or not it is used.
def library_roots(settings: Env.Settings, root_dir: String, site: Failure.Site) -> Result[List[String]]
  configured: List[String] = []
  for entry in settings.env.agentica_path.split(":")
    if entry == ""
      next
    end
    if !entry.starts_with?("/")
      return error(
        Failure.fail_at(site, "CHECK-IMPORT-PATH", "AGENTICA_PATH roots must be absolute", Diag.Help.NoHelp),
      )
    end
    configured = configured.push(entry)
  end
  roots = [Paths.join(root_dir, "agc_libs")].concat(configured).concat(user_roots(settings.env))
  return ok(roots.concat(["/usr/local/share/agentica/lib", "/usr/share/agentica/lib"]))
end

# XDG_DATA_HOME when it is absolute, else ~/.local/share. An unset HOME leaves the user root out (Racket asks the
# system for the home folder there).
def user_roots(env: Env.Env) -> List[String]
  if env.xdg_data_home.starts_with?("/")
    return [Paths.join(env.xdg_data_home, "agentica/lib")]
  end
  if env.home == ""
    return []
  end
  return [Paths.join(env.home, ".local/share/agentica/lib")]
end

# Links are resolved before the check, so a link out of the root is refused.
def contained(root: String, candidate: String, site: Failure.Site) -> Result[String]
  base = Path.real(root)
  target = Path.real(candidate)
  if !base.ok? or !target.ok?
    return error(io_failure(site, "cannot resolve import"))
  end
  if !inside?(parts(base.unwrap!), parts(target.unwrap!))
    return error(Failure.fail_at(site, "CHECK-IMPORT-PATH", "library path escapes its root", Diag.Help.NoHelp))
  end
  return ok(target.unwrap!)
end

def parts(path: String) -> List[String]
  return path.split("/").filter do |part| part != "" end
end

def inside?(base: List[String], target: List[String]) -> Bool
  if target.size < base.size
    return false
  end
  for index in 0...base.size
    if base[index] != target[index]
      return false
    end
  end
  return true
end

# The file next to the importing one. Racket's normalize-path accepts a missing last part and refuses a missing folder
# (CHECK-IMPORT-IO "cannot resolve import"); a missing file is found by the read ("cannot read import"), which this
# reports at once.
def relative(key: String, file: String, site: Failure.Site) -> Result[String]
  if file.starts_with?("/") or file.contains?(String.from_code(0))
    return error(io_failure(site, "cannot resolve import"))
  end
  folder = Paths.directory_of(key)
  inner = Paths.directory_of(file)
  if inner != ""
    folder = Paths.join(folder, inner)
  end
  parent = Path.real(folder)
  if !parent.ok? or !directory?(parent.unwrap!)
    return error(io_failure(site, "cannot resolve import"))
  end
  target = Path.real(Paths.join(parent.unwrap!, Paths.last_part(file)))
  if !target.ok?
    return error(io_failure(site, "cannot read import"))
  end
  return ok(target.unwrap!)
end
compiler/rewrite.agc:
## The second half of the linker: rewrites the declarations of one file so that every name is the name of the linked
## program (resolve.agc), and so every file can share one program. This is the rewrite function of src/modules.rkt.
##
## Names are resolved in the order Racket resolves them (a node's own name first, then its parts in field order), so
## the first failure is the same. Nodes keep their ids and spans. The recursion follows the depth of the tree: about
## one VM call per level (rewrite_expr passes to rewrite_compound with a tail call), so trees up to about 9,900 levels
## fit in the limit of 10,000 calls (the parser's nesting limit bounds the calls it makes, not the depth of the tree;
## see ast.agc).

import Ast from "ast"
import Declarations from "declarations"
import Resolve from "resolve"
import Source from "source"

## The declarations of a file in the linked program: its functions, structs and enums without the export, imports left
## out.
export def rewrite_declarations(cx: Resolve.Context) -> Result[List[Ast.Decl]]
  out: List[Ast.Decl] = []
  for wrapped in cx.me.program.declarations
    if !Declarations.import?(Declarations.kind_of(wrapped))
      out = out.push(try rewrite_decl(cx, Declarations.unwrap(wrapped)))
    end
  end
  return ok(out)
end

def rewrite_decl(cx: Resolve.Context, decl: Ast.Decl) -> Result[Ast.Decl]
  case decl
    Ast.Decl.Function(node) -> return rewrite_function(cx, node)
    Ast.Decl.Struct(node) -> return rewrite_struct(cx, node)
    Ast.Decl.Enum(node) -> return rewrite_enum(cx, node)
    Ast.Decl.Constant(node) -> return rewrite_constant(cx, node)
    _ -> return ok(decl)
  end
end

def rewrite_function(cx: Resolve.Context, node: Ast.FunctionDecl) -> Result[Ast.Decl]
  params: List[Ast.Param] = []
  for param in node.params
    params = params.push(param.with(type: try rewrite_type(cx, param.type)))
  end
  result = try rewrite_type(cx, node.result)
  body = try rewrite_stmts(cx, node.body)
  return ok(
    Ast.Decl.Function(node.with(name: Resolve.identity(cx, node.name), params: params, result: result, body: body)),
  )
end

# A constant keeps its place, takes its linked name and loses its export (the linked program has no exports).
def rewrite_constant(cx: Resolve.Context, node: Ast.ConstDecl) -> Result[Ast.Decl]
  type = try rewrite_optional_type(cx, node.type)
  value = try rewrite_expr(cx, node.value)
  return ok(
    Ast.Decl.Constant(node.with(name: Resolve.identity(cx, node.name), type: type, value: value, exported: false)),
  )
end

def rewrite_struct(cx: Resolve.Context, node: Ast.StructDecl) -> Result[Ast.Decl]
  fields: List[Ast.FieldDecl] = []
  for field in node.fields
    fields = fields.push(field.with(type: try rewrite_type(cx, field.type)))
  end
  return ok(Ast.Decl.Struct(node.with(name: Resolve.identity(cx, node.name), fields: fields)))
end

def rewrite_enum(cx: Resolve.Context, node: Ast.EnumDecl) -> Result[Ast.Decl]
  variants: List[Ast.EnumVariant] = []
  for variant in node.variants
    payload: List[Ast.TypeRef] = []
    for type in variant.payload_types
      payload = payload.push(try rewrite_payload(cx, node.type_parameters, type))
    end
    variants = variants.push(variant.with(payload_types: payload))
  end
  return ok(Ast.Decl.Enum(node.with(name: Resolve.identity(cx, node.name), variants: variants)))
end

# A payload type that is a type parameter of the enum (T) stays as it is.
def rewrite_payload(cx: Resolve.Context, parameters: List[String], type: Ast.TypeRef) -> Result[Ast.TypeRef]
  name = type.name
  if type.args.size > 0 or !parameters.any? do |parameter| parameter == type.name end
    name = try Resolve.resolve(cx, type.name, Resolve.Want.Type, type.span, false)
  end
  args: List[Ast.TypeRef] = []
  for arg in type.args
    args = args.push(try rewrite_payload(cx, parameters, arg))
  end
  return ok(type.with(name: name, args: args))
end

def rewrite_type(cx: Resolve.Context, type: Ast.TypeRef) -> Result[Ast.TypeRef]
  name = try Resolve.resolve(cx, type.name, Resolve.Want.Type, type.span, false)
  args: List[Ast.TypeRef] = []
  for arg in type.args
    args = args.push(try rewrite_type(cx, arg))
  end
  return ok(type.with(name: name, args: args))
end

def rewrite_optional_type(cx: Resolve.Context, type: Ast.Optional[Ast.TypeRef]) -> Result[Ast.Optional[Ast.TypeRef]]
  case type
    Ast.Optional.Present(found) -> return ok(Ast.Optional.Present(try rewrite_type(cx, found)))
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return ok(type)
  end
end

def rewrite_stmts(cx: Resolve.Context, stmts: List[Ast.Stmt]) -> Result[List[Ast.Stmt]]
  out: List[Ast.Stmt] = []
  for stmt in stmts
    out = out.push(try rewrite_stmt(cx, stmt))
  end
  return ok(out)
end

def rewrite_stmt(cx: Resolve.Context, stmt: Ast.Stmt) -> Result[Ast.Stmt]
  case stmt
    Ast.Stmt.Binding(node) ->
      type = try rewrite_optional_type(cx, node.type)
      value = try rewrite_expr(cx, node.value)
      return ok(Ast.Stmt.Binding(node.with(type: type, value: value)))
    Ast.Stmt.Return(node) ->
      value = try rewrite_optional_expr(cx, node.value)
      return ok(Ast.Stmt.Return(node.with(value: value)))
    Ast.Stmt.Expression(node) -> return ok(Ast.Stmt.Expression(node.with(value: try rewrite_expr(cx, node.value))))
    Ast.Stmt.If(node) -> return rewrite_if(cx, node)
    Ast.Stmt.While(node) ->
      condition = try rewrite_expr(cx, node.condition)
      body = try rewrite_stmts(cx, node.body)
      return ok(Ast.Stmt.While(node.with(condition: condition, body: body)))
    Ast.Stmt.For(node) ->
      iterable = try rewrite_expr(cx, node.iterable)
      body = try rewrite_stmts(cx, node.body)
      return ok(Ast.Stmt.For(node.with(iterable: iterable, body: body)))
    Ast.Stmt.Control(node) -> return ok(stmt)
    Ast.Stmt.Case(node) -> return rewrite_case(cx, node)
  end
end

def rewrite_if(cx: Resolve.Context, node: Ast.IfStmt) -> Result[Ast.Stmt]
  branches: List[Ast.IfBranch] = []
  for branch in node.branches
    condition = try rewrite_expr(cx, branch.condition)
    body = try rewrite_stmts(cx, branch.body)
    branches = branches.push(branch.with(condition: condition, body: body))
  end
  else_body = node.else_body
  case node.else_body
    Ast.Optional.Present(body) -> else_body = Ast.Optional.Present(try rewrite_stmts(cx, body))
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> else_body = node.else_body
  end
  return ok(Ast.Stmt.If(node.with(branches: branches, else_body: else_body)))
end

def rewrite_case(cx: Resolve.Context, node: Ast.CaseStmt) -> Result[Ast.Stmt]
  value = try rewrite_expr(cx, node.value)
  arms: List[Ast.CaseArm] = []
  for arm in node.arms
    pattern = try rewrite_pattern(cx, arm.pattern)
    body = try rewrite_stmts(cx, arm.body)
    arms = arms.push(arm.with(pattern: pattern, body: body))
  end
  return ok(Ast.Stmt.Case(node.with(value: value, arms: arms)))
end

def rewrite_pattern(cx: Resolve.Context, pattern: Ast.Pattern) -> Result[Ast.Pattern]
  case pattern
    Ast.Pattern.Variant(node) ->
      name = try Resolve.resolve(cx, node.enum_name, Resolve.Want.Enum, node.span, false)
      return ok(Ast.Pattern.Variant(node.with(enum_name: name)))
    _ -> return ok(pattern)
  end
end

def rewrite_optional_expr(cx: Resolve.Context, expr: Ast.Optional[Ast.Expr]) -> Result[Ast.Optional[Ast.Expr]]
  case expr
    Ast.Optional.Present(found) -> return ok(Ast.Optional.Present(try rewrite_expr(cx, found)))
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return ok(expr)
  end
end

def rewrite_exprs(cx: Resolve.Context, exprs: List[Ast.Expr]) -> Result[List[Ast.Expr]]
  out: List[Ast.Expr] = []
  for expr in exprs
    out = out.push(try rewrite_expr(cx, expr))
  end
  return ok(out)
end

def rewrite_named(cx: Resolve.Context, args: List[Ast.NamedArg]) -> Result[List[Ast.NamedArg]]
  out: List[Ast.NamedArg] = []
  for arg in args
    out = out.push(arg.with(value: try rewrite_expr(cx, arg.value)))
  end
  return ok(out)
end

def rewrite_expr(cx: Resolve.Context, expr: Ast.Expr) -> Result[Ast.Expr]
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.Literal(node) -> return ok(expr)
    Ast.Expr.Name(node) -> return ok(expr)
    Ast.Expr.TypeName(node) -> return rewrite_type_name(cx, node)
    Ast.Expr.Call(node) -> return rewrite_call(cx, node)
    Ast.Expr.EnumConstructor(node) ->
      name = try Resolve.resolve(cx, node.enum_name, Resolve.Want.Enum, node.span, false)
      args = try rewrite_exprs(cx, node.args)
      return ok(Ast.Expr.EnumConstructor(node.with(enum_name: name, args: args)))
    Ast.Expr.FunctionRef(node) ->
      name = try Resolve.resolve(cx, node.name, Resolve.Want.Function, node.span, false)
      return ok(Ast.Expr.FunctionRef(node.with(name: name)))
    Ast.Expr.Construct(node) -> return rewrite_construct(cx, node)
    _ -> return rewrite_compound(cx, expr)
  end
end

def rewrite_call(cx: Resolve.Context, node: Ast.Call) -> Result[Ast.Expr]
  parts = node.name.split(".")
  if parts.size == 2 and Resolve.constant_identity(cx, parts[0]) != ""
    return rewrite_constant_member(cx, node, Resolve.constant_identity(cx, parts[0]), parts[0].length, parts[1])
  end
  name = try Resolve.resolve(cx, node.name, Resolve.Want.Function, node.span, false)
  args = try rewrite_exprs(cx, node.args)
  return ok(Ast.Expr.Call(node.with(name: name, args: args)))
end

# NAME.x on a constant: a field access when written with no parentheses and no arguments (a block is an argument), a
# method call otherwise (docs/future/44-module-constants.md 44.3). The receiver is the name alone, with an id past the
# ids of the program, since the call has only one.
def rewrite_constant_member(
  cx: Resolve.Context,
  node: Ast.Call,
  linked: String,
  length: Int,
  member: String,
) -> Result[Ast.Expr]
  start = node.span.start
  stop = Source.Position(offset: start.offset + length, line: start.line, column: start.column + length)
  receiver = Ast.Expr.ConstRef(
    Ast.ConstRef(id: cx.ids + node.id, name: linked, span: Source.Span(start: start, stop: stop)),
  )
  if node.args.size == 0 and !node.parenthesized
    return ok(Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(Ast.FieldAccess(id: node.id, target: receiver, name: member, span: node.span)))
  end
  args = try rewrite_exprs(cx, node.args)
  return ok(
    Ast.Expr.MethodCall(Ast.MethodCall(id: node.id, target: receiver, name: member, args: args, span: node.span)),
  )
end

# The expressions that only rewrite their parts, in the order of their fields.
def rewrite_compound(cx: Resolve.Context, expr: Ast.Expr) -> Result[Ast.Expr]
  case expr
    Ast.Expr.Invoke(node) ->
      target = try rewrite_expr(cx, node.target)
      args = try rewrite_exprs(cx, node.args)
      return ok(Ast.Expr.Invoke(node.with(target: target, args: args)))
    Ast.Expr.Update(node) ->
      target = try rewrite_expr(cx, node.target)
      args = try rewrite_named(cx, node.args)
      return ok(Ast.Expr.Update(node.with(target: target, args: args, visible: Ast.Optional.Present(cx.visible))))
    Ast.Expr.ListLit(node) -> return ok(Ast.Expr.ListLit(node.with(elements: try rewrite_exprs(cx, node.elements))))
    Ast.Expr.MapLit(node) -> return rewrite_map(cx, node)
    Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(node) -> return ok(Ast.Expr.FieldAccess(node.with(target: try rewrite_expr(cx, node.target))))
    Ast.Expr.MethodCall(node) ->
      target = try rewrite_expr(cx, node.target)
      args = try rewrite_exprs(cx, node.args)
      return ok(Ast.Expr.MethodCall(node.with(target: target, args: args)))
    Ast.Expr.Interpolation(node) -> return rewrite_interpolation(cx, node)
    Ast.Expr.BlockLit(node) -> return rewrite_block(cx, node)
    Ast.Expr.Index(node) ->
      target = try rewrite_expr(cx, node.target)
      index = try rewrite_expr(cx, node.index)
      return ok(Ast.Expr.Index(node.with(target: target, index: index)))
    Ast.Expr.Try(node) -> return ok(Ast.Expr.Try(node.with(operand: try rewrite_expr(cx, node.operand))))
    Ast.Expr.Unary(node) -> return ok(Ast.Expr.Unary(node.with(operand: try rewrite_expr(cx, node.operand))))
    Ast.Expr.Binary(node) ->
      left = try rewrite_expr(cx, node.left)
      right = try rewrite_expr(cx, node.right)
      return ok(Ast.Expr.Binary(node.with(left: left, right: right)))
    _ -> return ok(expr)
  end
end

def rewrite_map(cx: Resolve.Context, node: Ast.MapLit) -> Result[Ast.Expr]
  entries: List[Ast.MapEntry] = []
  for entry in node.entries
    key = try rewrite_expr(cx, entry.key)
    value = try rewrite_expr(cx, entry.value)
    entries = entries.push(entry.with(key: key, value: value))
  end
  return ok(Ast.Expr.MapLit(node.with(entries: entries)))
end

def rewrite_interpolation(cx: Resolve.Context, node: Ast.Interpolation) -> Result[Ast.Expr]
  parts: List[Ast.Part] = []
  for part in node.parts
    case part
      Ast.Part.Text(text) -> parts = parts.push(part)
      Ast.Part.Code(code) -> parts = parts.push(Ast.Part.Code(try rewrite_expr(cx, code)))
    end
  end
  return ok(Ast.Expr.Interpolation(node.with(parts: parts)))
end

def rewrite_block(cx: Resolve.Context, node: Ast.BlockLit) -> Result[Ast.Expr]
  params: List[Ast.BlockParam] = []
  for param in node.params
    params = params.push(param.with(type: try rewrite_optional_type(cx, param.type)))
  end
  body = try rewrite_stmts(cx, node.body)
  return ok(Ast.Expr.BlockLit(node.with(params: params, body: body)))
end

# Enum.Variant, written without parentheses, is a variant of an enum of this file, one imported by name or a builtin
# one; a name that is a constant of this file is a read of it; any other name is a type.
def rewrite_type_name(cx: Resolve.Context, node: Ast.TypeName) -> Result[Ast.Expr]
  parts = node.name.split(".")
  if parts.size == 2 and Resolve.local_enum?(cx, parts[0])
    return ok(variant(node.id, Resolve.identity(cx, parts[0]), parts[1], [], [], node.span))
  elsif parts.size == 2 and Resolve.named_enum?(cx, parts[0])
    enum_name = try Resolve.resolve(cx, parts[0], Resolve.Want.Enum, node.span, false)
    return ok(variant(node.id, enum_name, parts[1], [], [], node.span))
  elsif parts.size == 2 and cx.settings.catalog.enums.has_key?(parts[0])
    return ok(variant(node.id, parts[0], parts[1], [], [], node.span))
  end
  constant = Resolve.constant_identity(cx, node.name)
  if parts.size == 1 and constant != ""
    return ok(Ast.Expr.ConstRef(Ast.ConstRef(id: node.id, name: constant, span: node.span)))
  end
  if parts.size == 1 and Resolve.unknown_constant?(cx, node.name)
    return error(Resolve.unknown_constant_failure(cx, node.name, node.span))
  end
  name = try Resolve.resolve(cx, node.name, Resolve.Want.Type, node.span, true)
  return ok(Ast.Expr.TypeName(node.with(name: name)))
end

def variant(
  id: Int,
  enum_name: String,
  variant_name: String,
  args: List[Ast.Expr],
  named: List[Ast.NamedArg],
  span: Source.Span,
) -> Ast.Expr
  return Ast.Expr.EnumConstructor(
    Ast.EnumConstructor(
      id: id,
      enum_name: enum_name,
      variant_name: variant_name,
      args: args,
      named: named,
      span: span,
    ),
  )
end

# Name(field: value) builds a struct, unless the name is a variant (Enum.Variant, or Alias.Enum.Variant): that is an
# enum constructor with named arguments, which the checker refuses.
def rewrite_construct(cx: Resolve.Context, node: Ast.Construct) -> Result[Ast.Expr]
  parts = node.type_name.split(".")
  if parts.size == 2 and Resolve.local_enum?(cx, parts[0])
    return ok(
      variant(node.id, Resolve.identity(cx, parts[0]), parts[1], [], try rewrite_named(cx, node.args), node.span),
    )
  elsif parts.size == 2 and Resolve.named_enum?(cx, parts[0])
    enum_name = try Resolve.resolve(cx, parts[0], Resolve.Want.Enum, node.span, false)
    return ok(variant(node.id, enum_name, parts[1], [], try rewrite_named(cx, node.args), node.span))
  elsif parts.size == 2 and cx.settings.catalog.enums.has_key?(parts[0])
    return ok(variant(node.id, parts[0], parts[1], [], try rewrite_named(cx, node.args), node.span))
  elsif parts.size == 3 and exported_enum?(cx, parts[0], parts[1])
    name = try Resolve.resolve(cx, "#{parts[0]}.#{parts[1]}", Resolve.Want.Enum, node.span, false)
    return ok(variant(node.id, name, parts[2], [], try rewrite_named(cx, node.args), node.span))
  end
  name = try Resolve.resolve(cx, node.type_name, Resolve.Want.Type, node.span, false)
  args = try rewrite_named(cx, node.args)
  return ok(Ast.Expr.Construct(node.with(type_name: name, args: args)))
end

def exported_enum?(cx: Resolve.Context, alias: String, name: String) -> Bool
  target = cx.me.aliases.get(alias, "")
  return target != "" and Resolve.exports_enum?(cx.modules[target], name)
end

export struct Position
  offset: Int
  line: Int
  column: Int
end

export struct Span
  start: Position
  stop: Position
end

export def position(offset: Int, line: Int, line_start: Int) -> Position
  return Position(offset: offset, line: line, column: offset - line_start + 1)
end
compiler/source_file.agc:
## Reads a source file for the front end: the whole file, as strict UTF-8, with no size limit.
##
## `File.read_text` stops at 1 MiB and `File.read_bytes` gives at most that many bytes per call, so the file is read
## in chunks. Each chunk is decoded alone and the pieces are joined once, which costs time linear in the size of
## the file (`concat` of two large lists would copy again and again). The bytes of a character that a chunk cuts in
## two wait in `carry` for the next chunk.

import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Source from "source"

## What reading a source file gives: its text; the place of the first invalid byte (the position the lexer would
## have, counting the characters before it); or the system's message when the file cannot be read.
export enum Read
  Text(String)
  Invalid(Source.Position)
  Unreadable(String)
end

## Reads the file at `path`.
export def read(path: String, timeout_ms: Int) -> Read
  opened = File.open(path, "read", timeout_ms)
  if !opened.ok?
    return Read.Unreadable(opened.message)
  end
  handle = opened.unwrap!
  result = read_chunks(handle, timeout_ms)
  File.close(handle, timeout_ms)
  return result
end

## The LEX-INVALID-UTF8 diagnostic for the invalid byte at `at`: a span of length 1 that starts there. Racket has
## the same code, message and help (src/source-file.rkt).
export def invalid_utf8(at: Source.Position) -> Diag.Diagnostic
  stop = Source.Position(offset: at.offset + 1, line: at.line, column: at.column + 1)
  help = Diag.Help.Hint("source files are UTF-8: save the file as UTF-8 text")
  return Diag.fail("LEX-INVALID-UTF8", "source file is not valid UTF-8", Source.Span(start: at, stop: stop), help)
end

def read_chunks(handle: FileHandle, timeout_ms: Int) -> Read
  parts: List[String] = []
  carry: List[Int] = []
  finished = false
  while !finished
    got = File.read_bytes(handle, 262144, timeout_ms)
    if !got.ok?
      return Read.Unreadable(got.message)
    end
    chunk = got.unwrap!
    finished = chunk.size == 0
    data = carry.concat(chunk)
    cut = data.size
    if !finished
      cut = complete_prefix(data)
    end
    head = data.take(cut)
    carry = data.drop(cut)
    decoded = String.from_bytes(head)
    if !decoded.ok?
      return Read.Invalid(error_position(parts, head))
    end
    parts = parts.push(decoded.unwrap!)
  end
  return Read.Text(parts.join(""))
end

# How many leading bytes of `data` end on a character boundary. A lead byte in the last three bytes whose
# sequence is not complete yet stays out, so the next chunk can finish it. Anything else (an invalid lead byte,
# a stray continuation byte) is left in: String.from_bytes then rejects it.
def complete_prefix(data: List[Int]) -> Int
  size = data.size
  back = 1
  while back <= 3 and back <= size
    byte = data[size - back]
    if byte < 128
      return size
    end
    if byte >= 192
      if lead_width(byte) > back
        return size - back
      end
      return size
    end
    back += 1
  end
  return size
end

# The length of the sequence a lead byte starts, or 0 when it cannot start one.
def lead_width(byte: Int) -> Int
  if byte >= 194 and byte <= 223
    return 2
  end
  if byte >= 224 and byte <= 239
    return 3
  end
  if byte >= 240 and byte <= 244
    return 4
  end
  return 0
end

# `head` did not decode. The position is that of the first invalid sequence, found by hand (the error path only).
# The characters, lines and columns before it are counted in loops, as src/source-file.rkt does: the decoded chunks
# by their newlines, and the valid bytes of `head` by their lead bytes. The text before it is never built in one piece.
def error_position(parts: List[String], head: List[Int]) -> Source.Position
  bad = first_invalid(head)
  valid = head.size
  if bad >= 0
    valid = bad
  end
  offset = 0
  line = 1
  since_newline = 0
  for part in parts
    pieces = part.split("\n")
    offset += part.length
    line += pieces.size - 1
    last = pieces[pieces.size - 1].length
    if pieces.size > 1
      since_newline = last
    else
      since_newline += last
    end
  end
  at = 0
  while at < valid
    byte = head[at]
    # A continuation byte (128 to 191) belongs to the character its lead byte started.
    if byte < 128 or byte >= 192
      offset += 1
      since_newline += 1
      if byte == 10
        line += 1
        since_newline = 0
      end
    end
    at += 1
  end
  return Source.Position(offset: offset, line: line, column: since_newline + 1)
end

# The index of the first byte of the first invalid sequence, or -1. The rules of agc_utf8_valid in vm/value.c.
def first_invalid(data: List[Int]) -> Int
  at = 0
  while at < data.size
    width = sequence_width(data, at)
    if width == 0
      return at
    end
    at += width
  end
  return -1
end

# The length of the valid sequence that starts at `at`, or 0: no overlong form, no surrogate, nothing above
# U+10FFFF, and no sequence cut short by the end of the data.
def sequence_width(data: List[Int], at: Int) -> Int
  lead = data[at]
  if lead < 128
    return 1
  end
  width = lead_width(lead)
  if width == 0 or at + width > data.size
    return 0
  end
  code = lead - 192
  if width == 3
    code = lead - 224
  end
  if width == 4
    code = lead - 240
  end
  for k in 1...width
    next_byte = data[at + k]
    if next_byte < 128 or next_byte > 191
      return 0
    end
    code = code * 64 + next_byte - 128
  end
  if (width == 3 and code < 2048) or (width == 4 and code < 65536) or code > 1114111
    return 0
  end
  if code >= 55296 and code <= 57343
    return 0
  end
  return width
end

## The "did you mean" help of an unknown name: src/builtins.rkt (did-you-mean, edit-distance).

import Ast from "ast"
import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Types from "types"
import Declarations from "declarations"

## The help text for the exported name closest to name, or Absent when none is close. A name of up to 4 characters may
## differ by 1 edit, a longer one by 2; the nearest wins, and the smaller name breaks a tie.
export def did_you_mean(name: String, candidates: List[String]) -> Ast.Optional[String]
  return did_you_mean_among(name, candidates, [])
end

## did_you_mean for the names of a linked program (src/builtins.rkt, did-you-mean). A linked name starts with "@N::",
## the prefix of its file; only the candidates of the same file are offered, and without their prefix. shared are extra
## candidates that have no prefix, such as the builtin names.
export def did_you_mean_among(
  full_name: String,
  candidates: List[String],
  shared: List[String],
) -> Ast.Optional[String]
  case closest_among(full_name, candidates, shared)
    Ast.Optional.Present(name) -> return Ast.Optional.Present("did you mean \"#{name}\"?")
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return Ast.Optional.Absent
  end
end

## The name nearest to full_name among the candidates of its file and the shared ones, or Absent when none is close
## (src/builtins.rkt, closest-name).
export def closest_among(full_name: String, candidates: List[String], shared: List[String]) -> Ast.Optional[String]
  prefix = file_prefix(full_name)
  name = Types.display_name(full_name)
  limit = 2
  if name.length <= 4
    limit = 1
  end
  pool: List[String] = []
  for candidate in candidates
    if file_prefix(candidate) == prefix
      pool = pool.push(Types.display_name(candidate))
    end
  end
  return nearest(name, pool.concat(shared).sort, limit)
end

## The help of CHECK-IMPORT-NAME for member, which the module key does not export: the fixed texts for the removed
## std/http functions and std/logger error, or the did-you-mean over the exports (a private name is never suggested).
## Through an alias (Mod.nme) a constant is suggested as the import that reads it.
export def unknown_import_help(
  key: String,
  exports: Map[String, Declarations.Kind],
  member: String,
  via_alias: Bool,
) -> Diag.Help
  removed = ["respond", "begin", "write", "write_bytes", "finish"].any? do |name| name == member end
  if key == "std/http.agc" and removed
    return Diag.Help.Hint(
      "a handler returns its whole response: return ok(HttpResponse(status: 200, headers: [], body: text))",
    )
  elsif key == "std/logger.agc" and member == "error"
    return Diag.Help.Hint("the function for the error level is Logger.err; error is a reserved name")
  end
  case closest_among(member, exports.keys, [])
    Ast.Optional.Present(name) ->
      if via_alias and Declarations.constant?(exports[name])
        return Diag.Help.Hint("did you mean \"import {#{name}}\"?")
      end
      return Diag.Help.Hint("did you mean \"#{name}\"?")
    Ast.Optional.Absent -> return Diag.Help.NoHelp
  end
end

## The "@N::" a linked name starts with, or "".
export def file_prefix(name: String) -> String
  shown = Types.display_name(name)
  return name.slice(0, name.length - shown.length)
end

## The number of single-character edits (insert, delete, replace) from a to b.
export def edit_distance(a: String, b: String) -> Int
  right = b.split("")
  first: List[Int] = (0..right.size).to_a
  return last_row(a.split(""), right, 1, first)
end

# The candidates are sorted, so the first one at the smallest distance is the smaller name of a tie. A candidate whose
# length differs by more than the limit cannot be near, which skips most of the table.
def nearest(name: String, ordered: List[String], limit: Int) -> Ast.Optional[String]
  best = ""
  best_distance = limit + 1
  for candidate in ordered
    if candidate != name and close_in_length?(candidate, name, limit)
      distance = edit_distance(name, candidate)
      if distance < best_distance
        best = candidate
        best_distance = distance
      end
    end
  end
  if best_distance > limit
    return Ast.Optional.Absent
  end
  return Ast.Optional.Present(best)
end

# One row of the table per character of the left word; the answer is the end of the last row.
def last_row(left: List[String], right: List[String], index: Int, previous: List[Int]) -> Int
  if index > left.size
    return previous[right.size]
  end
  return last_row(left, right, index + 1, next_row(left[index - 1], right, index, previous))
end

def next_row(character: String, right: List[String], index: Int, previous: List[Int]) -> List[Int]
  row: List[Int] = [index]
  for column in 1..right.size
    cost = 1
    if right[column - 1] == character
      cost = 0
    end
    best = smallest(previous[column] + 1, row[column - 1] + 1, previous[column - 1] + cost)
    row = row.push(best)
  end
  return row
end

def smallest(a: Int, b: Int, c: Int) -> Int
  least = a
  if b < least
    least = b
  end
  if c < least
    least = c
  end
  return least
end

def close_in_length?(a: String, b: String, limit: Int) -> Bool
  return a.length - b.length <= limit and b.length - a.length <= limit
end
compiler/text.agc:
## Text helpers shared by the text forms of the lexer and the parser.

import Diag from "diagnostic"
import Source from "source"
import Unicode from "unicode"

## A String as ASCII text between double quotes; every other character is written as \\u{HEX}.
export def quote(text: String) -> String
  codes = text.split("").map do |character| String.code(character) end
  parts: List[String] = ["\""]
  segment = 0
  index = 0
  while index < codes.size
    code = codes[index]
    if code < 32 or code > 126 or code == 34 or code == 92
      parts = parts.push(text.slice(segment, index - segment))
      parts = parts.push(escaped(code))
      segment = index + 1
    end
    index += 1
  end
  parts = parts.push(text.slice(segment, codes.size - segment))
  parts = parts.push("\"")
  return parts.join("")
end

## A span as offset:line:column-offset:line:column.
export def span_text(span: Source.Span) -> String
  return "#{position_text(span.start)}-#{position_text(span.stop)}"
end

## The ERROR line of a diagnostic: code, span, message and help (- when there is none).
export def diagnostic_line(problem: Diag.Diagnostic) -> String
  return "ERROR #{problem.code} #{span_text(problem.span)} #{quote(problem.message)} #{help_text(problem.help)}"
end

def escaped(code: Int) -> String
  case code
    34 -> return "\\\""
    92 -> return "\\\\"
    10 -> return "\\n"
    13 -> return "\\r"
    9 -> return "\\t"
    _ -> return "\\u{#{Unicode.hex_text(code)}}"
  end
end

def position_text(position: Source.Position) -> String
  return "#{position.offset}:#{position.line}:#{position.column}"
end

def help_text(help: Diag.Help) -> String
  case help
    Diag.Help.NoHelp -> return "-"
    Diag.Help.Hint(text) -> return quote(text)
  end
end

compiler/types.agc:
## The types the checker works with: the lists headed by a name of src/checker.rkt ('Int, '(List T), '(Struct "Point"))
## as an enum.

## A resolved type. Opaque holds the name of a handle or other builtin type with no structure (Socket, Process,
## TestCase). Struct and Enum hold the linked name; Enum carries its type arguments (none for a plain enum). Var is a
## type variable of a builtin signature or a generic enum. Fn lists the parameters, then the result. Unknown is no
## type: the expected type when none is known (src/checker.rkt uses #f), and the type of a literal the lexer could not
## classify.
export enum Type
  Int
  Float
  Bool
  String
  Nil
  Void
  Json
  Range
  Unknown
  Opaque(String)
  Result(Type)
  Task(Type)
  Channel(Type)
  List(Type)
  Set(Type)
  Map(Type, Type)
  Fn(List[Type], Type)
  Struct(String)
  Enum(String, List[Type])
  Var(String)
end

## The variant of a type as a word: "Int", "List", "Struct", ... Every test of a type's shape is a comparison with this
## word.
export def tag(type: Type) -> String
  case type
    Type.Int -> return "Int"
    Type.Float -> return "Float"
    Type.Bool -> return "Bool"
    Type.String -> return "String"
    Type.Nil -> return "Nil"
    Type.Void -> return "Void"
    Type.Json -> return "Json"
    Type.Range -> return "Range"
    Type.Unknown -> return "Unknown"
    Type.Opaque(name) -> return "Opaque"
    Type.Result(item) -> return "Result"
    Type.Task(item) -> return "Task"
    Type.Channel(item) -> return "Channel"
    Type.List(item) -> return "List"
    Type.Set(item) -> return "Set"
    Type.Map(key, value) -> return "Map"
    Type.Fn(params, result) -> return "Fn"
    Type.Struct(name) -> return "Struct"
    Type.Enum(name, args) -> return "Enum"
    Type.Var(name) -> return "Var"
  end
end

## True when the type is that variant: is(type, "List").
export def is(type: Type, word: String) -> Bool
  return tag(type) == word
end

## True for no type (Unknown).
export def unknown?(type: Type) -> Bool
  return tag(type) == "Unknown"
end

## The element type of a List, Set, Result, Task or Channel; Unknown for any other type.
export def item(type: Type) -> Type
  case type
    Type.Result(inner) -> return inner
    Type.Task(inner) -> return inner
    Type.Channel(inner) -> return inner
    Type.List(inner) -> return inner
    Type.Set(inner) -> return inner
    _ -> return Type.Unknown
  end
end

## The key type of a Map; Unknown for any other type.
export def key(type: Type) -> Type
  case type
    Type.Map(inner, value) -> return inner
    _ -> return Type.Unknown
  end
end

## The value type of a Map; Unknown for any other type.
export def value(type: Type) -> Type
  case type
    Type.Map(key, inner) -> return inner
    _ -> return Type.Unknown
  end
end

## The parameter types of an Fn; empty for any other type.
export def params(type: Type) -> List[Type]
  case type
    Type.Fn(found, result) -> return found
    _ -> return []
  end
end

## The result type of an Fn; Unknown for any other type.
export def result(type: Type) -> Type
  case type
    Type.Fn(found, last) -> return last
    _ -> return Type.Unknown
  end
end

## The name of an Opaque, Var, Struct or Enum type; "" for any other type.
export def name(type: Type) -> String
  case type
    Type.Opaque(found) -> return found
    Type.Var(found) -> return found
    Type.Struct(found) -> return found
    Type.Enum(found, args) -> return found
    _ -> return ""
  end
end

## The type arguments of an Enum type; empty for any other type.
export def args(type: Type) -> List[Type]
  case type
    Type.Enum(found, list) -> return list
    _ -> return []
  end
end

## Structural equality, since an enum cannot be compared with ==. This is equal? on the types of src/checker.rkt.
export def same(a: Type, b: Type) -> Bool
  if tag(a) != tag(b)
    return false
  end
  case a
    Type.Opaque(found) -> return found == name(b)
    Type.Var(found) -> return found == name(b)
    Type.Struct(found) -> return found == name(b)
    Type.Enum(found, list) -> return found == name(b) and same_all(list, args(b))
    Type.Map(key_type, value_type) -> return same(key_type, key(b)) and same(value_type, value(b))
    Type.Fn(list, last) -> return same_all(list, params(b)) and same(last, result(b))
    Type.Result(inner) -> return same(inner, item(b))
    Type.Task(inner) -> return same(inner, item(b))
    Type.Channel(inner) -> return same(inner, item(b))
    Type.List(inner) -> return same(inner, item(b))
    Type.Set(inner) -> return same(inner, item(b))
    _ -> return true
  end
end

## True when the two lists have the same length and equal types in order.
export def same_all(a: List[Type], b: List[Type]) -> Bool
  if a.size != b.size
    return false
  end
  index = 0
  while index < a.size
    if !same(a[index], b[index])
      return false
    end
    index += 1
  end
  return true
end

## Result[type], or Unknown when there is no type: the expected type of the operand of try.
export def result_of(type: Type) -> Type
  if unknown?(type)
    return type
  end
  return Type.Result(type)
end

## Task[type], or Unknown when there is no type.
export def task_of(type: Type) -> Type
  if unknown?(type)
    return type
  end
  return Type.Task(type)
end

## List[type], or Unknown when there is no type.
export def list_of(type: Type) -> Type
  if unknown?(type)
    return type
  end
  return Type.List(type)
end

## The type itself when it is a List, else Unknown: the expected type that a list operation passes on.
export def only_list(type: Type) -> Type
  if is(type, "List")
    return type
  end
  return Type.Unknown
end

## The type itself when it is a Map, else Unknown.
export def only_map(type: Type) -> Type
  if is(type, "Map")
    return type
  end
  return Type.Unknown
end

## The type itself when it is a Set, else Unknown.
export def only_set(type: Type) -> Type
  if is(type, "Set")
    return type
  end
  return Type.Unknown
end

## The item of a Result, else Unknown: the expected type of the value inside a Result.
export def only_result_item(type: Type) -> Type
  if is(type, "Result")
    return item(type)
  end
  return Type.Unknown
end

## The name as the user wrote it: the linker gives a name from another file the prefix "@N::" to keep it unique, and
## messages leave it out.
export def display_name(name: String) -> String
  if not name.starts_with?("@")
    return name
  end
  digits_end = 1
  while digits_end < name.length and digit?(name.at(digits_end))
    digits_end += 1
  end
  if digits_end > 1 and name.length >= digits_end + 2 and name.slice(digits_end, 2) == "::"
    return name.slice(digits_end + 2, name.length - digits_end - 2)
  end
  return name
end

## The type as the messages print it: Int, List[String], Map[String, Int], Fn[Int, Void], Point, Option[Int].
export def to_text(type: Type) -> String
  case type
    Type.Int -> return "Int"
    Type.Float -> return "Float"
    Type.Bool -> return "Bool"
    Type.String -> return "String"
    Type.Nil -> return "Nil"
    Type.Void -> return "Void"
    Type.Json -> return "Json"
    Type.Range -> return "Range"
    Type.Unknown -> return "?"
    Type.Opaque(name) -> return name
    Type.Var(name) -> return name
    Type.Struct(name) -> return display_name(name)
    Type.Enum(name, args) -> return enum_text(name, args)
    Type.Result(item) -> return "Result[#{to_text(item)}]"
    Type.Task(item) -> return "Task[#{to_text(item)}]"
    Type.Channel(item) -> return "Channel[#{to_text(item)}]"
    Type.List(item) -> return "List[#{to_text(item)}]"
    Type.Set(item) -> return "Set[#{to_text(item)}]"
    Type.Map(key, value) -> return "Map[#{to_text(key)}, #{to_text(value)}]"
    Type.Fn(params, result) -> return "Fn[#{list_text(params.concat([result]))}]"
  end
end

## The type with its variant written out, for tests: Struct(Header), Enum(Await, [Var(T)]), Fn([Int], Void). Unlike
## to_text, two variants never print the same.
export def debug_text(type: Type) -> String
  case type
    Type.Opaque(name) -> return "Opaque(#{name})"
    Type.Var(name) -> return "Var(#{name})"
    Type.Struct(name) -> return "Struct(#{name})"
    Type.Enum(name, args) -> return "Enum(#{name}, [#{debug_list(args)}])"
    Type.Result(item) -> return "Result(#{debug_text(item)})"
    Type.Task(item) -> return "Task(#{debug_text(item)})"
    Type.Channel(item) -> return "Channel(#{debug_text(item)})"
    Type.List(item) -> return "List(#{debug_text(item)})"
    Type.Set(item) -> return "Set(#{debug_text(item)})"
    Type.Map(key, value) -> return "Map(#{debug_text(key)}, #{debug_text(value)})"
    Type.Fn(params, result) -> return "Fn([#{debug_list(params)}], #{debug_text(result)})"
    _ -> return to_text(type)
  end
end

## The types joined by ", ".
export def list_text(types: List[Type]) -> String
  return types.map do |type: Type| to_text(type) end.join(", ")
end

def debug_list(types: List[Type]) -> String
  return types.map do |type: Type| debug_text(type) end.join(", ")
end

def enum_text(name: String, args: List[Type]) -> String
  if args.size == 0
    return display_name(name)
  end
  return "#{display_name(name)}[#{list_text(args)}]"
end

def digit?(character: String) -> Bool
  code = character.code
  return code >= 48 and code <= 57
end

import Table from "unicode_table"

export def graphic?(code: Int) -> Bool
  ranges = Table.graphic_ranges()
  return search(ranges, code, 0, ranges.size / 2)
end

## An Int as upper-case hexadecimal digits, padded with zeros to width.
export def hex(value: Int, width: Int) -> String
  digits = "0123456789ABCDEF"
  parts: List[String] = []
  rest = value
  while rest > 0
    parts = parts.push(digits.slice(rest % 16, 1))
    rest = rest / 16
  end
  while parts.size < width
    parts = parts.push("0")
  end
  return parts.reverse.join("")
end

export def hex_text(value: Int) -> String
  return hex(value, 1)
end

export def written(code: Int) -> String
  case code
    0 -> return "#\\nul"
    8 -> return "#\\backspace"
    9 -> return "#\\tab"
    10 -> return "#\\newline"
    11 -> return "#\\vtab"
    12 -> return "#\\page"
    13 -> return "#\\return"
    32 -> return "#\\space"
    127 -> return "#\\rubout"
    _ ->
      if code < 65536
        return "#\\u#{hex(code, 4)}"
      end
      return "#\\U#{hex(code, 8)}"
  end
end

## A String as Racket writes it (`write`): quotes, with \\a \\b \\t \\n \\v \\f \\r \\e, \\" and \\\\, and \\uXXXX or
## \\UXXXXXXXX for characters that are neither graphic nor blank.
export def written_text(text: String) -> String
  ranges = Table.graphic_ranges()
  parts: List[String] = ["\""]
  for character in text.split("")
    parts = parts.push(written_character(ranges, String.code(character), character))
  end
  parts = parts.push("\"")
  return parts.join("")
end

def search(ranges: List[Int], code: Int, low: Int, high: Int) -> Bool
  while low < high
    middle = (low + high) / 2
    if ranges[middle * 2 + 1] < code
      low = middle + 1
    else
      high = middle
    end
  end
  return low * 2 < ranges.size and ranges[low * 2] <= code
end

def blank?(code: Int) -> Bool
  return (
    code == 32 or
    code == 160 or
    code == 5760 or
    (code >= 8192 and code <= 8202) or
    code == 8239 or
    code == 8287 or
    code == 12288
  )
end

def written_character(ranges: List[Int], code: Int, character: String) -> String
  case code
    34 -> return "\\\""
    92 -> return "\\\\"
    7 -> return "\\a"
    8 -> return "\\b"
    9 -> return "\\t"
    10 -> return "\\n"
    11 -> return "\\v"
    12 -> return "\\f"
    13 -> return "\\r"
    27 -> return "\\e"
    _ ->
      if (code > 32 and code < 127) or blank?(code) or search(ranges, code, 0, ranges.size / 2)
        return character
      end
      if code < 65536
        return "\\u#{hex(code, 4)}"
      end
      return "\\U#{hex(code, 8)}"
  end
end
